value: wisdom — the wise son who gladdens his father
the wise son whose wisdom makes his father glad
welded to the joy the wise son produces
chakam (wise) — 'a WISE son makes a glad father'; wisdom's fruit reaches beyond the self into the family's joy. The son's inner character shapes the parents' heart.
gladness — the joy a wise son brings his father
the father's gladness produced by his son's wisdom
welded to the wisdom that produces it
samach (rejoice/be glad) — 'makes a GLAD father'; the parental joy that wise children give. Wisdom is relational, gladdening those who love the child.
folly — the foolish son who grieves his mother
the foolish son whose folly is grief to his mother
welded to the grief the fool produces
kesil (dull fool) — 'a FOOLISH son'; the antithesis to the wise son. Folly too reaches the family — as sorrow.
grief — the pain a foolish son brings his mother
the mother's grief caused by her son's folly
welded to the folly that produces it
tugah (grief/sorrow) — 'a sorrow to his MOTHER'; the answering grief to the father's gladness. The couplet frames a child's character by the joy or pain it gives the parents.
trouble-making — the sly winker causes trouble
the trouble the sly, eye-winking schemer gives to others
welded to the sorrow it produces
nathan (give) — 'whoever WINKS the eye CAUSES trouble'; the furtive gesture of the malicious, sowing sorrow by sly signals. Emergent: the giving/causing of trouble by covert malice.
sorrow — the trouble the winker causes
the sorrow/pain the deceitful winker inflicts
welded to the malice that produces it
atsebet (pain/sorrow) — 'causes TROUBLE'; the grief that sly malice sows. Emergent: trouble/sorrow as the fruit of covert deceit.
folly — the babbling fool who comes to ruin
the prating, lip-foolish fool who talks his way to ruin
the chattering folly that ends in ruin
evil (fool) — 'a babbling fool will come to ruin' (echoing 10:8b); the fool of the lips ruins himself with chatter, paired here with the malice of the winker. Two mouths that destroy.
righteousness — whose mouth is a fountain of life
the righteous whose speech gives life like a spring
welded to the life its mouth pours
tsaddiq — 'the mouth of the RIGHTEOUS is a fountain of life'; righteous speech nourishes and revives. Character shows in the mouth.
life — the life-giving power of righteous speech
the life that the righteous mouth pours out like a fountain
welded to the righteous whose mouth gives it
chayyim (life) — 'a FOUNTAIN OF LIFE'; the righteous word is life-giving, reviving those who hear. Emergent: life as the yield of righteous speech.
the wicked whose smooth speech hides brutality
the wicked mouth masking the violence within
rasha — 'the mouth of the WICKED conceals violence' (=10:6b); speech as a mask for inner brutality. The violence (chamas) hidden is the qualifier.
the hatred that rouses and inflames conflict
welded to the rousing it drives
sinah (hatred) — 'HATRED stirs up strife'; enmity is generative — it breeds conflict. The antithesis of covering love.
the stirring-up/rousing by which hatred kindles conflict
uor (rouse/stir up) — hatred 'STIRS UP' strife, actively kindling it. Emergent: the rousing of conflict as hatred's characteristic act. The strife (madon) is the qualifier.
the love that covers over and forgives all transgressions
welded to the wrongs it overlooks
ahabah (love) — 'LOVE covers all offenses'; where hatred inflames, love forgives and conceals wrong. The generous overlooking of the loving heart.
the transgressions that love covers over rather than exposes
welded to the love that overlooks them
pesha (transgression/offense) — 'love covers all OFFENSES'; the wrongs that love, unlike hatred, chooses to cover. Forgiveness as love's answer to sin.
discernment — on whose lips wisdom is found
the understanding whose lips carry wisdom
welded to the wisdom his lips bear
bin (discern/understand) — 'on the lips of him who has UNDERSTANDING, wisdom is found'; discernment shows in speech. The wise mouth reveals the wise heart.
wisdom — found on the discerning lips
the wisdom that is found on the lips of the understanding
welded to the discernment whose lips carry it
chokmah — 'WISDOM is found' on the lips of the discerning; the outflow of an understanding heart, in contrast to the senseless who need the rod.
heartlessness — the one who lacks sense, fit for the rod
the lack of sense/heart that earns a rod on the back
(the wisdom on discerning lips, by contrast)
set against the discernment that bears wisdom
leb (heart/sense) — 'a rod for the back of him who LACKS sense'; where discernment speaks wisdom, senselessness must be beaten. Two ends of the same axis.
wisdom — the wise lay up knowledge
the wise who store up and treasure knowledge
welded to the knowledge they lay up
chakam (wise) — 'the wise LAY UP knowledge'; the prudent accumulate wisdom as a reserve, unlike the fool whose mouth spills ruin.
knowledge — the store the wise lay up
the knowledge that the wise treasure and reserve
welded to the wise who hoard it
daath (knowledge) — 'lay up KNOWLEDGE'; a treasured reserve, held in readiness. Wisdom accumulates quietly.
folly — the fool's mouth brings ruin near
the fool whose mouth brings destruction close at hand
the fool's mouth that hastens ruin
evil (fool) — 'the mouth of a FOOL brings ruin near'; where the wise store knowledge, the fool's mouth invites destruction. The ruin (mechittah) is the qualifier.
riches — the rich man whose wealth is his fortress
the rich man who leans on his wealth as a strong city
welded to the wealth he trusts
ashir (rich) — 'a RICH man's wealth is his strong city'; the rich lean on riches for security. Emergent. The read notes the trust placed in wealth (which elsewhere proves false, 11:28).
wealth — the rich man's imagined stronghold
the wealth that the rich treat as a fortified city
welded to the security it seems to give
hon (wealth) — 'his strong city'; wealth as a felt fortress. Emergent. The inner reliance on riches for safety.
security — the fortress-strength wealth seems to give
the sense of strength/security the rich draw from their wealth
welded to the wealth imagined as strength
oz (strength) — 'his STRONG city'; the felt security of the wealthy, a stronghold of the mind. Set against the poor whose want is ruin.
poverty — the poor whose want is their ruin
the poor/lowly whose poverty is their undoing
welded to the ruin poverty brings them
dal (poor/weak/low) — 'the POVERTY of the poor is their ruin'; the destitute have no fortress. The inner-and-outer helplessness of want, opposite the rich man's confidence.
ruin — the destruction poverty brings the poor
the ruin/destruction that the poverty of the poor becomes for them
welded to the poverty that dooms them
mechittah (ruin/terror) — the poor's poverty IS 'their ruin'; want as a kind of destruction. The dark counterpart to the rich man's strong city.
righteousness — whose wage leads to life
the righteous whose earnings issue in life
welded to the life it produces
tsaddiq — 'the wage of the RIGHTEOUS leads to life'; what the righteous earn tends to life, because rightly used.
life — where the righteous wage leads
the life to which the righteous person's earnings lead
welded to the righteous whose wage yields it
chayyim (life) — 'leads to LIFE'; righteous gain is life-directed. Emergent: life as the terminus of righteous labour.
wickedness — whose gain leads to sin
the wicked whose profit issues in sin
welded to the sin it produces
rasha — 'the gain of the WICKED to sin'; ill-directed profit breeds more sin. Gain follows the moral bent of its owner.
sin — where the wicked's gain leads
the sin to which the wicked person's gain leads
welded to the wicked whose gain yields it
chattah (sin) — 'to SIN'; the wicked's profit compounds into further sin, the dark antithesis of the righteous wage that leads to life.
heeding — keeping instruction, the path to life
the keeping/heeding of instruction that sets one on the path to life
the heeding directed to the teaching
shamar (keep/heed) — 'whoever HEEDS instruction is on the path to life'; obedient keeping of correction leads to life. Instruction (musar) is the object (qualifier).
misleading — the reproof-rejecter leads others astray
the leading-astray by which the one who spurns reproof misleads others
(the heeding path to life, by contrast)
set against the disciple's path to life
taah (go/lead astray, Hiphil) — 'he who rejects reproof LEADS ASTRAY'; rejecting correction not only ruins oneself but misleads others. Error propagates.
the hatred that a man hides behind false, lying lips
the lying lips that hide it (262530)
welded to the falsehood that masks it
sinah (hatred) — 'the one who CONCEALS hatred has lying lips'; hidden enmity forces deceit — to hide hate one must lie. Inner malice corrupts speech.
falsehood — the lying lips that hide hatred
the false, lying lips required to conceal inner hatred
welded to the malice they cover
sheqer (falsehood/lie) — 'has LYING lips'; concealed hatred and deceit go together. The mouth betrays or masks the heart.
slander — the defamation the fool spreads
the slander/evil-report that the fool utters against others
welded to the folly of uttering it
dibbah (slander/evil report) — 'whoever utters SLANDER'; open defamation, the other face of concealed hatred. Whether hidden or spoken, malice marks the speech.
folly — the slanderer is a fool
the folly of the one who spreads slander
welded to the slander that proves it
kesil (fool) — 'whoever utters slander is a FOOL'; slander is not shrewd but foolish, self-condemning. Malicious speech brands its speaker.
transgression — abounding where words are many
the transgression that inevitably accompanies a flood of words
set against the restraint of the wise lips
pesha (transgression) — 'when words are MANY, transgression is not lacking'; verbosity breeds sin. The unrestrained tongue trips into wrong.
the prudence shown in holding back and restraining one's speech
(the sinful flood of words, by contrast)
set against the transgression of many words
sakal (act prudently) — 'whoever RESTRAINS his lips is prudent'; the wise govern their tongue. Restraint of speech is a mark of prudence, the antithesis of babbling.
wickedness — its treasures do not profit
the wickedness whose ill-gotten treasures bring no lasting profit
set against righteousness as the profitless way
resha (wickedness) — 'treasures gained by WICKEDNESS do not profit'; ill-gotten wealth is empty. Character, not gain, decides one's end.
the righteousness that rescues its owner from death, where wicked treasure cannot
set against wickedness as the delivering way
tsedaqah (righteousness) — 'RIGHTEOUSNESS delivers from death'; the antithesis — moral character, not material treasure, is what saves. The book's recurring wealth-vs-righteousness contrast.
righteousness — whose tongue is choice silver
the righteous whose speech is precious as choice silver
welded to the precious worth of his tongue
tsaddiq — 'the tongue of the RIGHTEOUS is choice silver'; righteous speech is precious, valuable to those who hear.
preciousness — the choice worth of the righteous tongue
the choice, select value of the righteous person's speech
welded to the righteous whose tongue it prizes
bachar (choice/select) — 'CHOICE silver'; the righteous tongue is of the finest worth, unlike the worthless heart of the wicked.
the heart — of the wicked, of little worth
the heart of the wicked, worth little or nothing
welded to the wickedness that empties it
leb (heart) — 'the HEART of the wicked is of little worth'; where righteous speech is choice silver, the wicked's inner life is worthless. The heart's worth tracks character.
wickedness — whose heart is of little worth
the wicked character whose heart is worthless
welded to the heart it hollows out
rasha — the wicked's heart 'is of little worth'; wickedness empties the inner life of value. The dark side of the couplet.
the righteous whose speech nourishes and feeds many
set against the fools who die for want of sense
tsaddiq — 'the lips of the RIGHTEOUS feed many'; righteous speech is nourishment for others, life-giving and generous.
folly — the fools who die for lack of sense
the fools who perish for want of sense
welded to the senselessness that kills them
evil (fool) — 'FOOLS die for lack of sense'; where the righteous feed many, fools cannot even keep themselves alive. Folly is fatal.
heartlessness — the lack of sense that kills fools
the lack of sense/heart for which fools die
welded to the fools whom it destroys
leb (heart/sense) — 'die for LACK of sense'; the empty heart is lethal (cf 10:13). Senselessness not merely fails but destroys.
blessing — the LORD's, which makes rich
the LORD's blessing that enriches without pain
welded to the wealth it gives
berakah (blessing) — 'the BLESSING of the LORD makes rich'; true wealth comes from God's blessing, not toil or greed. The read notes the source of real prosperity.
the enrichment that the LORD's blessing brings about
welded to the blessing that produces it
ashar (make rich) — 'MAKES rich'; God's blessing is what truly enriches. Emergent: divine enrichment, distinct from anxious gain.
sorrowlessness — God's blessing adds no painful toil
the painful toil/sorrow that God's blessing does NOT add to its wealth
the absence of grief that marks God-given wealth
etseb (painful toil/sorrow) — 'he adds no SORROW with it'; unlike anxious, self-won gain (which breeds grief), God's blessing enriches without the painful toil. Wealth without a sting.
mischief — the wrong a fool treats as sport
the wickedness/mischief that is mere amusement to a fool
the fool who sports at it (262575)
welded to the folly that makes light of it
zimmah (wickedness/mischief) — 'doing WRONG is like a joke to a fool'; the fool treats evil as entertainment, feeling no gravity. The moral numbness of folly.
folly — the fool who sports at wrongdoing
the fool to whom evil is a game
welded to the mischief he makes light of
kesil (fool) — 'like a joke to a FOOL'; folly finds pleasure in evil, unable to feel its weight. The opposite of the wise man's delight in wisdom.
wisdom — the delight of the discerning
the wisdom that is pleasure and delight to a man of understanding
the understanding that delights in it (262578)
welded to the discernment that enjoys it
chokmah — 'WISDOM is pleasure to a man of understanding'; where the fool delights in wrong, the wise delight in wisdom itself. Character shows in what one enjoys.
understanding — who takes pleasure in wisdom
the man of understanding whose delight is wisdom
welded to the wisdom that is his pleasure
tebunah (understanding) — 'to a man of UNDERSTANDING'; the discerning find their joy in wisdom, as the fool finds his in mischief. Delight reveals the heart.
wickedness — whose very dread overtakes him
the wicked upon whom the thing he dreads comes true
welded to the terror that befalls him
rasha — 'what the WICKED dreads will come upon him'; the wicked's fears are realised. Guilt anticipates its own doom.
dread — the wicked's terror, which befalls him
the dread/terror the wicked feels, which comes true upon him
welded to the wicked whom it overtakes
megorah (dread/terror) — 'what the wicked DREADS'; the anxious terror of the guilty, and its fulfilment. The wicked live in fear that materialises.
desire — the righteous', which is granted
the desire of the righteous, which is granted to them
welded to the granting that fulfils it
taavah (desire) — 'the DESIRE of the righteous will be granted'; the righteous' longings are fulfilled, the bright opposite of the wicked's realised dread.
the righteous whose longing is fulfilled
set against the wicked whose dread comes true
tsaddiq — 'the desire of the RIGHTEOUS will be granted'; their character draws fulfilment, where the wicked draw doom.
granting — the righteous' desire is given
the granting/giving of the righteous person's desire
welded to the desire it satisfies
nathan (give/grant) — 'will be GRANTED'; the righteous' desire is given them. Emergent: the granting of longing as the righteous' portion, against the wicked's realised fear.
wickedness — swept away when the tempest passes
the wicked who, when the storm passes, is no more
set against the righteous established forever
rasha — 'when the tempest passes, the WICKED is no more'; the wicked have no foundation; the storm of judgement sweeps them away utterly.
the righteous who stands firm, established forever, when the storm passes
welded to the permanence he is given
tsaddiq — 'the RIGHTEOUS is established forever'; where the wicked are swept off, the righteous have an eternal foundation. Character is the only thing that outlasts the storm.
the everlasting establishment/foundation of the righteous
welded to the righteous it grounds forever
olam (forever/everlasting) — 'established FOREVER'; the permanence of the righteous, an eternal foundation. Their inner solidity outlasts every tempest, against the wicked's nothingness.
exasperating sloth — the lazy man an irritation to those who rely on him
the sluggard who is, to those who send him on an errand, like vinegar to the teeth and smoke to the eyes — the exasperating irritation of laziness that fails and frets all who depend on it
(those he is sent by, whom he irritates)
the sloth that grates on everyone who must rely on it

atsel (sluggard) — 'like vinegar to the teeth and smoke to the eyes, so is the SLUGGARD to those who send him' (10:26); the lazy man is a stinging irritation to any who depend on him. Sloth does not merely fail; it exasperates.
fear of the LORD — which prolongs life
the fear of the LORD that lengthens a man's days
set against the wicked whose years are cut short
yirah (fear) — 'the fear of the LORD PROLONGS life'; reverence lengthens days, the antithesis of the wicked's shortened years.
wickedness — whose years are cut short
the wicked whose lifespan is shortened
set against the fear that prolongs life
rasha — 'the years of the WICKED will be short'; wickedness curtails life. Character shapes lifespan.
hope — of the righteous, which brings joy
the hope of the righteous that issues in gladness
welded to the joy it produces
tocheleth (hope/expectation) — 'the HOPE of the righteous brings joy'; the righteous' forward-looking hope is itself a source of gladness, and is fulfilled.
the righteous whose hope ends in joy
set against the wicked whose expectation dies
tsaddiq — the righteous' hope is joyful and sure, unlike the wicked's expectation that perishes.
joy — the fruit of the righteous' hope
the gladness that the righteous' hope brings
welded to the hope that produces it
simchah (joy/gladness) — 'brings JOY'; hope realised as joy for the righteous.
expectation — of the wicked, which perishes
the wicked's expectation, which comes to nothing
welded to the wickedness that dooms it
tiqvah (expectation/hope) — 'the EXPECTATION of the wicked will perish'; the wicked's hopes die with them. Emergent: expectation as a hope that character determines to fulfil or destroy.
the wicked whose forward hope comes to nothing
welded to the expectation it dooms
rasha — the wicked's expectation 'will perish'; wickedness has no future. The dark antithesis of the righteous' joyful hope.
refuge — the LORD's way is a stronghold to the blameless
the security/refuge the LORD's way gives to the blameless
welded to the blameless who find it a refuge

maoz (stronghold/refuge) — 'the way of the LORD is a STRONGHOLD to the blameless'; the same way that shelters the upright destroys the wicked. Emergent: the LORD's way experienced as refuge by the whole-hearted.
integrity — the whole-hearted for whom the LORD's way is refuge
the blameless/whole-hearted who find the LORD's way a stronghold
welded to the stronghold it gives them
tom (integrity/blamelessness) — 'to the BLAMELESS'; the same way is refuge or ruin depending on the heart. Integrity turns God's way into safety.
ruin — the LORD's way is destruction to evildoers
the destruction the LORD's way brings on the evildoers
(the refuge of the blameless, by contrast)
set against the stronghold given the blameless
mechittah (ruin/destruction) — 'but DESTRUCTION to evildoers'; God's way is not neutral — it shelters the upright and shatters the wicked. One road, two ends.
the soul — of the righteous, not left to hunger
the righteous person's nephesh/appetite, which the LORD will not let go hungry
welded to the righteous whose soul is sustained
nephesh (soul/appetite) — 'the LORD does not let the righteous nephesh go hungry'; the inner life/appetite of the righteous, divinely sustained. God provides for the soul of the upright.
righteousness — the righteous whom God sustains
the righteous character that God will not leave to hunger
set against the wicked whose desire is frustrated
tsaddiq (righteous) — the righteous are provided for; God sustains their soul. Character draws divine provision.
craving — the wicked's desire, thwarted by God
the greedy craving of the wicked, which the LORD frustrates
welded to the wickedness that drives it
havvah (craving/greedy desire, also destruction) — 'he THWARTS the craving of the wicked'; the wicked's greedy appetite is frustrated by God. Desire without righteousness is starved.
wickedness — the wicked whose craving is thwarted
the wicked character whose greedy desire God frustrates
set against the righteous whom God feeds
rasha (wicked) — the antithesis to the fed righteous: the wicked's craving is thwarted. Providence follows character.
the righteous who will never be uprooted
welded to the endurance he is given
tsaddiq — 'the righteous will NEVER be removed'; the righteous have permanence in the land, unlike the wicked who cannot dwell there.
the enduring permanence of the righteous, never to be removed
welded to the righteous it grounds
olam (forever) — 'NEVER be removed'; the settled permanence of the righteous (cf 10:25). Their inner stability grants outward endurance.
wickedness — who will not dwell in the land
the wicked who cannot remain in the land
rasha — 'the wicked will not DWELL in the land'; wickedness has no lasting place. Rootlessness is its portion.
righteousness — whose mouth brings forth wisdom
the righteous whose mouth produces wisdom
welded to the wisdom his mouth bears
tsaddiq — 'the mouth of the RIGHTEOUS brings forth wisdom'; righteous speech is fruitful, generating wisdom, unlike the perverse tongue that is cut off.
wisdom — brought forth by the righteous mouth
the wisdom that the righteous mouth produces
welded to the righteous whose mouth yields it
chokmah — 'brings forth WISDOM'; the righteous mouth is generative of wisdom, an overflow of the wise heart.
perversity — the perverse tongue, cut off
the perverse tongue that will be cut off
set against the fruitful mouth of the righteous
tahpukoth (perversity) — 'the PERVERSE tongue will be cut off'; twisted speech is doomed to silence, the antithesis of the wisdom-bearing mouth.
righteousness — whose lips know what is acceptable
the righteous whose lips know what is fitting and pleasing to speak
welded to the discernment of what pleases
tsaddiq — 'the lips of the RIGHTEOUS know what is acceptable'; righteous speech is fitting, knowing what pleases God and man.
knowing — what is acceptable to speak
the righteous lips' knowledge of what is fitting and acceptable
welded to the acceptable speech it discerns
yada (know) — the righteous lips 'KNOW what is acceptable'; a discernment of fitting speech, sensitivity to what pleases.
fittingness — what the righteous lips know to speak
the acceptable, pleasing quality of speech the righteous discern
welded to the discernment that finds it
ratson (favour/acceptableness) — 'what is ACCEPTABLE'; the pleasing, favour-winning speech the righteous know. Emergent: acceptableness as the quality righteous discernment aims at.
wickedness — whose mouth speaks what is perverse
the wicked whose mouth utters perversity
welded to the perverse speech it utters
rasha — 'the mouth of the WICKED, what is perverse'; the wicked mouth knows only perversity, the antithesis of the righteous lips.
perversity — what the wicked mouth speaks
the perverse speech that the wicked mouth produces
welded to the wickedness that speaks it
tahpukoth (perversity) — 'what is PERVERSE'; twisted speech is all the wicked mouth knows, where the righteous know what pleases.
slackness — the negligent hand that causes poverty
the slack, negligent laziness of hand that brings a man to poverty
remiyah (slackness/negligence) — 'a SLACK hand causes poverty'; laziness of hand as an inner disposition, the deceit of the slothful against his own good. Poverty its natural fruit.
enrichment — the diligent hand grows rich
the enriching that the diligent hand brings about
set against the slackness that impoverishes
ashar (be/make rich) — 'the hand of the DILIGENT makes rich'; diligence enriches, the antithesis of slack poverty. Emergent: enrichment as the fruit of the industrious inner disposition.
prudence — the son who gathers in season
the prudent, wise-acting son who gathers his crop in summer
set against the sleeping, shameful son
sakal (act prudently/wisely) — 'gathers in summer is a PRUDENT son'; foresight and timeliness as prudence. The wise read the seasons and act.
shamefulness — the son who sleeps through harvest
the son who sleeps in harvest and so acts shamefully
set against the prudent, gathering son
bosh (be ashamed/act shamefully) — 'sleeps in harvest is a son who brings SHAME'; sloth at the decisive hour is not neutral but shameful. The antithesis of prudent gathering.
blessing — resting on the head of the righteous
the blessings that rest upon the head of the righteous
welded to the righteous on whom they rest
berakah (blessing) — 'BLESSINGS are on the head of the righteous'; blessing crowns the righteous, an inner-and-outer flourishing.
righteousness — the head that bears blessings
the righteous character on whom blessings rest
welded to the blessing that crowns him
tsaddiq (righteous) — the righteous head is blessed, the antithesis of the wicked's violence-concealing mouth.
wickedness — the mouth that conceals violence
the wicked whose mouth hides the violence within
the wicked mouth masking the violence beneath
rasha (wicked) — 'the MOUTH of the wicked conceals violence'; smooth speech masking inner brutality. The violence (chamas) hidden is the qualifier — what the mouth covers.
the righteous whose very memory is a blessing to those who recall him
welded to the blessed memory he leaves
tsaddiq (righteous) — 'the MEMORY of the righteous is a blessing'; the righteous life blesses even in remembrance, outliving the person.
blessing — the righteous man's remembered legacy
the blessing that the memory of the righteous becomes
welded to the righteous whose memory it is
berakah (blessing) — the righteous man's memory 'is a BLESSING'; a legacy that continues to bless. Contrast the wicked name that rots.
reputation — the wicked's name, which rots
the name/reputation of the wicked, which decays and stinks
the wicked whose name it is (262675)
welded to the wicked whose memory perishes
shem (name/reputation) — 'the NAME of the wicked will rot'; reputation as an inner-social reality that outlives the person — but the wicked's decays. Memory divides along character.
wickedness — the wicked whose name rots
the wicked character whose name and memory decay
welded to the name that perishes
rasha (wicked) — the wicked's memory rots, the dark antithesis of the righteous remembered as blessing (10:7a). Character determines legacy.
wisdom — the wise of heart who receives commandments
the wise-hearted who receive and obey commandments
welded to the heart that makes him teachable
chakam (wise) — 'the WISE of heart will receive commandments'; teachability again the mark of wisdom (cf 9:9). The wise take instruction; the fool prates.
the heart — wise, the seat of teachability
the wise heart that receives and holds commandments
welded to the wisdom it seats
leb (heart) — 'the wise of HEART'; wisdom located in the heart, the inner seat that receives instruction. The heart's disposition decides teachability.
folly — the babbling fool who comes to ruin
the prating, lip-foolish fool who talks his way to ruin
evil (fool) — 'a BABBLING fool will come to ruin'; the fool of the lips, all talk and no reception. His chatter is the opposite of the wise heart's receiving, and it ruins him.
integrity — the blameless walk that goes secure
the blameless integrity in which one walks, giving security
welded to the security integrity confers
tom (integrity/blamelessness) — 'whoever walks in INTEGRITY walks securely'; wholeness of character gives a firm, unafraid step (cf 3:23). Nothing to hide, nothing to fear.
security — the confident walk of integrity
the secure, confident walk that integrity gives
welded to the integrity that grounds it
betach (security/confidence) — 'walks SECURELY'; the inner assurance of the blameless, who fear no exposure. The fruit of integrity.
exposure — the crooked-wayed will be known
the being-found-out of one who makes his ways crooked
set against the security of the blameless
yada (be known, Niphal) — 'he who makes his ways CROOKED will be FOUND OUT'; the crooked cannot hide forever — exposure is his end, the antithesis of the blameless one's security.
deceit — the false balance God abhors
the fraudulent, deceitful balance that is detestable to the LORD
welded to the divine revulsion it provokes
mirmah (deceit/fraud) — 'a FALSE balance'; dishonesty in dealing, the cheating scale. The LORD's ABOMINATION (toebah) of it is the qualifier.
divine favour — the LORD delights in a just weight
the LORD's delight/favour toward honest, just weights
the divine pleasure in honest dealing

ratson (favour/delight) — 'a just weight is his DELIGHT'; God's pleasure in honest dealing, set against his abhorrence of fraud. Emergent, locus external:god — the divine valuation that honesty draws.
righteousness — at whose good the city rejoices
the righteous whose prosperity makes the whole city rejoice
welded to the public gladness they bring
tsaddiq — 'when it goes well with the RIGHTEOUS, the city rejoices'; the righteous' good is a public good; a community is glad for them.
communal joy — the city rejoices at the righteous' good
the collective gladness of the city over the righteous' prosperity
welded to the righteous whose good evokes it
alats (rejoice/exult) — 'the city REJOICES'; public, communal joy at the flourishing of the righteous. Righteousness blesses the wider community.
wickedness — at whose fall there are shouts of gladness
the wicked whose perishing brings the city glad shouts
welded to the jubilation their ruin brings
rasha — 'when the wicked perish there are shouts of gladness'; the fall of the wicked is a relief and joy to the community they oppressed.
jubilation — the shouts at the wicked's fall
the glad shouting of the city when the wicked perish
the wicked whose fall evokes it (262704)
welded to the wicked whose ruin brings it
rinnah (ringing cry/jubilation) — 'shouts of GLADNESS'; the joyful relief of a community freed from the wicked. The city's collective exhalation.
blessing — of the upright, which exalts a city
the blessing of the upright that lifts up and exalts a whole city
welded to the upright whose blessing exalts
berakah (blessing) — 'by the BLESSING of the upright a city is exalted'; the upright are a civic asset; their blessing raises the whole community.
uprightness — whose blessing exalts the city
the upright whose blessing lifts the city
welded to the blessing they bring
yashar (upright) — the upright's blessing 'exalts' a city, where the wicked's mouth overthrows it. Character has civic consequence.
wickedness — whose mouth overthrows the city
the wicked whose mouth tears down and overthrows a city
set against the upright whose blessing raises it
rasha — 'by the mouth of the WICKED it is overthrown'; wicked speech is civically destructive, the antithesis of the upright's exalting blessing.
the belittling/despising of a neighbour that betrays a lack of sense
welded to the senselessness it reveals
buz (despise/belittle) — 'whoever BELITTLES his neighbour lacks sense'; contempt for others is itself senseless. Scorn exposes the scorner's emptiness.
the lack of sense/heart shown by the one who belittles his neighbour
welded to the contempt that betrays it
leb (heart/sense) — 'LACKS sense'; to despise a neighbour is to lack heart. Contempt and folly go together.
understanding — the discerning who stays silent
the man of understanding who holds his peace rather than belittle
welded to the restraint it produces
tebunah (understanding) — 'a man of UNDERSTANDING remains silent'; discernment restrains the tongue where folly belittles. Wisdom knows when to be silent.
restraint — the discerning holds his peace
the silence/holding-of-peace by which the understanding man forbears
welded to the discernment that governs it
charash (be silent/hold peace) — 'remains SILENT'; the wise man's restraint of speech, refusing the contempt the fool voices. Silence as discernment.
the confidences/secrets that the gossip goes about revealing
set against the faithful spirit that keeps covered
sod (secret/confidence) — 'whoever goes about slandering reveals SECRETS'; the gossip betrays confidence, the opposite of the trustworthy. Trust broken by the loose tongue.
the faithful, reliable person who keeps a matter covered
welded to the steadfast spirit that holds it
aman (be faithful/trustworthy) — 'he who is TRUSTWORTHY in spirit keeps a thing covered'; faithfulness guards what is entrusted. Reliability of the discreet.
the spirit — steadfast, that keeps confidence
the faithful, steadfast spirit that holds a confidence covered
welded to the faithfulness it carries
ruach (spirit) — 'trustworthy in SPIRIT'; the inner steadfastness of the faithful, the seat of discretion. A reliable spirit keeps what it is given.
guidance — whose absence topples a people
the wise guidance/steering whose lack brings a people to ruin
welded to the counsel that supplies it
tachbuloth (guidance/wise direction) — 'where there is no GUIDANCE, a people falls'; wise steering is essential; its absence is collapse. Counsel as the helm of a community.
counsel — the many advisers who give safety
the abundance of counselors whose counsel brings safety to a people
welded to the guidance their counsel provides
yaats (counsel/advise) — 'in an abundance of COUNSELORS there is safety'; many wise advisers give security. Emergent: counsel/advising as the collective wisdom that safeguards a people.
being harmed — the rash guarantor surely suffers
the harm that surely comes to one who pledges for a stranger
(the security of the cautious, by contrast)
set against the security of the one who refuses pledges
raa (be harmed, Niphal) — 'will surely SUFFER harm'; the rash pledge brings inevitable injury. Imprudent generosity that becomes bondage.
the prudent aversion to striking hands in surety
welded to the safety this aversion secures
sane (hate) — 'he who HATES striking hands in pledge'; a wise, protective aversion to rash surety. Prudence expressed as refusal.
security — the one who shuns surety is safe
the security enjoyed by the one who refuses rash pledges
welded to the prudent hatred that keeps him safe
batach (be secure/confident) — 'is SECURE'; caution about pledges keeps a man safe. Security as the fruit of prudent restraint.
graciousness — the gracious woman who gains honour
the graciousness by which a woman gains honour
welded to the honour her grace secures
chen (grace/graciousness) — 'a GRACIOUS woman gets honour'; inner grace wins lasting honour, set against the merely-grasping violent who get only riches.
the honour that the gracious woman secures
welded to the grace that earns it
kabod (honour) — 'gets HONOUR'; the enduring esteem grace wins, contrasted with the mere riches of the violent.
ruthlessness — the violent who grasp mere riches
the ruthless, aggressive men who seize riches
welded to the riches their violence grabs
arits (ruthless/violent/terror-striking) — 'VIOLENT men get riches'; the aggressive grasp wealth but not honour. The read notes the trade — grace wins honour, violence only riches.
the riches that ruthless, violent men seize
welded to the ruthlessness that grabs them
osher (riches) — 'violent men get RICHES'; wealth without honour, the lesser prize of the ruthless. Emergent: riches as the violent's grasp, set below the gracious woman's honour.
kindness — the kind man benefits his own soul
the kindness by which a man does good to his own soul
welded to the self it benefits
chesed (kindness/loyal-love) — 'a man who is KIND benefits himself'; kindness rebounds to bless its owner. Doing good to others is doing good to one's own soul.
the kind man's own soul, which his kindness benefits
welded to the kindness that does it good
nephesh (soul/self) — 'benefits HIMSELF'; kindness enriches the doer's own inner life. Virtue is self-rewarding at the level of the soul.
cruelty — the cruel man harms his own flesh
the cruelty by which a man injures his own self
welded to the self it wounds
akzari (cruel/ruthless) — 'a CRUEL man hurts himself'; cruelty rebounds to wound its owner. The ruthless damage their own flesh, the dark antithesis of self-benefiting kindness.
the cruel man's own flesh/self, which his cruelty wounds
welded to the cruelty that injures it
sheer (flesh/kin/self) — 'HURTS himself'; cruelty troubles one's own flesh. Vice is self-punishing, wounding the self it seems to arm.
the wicked whose earnings are illusory and deceptive
welded to the illusory reward it earns
rasha — 'the WICKED earns deceptive wages'; the wicked's gain is a lie that will not last, unlike the sure reward of righteousness.
the deceptive, false wage that the wicked's work yields
welded to the wickedness that earns it
sheqer (falsehood/deceit) — 'DECEPTIVE wages'; the wicked's reward is a false one, evaporating. Gain that betrays.
righteousness — sown for a sure reward
the righteousness that, sown, yields a sure and true reward
welded to the reliable reward it earns
tsedaqah (righteousness) — 'one who sows RIGHTEOUSNESS gets a sure reward'; righteous action is seed that yields a reliable harvest, against the wicked's deceptive wage.
sureness — the reliable reward of righteousness
the sure, true/faithful reward that righteousness yields
welded to the righteousness whose reward it is
emet (truth/faithfulness/reliability) — 'a SURE reward'; the harvest of righteousness is dependable, true, where the wicked's is deceptive.
the steadfast righteousness that leads to life
the evil that leads to death (262770)
set against the pursuit of evil that ends in death
tsedaqah — 'whoever is steadfast in RIGHTEOUSNESS will live'; firm righteousness is life-directed, the antithesis of the deadly pursuit of evil.
the evil that a man pursues, which leads him to death
set against the righteousness that leads to life
ra (evil) — 'he who pursues EVIL will die'; the eager pursuit of evil is a pursuit of death. Desire's direction decides destiny.
pride — which brings disgrace in its train
the presumptuous pride that draws disgrace after it
welded to the shame that follows it
zadon (pride/presumption) — 'when PRIDE comes, then comes disgrace'; arrogance carries shame with it. Pride's inevitable companion.
disgrace — the shame that pride brings
the disgrace that follows on the heels of pride
welded to the arrogance that summons it
qalon (disgrace/shame) — 'then comes DISGRACE'; shame is pride's shadow. The proud are humbled.
the modest, lowly ones with whom wisdom dwells
welded to the wisdom that accompanies them
tsana (be humble/modest) — 'with the HUMBLE is wisdom'; humility and wisdom go together, the bright antithesis to pride and disgrace.
the wisdom that accompanies the modest and lowly
welded to the humility that hosts it
chokmah — 'with the humble is WISDOM'; wisdom keeps company with humility, not pride. Teachable lowliness is its home.
the crooked heart — abomination to the LORD
the crooked/twisted heart that the LORD detests
welded to the divine revulsion it draws

leb (heart) with iqqesh (crooked) — 'those of CROOKED heart are an abomination to the LORD'; the twistedness of the inner life is what God abhors. Character at the level of the heart. The ABOMINATION (toebah) is the qualifier.
blamelessness — those of blameless ways, God's delight
the blameless/whole in their ways, in whom the LORD delights
welded to the divine favour they draw
tamim (blameless/whole) — 'those of BLAMELESS ways are his delight'; wholeness of way draws God's favour, the bright antithesis to the crooked heart.
divine favour — the LORD delights in the blameless
the LORD's delight/favour toward those of blameless ways
the divine pleasure in wholeness of way
ratson (favour/delight) — 'are his DELIGHT'; God's pleasure in the blameless, set against his abhorrence of the crooked heart. Emergent, external:god — the divine valuation of integrity.
evil — who will not go unpunished
the evildoer who will surely not escape punishment
set against the righteous whose offspring is delivered
ra (evil/evildoer) — 'an EVIL person will not go unpunished'; the certainty of the evildoer's judgement ('hand to hand'), against the deliverance of the righteous line.
the righteous whose descendants are delivered
set against the evildoer who cannot escape
tsaddiq — 'the offspring of the RIGHTEOUS will be delivered'; righteousness secures not only oneself but one's descendants. Character blesses the line.
indiscretion — beauty that turns from good sense
the turning-from/lack of discretion that makes beauty grotesque
(the incongruous gold ring in a snout)
the absent discretion that renders beauty absurd

sur (turn aside/depart) — 'a beautiful woman WITHOUT (turned from) discretion'; outward beauty voided by the lack of inner taste/discretion, as incongruous as gold in a pig's snout. Emergent: indiscretion as the inner defect that ruins outward grace.
desire — the righteous', ending only in good
the desire of the righteous, which issues only in good
welded to the righteous whose desire it is
taavah (desire) — 'the DESIRE of the righteous ends only in good'; the righteous' longings are wholesome and well-fulfilled, unlike the wicked's expectation that meets wrath.
righteousness — whose desire ends in good
the righteous whose longing issues only in good
welded to the desire that ends well
tsaddiq — the righteous' desire is good-directed and good-ending, the bright side of the couplet.
expectation — the wicked's, ending in wrath
the wicked's expectation, which comes to wrath
welded to the wickedness that dooms it
tiqvah (expectation/hope) — 'the EXPECTATION of the wicked in wrath'; the wicked's hopes end in fury and judgement. Emergent: expectation as forward-hope that character bends to good or wrath.
the wicked whose forward hope meets only wrath
welded to the expectation it dooms
rasha — the wicked's expectation ends 'in wrath'; no good future for wickedness, the dark antithesis of the righteous' good-ending desire.
generosity/its lack — withholding what is right brings want
the rightful giving that enriches when given, and brings want when withheld
(the freely-giving who grows richer, by contrast)
the due generosity set against the want that withholding brings

yosher (what is right/due) — 'another withholds what he should give and only suffers want'; the paradox of generosity — the liberal grow richer, the withholding grow poor. Rightful giving is self-enriching; hoarding self-impoverishing.
generosity — the soul of blessing that is enriched
the liberal, blessing-bringing soul that is itself enriched
welded to the blessing it dispenses
nephesh (soul) with berakah — 'a soul of BLESSING (a generous soul) will be enriched'; the liberal inner disposition that gives and is repaid. Generosity as a settled temper of soul.
blessing — that the generous bring and are enriched by
the blessing the liberal soul brings to others and gains for itself
welded to the generous who dispense it
berakah (blessing) — 'whoever brings BLESSING will be enriched'; the blessing given returns; 'one who waters is watered'. Generosity's boomerang of good.
the enrichment/being-made-fat of the one who blesses others
welded to the blessing that returns as wealth
dashen (be made fat/prosperous) — 'will be ENRICHED'; the generous grow prosperous, watered as they water. Emergent: enrichment as the return on generosity.
imprecation — the people curse the grain-hoarder
the communal cursing of the one who holds back grain in want
set against the blessing on the one who sells
qabab (curse) — 'the people CURSE him who holds back grain'; the community's moral condemnation of hoarding in scarcity. Public imprecation on selfish withholding.
blessing — on the head of the one who sells grain
the blessing that rests on the one who sells grain rather than hoard
set against the people's curse on the hoarder
berakah (blessing) — 'a BLESSING is on the head of him who sells it'; the generous seller is blessed by the community, the bright antithesis of the cursed hoarder.
the diligent, earnest seeking of good
the earnest pursuit that ends in favour
shachar (seek early/diligently) — 'whoever DILIGENTLY SEEKS good'; earnest pursuit of good, the same eager verb used of seeking Wisdom (8:17). What one seeks, one becomes.
the seeking that procures favour for the one who pursues good
welded to the favour it secures
baqash (seek/procure) — 'seeks FAVOUR'; the diligent seeker of good procures favour (with God and man). Seeking good draws favour.
favour — found by the seeker of good
the favour/goodwill that the seeker of good obtains
welded to the seeking that procures it
ratson (favour/goodwill) — 'seeks FAVOUR'; the good-seeker's reward. Emergent: favour as what earnest pursuit of good procures, against the evil that hunts its own seeker.
evil — comes to the one who searches for it
the evil that comes upon the one who searches it out
welded to the searching that brings it
ra (evil) — 'EVIL comes to him who searches for it'; the seeker of evil is found by it. Pursuit of evil is self-fulfilling, the dark mirror of seeking good.
searching — hunting after evil, which then finds him
the searching-out of evil that brings evil upon the searcher
welded to the evil that answers the search
darash (seek/search/inquire) — 'him who SEARCHES for it'; to hunt evil is to summon it upon oneself. What one searches for comes.
misplaced trust — trusting in riches, which fails
the trust placed in riches, which brings a man down
set against the righteous who flourish
batach (trust) — 'whoever TRUSTS in his riches will fall'; the false trust in wealth (contrast trusting the LORD, 3:5). Riches as a rotten foundation — the trust itself the fatal error.
righteousness — which flourishes like a green leaf
the righteous who flourish and thrive like green foliage
set against the one whose trust in wealth fails
tsaddiq — 'the RIGHTEOUS will flourish like a green leaf'; living vitality, rooted and thriving, against the collapse of those who trust in riches. Character, not wealth, is the living root.
strife-making — troubling one's own house, inheriting wind
the one who brings trouble on his own household and gains only emptiness
the self-troubling that ends in nothing
akar (trouble/stir up) — 'whoever TROUBLES his own household will inherit the wind'; the strife-maker ruins his own house and reaps emptiness. Self-destructive discord.
folly — the fool who serves the wise
the fool who becomes servant to the wise of heart
set against the wisdom that masters him
evil (fool) — 'the fool will be SERVANT to the wise of heart'; folly ends in servitude to wisdom. The natural hierarchy of character.
wisdom — the wise of heart whom the fool serves
the wise-of-heart to whom the fool becomes servant
welded to the heart that seats his wisdom
chakam — 'the wise of HEART'; wisdom masters folly. The wise rule where fools serve.
the heart — seat of the wise man's wisdom
the heart in which the wise man's wisdom is seated
welded to the wisdom it carries
leb (heart) — 'wise of HEART'; wisdom's seat, the inner ground from which mastery flows.
the integrity that leads and guides the upright safely
welded to the upright whom it leads
tummah (integrity/blamelessness) — 'the INTEGRITY of the upright guides them'; wholeness of character is itself a guide, keeping the upright on the right road.
the upright who are led by their own integrity
welded to the integrity that leads them
yashar (upright) — the upright are 'guided' by their integrity; character steers conduct.
the crookedness/perversity that ruins the treacherous
welded to the treacherous whom it ruins

selef (crookedness/perverseness) — 'the CROOKEDNESS of the treacherous destroys them'; twistedness of character self-destructs. Emergent: crookedness as a ruining inner disposition, the dark mirror of guiding integrity.
treachery — destroyed by their own crookedness
the treacherous/faithless who are ruined by their crookedness
welded to the crookedness that ruins them
bagad (deal treacherously) — the treacherous are 'destroyed' by their crookedness; faithlessness turns on its owner.
righteousness — whose fruit is a tree of life
the righteous whose fruit is life-giving, a tree of life
welded to the life its fruit bears
tsaddiq — 'the fruit of the RIGHTEOUS is a tree of life'; righteous living yields life to others, a tree that heals.
life — the tree-of-life fruit of the righteous
the life that the righteous person's fruit gives, a tree of life
welded to the righteous whose fruit yields it
chayyim (life) — 'a tree of LIFE'; the righteous' influence is life-giving. Emergent: life as the fruit the righteous produce for others.
the winning/capturing of souls that marks the wise
welded to the wisdom soul-winning demonstrates
nephesh (souls) — 'whoever captures SOULS is wise'; to win people (to life, to wisdom) is itself wisdom. The wise draw souls, not spoil.
the wisdom of the one who wins souls
welded to the soul-capturing it names as wise
chakam — 'is WISE'; the soul-winner's wisdom. Wisdom's fruit is not only self-good but the drawing of others to life.
the righteous who are recompensed even on earth
set against the wicked repaid all the more
tsaddiq — 'if the RIGHTEOUS is repaid on earth'; even the righteous are recompensed here — so how much more the wicked. A fortiori judgement.
the wicked who, more than the righteous, will be recompensed
welded to the sinner in the reckoning
rasha — 'how much more the WICKED and the sinner'; if the righteous do not escape recompense, the wicked certainly will not.
sin — the sinner recompensed with the wicked
the sinner reckoned with the wicked for recompense
welded to the wicked in the reckoning
chata (sin/sinner) — 'the wicked and the SINNER'; the habitual sinner shares the wicked's certain recompense.
riches — profitless in the day of wrath
the wealth that does not profit in the day of wrath
set against righteousness which alone delivers
hon (wealth) — 'RICHES do not profit in the day of wrath'; wealth is powerless before judgement. Emergent: riches as a false security, contrasted with delivering righteousness.
the righteousness that rescues from death where riches cannot
set against the riches that do not profit
tsedaqah (righteousness) — 'RIGHTEOUSNESS delivers from death'; moral character, not wealth, is what saves in the day of wrath (cf 10:2).
righteousness — of the blameless, keeping his way straight
the righteousness of the blameless that keeps his path straight
welded to the blameless it guides
tsedaqah — 'the righteousness of the BLAMELESS keeps his way straight'; right character steers a straight course.
blamelessness — whose righteousness keeps his way straight
the blameless/whole man whose righteousness straightens his road
welded to the righteousness that directs him
tamim (blameless/whole) — the blameless walk a straight road, kept by their righteousness, unlike the wicked who fall.
wickedness — who falls by his own wickedness
the wicked who is felled by his own wickedness
the wicked brought down by the evil in him
rasha — 'the WICKED falls by his own wickedness'; sin is self-defeating. The wicked's own evil (rishah) is the qualifier — the instrument of his fall.
righteousness — of the upright, which delivers them
the righteousness of the upright that rescues them
welded to the upright it delivers
tsedaqah — 'the righteousness of the UPRIGHT delivers them'; character rescues, where the treacherous are trapped by their craving.
the upright who are delivered by their righteousness
welded to the righteousness that saves them
yashar (upright) — the upright are 'delivered' by their righteousness, the bright antithesis of the treacherous caught by lust.
treachery — taken captive by their own lust
the treacherous/faithless who are captured by their craving
the treacherous ensnared by their own desire
bagad (deal treacherously) — 'the TREACHEROUS are taken captive by their lust'; faithless desire ensnares its own. Their craving (havvah) is the qualifier — the trap that holds them.
hope — the wicked's, which perishes at death
the wicked's hope, which dies when he dies
welded to the expectation that dies with it
tiqvah (hope) — 'when the wicked dies, his HOPE will perish'; the wicked's hope has no root beyond this life. Emergent: hope as the confidence that death exposes as empty for the wicked.
the wicked's expectation, resting on wealth, which comes to nothing
welded to the wealth-confidence that fails
tocheleth (expectation) — 'the EXPECTATION of wealth perishes'; hope grounded in wealth dies with its owner. Misplaced confidence.
vigour — the wicked's wealth-confidence, gone at death
the wealth/vigour on which the wicked's hope rested, perishing at death
welded to the expectation it grounded
on (wealth/strength/vigour) — 'the expectation of WEALTH'; the wicked's confidence in his own strength and riches, which death dissolves. Vigour without righteousness is fleeting.
the righteous who is rescued from trouble
set against the wicked who enters the trouble instead
tsaddiq — 'the RIGHTEOUS is delivered from trouble'; deliverance follows righteousness, and the wicked take the trouble in his place.
wickedness — who walks into trouble instead
the wicked who ends up in the trouble the righteous escaped
rasha — 'the wicked walks into it instead'; the trouble the righteous escapes falls on the wicked. A grim exchange.
destroying — the godless mouth would destroy his neighbour
the destruction the godless works on his neighbour with his mouth
set against the knowledge that rescues the righteous
shachath (destroy/ruin) — 'with his mouth the godless would DESTROY his neighbour'; speech as a weapon of ruin, against the knowledge that delivers.
knowledge — by which the righteous are delivered
the knowledge through which the righteous are rescued from the godless mouth
welded to the righteous it rescues
daath (knowledge) — 'by KNOWLEDGE the righteous are delivered'; discernment rescues, countering the destroying mouth of the godless.
the righteous who are delivered through knowledge
welded to the knowledge that saves them
tsaddiq — 'the righteous are delivered'; knowledge and righteousness together rescue from the destroyer's mouth.
love — of discipline, which is love of knowledge
the love of discipline that amounts to a love of knowledge
the love of correction that seeks knowledge
aheb (love) — 'whoever LOVES discipline loves knowledge'; to welcome correction is to love learning. The teachable heart embraces reproof as the road to knowledge.
love — of knowledge, shown by loving discipline
the love of knowledge that is proved by loving discipline
welded to the knowledge it seeks
aheb (love) — 'loves KNOWLEDGE'; the love of knowledge and the love of discipline are one — you cannot have the end without embracing the means.
knowledge — loved by the one who loves discipline
the knowledge that the discipline-lover loves and gains
welded to the love that pursues it
daath (knowledge) — 'loves KNOWLEDGE'; the prize the teachable seek through discipline.
hatred — of reproof, which is stupidity
the hating of reproof that marks a man as brutish
welded to the brutishness it betrays
sane (hate) — 'he who HATES reproof is stupid'; to resent correction is not shrewd but brutish. The unteachable close the door to knowledge.
the brutish stupidity of the one who hates reproof
welded to the reproof-hatred that proves it
baar (brutish/stupid) — 'is STUPID'; hatred of correction reduces a man to the level of a beast, unteachable and dull.
righteousness — who regards even his beast's life
the righteous whose care extends even to the life of his animal
welded to the compassion he shows his beast
tsaddiq — 'the righteous has REGARD for the life of his beast'; righteousness is tender even to animals. The breadth of true compassion.
care — the righteous knows/regards his beast's life
the knowing regard/care the righteous gives to his animal's need
welded to the beast's life he tends
yada (know/regard) — 'has REGARD for the life of his beast'; a knowing, attentive care. Compassion that notices even the animal's need.
life — of the beast, regarded by the righteous
the life/soul of the animal that the righteous man tends
welded to the care that attends it
nephesh (life/soul) — 'the LIFE of his beast'; even the animal's life is an object of the righteous man's care.
cruel-mercy — even the wicked's compassion is cruel
the so-called mercy of the wicked, which is in fact cruelty
welded to the cruelty it really is
racham (mercy/compassion) — 'the MERCY of the wicked is cruel'; the wicked's very tenderness is harsh. Even their kindest impulses are corrupted.
the wicked whose compassion is corrupted into cruelty
set against the righteous who spares his beast
rasha — the wicked's 'mercy' is cruel; wickedness poisons even compassion.
cruelty — the true nature of the wicked's mercy
the cruelty that is the real substance of the wicked's 'mercy'
welded to the mercy it belies
akzari (cruel/ruthless) — the wicked's mercy 'is CRUEL'; their compassion is a mask over ruthlessness.
diligence — working one's land for plenty of bread
the industrious working of one's land that yields plenty of bread
set against the one who chases worthless things
abad (work/serve/till) — 'whoever WORKS his land will have plenty of bread'; steady, honest labour feeds a man. Diligence at real work.
heartlessness — the pursuer of worthless things lacks sense
the lack of sense in the one who chases worthless, empty pursuits
set against the one who works his land
leb (heart/sense) — 'he who follows worthless pursuits LACKS sense'; chasing empty things instead of real work is senseless. Fantasy over labour.
wickedness — who covets the spoil of evildoers
the wicked who craves the plunder that evildoers seize
welded to the covetousness that drives him
rasha — 'whoever is WICKED covets the spoil of evildoers'; the wicked lust after ill-gotten gain, unlike the fruitful righteous root.
covetousness — the wicked's craving for evil spoil
the coveting/craving for the plunder of evildoers
welded to the wickedness that drives it
chamad (covet/desire) — 'COVETS the spoil of evildoers'; the wicked's desire fixes on the fruit of others' evil. Craving without labour.
the righteous whose root, unlike the wicked's craving, bears fruit
welded to the fruit its root yields
tsaddiq — 'the root of the RIGHTEOUS bears fruit'; righteousness is productive, rooted and fruitful, against the wicked's barren coveting.
fruitfulness — the righteous root yields fruit
the fruit-bearing/yielding of the righteous man's root
welded to the righteous whose root yields it
nathan (give/yield) — 'the root of the righteous BEARS fruit'; the righteous produce, where the wicked only crave. Emergent: fruitfulness as the yield of rooted righteousness.
evil — ensnared by the transgression of his lips
the evil man who is caught in the snare of his own sinful speech
welded to the sin of speech that traps him
ra (evil) — 'an EVIL man is ensnared by the transgression of his lips'; the evildoer is trapped by his own sinful words. Speech as a self-set snare.
lip-sin — the transgression that ensnares the evil man
the sinful transgression of the lips that snares the evildoer
welded to the evildoer it ensnares
pesha (transgression) — 'the TRANSGRESSION of his lips'; sinful speech becomes a trap. The mouth condemns its owner.
the righteous who escapes the trouble that snares the evil man
welded to the trouble he is delivered from
tsaddiq — 'the RIGHTEOUS escapes from trouble'; righteousness delivers where lip-sin ensnares. Character is escape.
distress — from which the righteous escapes
the trouble/distress from which the righteous is delivered
welded to the righteous it cannot hold

tsarah (trouble/distress) — 'the righteous escapes from TROUBLE'; the distress that snares the evildoer, from which the righteous walks free. Emergent: trouble as what character determines one to escape or be caught in.
satisfaction — filled with good from the fruit of one's mouth
the satisfaction with good that a man reaps from the fruit of his own mouth
the good-filled contentment good speech yields
saba (be satisfied/full) — 'from the fruit of his mouth a man is SATISFIED with good'; good speech feeds its speaker; words, like deeds, return to their author. The mouth's harvest.
folly — whose way is right in his own eyes
the fool who thinks his own way right, blind to correction
welded to the self-conceit that blinds him
evil (fool) — 'the way of a FOOL is right in his own eyes'; folly is self-satisfied, immune to advice. The unteachable conceit that will not hear.
self-conceit — the fool's way seems right to himself
the self-assessment by which the fool judges his own way right
welded to the folly it blinds
yashar (right/straight) — 'RIGHT in his own eyes'; the fool's fatal self-approval. Wisdom listens; folly is already sure.
the wise man who, unlike the fool, listens to advice
welded to the heeding that marks him wise
chakam — 'a WISE man listens to advice'; teachability again the mark of wisdom (cf 12:1). The wise are not sure of themselves but open to counsel.
the wise man's listening to and taking counsel
shama (hear/heed) — 'LISTENS to advice'; the wise seek and take counsel, against the fool's self-sufficiency. Advice (etsah) is the object (qualifier).
anger — the fool's vexation, known at once
the fool's provocation/anger that is displayed immediately
welded to the immediacy of its display
kaas (vexation/anger/provocation) — 'the VEXATION of a fool is known at once'; the fool cannot hide his irritation — it flashes out instantly, unlike the prudent's restraint.
the fool whose anger is uncontrolled and immediate
the folly that cannot govern its temper
evil (fool) — 'the vexation of a FOOL is known at once'; folly lacks self-control over its feelings; the temper betrays the fool.
display — the fool's vexation is known at once
the being-known/immediate display of the fool's vexation
welded to the anger it reveals
yada (be known) — 'is KNOWN at once'; the fool's feelings are transparent, uncontrolled, in contrast to the prudent who covers an insult.
the prudent man who covers/ignores an insult rather than react
welded to the offense he passes over
arum (prudent/shrewd) — 'the PRUDENT ignores an insult'; self-command to overlook offense. Prudence covers what folly would flare at.
the insult/shame that the prudent man passes over in silence
welded to the restraint that ignores it
qalon (insult/shame) — 'ignores an INSULT'; the offense the prudent chooses not to answer. Restraint that refuses to be provoked.
the faithfulness/truth that a man breathes out as honest testimony
welded to the righteous testimony it gives
emunah (faithfulness/truth) — 'whoever speaks the TRUTH gives honest evidence'; the truthful witness testifies righteously. Reliability of word.
righteous testimony — the truth-speaker's honest witness
the righteous, honest evidence the truthful man gives
welded to the faithfulness that speaks it
tsedeq (righteousness) — 'gives HONEST evidence'; true speech is righteous testimony, against the false witness's deceit.
the falseness of the witness who utters deceit
welded to the deceit he speaks
sheqer (falsehood) — 'a FALSE witness'; the perjurer, whose testimony is deceit. Falseness embodied in witness.
deceit — what the false witness utters
the deceit/treachery the false witness speaks
welded to the falseness that utters it
mirmah (deceit/treachery) — 'utters DECEIT'; the false witness breathes out treachery, the antithesis of honest testimony.
the wise whose tongue heals rather than wounds
welded to the healing his tongue gives
chakam (wise) — 'the tongue of the WISE brings healing'; wise speech heals, against the rash words that stab like a sword. The mouth as scalpel or balm.
healing — the balm of the wise tongue
the healing/health the wise tongue brings to those it addresses
the wise tongue that gives it (262987)
welded to the wisdom that speaks it
marpe (healing/health) — 'brings HEALING'; wise words mend where rash words wound (cf 4:22; 16:24). Speech that restores.
the truthful lips that stand and endure forever
set against the lying tongue that lasts a moment
emet (truth) — 'TRUTHFUL lips endure forever'; truth has permanence, outlasting every lie. What is true stands.
falsehood — the lying tongue, for but a moment
the lying tongue that lasts only an instant before it is exposed
set against the truthful lips that endure
sheqer (falsehood) — 'a LYING tongue is but for a moment'; lies are fleeting, soon undone. Falsehood has no future.
goodness — the good man who obtains favour
the goodness by which a man obtains the LORD's favour
welded to the divine favour his goodness draws
tob (good) — 'a GOOD man obtains favour from the LORD'; goodness draws divine favour, against the schemer whom God condemns.
favour — obtained from the LORD by the good
the favour/goodwill the good man obtains from the LORD
welded to the goodness that wins it
ratson (favour/goodwill) — 'obtains FAVOUR from the LORD'; the good man's reward is divine favour. Emergent: favour as what goodness draws from God.
scheming — the man of evil devices whom God condemns
the evil schemes/devices that mark the man God condemns
welded to the divine condemnation his schemes draw
mezimmah (devices/schemes, dark sense) — 'a man of EVIL DEVICES'; the calculating schemer, opposite of the good man. His plots draw God's condemnation.
divine condemnation — God condemns the schemer
the LORD's condemning/declaring-guilty of the man of evil devices
welded to the schemer it judges
rasha (condemn/declare guilty, Hiphil) — 'he CONDEMNS' the schemer; the LORD's judicial condemnation. Locus external:god — the divine verdict against calculated evil.
deceit — in the heart of those who devise evil
the deceit that fills the heart of those who plot evil
welded to the plotting it accompanies
mirmah (deceit) — 'DECEIT is in the heart of those who devise evil'; the schemer's heart is full of treachery. Plotting and deceit go together within.
the heart — of evil-devisers, full of deceit
the heart of the schemers, the seat where deceit resides
welded to the deceit that fills it
leb (heart) — 'in the HEART of those who devise evil'; the inner seat where the schemer's deceit lodges.
the devising/plotting of evil that fills the schemer's deceitful heart
charash (plough/devise/plot) — 'those who DEVISE evil'; the active scheming of the treacherous heart.
the planning/counselling of peace, which brings joy
welded to the peace their counsel seeks

yaats (counsel/plan) — 'those who PLAN peace have joy'; the peacemaker's counsel, set against the deceitful scheming of evil. Emergent: planning-peace as the constructive counterpart to devising-evil.
peace — planned by the peacemakers, bringing joy
the peace/wholeness that the peacemakers devise and enjoy
welded to the counsel that seeks it
shalom (peace/wholeness) — 'those who plan PEACE have joy'; peace as the object of good counsel, yielding gladness.
the joy that belongs to those who plan peace
(their peace, by contrast to schemers' deceit)
the gladness of the peace-devising heart
simchah (joy/gladness) — 'those who plan peace have JOY'; peacemaking brings inner gladness, where scheming breeds only deceit.
harm — no ill befalls the righteous
the harm/ill that does not befall the righteous
welded to the righteous whom it cannot touch
aven (trouble/iniquity/harm) — 'no ILL befalls the righteous'; the righteous are kept from real harm, while the wicked are filled with trouble.
righteousness — on whom no ill befalls
the righteous whom no real harm overtakes
welded to the ill they escape
tsaddiq — 'no ill befalls the RIGHTEOUS'; character shields from ultimate harm, unlike the trouble-filled wicked.
the wicked who are filled and overwhelmed with trouble
set against the righteous whom no ill befalls
rasha — 'the wicked are filled with TROUBLE'; wickedness draws trouble upon itself, the dark antithesis of the righteous kept from ill.
falsehood — lying lips, abomination to the LORD
the lying lips that the LORD detests
welded to the divine revulsion they draw
sheqer (falsehood) — 'LYING lips are an abomination to the LORD'; deceitful speech is detestable to God (cf 6:17). The ABOMINATION (toebah) is the qualifier.
faithfulness — those who act faithfully, God's delight
those who deal faithfully/truly, in whom the LORD delights
welded to the divine favour they draw
emunah (faithfulness) — 'those who act FAITHFULLY are his delight'; faithful dealing draws God's favour, the bright antithesis to lying lips.
divine favour — the LORD delights in the faithful
the LORD's delight/favour toward those who act faithfully
the divine pleasure in faithful dealing
ratson (favour/delight) — 'are his DELIGHT'; God's pleasure in faithfulness, set against his abhorrence of lies. Emergent, external:god — the divine valuation of truth in action.
the prudent man who holds his knowledge discreetly rather than flaunt it
welded to the knowledge he keeps hidden
arum (prudent/shrewd) — 'a PRUDENT man conceals knowledge'; discretion holds knowledge in reserve, not parading it. The wise do not blurt.
knowledge — held discreetly by the prudent
the knowledge that the prudent conceal rather than broadcast
welded to the discretion that guards it
daath (knowledge) — 'conceals KNOWLEDGE'; knowledge held in reserve, spoken when fitting. Discretion's treasure.
the heart — of fools, which proclaims folly
the heart of fools that blurts out and proclaims its folly
welded to the folly it broadcasts
leb (heart) — 'the HEART of fools proclaims folly'; the fool's heart cannot keep silence — it broadcasts its emptiness, the opposite of prudent concealment.
the fools whose very heart advertises their folly
set against the prudent who conceals knowledge
kesil (fool) — 'the heart of FOOLS proclaims folly'; folly cannot be hidden; it announces itself.
broadcasting — the fool's heart proclaims folly
the proclaiming/crying-out of folly by the fool's heart
welded to the folly it announces
qara (call/proclaim) — 'PROCLAIMS folly'; the fool's heart broadcasts what the prudent conceals. Folly advertises; wisdom reserves.
folly — what the fool's heart proclaims
the folly that the fool's heart cannot help but announce
welded to the broadcasting that reveals it
ivveleth (folly) — 'proclaims FOLLY'; the content the fool's heart blurts out, exposed to all.
dominion — the diligent hand will rule
the rule/mastery that the diligent hand attains
set against the sloth reduced to forced labour
mashal (rule/have dominion) — 'the hand of the diligent will RULE'; diligence rises to mastery. Emergent: dominion as the fruit of the industrious hand, against the sluggard's bondage.
the slack, negligent sloth that ends in forced labour
set against the diligence that rises to rule
remiyah (slackness/sloth) — 'the SLOTHFUL will be put to forced labour'; laziness ends in servitude. Sloth sinks where diligence rises.
anxiety — the care that weighs down the heart
the anxious care in a man's heart that presses and bows him down
welded to the heart it weighs down
deagah (anxiety/care) — 'ANXIETY in a man's heart weighs him down'; worry is a weight that bows the inner life. The oppressive burden of care.
the heart — weighed down by anxiety, gladdened by a word
the heart that anxiety bows down and a good word lifts
welded to the care that weighs it
leb (heart) — 'anxiety in a man's HEART'; the inner seat where care presses and a good word revives. The heart as the barometer of the inner weather.
goodness — the good word that gladdens
the good, kind word that lifts a downcast heart to gladness
welded to the joy it produces
tob (good) — 'a GOOD word makes him glad'; a kind word lifts the anxious heart. The power of good speech to revive.
gladness — the joy a good word brings the anxious
the gladness that a good word restores to the anxious heart
the good word that gives it (263045)
welded to the good word that produces it
samach (be glad) — 'makes him GLAD'; the lifting of the burdened heart by a good word. Anxiety weighs down; kindness lifts up.
righteousness — a guide to his neighbour
the righteous who guides and directs his neighbour rightly
set against the wicked whose way leads astray
tsaddiq — 'one who is RIGHTEOUS is a guide to his neighbour'; the righteous lead others rightly, where the wicked mislead. Character shapes influence.
wickedness — whose way leads others astray
the wicked whose way misleads and leads others astray
set against the righteous who guides his neighbour
rasha — 'the way of the WICKED leads them astray'; wickedness misdirects, the antithesis of the righteous guide.
sloth — who will not even roast his game
the sloth so deep it will not even cook the game it caught
set against the diligence that gains precious wealth
remiyah (slackness/sloth) — 'whoever is SLOTHFUL will not roast his game'; laziness so extreme it wastes even what it has caught. Sloth squanders its own gains.
the precious wealth that the diligent man acquires
set against the sloth that will not even cook its catch
hon (wealth) — 'the DILIGENT man will get precious wealth'; industry gains and keeps what is precious, where sloth wastes. Emergent: precious wealth as diligence's reward.
the righteousness whose way leads to life and away from death
welded to the life its path contains
tsedaqah (righteousness) — 'in the PATH of righteousness is life'; the way of righteousness is the way of life itself, with no death in it.
life — found in the path of righteousness
the life that fills the path of righteousness, where there is no death
the righteousness whose path it fills (263064)
welded to the righteousness that contains it
chayyim (life) — 'is LIFE... no death'; the righteous way is life, immune to death. Emergent: life as the very substance of the righteous path. The climactic summary of ch.12.
wickedness — by which no one is established
the wickedness that cannot give a man a firm footing
set against the immovable root of the righteous
resha (wickedness) — 'no one is established by WICKEDNESS'; evil gives no stable foundation. The wicked have no root.
righteousness — whose root is never moved
the righteous whose root is firm and never dislodged
set against the wickedness that cannot establish
tsaddiq — 'the root of the RIGHTEOUS will never be moved'; righteousness is deeply rooted, immovable, where wickedness has no ground.
worth — the excellent wife, her husband's crown
the strength/worth of a noble wife who crowns her husband
set against the shaming wife who is rottenness
chayil (strength/worth/virtue) — 'an EXCELLENT wife is the crown of her husband'; a wife of worth honours and adorns her husband (cf 31:10). Inner excellence made a crown.
shamefulness — the shaming wife, rottenness in the bones
the shameful wife who is like decay in her husband's bones
set against the crowning wife of worth
bosh (bring shame/act shamefully) — 'she who brings SHAME is like rottenness in his bones'; a shameful wife is a wasting disease, the dark antithesis of the crowning wife.
thoughts — of the righteous, which are just
the inner thoughts/plans of the righteous, which are just
welded to the justice that marks them

machashabah (thought/plan) — 'the THOUGHTS of the righteous are just'; even the inner deliberations of the righteous are just, against the wicked's deceitful counsels. Character reaches the level of thought.
the righteous whose very thoughts are just
set against the wicked whose counsels deceive
tsaddiq — the righteous' inner life is just through and through.
justice — the quality of the righteous' thoughts
the justice that characterises the righteous' inner thoughts
welded to the thoughts it qualifies
mishpat (justice) — the righteous' thoughts are 'JUST'; justice reaches into the mind, not just the deed.
counsels — of the wicked, which are deceitful
the schemes/counsels of the wicked, which are deceitful
welded to the deceit that marks them
tachbuloth (counsels/guidance) — 'the COUNSELS of the wicked are deceitful'; the wicked's steering is treachery, the dark mirror of the righteous' just thoughts.
the wicked whose inner counsels are treacherous
set against the just thoughts of the righteous
rasha — the wicked's counsels deceive; treachery to the core.
deceit — the character of the wicked's counsels
the deceit/treachery that marks the wicked's counsels
welded to the counsels it qualifies
mirmah (deceit/treachery) — the wicked's counsels are 'DECEITFUL'; treachery is their inner substance.
wickedness — whose words lie in wait for blood
the wicked whose words ambush and lie in wait for blood
set against the upright mouth that delivers
rasha — 'the words of the WICKED lie in wait for blood'; wicked speech is a deadly ambush, against the upright mouth that rescues.
the upright whose mouth rescues and delivers
set against the wicked words that ambush
yashar (upright) — 'the mouth of the UPRIGHT delivers them'; upright speech saves lives, the antithesis of the wicked's bloody ambush.
the wicked who are overthrown and cease to be
set against the righteous house that stands
rasha — 'the wicked are OVERTHROWN and are no more'; wickedness has no permanence, swept away.
the righteous whose house stands firm when the wicked fall
set against the wicked who are no more
tsaddiq — 'the house of the RIGHTEOUS will stand'; righteousness has enduring foundations, where the wicked are overthrown.
commendation — a man praised for his good sense
the praise a man receives according to his good sense
welded to the good sense that earns it
halal (praise, Pual) — 'a man is COMMENDED according to his good sense'; praise tracks prudence. Sound sense wins esteem.
prudence — for which a man is commended
the good sense/prudence that earns a man commendation
welded to the commendation it draws
sekel (good sense/prudence) — 'according to his GOOD SENSE'; prudence is the measure of a man's worth in others' eyes.
the twisted, perverse bent of mind that draws contempt

avah (bend/twist/pervert) — 'one of TWISTED mind is despised'; a warped mind draws scorn, the antithesis of the commended sensible man. Emergent: twistedness of mind as a despised inner condition. The contempt (buz) is the qualifier.
the mind/heart — twisted, and so despised
the mind/heart that is twisted and therefore held in contempt
welded to the perversity that bends it
leb (heart/mind) — 'one of TWISTED mind'; the heart itself is warped, the seat of the perversity that draws contempt.
evaluation — lowly-with-a-servant is better than proud-and-hungry
the judgement that a modest sufficiency outweighs a proud, hungry pretence
the valuation that prefers humble reality to proud show
