tob (better) — 'BETTER to be lowly...'; the wise valuation that prefers modest honesty to pretentious poverty. Substance over show.
lowliness — the humble estate that is better
the lowly, lightly-esteemed condition that, with sufficiency, is better than proud want
set against the pretentious greatness that lacks bread
qalah (be lightly esteemed/lowly) — 'better to be LOWLY and have a servant'; a humble, unpretentious estate with enough is better than proud show. Contentment in low place.
self-glorification — pretending greatness while lacking bread
the self-honouring pretence of greatness that hides an empty table
set against the modest estate with enough
kabad (honour oneself, Hithpael) — 'than to PLAY THE GREAT MAN and lack bread'; the vanity of keeping up appearances while starving. Pride that prefers show to substance.
wisdom — the wise son who hears instruction
the wise son who hears and heeds his father's instruction
(the scoffer who will not, by contrast)
set against the scoffer who does not listen
chakam (wise) — 'a WISE son hears his father's instruction'; teachability the mark of the wise (cf 12:1; 13:10). The wise son receives correction.
scorn — the scoffer who will not hear rebuke
the scoffer who refuses to listen to any rebuke
welded to the deaf contempt that marks him
luts (scoff/mock) — 'a SCOFFER does not listen to rebuke'; scorn closes the ear. The scoffer's contempt makes him unteachable, the antithesis of the wise son.
deafness — the scoffer does not listen to rebuke
the scoffer's refusal to listen to rebuke
welded to the contempt that stops his ear
shama (hear/heed) NEGATED — 'does not LISTEN to rebuke'; the scoffer's ears are closed by his scorn. Refusal to hear is his signature.
the presumptuous insolence that yields nothing but conflict
welded to the conflict it breeds
zadon (insolence/presumption) — 'by INSOLENCE comes nothing but strife'; arrogant self-will breeds only contention, where humility takes counsel.
producing — insolence gives rise only to strife
the producing/giving-rise by which insolence yields only strife
the insolence that generates only conflict
nathan (give/produce) — 'by insolence COMES nothing but strife'; insolence is generative — but of strife alone. Emergent: producing-strife as insolence's sole yield.
the strife/contention that is all insolence produces
welded to the presumption that produces it
matstsah (strife/contention) — 'nothing but STRIFE'; the sole harvest of insolence, against the wisdom of the well-counselled.
those who take counsel/allow themselves to be advised, in whom is wisdom
welded to the wisdom that attends counsel

yaats (be advised/take counsel, Niphal) — 'with those who TAKE ADVICE is wisdom'; humility to be counselled brings wisdom, against insolent self-will. Emergent: counsel-taking as the humble road to wisdom.
wisdom — with those who take advice
the wisdom that dwells with those who accept counsel
welded to the counsel that yields it
chokmah — 'with those who take advice is WISDOM'; wisdom keeps company with the teachable and counsel-taking, not the insolent.
get-rich haste — wealth grabbed quickly, which dwindles away
the wealth gained hastily that dwindles — riches grabbed by shortcut and haste, which have no root and melt away, against the patient gathering that grows
the patient increase it is set against (263141)
set against the little-by-little gathering that lasts
hon (wealth) — 'WEALTH gained hastily will dwindle' (13:11); riches got by haste and shortcut have no staying power. What is grabbed quickly slips away quickly (cf 20:21; 28:22).
patient diligence — steady accumulation that grows and lasts
the gathering little by little that increases wealth — the patient, steady diligence that builds slowly and surely, the opposite of the haste that dwindles
the hasty gain it is set against (263135)
set against the hastily-grabbed wealth that dwindles
rabah (increase) — 'but whoever gathers little by little will INCREASE it' (13:11); patient, steady accumulation lasts where haste fails. Diligence over time builds what haste cannot hold.
hope — deferred, which sickens the heart
the hope that, long deferred, makes the heart sick with waiting
welded to the heart worn by long waiting
tocheleth (hope/expectation) — 'HOPE deferred makes the heart sick'; unfulfilled longing is a wasting sickness of the inner life. The ache of prolonged waiting.
the heart — made sick by deferred hope
the heart that grows sick under long-deferred hope
the deferred hope that sickens it (263142)
welded to the hope whose delay wastes it
leb (heart) — 'makes the HEART sick'; the inner seat where deferred hope becomes a wasting illness.
desire — fulfilled, a tree of life
the one whose desire is met
the desire that, when fulfilled, becomes a tree of life
welded to the life its fulfilment gives
taavah (desire) — 'a DESIRE fulfilled is a tree of life'; the granting of longing revives and gives life, the bright answer to hope deferred.
life — the fulfilled desire become a tree of life
the one whose desire is met
the life that a fulfilled desire becomes, a tree of life
the fulfilled desire that yields it (263146)
welded to the desire whose fulfilment is life
chayyim (life) — 'is a tree of LIFE'; fulfilled longing is life-giving, healing the heart-sickness of deferral. Emergent: life as the fruit of granted desire.
the contempt for the word that brings destruction on the despiser himself
welded to the ruin it pledges him to
buz (despise) — 'whoever DESPISES the word brings destruction on himself'; scorn for the word recoils on the scorner. Contempt is self-ruinous.
self-ruin — the word-despiser is pledged to destruction
the destruction/being-pledged-to-ruin that the word-despiser brings on himself
welded to the scorn that dooms him
chabal (be pledged/bound to destruction, Niphal) — 'brings destruction on HIMSELF'; the despiser binds himself over to ruin. Emergent: self-destruction as the pledge contempt for the word exacts.
reverence — for the commandment, which is rewarded
the reverence/fear of the commandment that brings reward
(the destruction the despiser earns, by contrast)
yare (fear/revere) — 'he who REVERES the commandment will be rewarded'; reverence for the word is rewarded, the antithesis of the despiser's destruction.
wisdom — whose teaching is a fountain of life
the wise whose teaching is a life-giving fountain
welded to the life its teaching pours
chakam (wise) — 'the teaching of the WISE is a fountain of life'; wise instruction is a spring of life, turning men from death's snares.
life — the fountain of the wise teaching
the life that the wise man's teaching pours out like a fountain
the wise teaching that gives it (263157)
welded to the wisdom whose teaching yields it
chayyim (life) — 'a fountain of LIFE'; wise teaching gives life (cf 10:11; 14:27). Emergent: life as the yield of wise instruction.
turning-from — from the snares of death
the turning-away from the snares of death that the wise teaching enables
(the fountain of life it flows from)
the escape from death's snares that wise teaching works

sur (turn aside/away) — 'that one may TURN AWAY from the snares of death'; the purpose of wise teaching — to steer the hearer clear of the traps that kill. Emergent: turning-from-death as the fruit of wise teaching.
goodness — the good quality of sound sense
the goodness of sound sense that wins favour
welded to the good sense it marks
tob (good) — 'GOOD sense wins favour'; sound, good sense earns goodwill. The goodness of prudent understanding.
the good sense/prudence that wins favour with God and man
welded to the favour it procures
sekel (good sense/prudence) — 'good SENSE wins favour'; prudence draws goodwill, against the treacherous whose way is ruin.
the winning/procuring of favour by good sense
welded to the favour it gains
nathan (give/procure) — 'good sense WINS favour'; prudence procures goodwill. Emergent: the winning of favour as good sense's yield.
the favour/grace that good sense wins
the good sense that wins it (263166)
welded to the sense that procures it
chen (grace/favour) — 'wins FAVOUR'; the goodwill that prudence earns, against the ruin of the treacherous way.
treachery — whose way is their ruin
the treacherous whose way is hard and ends in ruin
welded to the hard ruin of their road
bagad (deal treacherously) — 'the way of the TREACHEROUS is their ruin'; faithlessness leads down a rugged road to ruin, against the favour good sense wins.
ruin — the hard, perpetual end of the treacherous way
the harsh, rugged ruin that is the treacherous' way and end
the treachery whose way it is (263170)
welded to the treachery that leads there
ethan (perennial/hard/rugged) — 'is their RUIN'; the treacherous' way is 'rugged/enduring' (harsh), their ruin. The hard road of faithlessness.
the prudent man who acts deliberately, out of knowledge
welded to the knowledge that guides his acts
arum (prudent/shrewd) — 'every PRUDENT man acts with knowledge'; the prudent act on knowledge, thoughtfully, against the fool who flaunts folly.
knowledge — the basis of the prudent man's action
the knowledge on which the prudent man acts
the prudence that acts on it (263173)
welded to the prudence it directs
daath (knowledge) — 'acts with KNOWLEDGE'; the prudent's deeds flow from knowledge, deliberate and informed.
the fool who spreads out and flaunts his folly for all to see
welded to the folly he displays
kesil (fool) — 'a FOOL flaunts his folly'; where the prudent act quietly on knowledge, the fool parades his folly. Display over substance.
the folly that the fool spreads out and displays
welded to the fool who parades it
ivveleth (folly) — 'flaunts his FOLLY'; the fool cannot hide his folly — he spreads it like a banner, the opposite of the prudent's quiet knowledge.
wickedness — the messenger who falls into trouble
the wicked/unreliable messenger who falls into trouble
set against the faithful envoy who brings healing
rasha — 'a WICKED messenger falls into trouble'; the unfaithful envoy brings harm on himself and his errand, against the faithful one who heals.
faithfulness — the reliable envoy who brings healing
the faithful, reliable envoy whose trustworthiness brings healing
set against the wicked messenger who falls into trouble
emun (faithful/trustworthy) — 'a FAITHFUL envoy brings healing'; reliability in a messenger heals — the errand prospers, relationships mend. Faithfulness as a healing force.
disgrace — the fate of ignoring instruction
the poverty and disgrace that come to one who ignores instruction
the one who heeds, by contrast (263190)
set against the one who heeds reproof and is honoured
qalon (disgrace/shame) — 'poverty and DISGRACE come to him who ignores instruction'; rejecting correction ends in shame, against the honour of the teachable.
heeding — whoever keeps reproof is honoured
the heeding/keeping of reproof that leads to honour
the one who ignores, by contrast (263187)
set against the disgrace of ignoring instruction
shamar (keep/heed) — 'whoever HEEDS reproof is honoured'; keeping correction leads to honour, the antithesis of the disgrace of ignoring it. Teachability honoured.
desire — fulfilled, sweet to the soul
the one whose desire is met
the desire that, fulfilled, is sweet to the soul
(the fools who abhor turning from evil, by contrast)
the sweet fulfilment set against the fools' loathing of good
taavah (desire) — 'a DESIRE fulfilled is sweet to the soul'; the granting of longing is sweetness — yet fools will not turn from the evil that would win it.
the turning-away from evil that is an abomination to fools
welded to the fools' loathing of the good
sur (turn aside/away) — 'to TURN AWAY from evil is an abomination to fools'; fools loathe the very repentance that would save them. Emergent: turning-from-evil as the good that folly detests.
loathing — fools abhor turning from evil
the fools' revulsion at the thought of turning from evil
welded to the good they cannot stomach

toebah (abomination) — here the FOOLS' abomination (not God's): 'to turn from evil is an ABOMINATION to fools'; folly finds repentance detestable. The moral inversion of the fool, who loathes his own cure.
craving — the treacherous soul desires violence
the desire/appetite of the treacherous, which is set on violence
welded to the treachery whose appetite it is
nephesh (soul/desire/appetite) — 'the DESIRE of the treacherous is for violence'; their very appetite craves harm. The inner hunger of the faithless is for violence.
treachery — whose desire is for violence
the treacherous whose soul craves violence
welded to the violent craving of their soul
bagad (deal treacherously) — 'the desire of the TREACHEROUS is for violence'; faithlessness and violence spring from the same craving heart.
wisdom — the company that makes wise
the wise whose company makes their companions wise
welded to the wisdom their company imparts
chakam (wise) — 'whoever walks with the WISE becomes wise'; wisdom is caught from company. Companionship shapes character.
growing-wise — through walking with the wise
the becoming-wise that comes of keeping wise company
the wise company that gives it (263213)
welded to the company that makes wise
chakam (be/become wise) — 'BECOMES wise'; the fruit of wise company. One grows into the character of one's companions.
the fools whose companionship brings harm
welded to the harm their company causes
kesil (fool) — 'the companion of FOOLS will suffer harm'; folly is contagious and injurious. Bad company corrupts and harms.
being harmed — the companion of fools suffers
the harm that comes to one who keeps company with fools
the fools whose company causes it (263216)
welded to the folly whose company harms
raa (be harmed, Niphal) — 'will SUFFER harm'; keeping fools' company injures. The cost of bad companionship.
the disaster/evil that pursues and hunts down sinners
welded to the sinners it hunts
ra (evil/disaster) — 'DISASTER pursues sinners'; calamity hunts the sinner down, where good rewards the righteous. Consequence follows character.
sin — the sinners whom disaster pursues
the sinners hunted down by disaster
welded to the calamity that hunts them
chatta (sinner) — 'disaster pursues SINNERS'; the sinner cannot outrun the calamity his sin summons.
the righteous who are rewarded with good
(the sinners pursued by disaster, by contrast)
set against the sinners whom disaster hunts
tsaddiq — 'the RIGHTEOUS are rewarded with good'; good repays the righteous, where disaster pursues the sinner.
goodness — the good man who leaves an inheritance
the goodness of the man who leaves an inheritance to his grandchildren
(the sinner whose wealth passes to the righteous)
the provident goodness that blesses posterity
tob (good) — 'a GOOD man leaves an inheritance to his children's children'; goodness looks beyond itself, providing for generations. Provident, generous character.
sin — whose wealth is laid up for the righteous
the sinner whose amassed wealth ends up in the righteous' hands
welded to the wealth that passes from him
chata (sin/sinner) — 'the SINNER's wealth is laid up for the righteous'; the sinner hoards, but his wealth passes to the righteous. Ill-gotten gain does not stay.
wealth — the sinner's, inherited by the righteous
the sinner's amassed wealth that is stored up for the righteous
welded to the sinner from whom it passes
chayil (wealth/substance) — 'the sinner's WEALTH is laid up for the righteous'; the sinner's substance ultimately serves the righteous. Providence redistributes.
righteousness — for whom the sinner's wealth is stored
the righteous for whom the sinner's wealth is finally laid up
(the sinner who amassed it, by contrast)
set against the sinner whose wealth passes to them
tsaddiq — 'laid up for the RIGHTEOUS'; the righteous inherit what the sinner hoarded. Character, not accumulation, secures lasting good.
poverty — the poor whose potential harvest injustice sweeps away
the poor whose fallow ground could yield much, but is swept away by injustice
the poor's lost potential, stolen by injustice

rush (be poor) — 'the fallow ground of the POOR would yield much food, but it is swept away through injustice'; the poor's potential is real but robbed by wrong. The read notes the injustice that keeps the poor poor — not sloth but oppression.
hatred — sparing the rod is hating one's son
the hatred that, disguised as indulgence, spares the rod and so ruins the son
set against the love that is diligent to discipline
sane (hate) — 'whoever SPARES the rod HATES his son'; withholding discipline is not kindness but hatred — it abandons the child to ruin. A startling redefinition of parental love.
the love that is diligent to discipline, seeking the son's good
the false 'love' that spares, by contrast (263241)
set against the hatred that spares the rod
aheb (love) — 'he who LOVES him is diligent to discipline him'; true love corrects, for the child's sake. Discipline is the labour of love, not its opposite.
the righteous who has enough to satisfy his appetite
welded to the fullness he enjoys
tsaddiq — 'the RIGHTEOUS has enough to satisfy his appetite'; the righteous are provided for, their soul filled, against the wicked's want.
the righteous man's appetite/soul, satisfied to the full
welded to the righteous whose soul is filled
nephesh (appetite/soul) — 'to satisfy his APPETITE'; the righteous' inner hunger is met, where the wicked's belly wants.
the wicked whose belly is empty and suffers want
set against the righteous whose appetite is filled
rasha — 'the belly of the WICKED suffers want'; wickedness ends in emptiness, the antithesis of the satisfied righteous.
self-guarding — guarding the mouth preserves life
the guarding of the mouth that preserves one's own life
welded to the life its restraint protects
shamar (keep/guard) — 'whoever GUARDS his mouth preserves his life'; watching the tongue is self-preservation; the loose lip comes to ruin.
the life — preserved by guarding the mouth
the life/soul that is preserved by guarding one's speech
welded to the restraint that protects it
nephesh (life/soul) — 'preserves his LIFE'; the whole self is kept safe by a guarded mouth. Speech and survival linked.
ruin — for the one who opens wide his lips
the ruin that comes on the one who opens his lips too wide
(the guarded mouth that preserves, by contrast)
set against the guarded mouth that preserves life
mechittah (ruin) — 'he who opens wide his lips comes to RUIN'; the unrestrained tongue destroys its owner. Loose speech is self-ruin.
appetite — the sluggard's soul craves yet gets nothing
the sluggard's soul/appetite that craves but receives nothing
welded to the futile desire it feels
nephesh (soul/appetite) — 'the SOUL of the sluggard craves and gets nothing'; the lazy man's appetite is all longing and no attainment. Desire without work is starvation.
sloth — whose soul craves but gains nothing
the sluggishness whose craving yields nothing
set against the diligent soul richly supplied
atsel (sluggard) — 'the soul of the SLUGGARD craves'; sloth reduces a man to hungry longing. Emergent: the sluggard whose desire never feeds him.
the craving/longing of the sluggard that comes to nothing
the empty soul that feels it (263262)
welded to the appetite that goes unfed
avah (crave/desire) — 'CRAVES and gets nothing'; the sluggard's desire is real but fruitless. Longing without labour.
appetite — the diligent's soul richly supplied
the diligent man's soul/appetite that is richly fed and satisfied
welded to the abundance that fills it
nephesh (soul/appetite) — 'the SOUL of the diligent is richly supplied'; industry feeds the appetite the sluggard leaves starving.
satisfaction — the diligent soul made fat/abundant
the rich satisfaction/abundance of the diligent man's soul
welded to the appetite it satisfies
dashen (be made fat/abundant) — 'is richly SUPPLIED'; the diligent's appetite is filled to fatness, against the sluggard's empty craving. Emergent: satisfaction as the fruit of diligence.
the righteous who hates and recoils from falsehood
welded to the aversion that marks him
tsaddiq — 'the RIGHTEOUS hates falsehood'; righteousness includes an active loathing of lies, the antithesis of the shame-bringing wicked.
aversion — the righteous' hatred of falsehood
the righteous man's hatred of and recoil from a lying word
welded to the righteousness that produces it
sane (hate) — 'HATES falsehood'; moral aversion to lies, a mark of the righteous heart.
wickedness — who brings shame and disgrace
the wicked who acts loathsomely and comes to shame
welded to the disgrace his conduct causes
rasha — 'the WICKED brings shame and disgrace'; wickedness produces stench and disgrace, the opposite of the righteous who hates falsehood.
the loathsome, stinking conduct by which the wicked brings shame
welded to the disgrace it produces
baash (stink/be loathsome) — 'brings SHAME'; the wicked's conduct is a stench, causing shame. Emergent: loathsomeness as the wicked's shame-making act.
disgrace — the shame the wicked comes to
the disgrace/shame that the wicked's loathsome conduct brings on him
welded to the loathsome act that earns it
chapher (be ashamed/come to disgrace) — 'and DISGRACE'; the wicked reap the shame their conduct sows.
the righteousness that guards and protects the one of blameless way
welded to the blameless whom it protects
tsedaqah (righteousness) — 'RIGHTEOUSNESS guards him whose way is blameless'; right character is a guardian, keeping the upright safe. The antithesis of sin that overthrows.
the blameless whose way righteousness protects
welded to the righteousness that keeps him
tom (integrity/blamelessness) — 'him whose way is BLAMELESS'; wholeness of way that righteousness guards.
the overthrowing/subverting of the wicked by sin
welded to the sinner whom sin subverts
salaph (twist/overthrow/subvert) — 'sin OVERTHROWS the wicked'; sin turns on its owner, subverting the sinner. Evil is self-defeating.
sin — the sinner whom sin overthrows
the sinner who is overthrown by his own sin
welded to the overthrowing it works
chattah (sin/sinner) — 'overthrows the WICKED/sinner'; the sinner is felled by sin, where the blameless are guarded by righteousness.
false show — pretending to be rich while having nothing
the false self-enrichment of one who acts rich yet has nothing
set against the pretender of poverty who is truly rich
ashar (make oneself rich, Hithpael) — 'one PRETENDS to be rich, yet has nothing'; the empty show of wealth. Emergent: the pretense of riches, appearance without substance.
false show — pretending poverty while holding great wealth
the feigned poverty of one who acts poor yet has great wealth
set against the pretender of riches who has nothing
rush (make oneself poor, Hithpael) — 'another PRETENDS to be poor, yet has great wealth'; the disguise of poverty over real riches. Appearances deceive both ways.
wealth — the hidden reality behind feigned poverty
the great wealth concealed beneath a pretence of poverty
(the empty pretence of riches, by contrast)
the real substance hidden under feigned want
hon (wealth) — 'yet has great WEALTH'; the substance behind the disguise. Emergent: wealth as the concealed reality that appearances mask.
the life — a rich man's, ransomed by his wealth
the rich man's life, which his wealth must ransom (making him a target)
welded to the riches that are its price
nephesh (life/soul) — 'the ransom of a man's LIFE is his wealth'; the rich man's very life is at hazard for his riches, which must buy it back. Wealth as a liability on the soul.
wealth — the ransom of the rich man's life
the rich man's wealth, which serves as the ransom for his threatened life
welded to the life it must buy back
osher (riches) — 'is his WEALTH'; riches make a man a target whose life must be ransomed, where the poor hear no threat. Emergent: wealth as a hazard, not only a good.
freedom-from-threat — the poor man hears no threat
the poor man who hears no threat, unburdened by the hazards of wealth
set against the rich whose life is at hazard
shama (hear) NEGATED — 'a poor man hears no THREAT'; poverty has this freedom — no one threatens the man with nothing to seize. The read notes the paradoxical safety of the poor.
righteousness — whose light rejoices and shines bright
the righteous whose light shines and rejoices
welded to the joyful light it gives
tsaddiq — 'the light of the RIGHTEOUS rejoices'; the righteous life shines with joy, against the wicked's lamp that is snuffed out.
joy — the righteous' light shines joyfully
the joyful shining of the righteous man's light
the righteous whose light it is (263298)
welded to the righteous whose light rejoices
samach (rejoice/be glad) — 'the light of the righteous REJOICES'; a bright, glad light, the inner radiance of the righteous, against the wicked's extinguished lamp.
wickedness — whose lamp is put out
the wicked whose lamp is extinguished
(the rejoicing light of the righteous, by contrast)
set against the righteous' joyful, shining light
rasha — 'the lamp of the WICKED will be put out'; wickedness ends in darkness, the antithesis of the righteous' rejoicing light.
wisdom — the wise woman who builds her house
the wisdom of the woman who builds up her household
the folly that tears down, by contrast (263307)
set against the folly that destroys the house
chakam (wise) — 'the WISEST of women builds her house'; wisdom is constructive, building up the home. The wise woman as builder.
folly — which tears the house down with its own hands
the folly that, with her own hands, tears down her own house
the wisdom that builds, by contrast (263303)
set against the wisdom that builds the house
ivveleth (folly) — 'FOLLY with her own hands tears it down'; folly is self-destructive, demolishing what it should build. The foolish woman ruins her own home.
the heart — knows its own bitterness alone
the heart that alone knows its own bitterness, unshared
welded to the intimate self-knowledge it holds
leb (heart) — 'the HEART knows its own bitterness'; the profound privacy of the inner life — the deepest grief is known to the heart alone. No one fully enters another's inner world.
self-knowing — the heart knows its own grief
the heart's intimate, private knowledge of its own bitterness
welded to the heart whose knowing it is
yada (know) — 'KNOWS its own bitterness'; the self's private, incommunicable knowledge of its own pain. The solitude of the suffering heart.
the self — whose bitterness only it knows
the self/soul whose bitterness is known to it alone
welded to the grief that is its own
nephesh (soul/self) — 'its OWN bitterness'; the bitterness belongs to the self alone. Grief is ultimately private, sealed within the soul.
bitterness — the private grief the heart alone knows
the bitterness/grief that the heart knows in solitude, unshared
welded to the soul that bears it alone
morah (bitterness) — 'its own BITTERNESS'; the deep, private grief of the heart, which no other fully knows. The incommunicable core of suffering.
joy — private, no stranger shares it
the joy of the heart, which no stranger can fully share
the gladness sealed within, as the bitterness is
simchah (joy) — 'no stranger shares its JOY'; even joy is finally private — its full sweetness known only to the heart that feels it. The inner life is a solitude of both grief and gladness.
the wicked whose house is torn down
set against the upright whose tent flourishes
rasha — 'the house of the WICKED will be destroyed'; wickedness ends in demolition, against the upright whose humbler tent flourishes.
the upright whose tent, though humble, flourishes
the destroyed wicked house, by contrast (263319)
set against the wicked's demolished house
yashar (upright) — 'the tent of the UPRIGHT will flourish'; even a humble upright dwelling thrives, where the wicked's house falls. Character, not grandeur, endures.
self-deception — a way that seems right but ends in death
the way that seems right to a man but whose end is death
the self-approving way set against its deadly end

yashar (right/straight) — 'there is a way that SEEMS RIGHT to a man, but its end is death'; the deadly deception of self-approval. What feels right is not always right; the heart can deceive itself to death.
the heart — aching even beneath laughter
the heart that can ache even in the midst of laughter
welded to the hidden pain beneath the mirth
leb (heart) — 'even in laughter the HEART may ache'; the profound observation that outward mirth can mask inner pain. The heart's true state is hidden even behind a smile.
pain — the hidden hurt beneath laughter
the ache/pain that the heart may feel even while laughing
welded to the heart that hides it
kaab (be in pain/ache) — 'the heart may ACHE'; a real pain concealed under laughter. Mirth is no proof of a whole heart.
joy — whose end may be grief
the joy whose ending may turn out to be grief
welded to the grief that may follow it
simchah (joy) — 'the end of JOY may be grief'; even gladness can turn to sorrow. The read holds the sober realism — no earthly joy is guaranteed to last.
grief — the possible end of joy
the grief that may be the aftermath of joy
welded to the joy whose end it may be
tugah (grief/sorrow) — 'may be GRIEF'; the sober note that joy can curdle into sorrow. Realism about the fragility of gladness.
the backslidden heart — filled with the fruit of his ways
the backslidden/turned-away heart that reaps the fruit of its own ways
set against the good man filled with his own good fruit
leb (heart) — 'the BACKSLIDER in heart will be filled with the fruit of his ways'; the heart turned away reaps its own ways. Each is filled from within, from what he is.
goodness — the good man filled with his own good fruit
the good man who is filled with the fruit of his good ways
set against the backslider filled with his own fruit
tob (good) — 'a GOOD man will be filled with the fruit of his ways'; the good reap good, as the backslider reaps his own. Each is satisfied from his own character.
naivety — the simple who believes everything
the naive who believes every word uncritically
welded to the uncritical trust that marks him
pethi (simple/naive) — 'the SIMPLE believes everything'; naivety is dangerous credulity — the simple swallow every claim, unguarded.
the uncritical believing of everything by the naive
welded to the simpleness that believes all
aman (believe/trust, Hiphil) — 'BELIEVES everything'; here credulity, not faith — belief without discernment. The naive are prey to every claim.
the prudent who gives careful thought to where he is going
welded to the consideration he gives his way
arum (prudent/shrewd) — 'the PRUDENT gives thought to his steps'; prudence weighs and considers, against the simple's uncritical belief. The examined step.
consideration — the prudent weighs his steps
the careful thought/discernment the prudent gives to his steps
welded to the prudence whose act it is
bin (discern/consider) — 'gives THOUGHT to his steps'; the prudent examine their way before walking it, unlike the credulous simple.
the wise man who is cautious/wary and turns away from evil
welded to the wary care that marks him
chakam (wise) — 'one who is WISE is cautious and turns from evil'; wisdom is wary, careful, avoiding evil, against the fool's reckless self-confidence.
caution — the wise man's wary fear
the caution/fear by which the wise man is wary and avoids evil
welded to the aversion it produces
yare (fear/be cautious) — 'is CAUTIOUS'; a wary, healthy fear that keeps the wise from evil. Caution as the reflex of wisdom.
the turning-away from evil that the wise man's caution produces
sur (turn aside/away) — 'and TURNS AWAY from evil'; the wise man's caution issues in active avoidance of evil. Emergent: turning-from-evil as wisdom's protective reflex.
the fool who is reckless and heedlessly self-confident
welded to the reckless overconfidence that marks him
kesil (fool) — 'a FOOL is reckless and careless'; folly barrels ahead without caution, overconfident, the antithesis of the wary wise.
the reckless, careless over-confidence of the fool
welded to the folly that makes him heedless
batach (be confident) — here NEGATIVE: 'reckless and CARELESS/overconfident'; the fool's self-assurance is heedless folly, not the true security of trust in God (cf 3:5). Confidence misplaced.
hot temper — the short-tempered who acts foolishly
the hasty, short temper of the man who acts foolishly in anger
welded to the folly his temper produces
aph (nose/anger) — 'a man of quick TEMPER acts foolishly'; the short-fused act rashly and foolishly. Uncontrolled anger breeds folly.
the folly with which the hot-tempered man acts
welded to the anger that produces it
ivveleth (folly) — 'acts FOOLISHLY'; the fruit of quick temper is foolish action. Anger clouds judgement.
scheming — the man of evil devices, hated
the calculating schemer of evil devices, who is hated
welded to the hatred his scheming earns
mezimmah (evil devices/schemes) — 'a man of EVIL DEVICES is hated'; the cold schemer, even more than the hot-tempered, earns hatred. Calculated evil is loathed.
the hatred that the man of evil devices draws upon himself
welded to the schemes that provoke it
sane (hate) — 'is HATED'; the schemer is hated by all. Calculated malice repels.
naivety — the simple who inherit folly
the naive who come into folly as their inheritance
welded to the folly that is their portion
pethi (simple/naive) — 'the SIMPLE inherit folly'; naivety, uncured, hardens into folly. The simple who never learn come into folly as an estate.
the folly that the simple inherit as their portion
welded to the naivety that ripens into it
ivveleth (folly) — 'inherit FOLLY'; the portion of the uncured simple. Naivety left to itself becomes folly.
the prudent who are crowned with knowledge
welded to the knowledge that is their crown
arum (prudent/shrewd) — 'the PRUDENT are crowned with knowledge'; prudence is adorned and honoured with knowledge, against the simple's inheritance of folly.
the knowledge with which the prudent are crowned
welded to the prudence it adorns
daath (knowledge) — 'crowned with KNOWLEDGE'; knowledge is the prudent's honour and adornment, the bright opposite of the simple's folly-inheritance.
evil — who bow down before the good
the evil who are brought to bow before the good
welded to the good before whom they stoop
ra (evil/evildoers) — 'the EVIL bow down before the good'; evil is finally humbled before goodness. The moral order asserts itself.
the good before whom the evil are brought to bow
the evil who bow to them (263373)
welded to the evil humbled before them
tob (good) — 'before the GOOD'; goodness triumphs, the evil bowing before it. The vindication of the good.
wickedness — bowing at the gates of the righteous
the wicked brought to bow at the gates of the righteous
the righteous at whose gates they wait (263379)
welded to the righteous before whom they stoop
rasha — 'the wicked at the gates of the righteous'; the wicked reduced to suppliants at the righteous' door. Character reverses the pecking order.
righteousness — at whose gates the wicked bow
the righteous at whose gates the wicked are brought to bow
welded to the wicked humbled at their gate
tsaddiq — 'at the gates of the RIGHTEOUS'; the righteous are vindicated, the wicked their suppliants. Righteousness exalted in the end.
uprightness — the walk that fears the LORD
the uprightness of walk that expresses the fear of the LORD
welded to the reverence it embodies
yosher (uprightness) — 'whoever walks in UPRIGHTNESS fears the LORD'; a straight walk is the outward form of inner reverence. Conduct reveals the heart's fear of God.
fear of the LORD — expressed in an upright walk
the fear of the LORD that shows itself in an upright walk
welded to the straight walk that expresses it
yare (fear) — 'FEARS the LORD'; reverence for God, evidenced by uprightness of life. The inner fear and the outer walk are one.
deviousness — the crooked-wayed who despises God
the deviousness of ways that amounts to a despising of God
welded to the contempt his crookedness reveals

luz (be devious/crooked) — 'he who is DEVIOUS in his ways despises him'; crookedness of life is contempt for God. Emergent: deviousness as a practical despising of God, the antithesis of the reverent upright walk.
the contempt for God shown by the one whose ways are crooked
welded to the crookedness that expresses it
bazah (despise) — 'DESPISES him'; the crooked-wayed hold God in contempt, whatever they profess. Conduct despises where the upright walk reveres.
poverty — the poor, disliked even by his neighbour
the poor man who is disliked even by his own neighbour
welded to the rejection his poverty brings

rush (be poor) — 'the POOR is disliked even by his neighbour'; a bleak observation — poverty repels even neighbours. The read notes the harsh social reality the wise must see clearly (and, per 14:21, resist).
rejection — the poor man is disliked
the dislike/hatred that even a neighbour shows the poor man
welded to the poverty that provokes it
sane (hate/dislike) — 'is DISLIKED'; the social rejection of the poor, even by neighbours. A hard truth about how the world treats the needy.
riches — the rich, with many friends
the rich man who is surrounded by many friends
welded to the friends his wealth attracts

ashir (rich) — 'the RICH has many friends'; wealth attracts crowds of 'friends'. Emergent: riches as a magnet for fair-weather friendship — the read hears the cynicism (are they friends of the man or his money?).
friendship — the many who court the rich
the many friends/lovers who attach themselves to the rich man
welded to the wealth that draws them
aheb (love/friend) — 'many FRIENDS'; the many who love the rich — but the read questions the quality of a love drawn by wealth, against the neighbourly love owed the poor (14:21).
contempt — despising one's neighbour, which is sin
the despising of a neighbour that is itself a sin
welded to the sin that contempt makes him

buz (despise) — 'whoever DESPISES his neighbour is a sinner'; contempt for a neighbour (esp. the poor, cf 14:20) is not just unkind but sin. The read binds this to 14:20 — the world despises the poor; to do so is to sin.
sin — the neighbour-despiser is a sinner
the sinner that despising one's neighbour makes a man
his contempt that makes him so (263395)
welded to the contempt that constitutes the sin
chata (sin/sinner) — 'is a SINNER'; despising a neighbour is reckoned as sin. Contempt is not neutral but guilt.
graciousness — kindness to the poor, which is blessed
the gracious generosity toward the poor that is blessed
welded to the poor his kindness serves

chanan (be gracious/show favour) — 'blessed is he who is GENEROUS to the poor'; graciousness to the needy is blessed, the antithesis of despising the poor. Kindness to the poor as the mark of blessing.
the poor — recipients of gracious generosity
the poor/afflicted to whom the blessed man shows generous kindness
welded to the kindness that blesses them
anav (poor/afflicted/humble) — 'generous to the POOR'; the needy whom the blessed man serves. The read holds up care for the poor as the counter to the world's contempt (14:20).
erring — those who devise evil go astray
the going-astray/erring of those who plot evil
welded to the scheming that leads them astray
taah (go astray/wander) — 'do they not GO ASTRAY who devise evil?'; plotting evil is itself a wandering from the way. The schemer errs.
scheming — plotting evil, which leads astray
the devising/plotting of evil that makes men wander
welded to the erring it causes
charash (plough/devise) — 'who DEVISE evil'; the active plotting of harm, which is a going-astray. To scheme evil is to lose the way.
good-planning — those who devise good meet chesed and emet
the devising/planning of good that is met with steadfast love and faithfulness
welded to the covenant-love that meets them
charash (devise/plan) — 'those who DEVISE good meet steadfast love and faithfulness'; planning good draws chesed and emet in return. Good purpose is met with loyal love.
loyal love — met by those who devise good
the steadfast love/loyalty that good-planners meet
welded to faithfulness as the covenant pair
chesed (steadfast love) — 'meet STEADFAST LOVE'; the loyal love that answers good intentions. Paired with emet as the reward of good-devising.
faithfulness — met by those who devise good
welded to steadfast love as the covenant pair
emet (faithfulness/truth) — 'and FAITHFULNESS'; the reliability that meets good purpose, paired with chesed.
labour — in all toil there is profit
the painful toil/labour in which there is real profit, against empty talk
(the mere talk that ends in poverty)
the profitable labour set against fruitless words
etseb (painful toil/labour) — 'in all TOIL there is profit'; real, sweating labour yields gain, where mere talk (lip-labour) leads only to want. Work over words.
wisdom — the wise, crowned with wealth
the wise whose wealth is their crown
welded to the wealth their wisdom gains
chakam (wise) — 'the crown of the WISE is their wealth'; wisdom is honoured, its wealth a crown, against the fools whose folly only yields more folly.
the wealth that adorns and crowns the wise
welded to the wisdom that gains it
osher (riches) — 'is their WEALTH'; the wise man's wealth is his crown (honourable, well-used). Emergent: wealth as the honourable adornment of wisdom, against folly's barren yield.
folly — the fools', which yields only more folly
the folly of fools that produces nothing but folly
welded to the folly it multiplies
ivveleth (folly) — 'the FOLLY of fools brings folly'; folly is self-multiplying, yielding only more of itself, where wisdom is crowned with wealth.
folly — what the fools' folly produces
the folly that is all the fools' folly yields
welded to the folly that produces it
ivveleth (folly) — 'brings FOLLY'; folly begets folly, a barren cycle. The dark opposite of wisdom crowned.
truthfulness — the true witness who saves lives
the truthful witness whose true testimony saves lives
welded to the lives his truth rescues
emet (truth) — 'a TRUTHFUL witness saves lives'; true testimony can rescue lives (from false accusation), where the false witness is pure deceit. Truth as life-saving.
lives — saved by the truthful witness
the lives/souls that a truthful witness rescues
welded to the true testimony that delivers them
nephesh (lives/souls) — 'saves LIVES'; the lives a true witness delivers. Truth in testimony has power over life and death.
deceit — the false witness who breathes lies
the deceit of the one who breathes out lies
set against the truthful witness who saves lives
mirmah (deceit) — 'one who breathes out lies is DECEITFUL'; the false witness is treachery itself, the deadly antithesis of the life-saving true one.
fear of the LORD — which gives strong confidence
the fear of the LORD that gives a man strong confidence and his children refuge
welded to the strong assurance it yields
yirah (fear) — 'in the FEAR of the LORD one has strong confidence'; reverence, far from timidity, is the ground of the deepest confidence and security (even for one's children).
strength — the strong confidence of the God-fearer
the strength/might of the confidence that the fear of the LORD gives
welded to the assurance it fortifies
oz (strength) — 'STRONG confidence'; the fear of God gives a mighty, unshakeable assurance. Strength of soul from reverence.
the confident trust that the fear of the LORD gives
welded to the reverence that produces it
mibtach (confidence/trust) — 'strong CONFIDENCE'; the settled trust of the God-fearer, the true security (cf 3:26) rooted in reverence, not self or wealth.
refuge — the God-fearer's children have a shelter
the refuge/shelter that the God-fearer's children have
the shelter the fear of God secures for the next generation
machseh (refuge/shelter) — 'his children will have a REFUGE'; the fear of the LORD shelters not only the man but his children. Reverence secures a generational refuge.
fear of the LORD — a fountain of life
the fear of the LORD that is a life-giving fountain
welded to the life its fountain pours
yirah (fear) — 'the FEAR of the LORD is a fountain of life'; reverence is a spring of life (cf 13:14, of the wise teaching), turning men from death's snares.
life — the fountain that the fear of the LORD is
the life that the fear of the LORD pours out like a fountain
welded to the reverence whose fountain it is
chayyim (life) — 'a fountain of LIFE'; the fear of God is a spring of life. Emergent: life as the yield of reverence, turning from death.
turning-from-death — enabled by the fear of the LORD
the turning-away from the snares of death that the fear of the LORD enables
(the fountain of life it flows from)
the escape from death's snares that reverence works
sur (turn aside/away) — 'that one may TURN AWAY from the snares of death'; the fear of the LORD steers men clear of the traps that kill (cf 13:14). Emergent: turning-from-death as reverence's fruit.
glory — a king's, resting in his multitude of people
the glory/splendour of a king that rests in the multitude of his people
the ruin of a peopleless prince, by contrast (263455)
set against the prince ruined for want of people
hadar (splendour/glory) — 'in a MULTITUDE of people is the glory of a king'; a ruler's true glory is his people, not his pomp. Emergent: glory as resting in the people a ruler serves, not in himself.
the ruin of a prince who has no people
set against the king whose glory is his multitude
mechittah (ruin) — 'without people a prince is RUINED'; a ruler is nothing without those he rules. Ruin is the fate of the leader who has emptied his realm.
patience — long-suffering, the mark of understanding
the slowness-to-anger/patience that goes with great understanding
welded to the discernment that produces it
aph (anger/nose) in 'slow to ANGER' (erek appayim) — 'whoever is SLOW TO ANGER has great understanding'; patience is the fruit of discernment. The long-suffering see further than their anger.
the great understanding that belongs to the slow-to-anger
the patience that flows from it (263457)
welded to the patience it produces
tebunah (understanding) — 'has great UNDERSTANDING'; discernment breeds patience. The understanding heart is not quickly provoked.
hastiness — the quick-tempered spirit that exalts folly
the hasty, short spirit that lifts up and exalts folly
welded to the folly it magnifies
ruach (spirit) in 'hasty of TEMPER/spirit' (qetsar ruach) — 'he who has a hasty temper exalts folly'; the short-spirited magnify folly. Impatience is folly enthroned.
the folly that the quick-tempered lifts up and displays
welded to the impatience that magnifies it
ivveleth (folly) — 'exalts FOLLY'; the hasty-tempered make a display of folly. Impatience parades what patience would restrain.
folly — whose mouth brings a rod for his pride
the fool whose proud speech brings a rod upon his own back
welded to the arrogance his mouth reveals
evil (fool) — 'by the MOUTH of a fool comes a rod for his back'; the fool's talk earns him a beating. His mouth is his undoing.
pride — the fool's, drawing the rod
the pride/arrogance in the fool's speech that draws the chastening rod
the fool whose mouth reveals it (263466)
welded to the foolish mouth that voices it
gaavah (pride) — 'a rod for his BACK/PRIDE' (shevet gaavah); the fool's proud speech is a rod of pride that beats him. Arrogance voiced invites the rod.
the wise whose lips guard and preserve them
welded to the protection their lips afford
chakam (wise) — 'the lips of the WISE will preserve them'; wise speech protects its speakers, the antithesis of the fool's self-condemning mouth.
the preserving/guarding that the wise man's lips work for him
the wise lips that give it (263470)
welded to the wisdom that speaks it
shamar (keep/guard/preserve) — 'will PRESERVE them'; wise speech is a guard, keeping its speaker safe where the fool's mouth ruins him.
the tranquillity/soundness of heart that gives life to the body
welded to the heart whose calm it is
marpe (healing/tranquillity) — 'a TRANQUIL heart gives life to the flesh'; inner calm is bodily health. The read notes the psychosomatic link — a sound, peaceful heart heals the body.
the heart — tranquil, giving life to the flesh
the calm heart that gives life and health to the flesh
welded to the calm that fills it
leb (heart) — 'a tranquil HEART gives life to the flesh'; the inner life governs the body. A settled heart is bodily life.
life — given to the flesh by a tranquil heart
the life/health that a tranquil heart gives to the flesh
welded to the body it revives
chayyim (life) — 'gives LIFE to the flesh'; the calm heart vivifies the body. Emergent: life as what inner tranquillity gives the flesh.
flesh — vivified by the tranquil heart
the flesh/body that the tranquil heart gives life to
welded to the life that revives it
basar (flesh/body) — 'life to the FLESH'; the body flourishes under a calm heart, but rots under envy. The read holds body and heart as one system.
envy — which makes the bones rot
the envy/jealousy that rots the very bones
set against the calm heart that gives life to the flesh
qinah (envy/jealousy) — 'ENVY makes the bones rot'; corrosive envy is a bodily disease, rotting the bones. The dark psychosomatic counterpart — inner poison as physical decay.
oppression — oppressing the poor, insulting God
the oppressing of a poor man, which insults the poor man's Maker
welded to the reproach of God it constitutes
ashaq (oppress/exploit) — 'whoever OPPRESSES a poor man insults his Maker'; to crush the poor is to reproach God who made him. Oppression as blasphemy.
reproach — oppressing the poor reproaches God
the insulting/reproaching of God that oppressing the poor amounts to
welded to the oppression that reproaches God
charaph (reproach/insult) — 'INSULTS his Maker'; the theological grounding of social justice — the poor bear God's image, so to oppress them is to insult God.
graciousness — kindness to the needy, which honours God
the gracious generosity to the needy that honours their Maker
welded to the honour of God it constitutes
chanan (be gracious/show favour) — 'he who is GENEROUS to the needy honours him'; kindness to the poor honours God. The positive side of 14:31 — mercy as worship.
honouring — generosity to the poor honours God
the honouring of God that generosity to the needy amounts to
welded to the kindness that honours God
kabad (honour) — 'HONOURS him'; to be gracious to the poor is to honour their Maker. Care for the needy is reckoned as reverence for God.
wickedness — overthrown by his own evildoing
the wicked who is thrust down and overthrown by his own evil
the wicked felled by the evil in him
rasha — 'the WICKED is overthrown through his evildoing'; sin fells the sinner. His own evil is his undoing. The EVILDOING (ra) is the qualifier — the instrument of his fall.
righteousness — who finds refuge even in his death
the righteous who has a refuge even in death
welded to the shelter he has even dying
tsaddiq — 'the RIGHTEOUS finds refuge in his death'; even death cannot rob the righteous of refuge — a hint of hope beyond the grave. Character shelters to the end and past it.
refuge — the righteous' shelter, even in death
the refuge/trust the righteous has, secure even in dying
welded to the righteous it shelters
chasah (seek/find refuge) — 'finds REFUGE in his death'; the righteous take shelter even as they die, secure in God. Trust that outlasts life.
wisdom — reposing quietly in the discerning heart
the wisdom that rests/reposes quietly in the heart of the understanding
welded to the repose it finds in the wise
chokmah — 'WISDOM rests in the heart of a man of understanding'; wisdom settles quietly, at home, in the discerning — needing no display, unlike the fool who broadcasts folly.
repose — wisdom settles quietly in the wise heart
the resting/reposing of wisdom, quiet and settled, in the understanding heart
welded to the wisdom whose repose it is
nuach (rest/settle/repose) — 'RESTS in the heart'; wisdom is quiet and settled in the wise, not needing to proclaim itself. The calm dwelling of wisdom.
discernment — in whose heart wisdom rests
the man of understanding in whose heart wisdom quietly reposes
the discernment that is wisdom's quiet home
bin (discern/understand) — 'the heart of a man of UNDERSTANDING'; the discerning heart where wisdom rests at ease. Wisdom's true home is the understanding heart.
self-revealing — wisdom shows itself even among fools
the making-itself-known of wisdom even in the midst of fools
(its quiet rest in the wise, by contrast)
the self-revealing of wisdom that even fools' company cannot hide
yada (be/make known, Niphal) — 'it makes itself KNOWN even in the midst of fools'; wisdom cannot be wholly hidden — even among fools it shows itself. Truth will out.
the righteousness that lifts up and exalts a whole nation
the sin that disgraces, by contrast (263503)
set against the sin that reproaches a people
tsedaqah (righteousness) — 'RIGHTEOUSNESS exalts a nation'; righteousness has civic, national power — it raises a whole people, where sin disgraces. The moral order at the scale of nations.
sin — a reproach to any people
the sin that is a disgrace and reproach to any people
the righteousness that exalts, by contrast (263500)
set against the righteousness that exalts a nation
chattah (sin) — 'SIN is a reproach to any people'; sin disgraces a nation, the dark national counterpart to exalting righteousness. Corporate character has corporate consequence.
prudence — the servant who acts wisely wins favour
the prudent, skilful dealing of a servant that wins the king's favour
welded to the favour his wisdom earns
sakal (act wisely/prudently) — 'a servant who DEALS WISELY has the king's favour'; skilful, prudent service is rewarded, against shameful conduct that draws wrath.
favour — the wise servant's, from the king
the king's favour that the wise-dealing servant enjoys
welded to the prudent service that earns it
ratson (favour) — 'has the king's FAVOUR'; the wise servant's reward. Emergent: favour as what prudent service wins from a master.
shamefulness — the servant on whom wrath falls
the shameful conduct of the servant that brings the king's wrath
set against the wise servant who wins favour
bosh (act shamefully) — 'his wrath falls on one who ACTS SHAMEFULLY'; disgraceful service draws the master's anger, the antithesis of prudent dealing.
strength — the ox's power that yields abundant crops
the strength/power of the ox by which abundant crops are produced
(the clean but empty manger, by contrast)
the productive strength set against sterile emptiness

koach (strength/power) — 'abundant crops come by the STRENGTH of the ox'; productive power is worth the mess it makes. The read hears the principle — an empty stall is tidy but fruitless; strength put to work, though costly, yields abundance. Emergent: strength/capacity as the productive good.
faithfulness — the true witness who does not lie
the faithful witness who will not lie
set against the false witness who breathes lies
emun (faithful/trustworthy) — 'a FAITHFUL witness does not lie'; reliability of testimony, the mark of a true witness.
falseness — the false witness who breathes lies
the false witness whose testimony is a stream of lies
set against the faithful witness who does not lie
sheqer (falsehood) — 'a FALSE witness breathes out lies'; deceit is his very breath (cf 6:19). Falseness embodied in testimony.
scorn — the scoffer who seeks wisdom in vain
the scoffer whose scorn makes his search for wisdom fruitless
welded to the futile search his scorn dooms
luts (scoff/mock) — 'a SCOFFER seeks wisdom in vain'; scorn bars the door to wisdom, even when sought. The scoffer cannot find what his contempt refuses.
seeking — the scoffer's fruitless search for wisdom
the scoffer's seeking of wisdom that comes to nothing
welded to the contempt that empties it
baqash (seek) — 'seeks wisdom IN VAIN'; even the scoffer's seeking fails, because his heart is closed. Seeking without humility finds nothing.
the knowledge that comes easily to a man of understanding
the understanding to whom it comes (263534)
welded to the discernment that receives it easily
daath (knowledge) — 'KNOWLEDGE is easy for a man of understanding'; to the discerning, knowledge comes readily, where the scoffer labours in vain. The ready heart learns easily.
discernment — for whom knowledge is easy
the man of understanding for whom knowledge is easy to gain
the knowledge that comes to him (263532)
welded to the knowledge his discernment receives
bin (discern/understand) — 'a man of UNDERSTANDING'; discernment makes knowledge easy. The discerning receive readily what the scoffer cannot.
perceiving — no words of knowledge found with a fool
the one who leaves the fool
the not-finding of any words of knowledge in the fool's presence
welded to the knowledge one does not meet with a fool
yada (know/perceive) — 'there you do not MEET words of knowledge'; the fool's company yields no knowledge — leave it. One learns nothing from folly.
knowledge — absent from the fool's lips
the words of knowledge that are not found in the fool's presence
welded to the perceiving that comes up empty
daath (knowledge) — 'words of KNOWLEDGE'; what the fool's presence lacks. No knowledge is met where folly dwells.
prudence — whose wisdom discerns his own way
the prudent whose wisdom is to understand and discern his own way
welded to the discernment that is his wisdom
arum (prudent/shrewd) — 'the wisdom of the PRUDENT is to discern his way'; prudence is self-knowledge — understanding where one is going, unlike self-deceiving folly.
the discerning of one's own way that constitutes the prudent's wisdom
welded to the prudence whose wisdom it is
bin (discern/understand) — 'to DISCERN his way'; the prudent understand their own course. Self-aware discernment, against the fool's self-deception.
the folly of fools that deceives (itself and others)
welded to the deceit it works
ivveleth (folly) — 'the FOLLY of fools is deceiving'; folly is self-deceiving, blind to its own way, the antithesis of the prudent's discernment.
the deceit by which folly misleads itself and others
welded to the folly whose nature it is
mirmah (deceit) — 'is DECEIVING'; folly's very nature is deceit — it cannot see its own way, and misleads. Self-deception at the root.
folly — who mock at the guilt offering
the fools who scoff at guilt and its offering, making light of sin
welded to the guilt-reality they scorn
evil (fool) — 'FOOLS mock at the guilt offering'; folly makes light of sin and atonement, scoffing where it should tremble. Moral flippancy.
the guilt/guilt-offering that fools mock, refusing to take sin seriously
welded to the folly that makes light of it
asham (guilt/guilt-offering) — 'mock at the GUILT offering'; the reality of guilt and atonement, which fools scorn. To scoff at guilt is to be blind to one's own need.
the upright who enjoy acceptance and favour (with God)
welded to the favour they find
yashar (upright) — 'the UPRIGHT enjoy acceptance'; where fools scorn atonement, the upright find favour. Reverence toward guilt yields acceptance.
the acceptance/favour that the upright enjoy with God
welded to the uprightness that enjoys it
ratson (favour/acceptance) — 'the upright enjoy ACCEPTANCE'; favour with God, the fruit of taking sin and atonement seriously. Emergent: acceptance as the upright's portion, against the fools' scorn.
gentleness — a soft answer that turns away wrath
the soft, gentle answer that turns away and defuses wrath
welded to the anger it defuses

maaneh (answer/response) — 'a SOFT answer turns away wrath'; the gentle reply disarms anger. Emergent: the (soft) answer as the peacemaking word that quenches wrath. One of the great sayings on speech.
wrath — turned away by a soft answer
the wrath/hot anger that a gentle answer turns away
the soft answer that defuses it (263555)
welded to the gentleness that quenches it
chemah (wrath/hot anger) — 'turns away WRATH'; the fury that a soft word can quench. Anger is not fixed — a gentle answer disarms it.
harshness — a grievous word that stirs up anger
the harsh, painful word that provokes and stirs up anger
welded to the wrath it kindles
etseb (pain/grief) — 'a HARSH word stirs up anger'; the hurtful, grievous word inflames. Speech kindles or quenches; the harsh word ignites.
anger — stirred up by a harsh word
the anger that a harsh word kindles and stirs up
the harsh word that stirs it (263558)
welded to the harshness that provokes it
aph (anger/nose) — 'stirs up ANGER'; the anger a grievous word kindles. The mouth is the fire-starter or the fire-quencher.
severity — the grievous discipline for the wayward
the severe/grievous discipline awaiting the one who forsakes the way
welded to the deadly end of resisting correction
ra (evil/grievous/severe) — 'there is SEVERE discipline for him who forsakes the way'; abandoning the right way brings harsh correction. The grievous cost of straying.
hatred — of reproof, which ends in death
the hating of reproof that ends in death
welded to the harsh end of resisting correction
sane (hate) — 'whoever HATES reproof will die'; to hate correction is to choose death. The ultimate cost of the unteachable heart.
the heart — fully open before the LORD
the hearts of men, laid utterly open and known before the LORD
the inmost heart under the total gaze of God

leb (heart) — 'how much more the HEARTS of the children of man'; if even the realm of the dead lies open before God, how much more the human heart. The divine omniscience reaches the inmost self — nothing is hidden. A profound word on the exposed inner life (cf 15:3).
scorn — who dislikes reproof and shuns the wise
the scoffer who resents reproof and refuses to go to the wise
welded to the aversion to correction that marks him
luts (scoff/mock) — 'a SCOFFER does not like to be reproved'; scorn hates correction and avoids the wise who would give it. Self-imposed isolation from wisdom.
aversion — the scoffer does not love to be reproved
the scoffer's dislike/non-love of being reproved
welded to the contempt that hates correction
aheb (love/like) NEGATED — 'does not LIKE to be reproved'; the scoffer's aversion to correction. He loves his scorn more than the truth that would heal him.
wisdom — whom the scoffer will not approach
the wise whom the scoffer refuses to go to
the wisdom the scoffer will not seek
chakam (wise) — 'he will not go to the WISE'; the scoffer avoids the very wise who could help him, cutting himself off from wisdom. Pride's self-quarantine.
gladness — a glad heart that brightens the face
the gladness of heart that shows in a cheerful face
welded to the heart whose gladness it is
sameach (glad) — 'a GLAD heart makes a cheerful face'; inner gladness surfaces in the countenance. The face is the heart's window.
the heart — glad, brightening the face
the glad heart whose joy makes the face cheerful
welded to the gladness that fills it
leb (heart) — 'a glad HEART makes a cheerful face'; the heart governs the countenance. Inner state written on the face.
cheerfulness — the bright face a glad heart makes
the cheerful, bright face that a glad heart produces
(the crushed spirit of sorrow, by contrast)
the bright face set against the crushed spirit
yatab (do well/make good/be bright) — 'makes a CHEERFUL face'; the outward brightness of inner gladness, against the crushed spirit of heart-sorrow.
the heart — whose sorrow crushes the spirit
the heart whose sorrow crushes and breaks the spirit
welded to the spirit its sorrow breaks
leb (heart) — 'by SORROW of heart the spirit is crushed'; grief in the heart shatters the whole inner life. Heart-sorrow is spirit-crushing.
the spirit/inner life that heart-sorrow crushes and breaks
welded to the sorrow that shatters it
ruach (spirit) — 'the SPIRIT is crushed'; grief breaks the spirit (cf 15:4; 17:22; 18:14). The inner life bows under heart-sorrow.
the heart — of the discerning, seeking knowledge
the heart of the understanding man that actively seeks knowledge
welded to the discernment that drives its search
leb (heart) — 'the HEART of him who has understanding seeks knowledge'; the discerning heart is a seeker, hungry for knowledge, against the fool who feeds on folly.
the understanding whose heart actively seeks knowledge
welded to the seeking heart it drives
bin (discern/understand) — 'him who has UNDERSTANDING'; discernment makes the heart hungry for more knowledge. Wisdom is never sated.
seeking — the discerning heart pursues knowledge
the active seeking/pursuit of knowledge by the understanding heart
welded to the knowledge it pursues
baqash (seek) — 'SEEKS knowledge'; the discerning heart hunts for knowledge, where the fool grazes on folly. Wisdom is an appetite.
knowledge — sought by the discerning heart
the knowledge that the understanding heart actively seeks
welded to the seeking heart that pursues it
daath (knowledge) — 'seeks KNOWLEDGE'; the prize the discerning heart pursues, against the folly fools feed on.
the folly that the mouths of fools feed on
(the discerning heart that seeks knowledge, by contrast)
set against the heart that seeks knowledge
ivveleth (folly) — 'the mouths of fools feed on FOLLY'; fools graze on folly as their food, where the wise seek knowledge. You become what you consume.
affliction — the afflicted whose days are evil
the afflicted/oppressed whose days are all hard and evil
the cheerful heart's feast, by contrast (263605)
set against the continual feast of the glad heart

ani (afflicted/poor) — 'all the days of the AFFLICTED are evil'; affliction makes every day hard. Yet the read holds the contrast — it is the *cheerful heart*, not circumstance, that keeps continual feast (15:15b).
cheerfulness — the glad heart's continual feast
the cheerful/good heart that keeps a continual feast regardless of circumstance
welded to the glad heart that feasts
tob (good/cheerful) — 'the CHEERFUL of heart has a continual feast'; a glad heart turns every day into a feast, where affliction makes every day evil. Inner gladness outweighs outward hardship.
the heart — cheerful, keeping continual feast
the glad heart that makes life a continual feast
welded to the gladness that feasts
leb (heart) — 'the cheerful of HEART has a continual feast'; the heart, not the table, makes the feast. The inner life sets the tone of the outer.
evaluation — a little with the fear of the LORD is better than troubled wealth
the judgement that little with reverence beats great treasure and trouble
the fear that makes it better (263611)
welded to the reverence that outweighs treasure
tob (better) — 'BETTER is a little with the fear of the LORD than great treasure and trouble with it'; reverence with little beats wealth with anxiety. The value-scale of the wise.
fear of the LORD — worth more than great treasure
the fear of the LORD that makes a little better than troubled abundance
welded to the worth it gives the little
yirah (fear) — 'a little with the FEAR of the LORD'; reverence is the true wealth, making a little sufficient and a fortune-with-trouble worthless.
evaluation — herbs with love beat an ox with hatred
the judgement that a poor meal with love beats a rich feast with hatred
the love that makes it better (263621)
welded to the love that outweighs abundance
tob (better) — 'BETTER is a dinner of herbs where love is than a fattened ox and hatred with it'; love makes a poor table rich, hatred makes a feast bitter. Relationships outweigh abundance.
love — which makes a poor meal better than a feast
the love that makes a dinner of herbs better than a fattened ox
welded to (and set against) the hatred that poisons abundance
ahabah (love) — 'a dinner of herbs where LOVE is'; love transforms poverty into feast. The presence of love is worth more than any fare.
hatred — which poisons even a feast
the hatred that makes even a fattened ox bitter
the love it is set against (263621)
set against the love that enriches a poor meal
sinah (hatred) — 'a fattened ox and HATRED with it'; hatred sours the richest table. Enmity spoils abundance, as love sweetens poverty.
wrath — the hot-tempered who stirs up strife
the hot temper/wrath that stirs up and inflames strife
set against the patience that quiets contention
chemah (wrath/hot anger) — 'a HOT-TEMPERED man stirs up strife'; wrath inflames conflict, against the patient who calm it.
patience — the slow to anger who quiets contention
the slowness-to-anger/patience that calms and quiets contention
welded to the calming it works
aph (anger) in 'slow to ANGER' (erek appayim) — 'he who is slow to anger quiets contention'; patience is a peacemaker, cooling the strife that wrath inflames.
calming — the patient man quiets contention
the quieting/calming of contention by the slow-to-anger
welded to the strife it stills
shaqat (be quiet/still) — 'QUIETS contention'; patience actively stills conflict. The peacemaker's calming work.
the contention/strife that the patient man quiets
welded to the patience that calms it
rib (contention/strife) — 'quiets CONTENTION'; the conflict that patience stills, where wrath would inflame it.
sloth — whose way is a hedge of thorns
the sloth whose way is blocked and prickly like a thorn-hedge
the upright's level path, by contrast (263641)
set against the upright's smooth highway

atsel (sluggard) — 'the way of a SLUGGARD is like a hedge of thorns'; to the lazy, every path is obstructed and difficult (of his own making). Emergent: sloth that turns life into an impassable thicket.
uprightness — whose path is a level highway
the upright whose path is smooth and unobstructed, a level highway
the sluggard's thorny way, by contrast (263637)
set against the sluggard's hedge of thorns
yashar (upright) — 'the path of the UPRIGHT is a level highway'; uprightness makes a clear, open road, against the sluggard's self-made thicket.
the wise whose tongue makes knowledge attractive and good
welded to the knowledge it adorns
chakam (wise) — 'the tongue of the WISE commends knowledge'; wise speech presents knowledge well, making it appealing, against the fool's gushing folly.
adorning — the wise tongue makes knowledge good/pleasing
the making-good/commending by which the wise tongue adorns knowledge
the skilful presentation that adorns knowledge
yatab (do well/make good) — 'COMMENDS knowledge'; the wise not only know but present knowledge attractively, making it 'good' to hear. Winsome truth.
knowledge — well-presented by the wise tongue
the knowledge that the wise tongue commends and adorns
the knowledge made attractive by wise speech
daath (knowledge) — 'commends KNOWLEDGE'; the substance the wise tongue makes appealing, against the folly fools pour out.
folly — poured out by the mouths of fools
the folly that gushes and pours out from the mouths of fools
(the wise tongue that commends knowledge, by contrast)
set against the wise tongue that adorns knowledge
ivveleth (folly) — 'the mouths of fools POUR OUT folly'; folly gushes uncontrolled from the fool, where the wise commend knowledge. A fountain of folly.
wisdom — the wise son who gladdens his father
the wise son whose wisdom makes his father glad
welded to the joy the wise son brings
chakam (wise) — 'a WISE son makes a glad father' (cf 10:1); wisdom gladdens the parents, where folly despises them.
gladness — the joy a wise son brings his father
the father's gladness produced by his son's wisdom
welded to the wisdom that produces it
samach (rejoice/be glad) — 'makes a GLAD father'; the parental joy of wise children.
folly — the foolish man who despises his mother
the foolish man whose folly despises his own mother
welded to the contempt his folly breeds
kesil (fool) — 'a FOOLISH man despises his mother'; folly turns even against a mother. Contempt for parents is folly's mark.
contempt — the fool despises his mother
the contemptuous despising of his own mother by the fool
welded to the folly that scorns her
bazah (despise) — 'DESPISES his mother'; the fool's scorn reaches even his mother. Folly is ungrateful and contemptuous.
folly — a joy to the senseless
the folly that delights the one who lacks sense
welded to the perverse delight it brings
ivveleth (folly) — 'FOLLY is a joy to him who lacks sense'; the senseless take pleasure in folly itself. Delight reveals the empty heart.
perverse joy — the senseless delight in folly
the joy that the senseless take in folly itself
welded to the folly that pleases it
simchah (joy) — 'is a JOY to him who lacks sense'; joy misdirected — pleasure in folly. What one enjoys reveals the heart.
heartlessness — the one who lacks sense delights in folly
the lack of sense/heart that finds joy in folly
(the understanding that walks straight, by contrast)
set against the man of understanding
leb (heart/sense) — 'him who LACKS sense'; the empty heart delights in folly, where understanding walks a straight road.
the man of understanding who walks straight and purposefully
(the senseless who delights in folly, by contrast)
set against the senseless whose joy is folly
tebunah (understanding) — 'a man of UNDERSTANDING walks straight ahead'; discernment walks a straight, purposeful course, unlike the senseless who wander in folly's delight.
the counsel/consultation whose lack causes plans to fail
welded to the plans that fail without it
sod (counsel/consultation) — 'without COUNSEL plans fail'; plans without consultation collapse. Wisdom seeks counsel before acting.
the plans/purposes that fail for want of counsel but succeed with many advisers
welded to the counsel they need
machashabah (plan/purpose) — 'PLANS fail'; purposes come to nothing without counsel, but stand with many advisers. The plan needs the counsel.
counsel — the many advisers who bring success
the multitude of advisers whose counsel brings plans to success
the many counsellors who secure success
yaats (counsel/advise) — 'with many ADVISERS they succeed'; a multitude of counsellors secures a plan (cf 11:14; 24:6). Emergent: the collective wisdom of many advisers as what establishes plans.
apt reply — a fitting answer, a joy to give
the apt, fitting answer that is a joy to the one who gives it
welded to the joy of the fitting reply
maaneh (answer/reply) — 'to make an APT answer is a joy to a man'; the pleasure of a fitting, well-timed reply. Emergent: the apt answer as a source of joy to its speaker (cf 15:1).
joy — of giving an apt answer
the joy a man feels in giving a fitting, apt answer
the apt answer that gives it (263676)
welded to the fitting reply that brings it
simchah (joy) — 'is a JOY to a man'; the gladness of the well-spoken word. Right speech delights its speaker.
goodness — a word in season, how good
the goodness/excellence of a word spoken in its season
the excellence of the timely word
tob (good) — 'a word in season, how GOOD it is!'; the excellence of timely speech (cf 25:11). The right word at the right time is a delight.
life — the upward path of the prudent
the path of life that leads upward for the prudent, away from Sheol
welded to the prudent whose way it is
chayyim (life) — 'the path of LIFE leads upward for the prudent'; wisdom's road climbs toward life, away from the grave. Emergent: life as the upward direction of the prudent path.
prudence — for whom the path of life leads upward
the prudent for whom life's path leads upward, away from Sheol
welded to the life-path they walk
sakal (act prudently) — 'for the PRUDENT'; the prudent walk the upward road of life. Wisdom's direction is up, toward life.
the turning-away from Sheol beneath that the upward path of life enables
(the path of life that leads up)
the escape from the grave that prudence works
sur (turn aside/away) — 'that he may TURN AWAY from Sheol beneath'; the prudent's upward path is a turning-from-death (cf 13:14; 14:27). Emergent: turning-from-Sheol as the goal of the life-path.
pride — whose house the LORD tears down
the proud whose house the LORD tears down, while he protects the widow
the arrogance God abases, set against the humble he upholds
geeh (proud/haughty) — 'the LORD tears down the house of the PROUD'; God abases the arrogant and upholds the helpless widow. Pride draws divine demolition; humility, divine protection.
thoughts — of the wicked, an abomination to God
the inner thoughts/schemes of the wicked, detestable to the LORD
welded to the divine revulsion they draw

machashabah (thought/scheme) — 'the THOUGHTS of the wicked are an abomination to the LORD'; God judges the inner thoughts, not just deeds. Evil devised is already loathsome. The ABOMINATION (toebah) is the qualifier.
graciousness — pleasant words that are pure
the gracious, pleasant words that are pure before God
welded to the purity that marks them
noam (pleasantness/graciousness) — 'GRACIOUS words are pure'; kind, pleasant speech is clean before God, against the wicked's abominable thoughts. Grace in speech is purity.
the purity/cleanness of gracious, pleasant words
welded to the gracious words it qualifies
tahor (pure/clean) — 'gracious words are PURE'; pleasant speech is ritually and morally clean before God, the antithesis of the wicked's abominable thoughts.
greed's ruin — the greedy troubles his own household
the troubling/ruin the greedy man brings on his own house through unjust gain
set against the incorruptible who lives
akar (trouble/ruin) — 'whoever is greedy for unjust gain TROUBLES his own household'; greed for ill-gotten gain ruins one's own family. Covetousness is self-destructive.
incorruptibility — hating bribes, which brings life
the hating of bribes that marks the incorruptible and brings life
welded to the life integrity secures
sane (hate) — 'he who HATES bribes will live'; to loathe bribery is to choose life. Integrity refuses corruption and thereby lives.
the life that comes to the one who hates bribes
the hating of bribes that earns it (263710)
welded to the integrity that secures it
chayah (live) — 'will LIVE'; the incorruptible lives, where greed ruins. Integrity is life-giving.
the heart — of the righteous, pondering how to answer
the righteous heart that ponders and weighs how to answer before speaking
welded to the deliberation it performs
leb (heart) — 'the HEART of the righteous ponders how to answer'; the righteous weigh their words, unlike the wicked mouth that gushes evil. Speech considered in the heart first.
righteousness — whose heart ponders its answer
the righteous whose heart weighs its words before speaking
(the wicked mouth that pours evil, by contrast)
set against the wicked who pour out evil
tsaddiq — 'the heart of the RIGHTEOUS ponders'; righteousness shows in weighed, considered speech.
deliberation — the righteous heart weighs its answer
the pondering/meditating by which the righteous heart weighs how to answer
welded to the heart whose deliberation it is
hagah (ponder/meditate/mutter) — 'PONDERS how to answer'; the righteous rehearse and weigh their words inwardly before speaking. Considered speech.
wickedness — whose mouth pours out evil
the wicked whose mouth gushes out evil things without deliberation
set against the righteous who weigh their words
rasha — 'the mouth of the WICKED pours out evil things'; the wicked gush evil unconsidered, the antithesis of the pondering righteous heart.
wickedness — from whom the LORD is far
the wicked from whom the LORD keeps his distance
(the righteous whose prayer he hears, by contrast)
set against the righteous whose prayer God hears
rasha — 'the LORD is far from the WICKED'; God distances himself from the wicked, where he draws near to hear the righteous. Character determines access to God.
prayer — the righteous', which the LORD hears
the prayer of the righteous that the LORD hears and answers
its being heard (263725) by God, from the righteous (263727)
the righteous prayer that God attends
