tephillah (prayer) — 'he HEARS the prayer of the righteous'; the righteous' prayer reaches God, where he is far from the wicked. The HEARING (shama) is the divine response (qualifier); the prayer and the righteous are the human chars.
righteousness — whose prayer the LORD hears
the righteous whose prayer the LORD draws near to hear
welded to the prayer God attends
tsaddiq — 'the prayer of the RIGHTEOUS'; righteousness gives access to God, whose ear is open to the upright. Character opens heaven.
evil — watched by the eyes of the LORD
the evil upon whom the LORD's watching eyes rest everywhere
welded to the good under the same divine gaze
ra (evil) — 'keeping watch on the EVIL and the good'; the divine omniscience — no evil escapes God's eye. The read holds the searching gaze under which all conduct lies.
good — watched by the eyes of the LORD
the good upon whom the LORD's watching eyes also rest everywhere
welded to the evil under the same divine gaze
tob (good) — 'watch on the evil and the GOOD'; God sees the good too — a comfort as well as a warning. All are under the ever-present divine gaze.
gladdening — the light of the eyes rejoices the heart
the gladdening of the heart by the light of the eyes (a bright, cheerful sight)
welded to the heart it brightens
samach (rejoice/gladden) — 'the light of the eyes REJOICES the heart'; a bright, cheerful sight gladdens the inner life. The eye feeds the heart.
the heart — gladdened by light and good news
the heart that is gladdened by the light of the eyes and refreshed by good news
welded to the joy that fills it
leb (heart) — 'rejoices the HEART'; the inner seat that brightens at a good sight or word. The heart responds to what eye and ear bring it.
goodness — the good news that refreshes the bones
the good/glad news that brings refreshment to the very bones
welded to the report it makes good
tob (good) — 'GOOD news refreshes the bones'; a good report is bodily refreshment. Glad tidings reach even the bones.
report — good news that refreshes the bones
the good report/news that refreshes and invigorates the body
welded to the goodness that makes it glad
shemuah (report/news) — 'good NEWS refreshes the bones'; a glad report invigorates the whole person. Emergent: news/report as what reaches and refreshes the inner-and-bodily self.
refreshment — good news invigorates the bones
the refreshment/invigoration that good news brings to the bones
the bodily refreshment glad tidings give
dashen (make fat/refresh) — 'REFRESHES the bones'; good news is bodily refreshment, reaching the frame itself (cf 15:13; 17:22). Emergent: the invigoration good tidings work in the body.
heeding — the ear that heeds life-giving reproof
the ear that listens to and heeds life-giving reproof, dwelling among the wise
welded to the life-giving correction it receives
shama (hear/heed) — 'the ear that LISTENS to life-giving reproof will dwell among the wise'; heeding correction admits one to the company of the wise. Teachability is entry to wisdom.
life — the reproof that gives life
the life that reproof gives to the one who heeds it
welded to the heeding that takes it in
chayyim (life) — 'LIFE-GIVING reproof'; correction, though painful, gives life. Emergent: life as what heeded reproof imparts.
wisdom — the company the reproof-heeder joins
the wise among whom the one who heeds reproof comes to dwell
the company of the wise, entered by heeding
chakam (wise) — 'will dwell among the WISE'; the teachable join the wise. Company is gained by heeding correction.
the self-despising that ignoring instruction amounts to
welded to the self he scorns
maas (reject/despise) — 'whoever ignores instruction DESPISES himself'; to refuse correction is self-contempt — a man who will not be taught scorns his own soul.
the self — despised by ignoring instruction
the very soul/self that a man despises when he ignores instruction
welded to the contempt he shows himself
nephesh (soul/self) — 'despises HIMSELF'; the self is the casualty of refusing correction. To reject teaching is to harm one's own soul.
the listening to reproof that gains a man intelligence/heart
welded to the sense it acquires
shama (hear/heed) — 'he who LISTENS to reproof gains intelligence'; heeding correction acquires understanding. The ear feeds the heart with sense.
the intelligence/heart that a man gains by listening to reproof
welded to the listening that acquires it
leb (heart/intelligence) — 'gains INTELLIGENCE'; heeding correction acquires an understanding heart. Sense is earned by listening.
fear of the LORD — instruction in wisdom
the fear of the LORD that is itself schooling/instruction in wisdom
the reverence that schools the heart in wisdom
yirah (fear) — 'the FEAR of the LORD is instruction in wisdom'; reverence is the very schooling of wisdom (cf 1:7; 9:10). To fear God is to be taught wisdom.
the humility that precedes and prepares the way for honour
welded to the honour it goes before
anavah (humility) — 'HUMILITY comes before honour'; the lowly way leads up to honour (cf 18:12; 22:4). Humility is the road to being lifted up.
the honour that follows and crowns humility
welded to the humility that leads to it
kabod (honour) — 'humility comes before HONOUR'; honour is reached by the road of humility, not pride. The order is fixed: down, then up.
life — the gentle tongue is a tree of life
the life that a gentle/healing tongue gives, being a tree of life
the life-giving gentleness set against spirit-crushing perversity
chayyim (life) — 'a gentle tongue is a tree of LIFE'; healing speech gives life, where perverse speech crushes. Emergent: life as the fruit of a gentle tongue (cf 15:1).
perversity — in the tongue, which breaks the spirit
the perverseness/crookedness in a tongue that crushes the spirit of those who hear
welded to the crushing it works

selef (crookedness/perverseness) — 'PERVERSENESS in it breaks the spirit'; twisted speech does not merely offend but crushes the hearer's spirit. Emergent: perverse speech as a spirit-breaking force, the dark opposite of the healing tongue.
crushing — perverse speech breaks the spirit
the breaking/crushing of the spirit that perverse speech works
welded to the perversity that crushes
sheber (breaking/crushing) — 'breaks the SPIRIT'; perverse words shatter the inner life of the hearer. Emergent: the crushing of the spirit as the wound of a perverse tongue.
the spirit — crushed by perverse speech
the spirit/inner life that perverse speech breaks and crushes
welded to the crushing that shatters it
ruach (spirit) — 'breaks the SPIRIT'; the inner life is crushed by a perverse tongue, where a gentle tongue gives it life. The spirit as the casualty of cruel words.
folly — who despises his father's instruction
the fool who scorns his father's instruction
welded to the contempt that marks him
evil (fool) — 'a FOOL despises his father's instruction'; folly scorns correction, against the prudent who heed reproof.
the fool's contemptuous spurning of his father's instruction
welded to the folly that scorns correction
naats (spurn/despise) — 'DESPISES his father's instruction'; the fool's scorn for correction. Contempt for instruction is folly's signature.
heeding — whoever keeps reproof becomes prudent
the heeding/keeping of reproof that makes one prudent
welded to the prudence it produces
shamar (keep/heed) — 'whoever HEEDS reproof is prudent'; keeping correction breeds prudence, the antithesis of the fool's scorn.
prudence — the fruit of heeding reproof
the prudence that comes of heeding reproof
welded to the heeding that yields it
aram (be prudent/shrewd) — 'is PRUDENT'; heeding correction makes a man shrewd, where scorning it keeps him a fool.
righteousness — in whose house is much treasure
the righteous in whose house there is much (well-gotten) treasure
welded to the wealth his righteousness secures
tsaddiq — 'in the house of the RIGHTEOUS there is much treasure'; righteousness secures lasting store, where the wicked's income brings trouble.
the abundant treasure/store in the righteous man's house
welded to the righteousness that secures it
chosen (treasure/store/wealth) — 'much TREASURE'; the righteous house's lasting store, honestly gained and secure, against the trouble-laden income of the wicked.
the wicked whose very income/gain is attended with trouble
set against the righteous house's secure store
rasha — 'trouble befalls the income of the WICKED'; the wicked's gain is cursed with trouble. Ill-gotten income brings grief.
the wise whose lips scatter and spread knowledge abroad
welded to the knowledge their lips disseminate
chakam (wise) — 'the lips of the WISE spread knowledge'; wise speech disseminates knowledge like scattered seed, against the fools' hearts that spread nothing true.
knowledge — spread by the lips of the wise
the knowledge that the wise scatter abroad through their lips
the wise lips that spread it (263787)
welded to the wisdom that disseminates it
daath (knowledge) — 'spread KNOWLEDGE'; the wise sow knowledge widely. Wisdom is generous, not hoarding.
the heart — of fools, spreading no true knowledge
the hearts of fools, which (unlike the wise lips) spread no true knowledge
(the wise lips that spread knowledge, by contrast)
set against the wise lips that disseminate knowledge
leb (heart) — 'not so the HEARTS of fools'; the fool's heart has no true knowledge to spread. Emptiness within yields nothing worth scattering.
the wicked whose very sacrifice is detestable to the LORD
welded to the divine revulsion his sacrifice draws

rasha — 'the sacrifice of the WICKED is an abomination to the LORD'; ritual without righteousness is loathsome to God. The heart, not the offering, is judged. The ABOMINATION (toebah) is the qualifier.
prayer — the upright's, acceptable to God
the prayer of the upright, which is acceptable and pleasing to the LORD
welded to the uprightness that makes it acceptable
tephillah (prayer) — 'the PRAYER of the upright is acceptable to him'; the upright's prayer, unlike the wicked's sacrifice, pleases God. Prayer from a right heart is welcome.
the upright whose prayer is acceptable to God
welded to the acceptance their prayer finds
yashar (upright) — 'the prayer of the UPRIGHT'; uprightness makes prayer acceptable. Character qualifies worship.
acceptance — the upright prayer's favour with God
the acceptance/favour that the upright's prayer finds with God
welded to the uprightness whose prayer it accepts
ratson (favour/acceptance) — 'is ACCEPTABLE to him'; the favour the upright prayer enjoys with God, against the wicked's abominable sacrifice. Emergent: acceptance as what upright prayer finds.
the wicked whose way of life is detestable to the LORD
welded to the divine revulsion his way draws
rasha — 'the way of the WICKED is an abomination to the LORD'; not only their worship but their whole way is loathsome. The ABOMINATION (toebah) is the qualifier.
the pursuit of righteousness that the LORD loves
welded to the divine love it draws

tsedaqah (righteousness) — 'he LOVES him who pursues righteousness'; the pursuit of righteousness draws God's love. The human char is the pursuit; God's LOVE (aheb) is the divine response (qualifier, cf 3:12).
the heart — man's, which makes the plans
the human heart that arranges and makes its plans, which yet God overrules
set against the answer that comes from the LORD
leb (heart) — 'the PLANS of the HEART belong to man'; man's heart plans, but the outcome (the tongue's answer) is God's. The read holds the tension of human planning under divine sovereignty.
the answer — of the tongue, given by the LORD
the answer of the tongue that, though man plans, comes from the LORD
set against the human heart that plans

maaneh (answer/reply) — 'the ANSWER of the tongue is from the LORD'; man arranges his thoughts, but the actual word that comes out is God-given. Emergent: the answer as the point where divine sovereignty meets human speech.
faithlessness — the true king's mouth does not sin in judgment
the faithlessness/treachery that the true king's mouth avoids in giving judgement
the integrity of the king's judging mouth

maal (act unfaithfully/treacherously) NEGATED — 'his mouth does not SIN in judgment'; the king's judging word is free of treachery, faithful and just. Emergent: faithlessness (negated) as the mark of just royal judgement.
justice — a just balance, the LORD's own standard
the just balance and scales that belong to the LORD, his own standard of justice
the divine standard of justice behind honest weights
mishpat (justice) — 'a JUST balance and scales are the LORD's'; honest weights are God's own — the standard of justice belongs to him. Fair dealing is grounded in the character of God.
abhorrence — kings should detest doing evil
the abhorrence with which kings ought to regard the doing of evil
the righteousness that establishes the throne (263839)
welded to the righteousness that grounds royal rule
toebah (abomination) — 'it is an ABOMINATION to kings to do evil'; here the KINGS' loathing (not God's) — good rulers detest evil, because the throne stands on righteousness, not wickedness.
righteousness — by which the throne is established
the righteousness by which a king's throne is made firm and secure
welded to the loathing of evil that upholds the throne
tsedaqah (righteousness) — 'the throne is established by RIGHTEOUSNESS'; a throne stands secure only on righteous rule. Justice is the foundation of lasting authority.
righteousness — of speech, a king's delight
the righteousness of lips/speech in which a king delights
welded to the royal delight it draws
tsedeq (righteousness) — 'RIGHTEOUS lips are the delight of a king'; honest, righteous speech pleases a good king. Character in speech wins favour.
delight — the king's, in righteous lips
the king's delight/favour toward righteous, honest speech
the righteous lips he delights in (263840)
welded to the honest speech that pleases him
ratson (delight/favour) — 'are the DELIGHT of a king'; the king's pleasure (a human delight, not God's) in righteous speech. Emergent: royal delight as what honest lips draw.
love — the king loves the one who speaks right
the king's love for the one who speaks what is right and honest
welded to the honest speech that wins his love
aheb (love) — 'he LOVES him who speaks what is right'; the king's love (human) for the honest speaker. Right speech is loved by good authority.
uprightness — the honest speech the king loves
the upright, honest speech that wins a king's love
welded to the royal love it draws
yashar (right/upright) — 'him who speaks what is RIGHT'; honest, upright speech is loved by a good king. Integrity of word is prized.
wrath — a king's, a messenger of death
the wrath of a king, deadly as a messenger of death
set against the wise man who pacifies it
chemah (wrath/fury) — 'a king's WRATH is a messenger of death'; royal anger can kill. The wise treat it with grave care.
wisdom — who appeases a king's deadly wrath
the wise man who knows how to pacify and appease a king's deadly wrath
welded to the pacifying he works
chakam (wise) — 'a WISE man will appease it'; wisdom knows how to defuse even a king's deadly anger. Prudence handles power carefully.
pacifying — the wise man covers/appeases wrath
the appeasing/pacifying by which the wise man covers a king's wrath
welded to the wisdom that pacifies
kaphar (cover/pacify/appease) — 'a wise man will APPEASE it'; the wise cover and calm deadly wrath. Emergent: appeasing/pacifying as the wise handling of dangerous anger.
benevolent goodwill — a king's favour, life-giving as spring rain
the favour of a king, whose lighted face means life and whose goodwill is like the clouds that bring the spring rain — the benevolent regard of power that revives and refreshes those it rests upon
the ruler's goodwill that falls life-giving as rain on those beneath it

ratson (favour/goodwill) — 'his FAVOR is like the clouds that bring the spring rain' (16:15); a king's benevolent goodwill is life-giving, refreshing as timely rain. The favour of the powerful, rightly given, revives (cf 19:12; 16:14).
evaluation — wisdom is far better than gold
the judgement that getting wisdom far outweighs getting gold
the surpassing worth of wisdom over wealth
tob (better) — 'how much BETTER to get wisdom than gold!'; wisdom's worth far exceeds gold. The emphatic value-judgement of the wise (cf 3:14; 8:19).
understanding — to be chosen over silver
the understanding whose getting is to be chosen rather than silver
the choosing of it over silver (263871)
welded to the preference it commands
binah (understanding) — 'to get UNDERSTANDING is to be chosen rather than silver'; discernment outvalues silver. The deliberate preference of the wise.
the deliberate choosing/preferring of understanding above silver
welded to the understanding it chooses
bachar (choose/select) — 'to be CHOSEN rather than silver'; the wise deliberately choose understanding over wealth. Valuing as an act of will.
uprightness — whose highway turns aside from evil
the upright whose settled way (highway) turns aside from evil
welded to the avoidance of evil that marks it
yashar (upright) — 'the highway of the UPRIGHT turns aside from evil'; the upright life is a raised road that avoids evil. Character keeps to the clear way.
turning-from-evil — the upright highway avoids evil
the turning-away from evil that characterises the upright's highway
the uprightness whose way it is (263875)
welded to the upright way it marks
sur (turn aside/away) — 'TURNS ASIDE from evil'; the upright's road is defined by its avoidance of evil (cf 16:6). Emergent: turning-from-evil as the built-in course of the upright way.
self-guarding — guarding one's way preserves one's life
the guarding of one's way that preserves one's own life
welded to the life its watchfulness protects
shamar (keep/guard) — 'whoever GUARDS his way preserves his life'; watching one's conduct is self-preservation. Vigilance over the way keeps the soul.
the life — preserved by guarding one's way
the life/soul that is preserved by guarding one's way
welded to the watchfulness that keeps it
nephesh (life/soul) — 'preserves his LIFE'; the self is kept safe by a guarded way. Watchfulness over conduct guards the soul.
the pride/arrogance that precedes and ushers in destruction
welded to the ruin it goes before
gaon (pride/majesty→arrogance) — 'PRIDE goes before destruction'; arrogance is the herald of ruin. The most famous warning against pride — self-exaltation is the prelude to collapse.
the destruction/ruin that follows on pride
welded to the arrogance that ushers it in
sheber (breaking/destruction) — 'before DESTRUCTION'; the ruin that pride brings. Emergent: destruction as the sequel to pride, the fall the haughty court.
haughtiness — a high spirit before a fall
the haughty, high/lofty spirit that goes before a fall
the lofty spirit set against the fall it courts

gobah (height/haughtiness) — 'a HAUGHTY spirit before a fall'; the lofty spirit is on the edge of falling. Height of pride, then the drop. Emergent: haughtiness of spirit as the disposition that precedes a fall.
evaluation — a lowly spirit with the poor beats spoil with the proud
the judgement that a lowly spirit among the poor is better than dividing spoil with the proud
the lowliness that makes it better (263892)
welded to the humility that outweighs spoil
tob (better) — 'BETTER to be of a lowly spirit with the poor than to divide the spoil with the proud'; humility with the lowly beats gain with the arrogant. The value-scale inverts worldly reckoning.
lowliness — a humble spirit, better than proud spoil
the lowly, humble spirit that is better than sharing spoil with the proud
welded to the value humility gives
shaphal (be low/humble) — 'of a LOWLY spirit with the poor'; a humble spirit among the poor is worth more than gain among the proud. Emergent: lowliness of spirit as the better estate.
the poor/humble — good company for the lowly spirit
the poor/humble among whom a lowly spirit is better than spoil with the proud
set against the proud with whom one might divide spoil
anav (poor/humble/afflicted) — 'with the POOR'; the humble company that is better than the proud, even with less. The read notes where the wise choose to stand.
pride — bad company, even with spoil to divide
the proud with whom dividing spoil is worse than lowliness with the poor
geeh (proud) — 'to divide the spoil with the PROUD'; even shared plunder among the proud is worse than humble poverty. Company of character over company of gain.
attentiveness — heeding the word, finding good
the giving-of-thought/attention to the word that discovers good
(the good it finds; the trust that blesses)
the attentive heeding that finds good
sakal (give attention/act prudently) — 'whoever GIVES THOUGHT to the word will discover good'; attentive heeding of the word finds good. Prudence in receiving the word is rewarded.
trust — in the LORD, which is blessedness
the trust in the LORD that makes a man blessed
(the good found by heeding the word)
the God-trust that crowns the attentive with blessing
batach (trust) — 'blessed is he who TRUSTS in the LORD'; trust in God is the crown of the attentive heart. The true security (cf 3:5; 28:25) that makes one blessed.
wisdom — the wise of heart, called discerning
the wise-hearted who is recognised and called discerning
welded to the heart that seats his wisdom
chakam (wise) — 'the WISE of heart is called discerning'; wisdom of heart earns the name of discernment. Inner wisdom wins the reputation.
the heart — wise, the seat of discernment
the wise heart that is the seat of the discernment for which one is named
welded to the wisdom it carries
leb (heart) — 'the wise of HEART'; wisdom's seat, whence discernment flows and by which one is known.
being-named — the wise-hearted is called discerning
the being-called/named discerning that the wise heart earns
the discernment he is named for (263912)
welded to the discernment his name reflects
qara (call/name) — 'is CALLED discerning'; reputation follows character — the wise heart is publicly recognised as discerning.
discernment — the reputation of the wise-hearted
the discernment that the wise-hearted is recognised and named for
welded to the recognition it earns
bin (discern) — 'is called DISCERNING'; the discernment of the wise heart, publicly acknowledged. Wisdom is known by its fruit.
prudence — a fountain of life to its owner
the good sense/prudence that is a fountain of life to the one who has it
welded to the life its fountain pours
sekel (good sense/prudence) — 'GOOD SENSE is a fountain of life to him who has it'; prudence is a spring of life to its possessor, against the folly of fools' instruction.
life — the fountain that good sense is
the life that good sense pours out like a fountain to its owner
the good sense whose fountain it is (263917)
welded to the prudence that gives it
chayyim (life) — 'a fountain of LIFE'; good sense is life-giving to the one who has it (cf 10:11; 13:14; 14:27). Emergent: life as the yield of prudence.
the fools whose very instruction/discipline amounts only to folly
welded to the folly their teaching yields
evil (fool) — 'the instruction of FOOLS is folly'; what fools teach is only folly. Their correction has no wisdom in it, the antithesis of life-giving good sense.
folly — what the fools' instruction amounts to
the folly that is all the fools' instruction comes to
welded to the fools whose teaching it is
ivveleth (folly) — 'is FOLLY'; the fools' teaching is folly through and through, giving no life. Empty instruction from empty hearts.
the heart — of the wise, governing his speech
the wise heart that instructs the mouth and makes speech judicious
welded to the wisdom that fills it
leb (heart) — 'the HEART of the wise makes his speech judicious'; the inner life governs the outer word — the wise heart teaches the mouth. Speech flows from the heart's wisdom.
wisdom — whose heart teaches the mouth
the wisdom whose heart makes the speech prudent and persuasive
welded to the heart it governs
chakam (wise) — 'the heart of the WISE'; wisdom in the heart shapes wise speech. The mouth is schooled by the heart.
prudence — the wise heart makes speech judicious
the judiciousness/prudence that the wise heart gives to the speech
the prudent speech the wise heart produces
sakal (make prudent/wise) — 'makes his speech JUDICIOUS'; the wise heart makes the mouth prudent and persuasive. Inner wisdom becomes wise speech.
graciousness — pleasant words, sweet as honey
the gracious, pleasant words that are like a honeycomb, sweet and healing
welded to the soul they delight
noam (pleasantness/graciousness) — 'GRACIOUS words are like a honeycomb'; kind, pleasant speech is sweet and nourishing, healing to soul and body. Grace in words as medicine.
the soul — sweetened by gracious words
the soul to which gracious words are sweetness, like honey
welded to the pleasant words that delight it
nephesh (soul) — 'sweetness to the SOUL'; the inner life delighted by gracious words. Kind speech feeds the soul.
health — gracious words heal the body
the health/healing that gracious words bring to the body
the bodily healing gracious words work
marpe (health/healing) — 'HEALTH to the body'; gracious words heal not only the soul but the frame (cf 15:30; 17:22). The psychosomatic power of kind speech — sweetness within, health without.
self-deception — a way that seems right but ends in death
the way that seems right to a man but whose end is death
the self-approving way set against its deadly end
yashar (right/straight) — 'a way that SEEMS RIGHT to a man, but its end is death' (=14:12); the deadly deception of self-approval. What feels right can lead to death — the heart can deceive itself.
labour — the toiler driven to work by his hunger
the labouring worker whose own appetite works on his behalf, driving him on
welded to the hunger that presses him to labour
amel (labourer/toiler) — 'a WORKER's appetite works for him'; the toiler is driven by his own hunger. Emergent: the labourer as one whose need presses him to productive work.
hunger — the worker's, which drives him to labour
the appetite/hunger that presses and urges the worker to labour
welded to the toiler it presses
nephesh (appetite/hunger) — 'a worker's APPETITE works for him; his mouth urges him on'; hunger is a taskmaster, pressing a man to work. Need as the spur to labour.
malice — the evil the worthless man plots
the evil/mischief that a worthless man digs up and plots, his speech a scorching fire
the plotted evil that his burning words unleash
ra (evil) — 'a worthless man PLOTS evil'; the good-for-nothing digs up mischief, and his speech scorches like fire. Malice devised within, then loosed by a burning tongue.
perversity — the perverse man who spreads strife
the perverse/dishonest man who scatters and spreads strife
welded to the discord he sows
tahpukoth (perversity/dishonesty) — 'a DISHONEST man spreads strife'; the perverse sow discord, and the whisperer parts even close friends. Perversity is socially corrosive.
strife — spread by the perverse man
the strife/discord that the perverse man scatters and spreads abroad
the perverse man who sows it (263960)
welded to the perversity that spreads it
madon (strife/contention) — 'spreads STRIFE'; the discord the perverse man sows, dividing even close friends. Community's fabric torn by perversity.
violence — the violent man who entices his neighbour
the violent man who entices/seduces his neighbour onto a bad path
the not-good way he leads to (263974)
welded to the evil way he draws his neighbour into
chamas (violence) — 'a man of VIOLENCE entices his neighbour'; the violent seduce others into evil. Violence is not solitary — it recruits.
not-good — the evil way the violent leads to
the way that is NOT good, into which the violent man leads his neighbour
welded to the violent man who draws him in
tob (good) NEGATED — 'leads him in a way that is NOT good'; the violent draw the neighbour into an evil course. Bad company corrupts by enticement.
plans — established when committed to the LORD
the one who commits his work
the plans/purposes that are established and made firm when one's work is rolled onto the LORD
the purposes secured by entrusting them to God

machashabah (plan/purpose) — 'commit your work to the LORD, and your PLANS will be established'; purposes are made firm not by anxious self-effort but by entrusting them to God. Rolling one's work on the LORD steadies the plan.
scheming — the winker plots perverse things
the plotting/devising of perverse things by the one who winks his eyes
welded to the perversity he devises
chashab (devise/plot) — 'whoever winks his eyes PLANS dishonest things'; the sly gesture (the wink) betrays the inner scheming of perversity. The body signals the plotting heart.
perversity — the schemes the winker plots
the perverse/dishonest things that the winking schemer devises
welded to the scheming that produces them
tahpukoth (perversity) — 'plans DISHONEST things'; the perverse schemes of the sly. Perversity signalled by the wink, worked out in the heart.
evil — brought to pass by the lip-purser
the evil that the one who purses his lips brings to pass
the evil accomplished by the scheming signaller
ra (evil) — 'he who purses his lips brings EVIL to pass'; the completed mischief. The gestures (wink, pursed lips) are the outward marks of an inner resolve on evil.
righteousness — the way to the crown of gray hair
the righteousness by which the crown of gray hair (long life, honour) is attained
the righteous life that earns honoured old age
tsedaqah (righteousness) — 'gray hair is a crown of glory; it is gained in a RIGHTEOUS life'; honoured old age is the reward of righteous living. Long life crowns the righteous.
patience — better than the mighty warrior
the slowness-to-anger/patience that is better than a mighty warrior
welded to the worth that exceeds might
aph (anger) in 'slow to ANGER' (erek appayim) — 'whoever is SLOW TO ANGER is better than the mighty'; self-control over one's temper outranks military might. The greatest conquest is of oneself.
evaluation — self-mastery outranks might and conquest
the judgement that patience and self-rule are better than might and city-taking
welded to the self-control it exalts
tob (better) — 'is BETTER than the mighty'; the value-scale that ranks inner mastery above outward power. To rule oneself is the higher victory.
the ruling/governing of one's own spirit, better than taking a city
welded to the inner self he governs

mashal (rule/govern) — 'he who RULES his spirit than he who takes a city'; self-government is a greater conquest than capturing a city. Emergent: self-rule as the supreme mastery — the hardest and highest dominion.
the spirit — governed by the self-mastered
the spirit/inner self that the wise man rules and governs
welded to the ruling that masters it
ruach (spirit) — 'rules his SPIRIT'; the inner self that must be governed. The domain of the greatest conquest is one's own spirit.
providence — the lot's every decision is from the LORD
the one who casts the lot
the decision/outcome of the cast lot, which is wholly from the LORD
the divine decision behind apparent chance

mishpat (decision/judgement) — 'the lot is cast into the lap, but its every DECISION is from the LORD'; even what seems chance is God's decision. Divine sovereignty reaches into the roll of the dice. The read holds the human act (casting) under the divine outcome.
wickedness — made for the day of trouble
the wicked whom God has appointed for the day of doom
welded to the doom appointed for them
rasha — 'even the WICKED for the day of trouble'; even the wicked serve God's purposes, appointed to the day of judgement. Divine sovereignty reaches even over evil.
doom — the day of trouble appointed for the wicked
the day of trouble/doom for which the wicked are appointed
welded to the wicked destined for it
ra (evil/trouble/doom) — 'for the day of TROUBLE'; the appointed day of the wicked's judgement. Even evil is bounded by God's purpose.
arrogance — the high-hearted, an abomination to God
the arrogance of heart (the high, lofty heart) that God detests
God's abomination of it (264023) / his heart (264022)
welded to the divine revulsion his pride draws

gaboah (high/lofty) — 'everyone who is ARROGANT in heart is an abomination to the LORD'; the proud-hearted are detestable to God and will not escape. Pride is the root vice God most abhors. The ABOMINATION (toebah) is the qualifier.
the heart — arrogant, high, abominable to God
the high, lofty heart in which arrogance is seated
welded to the pride that lifts it up
leb (heart) — 'arrogant in HEART'; pride is a condition of the heart itself, the inner loftiness God detests. The proud heart is the seat of the abomination.
steadfast love — by which iniquity is atoned
the steadfast love (loyal covenant-love) by which iniquity is covered/atoned
welded to faithfulness as the atoning pair

chesed (steadfast love) — 'by STEADFAST LOVE and faithfulness iniquity is atoned for'; loyal love and truth cover sin. The read holds the moral-relational way of atonement — chesed and emet make guilt-covering possible.
faithfulness — by which iniquity is atoned
the faithfulness/truth that, with steadfast love, atones for iniquity
welded to steadfast love as the atoning pair
emet (faithfulness/truth) — 'and FAITHFULNESS'; paired with chesed as the means by which iniquity is covered. Loyal truth atones.
iniquity — atoned for by love and faithfulness
the iniquity/guilt that steadfast love and faithfulness cover and atone for
welded to the atoning that covers it
avon (iniquity/guilt) — 'INIQUITY is atoned for'; the guilt that chesed and emet cover. Sin is real but coverable.
atonement — iniquity covered by love and faithfulness
the atoning/covering of iniquity that steadfast love and faithfulness effect
welded to the guilt it atones
kaphar (cover/atone) — 'is ATONED for'; the covering of guilt. Emergent: atonement as the covering of iniquity that loyal love and truth make possible.
fear of the LORD — by which one turns from evil
the fear of the LORD by which a man turns away from evil
welded to the aversion to evil it works
yirah (fear) — 'by the FEAR of the LORD one turns away from evil'; reverence is the power that turns men from evil. Fear of God and departure from evil go together.
turning-from-evil — by the fear of the LORD
the turning-away from evil that the fear of the LORD produces
welded to the reverence that works it
sur (turn aside/away) — 'one TURNS AWAY from evil'; the fear of God issues in departure from evil (cf 3:7; 14:16). Emergent: turning-from-evil as reverence's fruit.
pleasing God — the man whose ways please the LORD
the man whose ways please and win the favour of the LORD
the God-pleasing life that even disarms enemies

ratsah (be pleased with/accept) — 'when a man's ways PLEASE the LORD'; a life that pleases God draws such favour that even enemies are made peaceable. Emergent: pleasing God as the disposition that wins peace, even from foes.
evaluation — a little with righteousness beats great unjust revenue
the judgement that little with righteousness outweighs great revenues with injustice
the righteousness that makes it better (264047)
welded to the righteousness that outweighs wealth
tob (better) — 'BETTER is a little with righteousness than great revenues with injustice' (cf 15:16); righteousness with little beats wealth with wrong. The value-scale of the wise.
righteousness — worth more than unjust revenues
the righteousness that makes a little better than great unjust gain
welded to the worth it gives the little
tsedaqah (righteousness) — 'a little with RIGHTEOUSNESS'; righteousness is the true wealth, outweighing any amount of unjust revenue.
the heart — man's, which plans his way
the human heart that plans and devises its own way, which yet God directs
welded to the devising it performs
leb (heart) — 'the HEART of man plans his way'; man's heart devises the course, but the LORD directs the actual steps. Human planning under divine direction.
planning — the heart devises its way
the planning/devising by which the human heart maps its own way
welded to the heart whose devising it is
chashab (think/devise/plan) — 'the heart of man PLANS his way'; the mind maps its course, yet the LORD establishes the steps. Man proposes; God disposes.
evaluation — a dry morsel with peace beats a feast with strife
the judgement that a dry crust with quiet is better than a house of feasting with strife
the strife that spoils the feast (264068)
welded to the strife that makes abundance bitter
tob (better) — 'BETTER is a dry morsel with quiet than a house full of feasting with strife'; peace with little beats plenty with conflict. Quiet is worth more than a laden table (cf 15:17).
strife — which spoils a house of feasting
the strife/contention that turns a house of feasting bitter
the peace it is set against (264060)
set against the quiet that makes a poor meal good
rib (strife/contention) — 'a house full of feasting with STRIFE'; conflict sours abundance. The strife-filled feast is worse than the peaceful crust.
discernment — into whom a rebuke sinks deep
the man of understanding into whom a single rebuke sinks deeper than a hundred blows into a fool
set against the fool unmoved by blows
bin (understand/discern) — 'a rebuke goes deeper into a man of UNDERSTANDING'; the discerning feel a word more than the fool feels a beating. Teachability is a tender conscience — a word suffices.
folly — unmoved even by a hundred blows
the fool whom even a hundred blows do not reach, where a word pierces the wise
set against the discerning pierced by a word
kesil (fool) — 'than a hundred blows into a FOOL'; folly is thick-skinned, unreached even by beating. The fool's dullness is impervious where the wise are pierced by a word.
the evil man whose whole aim is rebellion
welded to the rebellion he pursues
ra (evil) — 'an EVIL man seeks only rebellion'; the evildoer is bent on rebellion (against authority, against God). Rebellion is his single pursuit.
seeking — the evil man pursues rebellion
the seeking/pursuit of rebellion that consumes the evil man
welded to the rebellion that is his aim
baqash (seek) — 'SEEKS only rebellion'; the evil man's desire is fixed on rebellion. What one seeks reveals the heart.
rebellion — the evil man's sole aim
the rebellion/defiance that is the evil man's only pursuit
welded to the seeking that is bent on it
meri (rebellion/defiance) — 'seeks only REBELLION'; defiant rebellion as the evil man's aim, which brings a cruel messenger of judgement. Emergent: rebellion as the settled bent of the evil will.
cruelty — the ruthless messenger sent against the rebel
the cruel/ruthless messenger (of judgement) sent against the rebel
the ruthless agent of judgement the rebel draws
akzari (cruel/ruthless) — 'a CRUEL messenger will be sent against him'; the rebel's defiance draws a merciless agent of judgement. Rebellion invites ruthless recompense.
folly — more dangerous than a robbed bear
the fool in his folly, more to be feared than a she-bear robbed of her cubs
welded to the folly that makes him fearsome
kesil (fool) — 'rather than a FOOL in his folly'; a fool bent on folly is more dangerous than an enraged bear. Folly unleashed is a terror.
folly — the raging state that makes a fool fearsome
the folly (raging, unrestrained) that makes meeting a fool worse than meeting a bereaved bear
welded to the fool it makes fearsome
ivveleth (folly) — 'a fool in his FOLLY'; folly in full spate is more perilous than a wild beast. Unreasoning folly cannot be reasoned with.
the returning of evil for good — the black ingratitude that repays kindness with harm
welded to the abiding evil it summons
ra (evil) — 'if anyone returns EVIL for good'; to repay kindness with harm is the depth of ingratitude, and it curses one's own house. The read holds the moral gravity of returning evil for good.
abiding curse — evil will not leave the ingrate's house
the evil that will not depart from the house of the one who returns evil for good
welded to the evil-for-good that brings it
ra (evil) — 'EVIL will not depart from his house'; the ingrate's house is haunted by abiding evil. Returning evil for good sows a lasting curse.
strife — whose beginning is a breach in a dam
the strife whose very beginning is like a breach through which water bursts uncontrollably
welded to the bursting quarrel it grows into
madon (strife) — 'the beginning of STRIFE is like letting out water'; once begun, strife bursts its banks like water through a breach — uncontrollable. Better never to start.
quarrel — to be quit before it bursts out
the quarrel that one must abandon before it breaks out and floods
the strife whose beginning it is (264101)
welded to the strife that swells into it
rib (quarrel/contention) — 'quit before the QUARREL breaks out'; wisdom abandons a dispute before it bursts. Once the dam breaks, it cannot be stopped.
the wrongful justifying/acquitting of the wicked, a perversion of justice
welded to the wickedness it wrongly clears
tsadeq (justify/declare righteous, Hiphil) — 'he who JUSTIFIES the wicked'; to acquit the guilty is to pervert justice, an abomination to God. Injustice inverts right and wrong.
the wicked who are wrongly acquitted by the corrupt judge
rasha — 'justifies the WICKED'; the guilty wrongly cleared. Perverted justice lets wickedness stand.
the wrongful condemning/convicting of the righteous, a perversion of justice
welded to the innocence it wrongly convicts
rasha (Hiphil: condemn/declare guilty) — 'he who CONDEMNS the righteous'; to convict the innocent is the mirror injustice, equally abominable. Both pervert the truth.
the righteous who are wrongly convicted by the corrupt judge
tsaddiq — 'condemns the RIGHTEOUS'; the innocent wrongly convicted. Injustice punishes the good.
divine abhorrence — both perversions of justice detestable to God
the LORD's abhorrence of both injustices — acquitting the guilty and condemning the innocent
the divine detestation of perverted justice

toebah (abomination) — 'both alike an ABOMINATION to the LORD'; God detests perverted justice in either direction. Justice is grounded in his character, and its perversion is loathsome to him. Locus external:god — the divine verdict on injustice.
folly — who cannot use wisdom though he could buy it
the fool who might have money to buy wisdom but, lacking sense, cannot use it
welded to the heartlessness that wastes the chance
kesil (fool) — 'why should a FOOL have money to buy wisdom?'; wisdom cannot be bought by one who has no heart to receive it. The fool wastes even the means to wisdom.
heartlessness — the fool has no sense to use wisdom
the lack of sense/heart that makes wisdom useless to the fool even if he could buy it
welded to the folly it leaves empty
leb (heart/sense) — 'when he has no SENSE'; without a heart to receive it, wisdom is useless — it cannot be bought like a commodity. The empty heart cannot hold wisdom.
faithful love — a friend loves at all times
the constant, faithful love of a friend, which does not fail in any season, and the brotherly love born for adversity
the steadfast love that holds through every time and trouble

aheb (love) — 'a friend LOVES at all times, and a brother is born for adversity'; the great word on faithful friendship — true love is constant, not fair-weather, and kinship-love is proven in trouble. Love that endures every season and rises in hardship.
imprudence — the senseless give rash surety
the lack of sense/heart shown by one who strikes hands in pledge and puts up security for a neighbour
the heartlessness that stakes itself on another's debt
leb (heart/sense) — 'one who LACKS sense gives a pledge'; rash surety is a mark of senselessness (cf 6:1-5; 11:15). The imprudent stake their own security on another's obligation.
the perverse love of transgression that is also a love of strife
welded to the sin it delights in
aheb (love) — 'whoever LOVES transgression loves strife'; to love sin is to love conflict — the two go together. Perverse affection fixed on transgression.
the transgression that the strife-lover delights in
the love that delights in it (264141)
welded to the perverse love that embraces it
pesha (transgression) — 'loves TRANSGRESSION'; the sin that the quarrelsome heart embraces. Love of sin and love of strife are one.
the love of strife that goes with loving transgression
welded to the conflict it delights in
aheb (love) — 'loves STRIFE'; the quarrelsome love conflict itself. To love transgression is to love the strife it breeds.
the strife/contention that the sin-lover delights in
welded to the perverse love of conflict
matstsah (strife) — 'loves STRIFE'; contention embraced. The heart that loves sin loves the conflict sin creates.
self-exaltation — raising one's gate, courting ruin
the self-exalting of one who 'makes his door high' — pride that courts destruction
welded to the ruin that pride invites
gabah (be high/exalt) — 'he who makes his door HIGH seeks destruction'; raising one's gate high (ostentatious pride) invites ruin. Self-exaltation courts the fall.
the seeking (all-but-deliberate) of destruction by the self-exalting
welded to the ruin it invites
baqash (seek) — 'SEEKS destruction'; the proud, by exalting himself, all but seeks his own ruin. Pride hunts its own downfall.
ruin — sought by the self-exalting proud
the destruction/ruin that the self-exalting proud invites upon himself
welded to the pride that seeks it
sheber (breaking/destruction) — 'seeks DESTRUCTION'; the ruin pride courts (cf 16:18). Emergent: destruction as the end the self-exalting invite.
prudence — the wise servant who rises to rule
the prudent, skilful dealing of a servant that lifts him to rule over a shameful son
his rule over the shameful son (264151)
welded to the ascendancy his wisdom earns

sakal (act wisely/prudently) — 'a servant who DEALS WISELY will rule over a son who acts shamefully'; character overturns birth — the wise servant rises above the shameful heir. Wisdom, not blood, ennobles.
dominion — the wise servant rules the shameful son
the rule/dominion the wise servant attains over the shameful heir
welded to the prudent dealing that earns it

mashal (rule/have dominion) — 'will RULE over a son who acts shamefully'; the wise servant's ascendancy, even sharing the inheritance. Emergent: rule as what wisdom wins, overturning the accident of birth.
shamefulness — the son whom the wise servant rules
the shameful conduct of the son who is ruled by the wise servant
set against the wise servant who rises above him
bosh (act shamefully) — 'a son who ACTS SHAMEFULLY'; the disgraceful heir, whose folly forfeits his place to the wise servant. Shameful conduct loses even a birthright.
the crooked heart — which finds no good
the crooked/twisted heart that discovers no good
the calamity the crooked tongue falls into (264166)
welded to the ruin that crookedness brings
leb (heart) with iqqesh (crooked) — 'a man of CROOKED heart does not discover good'; twistedness within blinds one to good and lands one in calamity. Inner crookedness has outer consequence.
calamity — into which the dishonest tongue falls
the calamity/evil into which one with a dishonest, turned tongue falls
the crooked heart that leads there (264159)
welded to the crookedness that ends there
ra (evil/calamity) — 'one with a dishonest tongue falls into CALAMITY'; the perverse tongue brings its owner to ruin. Crooked heart and dishonest tongue land in disaster.
folly — the fool who is his father's sorrow
the fool whose folly brings sorrow to the one who begets him
welded to the grief his folly causes
kesil (fool) — 'he who sires a FOOL gets himself sorrow'; a foolish child is a grief to the parent. Folly wounds those who love the fool.
grief — the father's, over a foolish child
the sorrow/grief that a fool brings on the one who begets him
welded to the folly that produces it
tugah (grief/sorrow) — 'gets himself SORROW'; the parental grief of raising a fool. A foolish child is a lasting sorrow.
joylessness — the father of a fool has no joy
the joy that is absent to the father of a fool
the gladness a foolish child denies his parent
samach (rejoice) NEGATED — 'the father of a fool has no JOY'; folly robs a parent of gladness. Where a wise child gives joy (10:1), a fool gives only grief.
joy — a glad heart that is good medicine
the joyful heart that works like good medicine on the body
welded to the glad heart it heals
sameach (joyful/glad) — 'a JOYFUL heart is good medicine'; inner gladness is bodily healing. The read holds the psychosomatic truth — joy heals, a crushed spirit withers.
the heart — joyful, good medicine to the body
the glad heart that is good medicine, healing the body
welded to the gladness that fills it
leb (heart) — 'a joyful HEART is good medicine'; the inner life governs the body's health. A glad heart is a healing thing.
healing — the joyful heart does the body good
the good/healing that a joyful heart works, like medicine, on the body
the bodily good that gladness brings
yatab (do good/make well) — 'is GOOD medicine'; the joyful heart 'makes well' — its healing effect on the body. Gladness as therapy.
the crushed spirit — which dries up the bones
the crushed/broken spirit that dries up and withers the very bones
set against the glad heart that is good medicine

ruach (spirit) — 'a crushed SPIRIT dries up the bones'; a broken spirit is a wasting sickness, withering the frame (cf 15:13; 18:14). The dark psychosomatic counterpart — inner brokenness as bodily decay.
the wicked who secretly takes a bribe to twist justice
welded to the justice his bribe corrupts
rasha — 'the WICKED accepts a bribe in secret'; the corrupt take bribes to pervert justice. Secret corruption twists the law.
the ways of justice that the wicked bribe-taker twists and perverts
welded to the corruption that bends it
mishpat (justice) — 'to pervert the ways of JUSTICE'; the justice the corrupt twist for a bribe. What God grounds in his character (17:15), the wicked bend for gain.
wisdom — on which the discerning fixes his face
the wisdom toward which the discerning sets his face, keeping it in view
the fool's roving eyes, by contrast (264193)
set against the fool whose gaze wanders
chokmah — 'the discerning sets his face toward WISDOM'; the wise keep wisdom before them, focused, where the fool's eyes rove to the ends of the earth. Focus vs distraction.
folly — whose eyes rove to the ends of the earth
the fool whose gaze wanders aimlessly to the ends of the earth, fixed on nothing
set against the discerning who fixes on wisdom
kesil (fool) — 'the eyes of a FOOL are on the ends of the earth'; folly is unfocused, its gaze wandering everywhere and settling nowhere. Distraction is folly's mark.
folly — the foolish son, grief and bitterness to his parents
the foolish son who is grief to his father and bitterness to his mother
the grief and bitterness he brings (264198)
welded to the pain his folly causes his parents
kesil (fool) — 'a FOOLISH son is a grief to his father'; folly wounds both parents (cf 10:1; 17:21). A foolish child is a double sorrow.
grief — the father's, over a foolish son
the grief/vexation that a foolish son brings his father
the foolish son who causes it (264196)
welded to the folly that produces it
kaas (grief/vexation) — 'a grief to his FATHER'; the father's vexation over a foolish child. Paired with the mother's bitterness.
bitterness — the mother's, over a foolish son
the bitterness that a foolish son brings to the mother who bore him
the mother's bitter sorrow over her foolish child
memer (bitterness) — 'bitterness to her who bore him'; the mother's bitter grief over a foolish son. Folly embitters even the womb that bore it.
the righteous man whom it is not good to fine/punish
welded to the injustice of punishing the good
tsaddiq — 'to impose a fine on a RIGHTEOUS man is not good'; to punish the innocent righteous is a wrong. Justice does not penalise goodness.
wrongness — punishing the righteous is not good
the not-good-ness of fining a righteous man or striking the noble
welded to the injustice it names
tob (good) NEGATED — 'is NOT good'; the moral wrong of punishing the righteous. Injustice against the good is condemned.
the noble/upright who are wrongly struck for the very uprightness they show
welded to the virtue for which they are wrongly punished
nadib (noble) — 'nor to strike the NOBLE for their uprightness'; to beat the upright for being upright is a double wrong. Virtue should not be punished.
uprightness — the virtue for which the noble are wrongly struck
the uprightness for which it is wrong to strike the noble
welded to the noble wrongly beaten for it
yosher (uprightness) — 'for their UPRIGHTNESS'; the very virtue that is wrongly punished. To beat a man for doing right inverts justice.
knowing — the one who restrains his words has knowledge
the knowledge possessed by the one who restrains and spares his words
welded to the knowledge his restraint reveals
yada (know/have knowledge) — 'whoever restrains his words HAS knowledge'; the one who spares his words shows he knows. Restraint of speech is a mark of knowledge.
knowledge — of the one who restrains his words
the knowledge that the word-restrainer possesses
welded to the restraint that reveals it
daath (knowledge) — 'has KNOWLEDGE'; the knowing behind restrained speech. The wise spare their words.
calmness — a cool spirit marks understanding
the cool/calm spirit that belongs to a man of understanding
welded to the discernment it marks
ruach (spirit) in 'COOL of spirit' (qar ruach) — 'he who has a cool spirit is a man of understanding'; a calm, unheated spirit is the mark of the discerning. Self-possession is understanding.
the understanding of the man who has a cool, calm spirit
welded to the calm spirit that reveals it
tebunah (understanding) — 'a man of UNDERSTANDING'; the discerning are cool-spirited, not easily heated. Calm and understanding go together.
folly — the fool who seems wise by silence
the fool who, by keeping silent, is even reckoned wise
welded to the silence that masks his folly
evil (fool) — 'even a FOOL who keeps silent is considered wise'; silence hides folly. The fool's best wisdom is to say nothing.
silence — the fool's, which passes for wisdom
the keeping-silent by which even a fool is reckoned wise
welded to the folly it conceals
charash (be silent/hold peace) — 'who keeps SILENT'; the silence that lends even a fool a reputation for wisdom. A shut mouth conceals an empty head.
being-reckoned — the silent fool is thought wise
the reckoning by which a silent fool is considered wise
the wisdom he is thought to have (264222)
welded to the reputation his silence lends
chashab (reckon/consider) — 'is CONSIDERED wise'; reputation follows silence — the quiet fool is credited with wisdom he lacks. Perception, not reality.
wisdom — the reputation silence lends the fool
the wisdom that the silent fool is credited with, though he lacks it
welded to the silence that earns the credit
chakam (wise) — 'is considered WISE'; the appearance of wisdom that silence gives even a fool. The read notes the irony — a shut mouth is taken for a full mind.
intelligence — the silent fool is deemed to have it
the intelligence the silent fool is deemed to possess when he closes his lips
the borrowed reputation for discernment silence gives
bin (understand/discern) — 'when he closes his lips, he is deemed INTELLIGENT'; even a fool seems discerning when silent. Wisdom is often the art of knowing when to shut up.
the heart — tested/assayed by the LORD
the heart that the LORD tests and assays, as fire tests silver and gold
the inner heart under the divine assay

leb (heart) — 'the LORD tests HEARTS'; as the crucible proves metal, God proves the heart. The inner life is assayed by God — its true worth revealed under his testing. The heart is the object of divine scrutiny (cf 15:11; 16:2; 21:2).
evildoing — who listens to wicked lips
the evildoer who attends and listens to wicked, iniquitous lips
welded to the attention he gives evil speech
raa (do evil) — 'an EVILDOER listens to wicked lips'; the wicked heed wicked speech. Like attracts like — you listen to what suits your heart.
heeding — the evildoer attends to wicked lips
the attentive listening/heeding that the evildoer gives to wicked speech
welded to the iniquitous speech he attends
qashab (attend/give heed) — 'LISTENS to wicked lips'; the evildoer's ear is tuned to evil. Attention reveals the heart's affinity.
iniquity — the wicked lips the evildoer heeds
the wicked, iniquitous lips that the evildoer listens to
welded to the attention they draw
aven (iniquity/wickedness) — 'listens to WICKED lips'; the iniquitous speech that the evildoer feeds on. Evil words find evil ears.
falseness — who gives ear to a mischievous tongue
the false/lying man who gives ear to a destructive, mischievous tongue
welded to the attention he gives destructive speech
sheqer (falsehood) — 'a LIAR gives ear to a mischievous tongue'; the false heed the malicious. Deceit listens to destruction. Character shapes what the ear welcomes.
heeding — the liar attends to a mischievous tongue
the giving-of-ear/heeding that the liar offers a destructive tongue
welded to the malice he attends
azan (give ear/listen) — 'gives EAR to a mischievous tongue'; the liar's ear is open to malice. What we welcome in others reveals us.
malice — the destructive tongue the liar heeds
the mischievous/destructive tongue that the liar gives ear to
welded to the attention it draws
havvah (mischief/destruction/craving) — 'a MISCHIEVOUS tongue'; the destructive, ruinous speech that the liar welcomes. Malice speaks and the false listen.
mockery — mocking the poor, which insults God
the mocking/derision of the poor that insults the poor man's Maker
welded to the reproach of God it constitutes
laag (mock/deride) — 'whoever MOCKS the poor insults his Maker'; to deride the poor is to reproach God who made him (cf 14:31). Contempt for the poor is contempt for their Creator.
reproach — mocking the poor reproaches God
the insulting/reproaching of God that mocking the poor amounts to
welded to the mockery that reproaches him
charaph (reproach/insult) — 'INSULTS his Maker'; the theology of the poor — they bear God's image, so to mock them is to insult God. Social scorn is blasphemy.
gloating — being glad at calamity, which is punished
the gladness/gloating at another's calamity that will not go unpunished
(the mockery of the poor beside it)
the malicious joy at disaster that draws punishment
sameach (glad) — 'he who is GLAD at calamity will not go unpunished'; gloating over another's disaster is a punishable malice. Joy at others' ruin condemns the gloater (cf 24:17).
fittingness — fine speech does not suit a fool
the unfittingness of eloquent/fine speech on a fool
welded to the folly it does not match
naveh (fitting/becoming) — 'fine speech is not BECOMING to a fool'; eloquence on a fool is a mismatch, as false speech is worse on a prince. Emergent: fittingness — character and speech must match.
folly — the boor whom fine speech ill-suits
the boorish fool on whom fine speech sits incongruously
welded to the mismatch it creates
nabal (fool/boor) — 'not becoming to a FOOL'; the coarse fool, on whom eloquence is absurd. Words reveal, and mismatch exposes.
falseness — lying speech, most unfit for a prince
the false, lying speech that is even more unfitting to a noble prince
welded to the nobility it disgraces
sheqer (falsehood) — 'still less is FALSE speech to a prince'; lying lips are most incongruous on a noble. High station demands truthful speech.
nobility — the noble, whom false speech most ill-suits
the noble/prince to whom lying speech is most unbecoming
welded to the lie that disgraces it
nadib (noble/generous) — 'false speech to a PRINCE'; the noble's dignity is disgraced by lying. Rank should mean truthfulness.
perceived power — the bribe seen as a magic charm
the charm/magic power the bribe seems to have in the eyes of the one who gives it
welded to the prospering it seems to guarantee

chen (grace/favour, here 'stone of favour/charm') — 'a bribe is like a MAGIC stone in the eyes of the one who gives it'; to the briber, his bribe seems a magic charm opening every door. The read notes this is the *giver's* view — the cynical faith in bribery's power, observed, not endorsed.
apparent success — the briber seems to prosper everywhere
the apparent success the briber imagines — that wherever he turns his bribe prospers him
welded to the magic power he ascribes to it

sakal (prosper/succeed/act shrewdly) — 'wherever he turns he PROSPERS'; the briber's belief that his bribe makes him succeed everywhere. The read holds the irony — the world's confidence in corruption, which God abhors (17:15, 23).
the offence — covered by love, or repeated to divide
the offence/transgression that one either covers (seeking love) or repeats (dividing friends)
welded to the love that overlooking it fosters
pesha (offence/transgression) — 'whoever covers an OFFENCE seeks love'; the wrong that love overlooks. To cover an offence is to seek relationship; to broadcast it is to destroy it.
love-seeking — covering an offence fosters love
the seeking-of-love by which one covers rather than repeats an offence
welded to the love it fosters
baqash (seek) — 'covers an offence SEEKS love'; forgiveness is love-seeking. To overlook a wrong is to pursue relationship, against the gossip who divides.
love — sought by covering an offence
the love that is sought and fostered by covering an offence
welded to the seeking that fosters it
ahabah (love) — 'seeks LOVE'; the love that forgiveness pursues (cf 10:12). Covering wrong builds love; repeating it destroys friendship.
self-seeking — the isolated pursue their own desire
the self-seeking pursuit of one's own desire that drives a man to isolate himself
welded to the private desire that isolates him
baqash (seek) — 'whoever isolates himself SEEKS his own desire'; the one who cuts himself off does so to pursue his private craving. Isolation as self-will.
desire — the private craving that drives isolation
the private desire/craving that the self-isolating man pursues, cut off from others
welded to the self-seeking that chases it
taavah (desire) — 'seeks his own DESIRE'; the self-isolating chase their private craving. Individualism serving self-will, not counsel.
sound wisdom — which the self-isolating defies
the sound wisdom/judgment against which the self-isolating man rages and breaks out
the wise counsel the self-seeker rejects
tushiyah (sound wisdom/judgment) — 'he breaks out against all SOUND JUDGMENT'; the self-isolating defies all wise counsel, quarrelling with wisdom itself. Self-will versus sound sense.
refuge — the LORD's name a strong tower
the name of the LORD as a strong tower, the true refuge into which the righteous run
welded to the strength of the divine refuge

shem (name) — 'the NAME of the LORD is a strong tower'; God's revealed character/presence is the real refuge (contrast the rich man's imagined fortress, 18:11). Locus external:god — the divine name to which the righteous flee for safety.
strength — the fortress-strength of the LORD's name
the strength/security of the LORD's name, a strong tower for the righteous
the name whose strength it is (264280)
welded to the divine name it fortifies
oz (strength) — 'a STRONG tower'; the real, unassailable strength of God's name, into which the righteous run and are set safe on high.
righteousness — who runs to the LORD's name and is safe
the righteous who runs into the strong tower of the LORD's name and is set safe
the righteous who takes refuge in God's name
tsaddiq — 'the RIGHTEOUS runs into it and is safe'; the righteous flee to God's name as a refuge — an act of trust, the true security (contrast trusting wealth). Character runs to God.
riches — the rich man's imagined fortress
the rich man who treats his wealth as a strong city, a fortress of the imagination
welded to the wealth he trusts as a wall

ashir (rich) — 'a RICH man's wealth is his strong city'; the rich lean on riches as a fortress — but only 'in his imagination' (contrast God's name, the real tower). Emergent: the rich man's false, imagined security in wealth.
wealth — the rich man's imagined stronghold
the wealth that the rich man imagines to be a high, protecting wall
welded to the false security it seems to give
hon (wealth) — 'his strong city, like a high wall in his imagination'; wealth as a felt but false fortress. Emergent: the illusory refuge of riches, standing only in the mind.
false security — the imagined strength of wealth
the strength/security the rich man imagines his wealth to give — a high wall only in his mind
welded to the wealth whose strength is imagined

oz (strength) — 'a high wall in his IMAGINATION'; the same word for the real strength of God's name (18:10) here of the imagined strength of wealth. The read holds the deliberate contrast — one refuge is real, one only fancied.
ruin — which a haughty heart precedes
the destruction that a man's haughty heart goes before
the haughty heart that precedes it (264299)
welded to the pride that ushers it in
sheber (destruction) — 'before DESTRUCTION a man's heart is haughty'; pride of heart is the herald of ruin (cf 16:18). Emergent: destruction as the sequel to a haughty heart.
the heart that is haughty/lifted up before destruction
welded to the pride that lifts it
leb (heart) — 'a man's HEART is haughty' before ruin; pride is a condition of the heart itself, the inner loftiness that precedes the fall.
haughtiness — the high heart before destruction
the haughtiness/lifting-up of the heart that precedes destruction
welded to the heart it exalts
gabah (be high/haughty) — 'is HAUGHTY'; the heart's self-exaltation before the fall. The higher the pride, the harder the ruin.
the humility that precedes and prepares the way for honour
welded to the honour it goes before
anavah (humility) — 'HUMILITY comes before honour' (cf 15:33); the lowly road leads up. The order is fixed — down before up, humility before honour.
the honour that follows and crowns humility
welded to the humility that leads to it
kabod (honour) — 'humility comes before HONOUR'; honour is reached by humility, as ruin by pride. The two ways diverge from the heart's posture.
the failure to hear before answering — replying before one has listened
welded to the folly of the unheard answer
shama (hear) — 'if one gives an answer before he HEARS'; to answer before listening is the mark of the hasty. The virtue of hearing fully first is implied by its absence.
the folly of the one who answers a matter before he has heard it
the premature answering that shows it (264306)
welded to the hasty reply that reveals it
ivveleth (folly) — 'it is his FOLLY and shame'; answering unheard is folly. Wisdom listens before it speaks.
the shame/disgrace that comes of answering before one has heard
the disgrace of the premature answer
kelimmah (shame/disgrace) — 'his folly and SHAME'; hasty answering brings not only folly but public shame. To speak before listening exposes the speaker.
understanding — the discerning heart acquires knowledge
the intelligent/discerning heart that actively acquires knowledge
welded to the heart that gains knowledge
bin (understand/discern) — 'an INTELLIGENT heart acquires knowledge'; the discerning heart is always gaining — never full, ever acquiring. Wisdom has an appetite.
the discerning heart that acquires and stores knowledge
welded to the discernment that gathers
leb (heart) — 'an intelligent HEART acquires knowledge'; the heart as the gatherer of knowledge. The wise heart is an active acquirer.
knowledge — acquired by the intelligent heart
the knowledge that the intelligent heart acquires and the wise ear seeks
the knowledge the wise are always gathering
daath (knowledge) — 'acquires KNOWLEDGE'; the prize the discerning heart gathers and the wise ear seeks. Never enough for the wise.
the wise whose very ear seeks and hunts for knowledge
welded to the ear that hunts knowledge
chakam (wise) — 'the ear of the WISE seeks knowledge'; wisdom's ear is tuned to seek knowledge. The wise are listeners, always learning.
seeking — the wise ear hunts for knowledge
the seeking/hunting for knowledge by the ear of the wise
welded to the knowledge it pursues
baqash (seek) — 'the ear of the wise SEEKS knowledge'; the wise actively pursue knowledge with their ears. Learning is an appetite, not a chore.
knowledge — sought by the wise ear
the knowledge that the wise ear actively seeks
welded to the wise ear that hunts it
daath (knowledge) — 'the ear of the wise seeks KNOWLEDGE'; the object of the wise ear's hunger. The wise never stop seeking.
the plea — the first-stated argument that seems right
the case/argument that the first to speak lays out, which seems right until challenged
welded to the plausibility of the first plea
rib (case/dispute) — 'the one who states his CASE first seems right'; the first plea sounds convincing — until cross-examined. The read commends hearing both sides.
apparent rightness — the first speaker seems right till examined
the seeming-rightness of the one who speaks first, which lasts only until the other examines him
welded to the first plea whose plausibility it is

tsaddiq (righteous/right) — 'SEEMS right, until the other comes and examines him'; the plausibility of the first account, which cross-examination undoes. Wisdom suspends judgement until both are heard.
the quarrels/contentions that the cast lot brings to an end
welded to the powerful whose dispute it decides
midyan (quarrel/contention) — 'the lot puts an end to QUARRELS'; even the disputes of the powerful are settled by the lot (whose outcome is God's, 16:33). Contention resolved by an impartial means.
the mighty — powerful disputants the lot separates
the mighty/powerful contenders between whom the lot decides
welded to the contention it resolves

atsum (mighty/strong) — 'decides between POWERFUL contenders'; the strong disputants whose quarrel needs an impartial lot to settle. Emergent: the mighty as those whose disputes require the lot to resolve.
estrangement — a brother offended, harder than a fortress
the offended/estranged brother who is more unyielding than a fortified city
welded to the strong city his hardness surpasses

pasha (transgress/rebel→be estranged) — 'a brother OFFENDED is more unyielding than a strong city'; wounded kinship hardens into an impregnable barrier. The offence of a close relation is the hardest of all to overcome.
strength — the fortress the offended brother surpasses
the fortress-strength of a strong city, which the hardness of an offended brother exceeds
welded to the estrangement harder than it
oz (strength) — 'than a STRONG city'; the fortified strength that an offended brother's hardness outdoes. Broken kinship is harder to breach than a citadel.
folly — who delights only in airing his own mind
the fool who has no delight in understanding but only in expressing his own opinion
welded to the self-airing he delights in
kesil (fool) — 'a FOOL takes no pleasure in understanding, but only in expressing his opinion'; folly loves the sound of its own mind, not the labour of understanding. Self-display over learning.
delight — the fool has none in understanding
the pleasure/delight that the fool does NOT take in understanding
set against the understanding he takes no joy in
chaphets (delight/take pleasure) NEGATED — 'a fool takes NO PLEASURE in understanding'; the fool finds no joy in the labour of understanding. Delight misdirected reveals the heart.
understanding — in which the fool takes no pleasure
the understanding that the fool slights, taking no pleasure in it
the pleasure he withholds from it (264340)
welded to the delight he denies it
tebunah (understanding) — 'no pleasure in UNDERSTANDING'; the understanding the fool has no appetite for. He prefers his own voice to learning.
self-opinion — the fool delights in airing his own mind
the fool's own mind/opinion (heart), in the airing of which alone he takes delight
welded to the folly that loves self-display
leb (heart/mind→opinion) — 'only in expressing his OPINION'; the fool delights to reveal his own heart/mind, to air his opinion, rather than to learn. Self-revelation as the fool's one pleasure.
life — and death, in the power of the tongue
the life (and death) that lie in the power of the tongue — speech can give life or deal death
the love of the tongue that reaps it (264352)
welded to those who love speech and eat its fruit

chayyim (life) — 'DEATH and LIFE are in the power of the tongue'; the tongue wields power over life and death — words heal or kill, bless or curse. Emergent: life (with death) as what the tongue's power decides. The climactic word on speech.
love of the tongue — those who love it eat its fruits
the talkative / those who love speech
the love of the tongue/speaking, whose lovers eat its fruits — life or death
welded to the tongue's power they reap
aheb (love) — 'those who LOVE it will eat its fruits'; those who love the tongue (love to talk) will reap what it sows — its life or its death. Love of speech carries its own harvest.
goodness — a wife is a good thing found
the good thing that finding a wife is — a genuine good
welded to the divine favour it signifies
tob (good) — 'he who finds a wife finds a GOOD thing'; a good wife is a genuine good, a gift. The read holds the affirmation of marriage as a good.
favour — obtained from the LORD in finding a wife
the favour from the LORD that comes with finding a good wife
welded to the goodness of the gift
ratson (favour) — 'obtains FAVOUR from the LORD'; a good wife is a mark of divine favour, a gift from God. Emergent: favour as what the finder of a good wife receives.
poverty — the poor, who must plead with entreaties
the poor man who must use entreaties/supplications, having no power to demand
welded to the pleading his poverty forces
rush (be poor) — 'the POOR use entreaties'; poverty reduces a man to pleading. The read notes the powerlessness of the poor, forced to beg where the rich command.
the entreaties/supplications the poor man must offer, having no other recourse
welded to the poverty that reduces him to pleading
tachanun (supplication/entreaty) — 'the poor use ENTREATIES'; humble pleading is the poor man's only power. The posture of the powerless.
riches — the rich, who answer roughly
the rich man who answers harshly/roughly, secure in his power
welded to the harshness his wealth affords
ashir (rich) — 'the RICH answer roughly'; wealth breeds a harsh, imperious manner. Emergent: the rich as those whose power makes them rough in reply, against the pleading poor.
harshness — the rich man's rough answer
the harsh, rough manner in which the rich man answers
welded to the wealth that emboldens it
az (strong/fierce/rough) — 'the rich answer ROUGHLY'; the harshness of the powerful. Wealth hardens the manner, where poverty softens it to pleading.
faithful friendship — a friend closer than a brother
the faithful friend who sticks closer than a brother, unlike shallow companions who bring ruin
(the many companions who fail, by contrast)
the steadfast love that outdoes even kinship

aheb (love/friend) — 'there is a FRIEND who sticks closer than a brother'; against a crowd of shallow companions (who bring ruin), one faithful friend, closer than kin. The depth of true friendship (cf 17:17). Love that cleaves.
wickedness — which brings contempt in its train
the wickedness that draws contempt after it
welded to the scorn that follows it
rasha (wickedness) — 'when WICKEDNESS comes, contempt comes also'; wickedness drags contempt and disgrace with it. Sin brings shame in its train.
welded to the wickedness that draws it
buz (contempt) — 'CONTEMPT comes also'; scorn attends the wicked. Wickedness earns the contempt of all who see it.
the dishonour/shame that comes with wickedness
welded to disgrace as the twin shame of wickedness
qalon (dishonour/shame) — 'with DISHONOUR comes disgrace'; shame accompanies the wicked. Sin's train is contempt, dishonour, and reproach.
disgrace — the reproach that comes with dishonour
the disgrace/reproach that comes with the dishonour attending wickedness
welded to dishonour as the twin shame
cherpah (reproach/disgrace) — 'comes DISGRACE'; reproach completes the cascade of shame that wickedness brings. Sin ends in disgrace.
wrongness — partiality to the wicked is not good
the not-good-ness of showing partiality to the wicked or wronging the righteous
welded to the injustice it names
tob (good) NEGATED — 'it is NOT good to be partial to the wicked'; favouritism to the guilty is a wrong. Justice must not be swayed by persons.
the wicked who are wrongly shown partiality in judgment
welded to the partiality that favours them
rasha — 'to be partial to the WICKED'; favouring the guilty perverts justice. The wicked wrongly lifted up.
the righteous who are wrongly deprived of justice by partiality
welded to the justice they are wrongly refused
tsaddiq — 'to deprive the RIGHTEOUS of justice'; to wrong the innocent is the flip side of favouring the guilty. Both pervert judgment.
justice — denied the righteous by partiality
the justice of which the righteous are wrongly deprived
welded to the righteous who are refused it
mishpat (justice) — 'deprive the righteous of JUSTICE'; the justice the innocent are wrongly denied. Partiality robs the righteous of their due.
folly — whose lips walk into a fight
the fool whose lips lead him into strife and invite a beating
welded to the conflict his lips court
kesil (fool) — 'a FOOL's lips walk into a fight'; the fool's speech drags him into conflict. His mouth is his undoing.
strife — into which the fool's lips walk
the fight/strife into which the fool's lips lead him
welded to the fool's lips that walk into it
rib (strife/quarrel) — 'a fool's lips walk into a FIGHT'; the conflict the fool's speech provokes. His words start fights he cannot win.
summoning — the fool's mouth invites a beating
the calling/inviting of a beating by the fool's own mouth
the fool's mouth that summons blows upon himself
qara (call/invite) — 'his mouth INVITES a beating'; the fool's speech calls down blows on his own head. His mouth summons his own punishment.
ruin — the fool's mouth destroys him
the ruin that the fool's own mouth brings upon him
welded to the soul his lips trap
mechittah (ruin) — 'a fool's mouth is his RUIN'; the fool's speech is his destruction. What he says undoes him.
the soul — snared by the fool's own lips
the soul/self that the fool's own lips ensnare and trap
welded to the mouth that destroys it
nephesh (soul/self) — 'his lips are a snare to his SOUL'; the fool traps his own life with his lips. Self-ensnaring speech.
negligent sloth — the slack worker as kin to a destroyer
the being slack in one's work — the negligent laziness that, by leaving things undone and neglected, is as ruinous as active destruction, sloth and sabotage reaching the same end
the negligence that wastes and ruins as surely as deliberate destruction

raphah (be slack/let drop) — 'whoever is SLACK in his work is a brother to him who destroys' (18:9); negligence ruins as surely as malice. The one who lets his work fall apart is kin to the one who tears it down. Sloth is a quiet destroyer.
the judgement that a poor man who walks in integrity is better than a crooked-tongued fool
the integrity that makes him better (264414)
welded to the integrity that outweighs wealth-with-folly

tob (better) — 'BETTER is a poor person who walks in his integrity than one who is crooked in speech and is a fool'; integrity-with-poverty beats crookedness-with-folly. Character over circumstance (cf 28:6).
