integrity — the poor man's blameless walk
the integrity/blamelessness in which the poor man walks, worth more than crooked folly
welded to the value his blamelessness confers
tom (integrity) — 'a poor person who walks in his INTEGRITY'; blameless walk is worth more than any crookedness. Integrity ennobles poverty.
folly — the crooked-tongued fool, worse than an honest poor man
the fool who is crooked in speech, worse off than a poor man of integrity
(the poor man of integrity, by contrast)
set against the blameless poor man
kesil (fool) — 'than one who is crooked in speech and is a FOOL'; crooked folly is worse than honest poverty. The crooked fool, though perhaps richer, is the lesser man.
unfittingness — luxury does not suit a fool
the unfittingness of luxury/delight for a fool, a thing out of its proper order
welded to the delight that ill-fits folly

naveh (fitting/becoming) — 'it is not FITTING for a fool to live in luxury'; luxury on a fool is incongruous, an inversion of the right order. Emergent: fittingness — things should sit with their proper owners (cf 17:7; 26:1).
folly — the fool for whom luxury is unfit
the fool for whom living in luxury is unbecoming and incongruous
set against the luxury that does not fit folly
kesil (fool) — 'not fitting for a FOOL to live in luxury'; the fool who, having no wisdom to use it well, is ill-matched to luxury. Prosperity wasted on folly.
luxury — the delight that ill-suits a fool
the luxury/delight that sits incongruously on a fool
welded to the folly it ill-matches
taanug (luxury/delight/pleasure) — 'to live in LUXURY'; the delight and ease that ill-fit a fool. Emergent: luxury as a good misplaced when given to folly.
dominion — ruling princes ill-suits a slave (misplaced order)
the ruling/dominion over princes that even more incongruously ill-suits a slave
the inverted order of a slave ruling nobles

mashal (rule/have dominion) — 'much less for a SLAVE to rule over princes'; a slave ruling nobles is a yet greater inversion of order than luxury for a fool. Emergent: rule misplaced — authority in the wrong hands overturns the proper order (cf 30:22).
prudence — which makes a man slow to anger
the good sense/prudence that makes a man slow to anger and able to overlook offence
welded to the slowness-to-anger it gives
sekel (good sense/prudence) — 'GOOD SENSE makes one slow to anger'; prudence produces patience. The wise are not quickly provoked.
patience — the fruit of good sense
the slowness-to-anger/patience that good sense produces in a man
the good sense that produces it (264427)
welded to the prudence that yields it
arak (be long/slow) — 'makes one SLOW to anger'; patience, the fruit of prudence. Emergent: slowness-to-anger as the temper that good sense creates.
forbearance — the glory of passing over an offence
the overlooking/passing-over of an offence, which is a man's glory
the glory of forbearance that ignores a wrong

pesha (offence/transgression) — 'it is his GLORY to overlook an offence'; to pass over a wrong is not weakness but glory (cf 12:16; 17:9). Forbearance is honour, not shame — a magnanimity that adorns the wise.
wrath — a king's, terrible as a lion's growl
the wrath of a king, fearsome as the growling of a lion
welded to the terrifying roar it is likened to
zaaph (wrath/rage) — 'a king's WRATH is like the growling of a lion'; royal anger is a terror. The read holds the danger of provoking power (cf 16:14; 20:2).
menace — the lion's growl of royal wrath
the growling/roaring, like a lion's, to which a king's wrath is likened
welded to the royal anger it pictures
naham (growl/roar) — 'like the GROWLING of a lion'; the low, deadly roar of royal wrath. Emergent: the growl as the image of dangerous, imminent anger.
favour — a king's, refreshing as dew
the favour of a king, refreshing and life-giving as dew on the grass
the royal favour set against the lion-roar of wrath
ratson (favour) — 'his FAVOUR is like dew on the grass'; royal favour is as refreshing as wrath is fearsome. Emergent: favour as the reviving dew, against the growl of wrath. The two faces of power.
folly — the foolish son, ruin to his father
the foolish son who is ruin/calamity to his father
welded to the calamity his folly causes
kesil (fool) — 'a FOOLISH son is ruin to his father'; folly wrecks the parent (cf 17:21, 25). A foolish child is a domestic disaster.
ruin — the calamity a foolish son brings
the ruin/calamity that a foolish son brings on his father
the foolish son who causes it (264442)
welded to the folly that produces it
havvah (ruin/calamity) — 'is RUIN to his father'; the disaster a foolish child works on the home.
contention — a wife's quarreling, a wearying drip
the wife's quarreling/contention, wearying as a roof that drips without ceasing
(the foolish son, the other domestic grief)
the endless nagging that wears like constant dripping
midyan (quarrel/contention) — 'a wife's QUARRELING is a continual dripping of rain'; incessant nagging wears a man down like a leaky roof (cf 27:15). Domestic contention as slow, relentless erosion.
the house and wealth that a man inherits from his fathers, unlike a prudent wife
the prudent wife from God, by contrast (264454)
set against the God-given prudent wife
hon (wealth) — 'house and WEALTH are inherited from fathers'; material inheritance comes from parents. Emergent: inherited wealth, set against the higher gift of a wise wife.
prudence — the wise wife, a gift from the LORD
the prudent/wise wife who is a gift from the LORD, above any inheritance
the mere wealth inherited, by contrast (264451)
set against the house and wealth from fathers
sakal (act prudently/wise) — 'a PRUDENT wife is from the LORD'; a wise wife is not inherited but given by God — a higher gift than any wealth. The read exalts a good wife as a divine gift.
sloth — which casts a man into torpor and hunger
the slothfulness that casts a man into a deep sleep/torpor, and leaves him hungry
welded to the idle hunger it induces
atslah (slothfulness) — 'SLOTHFULNESS casts into a deep sleep'; laziness is a stupor that ends in hunger. Emergent: sloth as a torpor that starves its owner.
the idle soul — which suffers hunger
the idle person/soul that suffers hunger through slothfulness
welded to the slothfulness that leaves it hungry
nephesh (soul/person) — 'an idle PERSON will suffer hunger'; the slothful soul goes unfed. Idleness is self-starvation.
the keeping/guarding of the commandment that preserves one's life
the obedience that guards the soul
shamar (keep/guard) — 'whoever KEEPS the commandment keeps his life'; obedience to the commandment is self-preservation. To guard God's word is to guard one's soul.
preserving — keeping the commandment keeps one's life
the keeping/preserving of one's own life that comes of keeping the commandment
welded to the life obedience guards
shamar (keep/guard) — 'keeps his LIFE'; the second 'keep' — obedience preserves the soul. What guards the commandment guards the man.
the life — preserved by keeping the commandment
the life/soul that keeping the commandment preserves
welded to the obedience that guards it
nephesh (life/soul) — 'keeps his LIFE'; the soul preserved by obedience, against the death of the one who despises his ways.
contempt — despising one's ways brings death
the despising of one's own ways (careless of conduct) that ends in death
(the keeper of the commandment, by contrast)
set against the one who keeps the commandment and lives
bazah (despise) — 'he who DESPISES his ways will die'; carelessness about one's conduct is fatal. To hold one's own way in contempt is to court death.
graciousness — kindness to the poor, a loan to the LORD
the gracious generosity to the poor that is reckoned as lending to the LORD himself, who will repay
the kindness to the poor that God himself takes as a loan

chanan (be gracious/show favour) — 'whoever is GENEROUS to the poor lends to the LORD, and he will repay'; the astonishing word — kindness to the poor is a loan to God, who repays it. Mercy to the needy is credited to God's own account (cf 14:31; 22:9). Generosity as faith in God's repayment.
hope — the ground for disciplining a son
the hope that makes disciplining a son worthwhile — there is yet hope while he is young
the hope that grounds correction while it can still avail
tiqvah (hope) — 'discipline your son, for there is HOPE'; correction is grounded in hope — while there is hope, discipline can save. Emergent: hope as the reason to correct, before it is too late.
the heart — not to be set on the son's destruction
the parent's own soul/desire, which must not be set on causing the son's death (through unrestrained anger)
the destructive impulse it must not indulge (264487)
welded to the fatal intent it must refuse
nephesh (soul/heart→desire) — 'do not set your HEART on putting him to death'; discipline must not become destructive rage. The parent's heart must aim at correction, not the child's ruin.
destructive intent — the impulse to ruin the son, to be refused
the destructive impulse (setting oneself on the son's death) that discipline must never become
the heart that must not indulge it (264486)
welded to the parental heart it warns

nasa (lift/carry→set oneself on) — 'do not set your heart on PUTTING him to death'; the warning against discipline that hardens into a wish for the child's destruction. Emergent: the fatal, over-angry intent that correction must never harbour. Discipline in hope, not in rage.
hot temper — the man of great wrath, ever paying the penalty
the great wrath/hot temper of a man who repeatedly incurs penalty, and cannot be rescued once for all
the ungoverned rage that keeps landing its owner in trouble

chemah (wrath/hot anger) — 'a man of great WRATH will pay the penalty'; the incorrigibly angry keep incurring trouble — rescue them once and they need it again. Ungoverned temper is a recurring debt. Character must change, not just consequences be paid.
knowledge — whose absence makes desire dangerous
the knowledge without which desire/zeal is not good
welded to the danger of zeal without knowledge
daath (knowledge) — 'DESIRE without knowledge is not good'; zeal or desire uninformed by knowledge is dangerous. The read notes that eagerness needs the guidance of knowledge.
wrongness — desire without knowledge is not good
the not-good-ness of desire/zeal that lacks knowledge
welded to the missing knowledge that would make it good
tob (good) NEGATED — 'is NOT good'; uninformed zeal misfires. Desire without knowledge, like haste without care, goes wrong.
erring — hasty feet miss the way
the missing-the-way/erring of one who makes haste with his feet
the haste that overshoots and misses the mark
chata (miss/sin) — 'whoever makes haste with his feet MISSES his way'; haste, like ignorant zeal, misses the mark. To hurry without knowledge is to go astray.
heeding — listening to advice to grow wise
the listening to advice and accepting of instruction that leads to future wisdom
welded to the counsel it receives
shama (hear/heed) — 'LISTEN to advice and accept instruction, that you may gain wisdom'; heeding counsel now yields wisdom later. Teachability compounds over time.
counsel — to be heeded for future wisdom
the advice/counsel that, heeded, brings future wisdom
welded to the heeding that receives it
etsah (counsel/advice) — 'listen to ADVICE'; the counsel that grows the wise. Wisdom is gained by receiving advice over time.
plans — man's many, which God overrules
the many plans/purposes in the mind of a man, which yet yield to the LORD's purpose
welded to the human heart where they arise
machashabah (plan/purpose) — 'MANY are the plans in the mind of a man'; the human heart teems with plans, but they bow to God's purpose (cf 16:1, 9). Man's planning under divine sovereignty.
the mind — where man's many plans arise
the mind/heart of a man in which many plans form, though God's purpose prevails
welded to the plans that arise in it
leb (heart/mind) — 'in the MIND of a man'; the inner seat of human planning, teeming with purposes that finally yield to God's.
divine purpose — the LORD's counsel, which alone stands
the purpose/counsel of the LORD that stands and prevails over all a man's plans
set against the many plans of the human mind

etsah (counsel/purpose) — 'the PURPOSE of the LORD that will stand'; God's counsel prevails over man's many plans. Locus external:god — the sovereign divine purpose that overrules human planning. The great sovereignty saying.
desirableness — what is wanted in a man is loyalty
the desirableness of a man — what is truly wanted in him is steadfast love/loyalty
welded to the loyalty that makes a man desirable
taavah (desire/desirableness) — 'what is DESIRED in a man is steadfast love'; the truly attractive thing in a person is loyal kindness, not wealth or show. Character, not capacity, is what is wanted.
loyalty — the desirable trait in a man
the steadfast love/loyal kindness that is what is truly desired in a person
welded to the desire it satisfies

chesed (steadfast love/kindness) — 'is STEADFAST LOVE'; loyal kindness is the most desirable thing in a man. The read prizes chesed as the mark of a good person — and a poor honest man over a rich liar.
evaluation — a poor honest man beats a liar
the judgement that a poor man (of steadfast love) is better than a liar
(the steadfast love that makes him better)
tob (better) — 'a poor man is BETTER than a liar'; honesty in poverty beats deceit. The loyal poor man outranks the false one, whatever his means (cf 19:1).
fear of the LORD — which leads to life and rest
the fear of the LORD that leads to life, and lets a man rest satisfied, untouched by harm
the reverence that yields life, contentment, and safety

yirah (fear) — 'the fear of the LORD leads to LIFE, and whoever has it rests satisfied; he will not be visited by harm'; reverence gives life, contentment, and security. The read holds the threefold fruit — life, restful satisfaction, and safety — of the fear of God.
paralysing sloth — laziness too great even to lift food to the mouth

the sluggard who buries his hand in the dish and will not even bring it back to his mouth — sloth so total it will not complete the simplest act for its own benefit, laziness that starves rather than stir
the laziness that will not finish even the act of feeding itself

atsel (sluggard) — 'the SLUGGARD buries his hand in the dish and will not even bring it back to his mouth' (19:24; cf 26:15); sloth grown so absolute it will not lift food to feed itself. The lazy man would sooner starve than stir.
scorn — the scoffer, struck as a warning to the simple
the scoffer who, when struck, becomes a warning by which the simple learn prudence
(the simple who learn from his punishment)
the incorrigible scorner whose beating teaches others

luts (scoff) — 'strike a SCOFFER, and the simple will learn prudence'; the scoffer himself cannot be taught (cf 9:7-8), but his punishment warns the naive. The incorrigible serve as a lesson to others.
naivety — the simple who learn prudence from the scoffer's beating
the naive who grow wary/prudent by seeing the scoffer punished
welded to the wariness the example teaches
pethi (simple/naive) — 'the SIMPLE will learn prudence'; the naive learn caution from another's punishment. What the scoffer cannot learn for himself, the simple learn from his fate.
growing-wary — the simple made prudent by example
the learning of prudence/wariness by the simple, taught by the scoffer's beating
welded to the simpleness it corrects
aram (be prudent/shrewd) — 'will LEARN prudence'; the naive gain caution from seeing the scoffer struck. Correction of one teaches many.
understanding — who gains knowledge from a mere reproof
the man of understanding who, merely reproved, gains knowledge
welded to the growth a word gives him

bin (understand/discern) — 'reprove a man of UNDERSTANDING, and he will gain knowledge'; the wise need only a word, where the scoffer needs a blow and the simple an example. Teachability graded by character (cf 17:10).
discerning — the wise grows by a word of reproof
the gaining/discerning by which the understanding man grows from mere reproof
welded to the understanding it enriches
bin (discern/understand) — 'he will GAIN knowledge'; the wise grow from a word. Reproof enriches the understanding, where blows barely reach the scoffer.
knowledge — gained by the wise from reproof
the knowledge that the man of understanding gains from being reproved
welded to the discernment that grows by it
daath (knowledge) — 'gain KNOWLEDGE'; the wise man's harvest from a word of correction. A rebuke enriches the discerning.
the violence/ruin a son does to his own father, driving off his mother
welded to the disgrace such a son becomes
shadad (destroy/do violence) — 'he who does VIOLENCE to his father'; a son who assaults or ruins his parents. The read holds the depth of the offence — violence against those who gave one life.
shamefulness — the son who brings shame
the shame that such a son brings on himself and his family
welded to reproach as the twin disgrace
bosh (act shamefully/bring shame) — 'a son who brings SHAME'; violence against parents makes a son a disgrace. Shame is his character.
reproach — the disgrace such a son becomes
the reproach/disgrace that the parent-abusing son becomes
welded to shame as the twin disgrace
chapher (be ashamed/reproach) — 'and REPROACH'; the son who wrongs his parents is a byword of disgrace. Reproach follows the unnatural child.
heeding — hearing instruction, whose cessation brings straying
the hearing/heeding of instruction, to cease from which is to stray from knowledge
welded to the knowledge that hearing preserves
shama (hear/heed) — 'CEASE to hear instruction... and you will stray'; to stop listening is to wander from knowledge. The ironic warning — the moment one stops heeding, one drifts from wisdom.
knowledge — strayed from by ceasing to hear
the words of knowledge from which one strays when one ceases to hear instruction
welded to the heeding that keeps one near it
daath (knowledge) — 'you will stray from the words of KNOWLEDGE'; knowledge is kept only by continual hearing. To stop listening is to drift from it.
scorn — the worthless witness mocks at justice
the mocking/scorning of justice by a worthless witness
welded to the justice his scorn derides
luts (scoff/mock) — 'a worthless witness MOCKS at justice'; the false witness scorns the very justice he perverts. Contempt for the law.
justice — mocked by the worthless witness
the justice that the worthless witness scorns and mocks
welded to the scorn that mocks it
mishpat (justice) — 'mocks at JUSTICE'; the justice the false witness holds in contempt. What God grounds in himself (17:15), the worthless mock.
the wicked whose mouth greedily devours iniquity as food
welded to the evil it feeds on
rasha — 'the mouth of the WICKED devours iniquity'; the wicked feed on iniquity, swallowing evil greedily (cf 4:17). Sin is their appetite.
iniquity — greedily devoured by the wicked mouth
the iniquity that the wicked mouth swallows down like food
welded to the wickedness that feeds on it
aven (iniquity) — 'devours INIQUITY'; the evil the wicked greedily consume. Iniquity as the wicked man's diet.
judgment — the penalties prepared for scoffers
the condemnation/judgments that stand ready for scoffers, and beatings for fools
the judgement prepared for the incorrigible

shephet (judgment/penalty) — 'CONDEMNATION is ready for scoffers, and beating for the backs of fools'; judgement is prepared and waiting for the scornful and foolish. Emergent: the penalties held in readiness for the incorrigible.
folly — which ruins a man's own way
the folly of a man that subverts and ruins his own way
welded to the overthrow of his own path
ivveleth (folly) — 'a man's FOLLY brings his way to ruin'; a man ruins himself by his own folly. Self-inflicted disaster.
subversion — folly overthrows a man's own way
the ruin/subverting of a man's own way that his folly works
welded to the folly that overthrows him
salaph (twist/subvert/overthrow) — 'brings his way to RUIN'; folly subverts the fool's own course. His path is wrecked by his own foolishness.
the heart — which rages against the LORD for self-caused ruin
the heart of a man that rages against the LORD for the ruin his own folly caused
welded to the rage it harbours against God

leb (heart) — 'his HEART rages against the LORD'; the profound psychology of blame-shifting — a man ruins himself by folly, then his heart rages at God for it. The self-deceived heart blames its Maker.
blame-rage — the heart fumes against the LORD
the raging/fretting of the heart against the LORD, blaming God for self-caused ruin
welded to the heart that fumes at God

zaaph (rage/fret/be angry) — 'his heart RAGES against the LORD'; the fool blames God for the disaster his own folly brought. Emergent: raging-against-God as the self-deceived heart's response to self-caused ruin. A piercing insight into the blaming heart.
the wealth that gathers many (fair-weather) friends to a man
the deserted poor man, by contrast (264595)
set against the poor man abandoned by his friend
hon (wealth) — 'WEALTH brings many new friends'; riches attract crowds of friends (of the money, cf 14:20; 19:6). Emergent: wealth as a magnet for fair-weather friendship.
poverty — the poor, deserted even by his friend
the poor man who is abandoned even by his one friend
the wealth that gathers friends, by contrast (264591)
set against the wealth that attracts many friends
dal (poor/weak) — 'a poor man is deserted by his friend'; poverty drives even a friend away. The bleak social truth — the poor are abandoned, the rich courted.
falseness — the false witness, who will not escape punishment
the falseness of the witness who bears false testimony and will not go unpunished
the false testimony that draws inescapable punishment
sheqer (falsehood) — 'a FALSE witness will not go unpunished'; the perjurer cannot escape (cf 19:9). False testimony brings certain judgement.
courting — many seek the favour of the generous
the seeking/entreating of the generous man's favour by many who court him
welded to the generosity that draws them
chalah (entreat/seek favour) — 'many SEEK the favour of a generous man'; the liberal are courted by many. The read notes the crowd that gathers to a giver — often for the gifts, not the man.
generosity — the liberal man whom many court
the generous/noble man to whom many seek favour and all are friends
the many who seek his favour (264607)
welded to the crowd his giving attracts
nadib (noble/generous) — 'a GENEROUS man... a man who gives gifts'; the liberal draw friends and suitors. Generosity attracts — though the read hints the friendship may be of the gifts (cf 19:4).
poverty — the poor, hated even by his brothers
the poor man whom even his own brothers hate, and whose friends go far off
welded to the rejection his poverty brings
rush (be poor) — 'all a POOR man's brothers hate him'; poverty repels even kin. The bleakest of the wealth-and-friendship sayings — the poor are abandoned by family and friends alike.
rejection — even brothers hate the poor man
the hatred/rejection that even a poor man's brothers show him
welded to the poverty that repels them
sane (hate) — 'all a poor man's brothers HATE him'; even family turns from the poor. A hard truth about how poverty is treated — and an implicit rebuke of it (cf 14:21, 31).
wisdom-getting — acquiring sense is loving one's own soul
the getting of sense/heart, which is an act of love toward one's own soul
welded to the love of soul it constitutes
leb (heart/sense) — 'whoever gets SENSE loves his own soul'; to acquire wisdom is to do good to oneself — the truest self-love. Getting sense is soul-care.
self-love — getting sense is loving one's soul
the love of one's own soul that getting sense amounts to
welded to the wisdom-getting it names
aheb (love) — 'LOVES his own soul'; the good self-love — to seek wisdom is to love oneself rightly. Virtue is self-benefiting.
the soul — benefited by getting sense
the soul/self that a man loves and benefits by getting sense
welded to the love that seeks its good
nephesh (soul/self) — 'loves his own SOUL'; the self that getting wisdom benefits. To get sense is to care for one's own life.
keeping — guarding understanding to discover good
the keeping/guarding of understanding by which one discovers good
welded to the understanding it guards
shamar (keep/guard) — 'he who KEEPS understanding will discover good'; guarding what one has learned leads to good. Retention, not just acquisition, is rewarded.
the understanding that, kept and guarded, leads one to discover good
welded to the guarding that treasures it
tebunah (understanding) — 'he who KEEPS understanding'; the understanding retained and guarded, which finds good. Wisdom held fast bears fruit.
falseness — the false witness, who will perish
the falseness of the witness who bears false testimony and will perish
the false testimony that ends in perishing
sheqer (falsehood) — 'a FALSE witness will not go unpunished... will perish' (=19:5, intensified); the perjurer not only fails to escape but perishes. False testimony is deadly.
sinners — those whose settled bent is to sin, here as enticers
the sinful who entice the son to join them
the son they seek to draw in
set against the son's refusal to consent
chatta = persons defined by sin; the danger the book warns of is not abstract evil but sinful companions who ENTICE. The threat is relational/social.
to consent — the will's yielding; here commanded NOT to yield
the act of the will refusing to yield to enticement (avah negated)
the counter-move to the sinners' enticement — will against pull

avah is the WILL itself — the decisive inner faculty. The book's first ethical command targets not knowledge but volition: 'do not consent.' Prohibition present (the negated will) though not a separate 113 here.
the innocent — the guiltless one, blameless of any provocation
the innocent standing guiltless, made the object of an unprovoked ambush
paired with 'without reason' (chinnam) — innocence stressed by the lack of any cause

naqi is the moral state of the VICTIM — guiltlessness — surfaced only to be violated 'without reason'. The read holds the innocence as a real inner state, not merely a plot-detail; the wickedness is that it targets the blameless.
evil — the moral wrong the wicked eagerly pursue
running to evil — the inner bent that hurries the whole person toward wrong and bloodshed
eager haste ('make haste to shed blood')
welded to bloodshed — evil here is not abstract but issues in violence

the feet 'run' — evil is figured as a bent that MOVES the person, an eager momentum toward wrong. Manner (haste) is marked here where most chars leave 108 none: the wicked's speed toward evil is the point.
their own lives/selves — the very self the ambush recoils upon
the self against which the plotters, unknowing, set their own ambush
paired with 'their own blood' — the self and its life-blood are what they truly hunt

nephesh here is the self/life turned into its own victim — the moral irony: violence plotted outward closes on the plotter's own soul. Read as characteristic (the self at stake), not a mere qualifier.
greed — the covetous grasping after unjust gain that cuts one off
greedily grasping unjust gain — the bent that seizes and, in seizing, destroys the self
welded to the loss of life/nephesh (1:19) — greed takes away the life of its possessor

EMERGENT: batsa (to cut off / be greedy for gain) is the DRIVER of the whole 1:10-19 unit — the covetous grasping the chapter warns against; it names the inner root of the violence. Seed-missed; recovered on the cycle check. Descent read at full weight.
the life/self that unjust gain seizes from the one who holds it
the life that greed (betsa) 'takes away' from its own possessor
welded to unjust gain (betsa) as the thing that consumes the self
distinct from 264699: here nephesh is the life GREED devours — the general maxim (1:19) that unjust gain costs the greedy their own life. The self is the price of covetousness.
to know — the acquisition of wisdom as its aim
knowing wisdom and instruction — taking them into the inner person
paired with understanding (995) and receiving (part of one acquisition)
1:2 opens the book's purpose as an interior verb (know), not an act on the world; wisdom is gained by being known/received inwardly.
wisdom — the skilled, ordered competence of the inner life
wisdom as the faculty to be acquired and lived
paired with instruction (musar) — the disposition and its shaping named together
chokmah heads the list — the master good the book exists to impart; here it is the object of know (yada), the two-axes case (its own char AND know's target).
instruction as moral discipline — correction that shapes the inner person
the disciplining/shaping of the inner life to be received
welded to wisdom (chokmah) in the pair chokmah-umusar
musar = discipline received, not knowledge grasped — it carries the note of correction/shaping the inner life must submit to (distinct from wisdom's competence).
to understand — to discern the sense of words
paired with know (yada) — the two cognitive acts of the aim
bin (discern) is distinct from yada (know): it is the penetrating grasp of meaning, and its object is 'words of insight' — understanding applied to speech.
the discerning faculty by which words are understood
paired with understand (bin) — faculty and act of the same root
binah is the noun-faculty of bin; here it is the target of understand — the two-axes case again (faculty AND object).
Wisdom personified — wisdom as a woman crying aloud in the street
Wisdom crying aloud, raising her voice in the public square to summon the simple
the simple/scoffers/fools she addresses (from the following verses)

a decisive shift: wisdom, the object gained in 1:2-9, becomes a SUBJECT that actively seeks — personified, she pursues the simple in the streets. The IB good is not passive; it appeals. Read as characteristic (wisdom-in-action) with the personification noted; manner marked (public, loud).
to cry out — Wisdom's public calling/proclamation
crying out at the head of the noisy streets and the city gates — proclaiming to all who pass
the passers-by / the simple in the public places
public, insistent (busiest places: street-head, city gates)
welded to Wisdom's crying-aloud (1:20); qara is how her appeal is voiced

qara sets Wisdom's appeal in the most public, trafficked places (street-heads, gates) — the calling is deliberate and inescapable. Read as characteristic (the proclaiming operation); the location stresses that wisdom's summons is offered to all, not hidden.
the simple ones — the naive whom Wisdom rebukes for loving their naivety
the naive who cling to their simpleness rather than gaining prudence
welded to their love of simplicity — the state they refuse to leave
the peti of 1:4 (to be given prudence) here indicted: naivety becomes culpable when it is LOVED, not merely suffered.
to love — here misdirected affection, loving one's own simpleness
loving/being-attached-to simpleness, refusing to be parted from it
love bound to the wrong object — the root of the refusal
ahav is bivalent; the DESCENT here is love fixed on the wrong good (one's naivety). Affection itself is not the fault — its object is.
simpleness — the naive condition, here the object loved
the simpleness the naive refuse to give up
distinct occurrence of peti from 264735: here the naivety as the loved OBJECT (two-axes with love's target), not the bearer-state.
scoffers — the mockers who scorn correction
the scoffer who takes delight in his own scoffing
luts (scoffer) is the hardened middle term between the simple and the fool — one who not only refuses wisdom but mocks it.
to delight in / crave — here the scoffer's relish for his scoffing
chamad (the coveting-desire) is here perverted like the love in the parallel line: appetite fixed on scorn. The three postures share one shape — a right faculty aimed wrong.
scoffing/scorn — the mockery the scoffer relishes
the scorn that is the scoffer's chosen pleasure
the object of the scoffer's delight (264739)
latson (scoffing) — the same root that H3856-type mockery names; here the settled scorn a scoffer feeds on. Two-axes with delight's target.
fools — the dull-hearted who hate knowledge
kesil (thick/dull fool) is distinct from evil (1:7) and peti (simple): the third and heaviest term, defined by ACTIVE hatred of knowledge, not mere lack.
to hate — the fool's aversion to knowledge
hating knowledge — active aversion, not passive ignorance
sane (hate) is the darkest of the three affects here: love mis-aimed, delight mis-aimed, but hate turned squarely on the good itself. The descent deepens across the verse.
knowledge — here the good the fool hates
the one who should love it
knowledge as the object of the fool's hatred
daat, gained by the God-fearer (1:7), is here HATED by the fool — the same good, opposite postures. Two-axes with hate's target.
spirit — the inner life/mind Wisdom pours out on those who turn to her
Wisdom (who pours it), given to the responsive
pouring out her spirit — the self-giving of Wisdom's inner life to the one who turns at reproof
welded to making-her-words-known — spirit and word given together
ruach here is Wisdom's self imparted, conditioned on 'if you turn' — the inner life is not seized but poured on the responsive. Personified-Wisdom's spirit, offered to the human interior.
to make known — Wisdom causing her words to be known to the responsive
making her words known — the act of imparting knowledge to the one who turns
paired with the outpoured spirit — the two gifts to the responsive
the Hiphil of yada (make-known) is the counter-movement to the fool's hating-knowledge (1:22): Wisdom actively GIVES the very knowledge the fool refuses.
welded to their refusal to listen
qara again (cf 1:21): the appeal that judgement will answer; here stated as spurned.
to refuse — the will's outright rejection of the call
refusing to listen to Wisdom's call
the human counter to the calling — will set against appeal
maen = flat refusal of the will; the decisive act that grounds 1:26's judgement. Read at full weight.
the attentive heeding that was wholly absent
paired with the refusal; attention withheld
qashab (attend) negated: not merely refusing words but ignoring the outstretched hand. Non-attention as culpable posture.
the will — here refusing all of Wisdom's counsel
the will setting itself against counsel and reproof, wanting none of it
the will's refusal binds to the counsel it spurns
avah (the will) recurs (cf 1:10 'do not consent'): here the will actively wants NONE of wisdom's counsel. counsel(264763) is its rejected object.
to mock/deride — Wisdom's answering derision at their calamity
mocking when their dreaded terror strikes
the just recoil of their scorn: Wisdom laughs as they once scoffed
laag pairs with 'I will laugh': Wisdom's mockery is the measured answer to the scoffers' delight (1:22) — scorn returned for scorn.
dread/terror — the sudden fear that overtakes them
the terror that strikes them in their calamity
welded to the calamity/storm that triggers it
pachad = the seizing dread; first of two occurrences in 1:27.
dread/terror — likened to a storm sweeping in
terror bearing down like a storm
coupled to the storm-image intensifying it
distinct second pachad (1:27b): the dread now given its simile (storm/whirlwind) — the same fear, its violence stressed.
distress — the straitness/anguish that comes upon them
distress coming upon the one who spurned wisdom
paired with anguish as the twin closing terror
EMERGENT (seed-missed): tsarah = constriction/distress, paired with tsuqah; the inner narrowing that judgement brings.
anguish — crushing pressure of the inner life
the twin of distress; the pair names the whole weight
tsuqah (pressure/anguish) closes the terror-sequence; distinct from tsarah though paired — the crushing that follows the constriction.
calling — the desperate, too-late appeal to Wisdom
calling upon Wisdom when it is too late for answer
the mirror of 1:24: the appeal now runs the other way, unanswered
qara reversed: those who spurned Wisdom's call now call her — but 'I will not answer'. The calling is real but forfeited.
to seek earnestly/at dawn — the frantic late search
seeking Wisdom diligently yet not finding
welded to the futility: earnest search, no finding
shachar (seek early/earnestly) — the intensity of the too-late search underscores that the door has closed; earnestness cannot undo the prior refusal.
to hate — their aversion to knowledge
hating knowledge, the settled aversion behind the refusal
sane recurs (1:22): here given as the ROOT reason for the coming judgement — knowledge was not missed but hated.
daat, the fruit of the fear of God (1:7), was the very thing they hated. Two-axes with hate's target.
the will declining to choose the fear of the LORD
the will's refusal parallel to the hatred: they would not elect reverence
bachar (elect) negated: the fear of God was set before them and NOT chosen — reverence is here a matter of the will's election, refused.
reverent fear of God — what they refused to choose
the reverence they declined to elect
paired with knowledge: the twin goods refused
yirah (cf 1:7) here as the object NOT chosen — the beginning of knowledge, deliberately passed over. God the target; the fear the human interior.
instruction in wise dealing — discipline received, now specified by its fruit
receiving the discipline that produces prudent, upright conduct
welded to wise-dealing/righteousness/justice/equity — the moral goods it instils

musar recurs in 1:3 but now aimed at CONDUCT (wise dealing, righteousness, justice, equity) — the same discipline, its ethical output specified. Distinct occurrence, not a repeat of 264712 (which paired with wisdom-cognition).
prudent, insightful conduct — acting with skill in living
acting wisely/prudently in the conduct of life
paired with righteousness, justice, equity as the ethical triad it heads
sakal (prudent dealing) is conduct-competence, distinct from chokmah (competence as such) — it turns the inner good outward into right living, hence it heads the ethical triad of 1:3.
righteousness — rightness of the inner person toward the norm
the disposition to what is right, gained through discipline
tsedeq = rightness as a state of the person; distinct from justice (mishpat, right judgement/order) and equity (meshar, straightness) — the read keeps the three apart though they are listed together.
justice — right judgement and ordered dealing
discerning and rendering what is just
middle of the triad, with righteousness and equity
mishpat carries the note of judgement/verdict — the inner sense of right order that issues in fair dealing, distinct from tsedeq (rightness-as-state).
third of the triad, closing righteousness-justice-equity
mesharim (plural, 'straightnesses') = evenness/fairness — the level, undistorted dealing; distinct from mishpat's judgement and tsedeq's rightness. The prologue thus names three moral goods, not one.
the will wanting none of Wisdom's counsel
the will bound against the counsel it spurns
avah recurs (cf 1:25): the refusing will, now paired with active contempt for reproof.
to spurn/despise — active contempt for reproof
the contempt that hardens the refusal
naats (spurn) is heavier than avah's refusal: not just declining counsel but DESPISING correction — the scoffer's posture (cf buz 1:7).
satiation — glutted, ironically, on the fruit of their own way
being filled to satiety with the results of their own schemes
the ironic coupling: appetite met by consequence
saba (be sated) turned to judgement: the fullness they get is the harvest of their devices — desire answered by its own fruit.
listening — the receptive attention that inherits safety
heeding Wisdom and thereby dwelling secure
the positive counterpart to 1:24's refusal: listening yields security
shama here the SAVING posture, opposite the refusal/non-heeding of 1:24-25 — the one act that changes the outcome.
dwelling in safety as the fruit of listening
the reward of heeding; genuine security
betach = grounded safety/trust — the TRUE security set against the fool's shalvah (1:32): one saves, the other destroys.
ease/untroubledness — quiet rest of the inner life
paired with security; the settled calm of the wise
shaan (be at ease/quiet) — the inner tranquillity of the one who heeds; distinct from complacency in that it rests on having listened, not on carelessness.
dread — here ABSENT: without dread of disaster
the fear of calamity that the listener does NOT feel
the dread negated; its object (disaster) held off
pachad (cf 1:26-27, where it seizes the refuser) here NEGATED for the listener: the same terror that overtakes the fool is absent from the one who heeded. The contrast is exact.
prudence — shrewd good sense (the wise use of the same craft that, misused, is craftiness)
the simple, to be given it
prudence put into the naive so they are no longer defenceless
the gift to the simple (peti), the counter to naivety

EMERGENT: ormah heads 1:4's purpose ('to give prudence to the simple') yet the seed missed it. Prudence is the sharp, wary good sense the naive lack — bivalent (craftiness in the wicked), here wholly positive. A central Proverbs char, recovered on the cycle check.
the simple — the naive, untaught, morally open inner condition
the simple/naive person the book addresses
the naive inner state that stands open, needing prudence put into it
paired with the youth (naar) as the un-formed recipients
peti is not an act but a CONDITION — the open, gullible inner state; the book exists to give it prudence (ormah). Read as a characteristic-state, the starting point the whole book works on.
knowledge given to fill the naive inner life
paired with discretion (mezimmah) as the gift to the youth
daat here is the content given, opposite of the simple's emptiness; distinct from binah (discernment) and chokmah (competence).
discretion — shrewd forethought (here the positive sense)
shrewd forethought put into the young inner life
paired with knowledge as the gift to the youth

mezimmah is BIVALENT — 'scheming' in the wicked (its usual Proverbs edge, the seed's 'IB:plot' tag) but here POSITIVE: the shrewd forethought given to the youth. The read records the good sense the context forces, noting the dark potential.
the wise one — the person of settled competence who still learns
the wise disposition that hears and grows rather than resting
welded to hearing (shama) and increase in learning
the wise here is the LEARNER-wise (still hearing/increasing), distinct from 264844 the sages-whose-words-carry-wisdom. The book's paradox: the wise are those who keep receiving.
to hear — receptive listening that takes instruction in
listening so as to increase in learning
paired with the wise (its bearer) and the growth in learning it yields
read as a characteristic (not the seed's qualifier): shama = the receptive-listening operation, an IB act the study registers (Reg 213 listen). It is the means by which the wise increase.
learning — the received teaching that is taken in and grows
the wise who increase in it
the wise increasing in learning by hearing
the fruit of the wise's hearing (shama) — what listening accumulates
EMERGENT: leqach ('what is taken/received') is the growing store of teaching the wise add to by listening (1:5) — the object of 'increase'. Seed-missed; recovered on the cycle check.
the discerning one — the person of understanding
paired with the wise; parallel figure in the couplet
nabon (Niphal participle) = the settled discerning person, parallel to the wise; here he obtains guidance (tachbulot). Distinct from 264840 the ACT of understanding a proverb.
guidance — steering, the skill of direction (from the sailor's ropes)
the discerning person who obtains it
the good obtained by the discerning (264836)
tachbulot pictures navigation — the inner capacity to steer a course through life; a distinct good from wisdom-as-competence and knowledge-as-content.
to understand — to penetrate the sense of wise speech
discerning a proverb, a saying, the words of the wise and their riddles
the act that closes the purpose-chain: the aim of all the foregoing
the Hiphil ACT of understanding (vs 264836 the discerning PERSON): its objects are the forms of wise speech — proverb, saying, words of the wise, riddles.
the wise/sages — those whose words carry authority
the wise as the source of the words and riddles to be understood
paired with their words/riddles as their expression

distinct occurrence of chakam from 264832: here the wise are the AUTHORITATIVE SOURCE ('the words of the wise'), not the learner who hears. The difference is the finding — the wise both receive and transmit.
the fear of the LORD — reverent awe before God
revering God as the very beginning/first-principle of knowledge
the LORD (God as the object of the fear)
welded to knowledge as its beginning (reshit) — fear is the door to knowing

the programmatic claim: knowledge does not begin in intellect but in a DISPOSITION of the inner life toward God (reverence). God is the target/arena; the fear itself is the human interior state. This anchors the whole book.
knowledge — the knowing that fear of God opens
knowledge as the fruit whose beginning is the fear of God
welded to the fear of the LORD as its root
daat is here the crown, not the entry — its beginning lies outside itself in reverence; knowledge is thus made dependent on a moral-religious disposition.
fools — the morally-obstinate who reject wisdom
the fool as the one who despises wisdom and instruction
welded to despising (buz); the fool is defined by his contempt
evil (the moral fool) is set as the antithesis of the God-fearer in the SAME verse: reverence begins knowledge, contempt refuses it. The fool is a disposition, not mere ignorance.
to despise — to hold wisdom in contempt
holding wisdom and instruction in contempt, refusing them
the defining act of the fool (264850)
buz is the DESCENT-operation — contempt turned on the very goods the book offers. Read at full weight: the fool's inner posture is active despising, not passive lack.
wisdom — here the object the fool despises
wisdom as the good held in contempt by the fool
paired with instruction (musar) as the despised goods
chokmah is the target of buz here (two-axes: its own char AND despise's object). The same good that reverence gains, contempt refuses.
the one who should receive it
paired with wisdom as the twin good despised
musar (discipline) recurs, now as an object of contempt — the fool refuses not just knowledge but the corrective shaping. Distinct occurrence from its 1:2-3 uses.
hear — the son commanded to receptive listening
heeding the father's instruction (an imperative of the will's attention)
set against the fool's despising — the son hears where the fool refuses
the imperative shama is the countermove to the fool's buz in the same passage: obedient listening vs contempt. Read as characteristic (the receptive-attentive operation).
the father's instruction — parental discipline to be heeded
the father's shaping discipline, the object of the son's hearing
paired with the mother's teaching (torah) in the parallel line
musar here is CONCRETE and relational — a father's discipline (not abstract), the thing the son's shama takes in; the target-endpoint of 264854.
grace — the favor and beauty heeded instruction confers, a garland of grace
the grace/favor that adorns the one who receives the parents' teaching
the fruit of hearing (1:8): obedience wears as grace and honour
chen here is an EFFECT, not an operation: the inner honour/favour that received discipline confers, imaged as an ornament. The metaphor (garland, pendants) grounds an interior good in adornment.
divine abhorrence — dishonest weights are detestable to God
the LORD's abhorrence of unequal weights and measures — of fraud in dealing
the divine detestation of dishonest trade

toebah (abomination) — 'unequal weights and measures are both alike an ABOMINATION to the LORD'; God detests cheating in commerce (cf 11:1; 20:23). Locus external:god — honest dealing is grounded in God's own character; fraud is loathsome to him.
purity — a child's conduct known to be clean
the purity/cleanness of conduct by which even a child makes himself known
welded to the uprightness that marks it
zak (pure/clean) — 'even a child makes himself known by his acts, by whether his conduct is PURE'; character shows early, in deeds. Even a child is revealed by whether his conduct is clean.
uprightness — a child's conduct known to be straight
the uprightness/straightness of conduct by which a child reveals his character
welded to the purity that marks it
yashar (upright) — 'and UPRIGHT'; a child's deeds reveal whether he is upright. Conduct, even in the young, discloses the heart.
hearing — the faculty of attention, God-given
the hearing ear — the faculty of attentive hearing that the LORD himself has made
the God-given faculty of perception, implying accountability for its use

shama (hear) — 'the HEARING ear and the seeing eye, the LORD has made them both'; the faculties of perception are God's gift. The read hears the implication — since God made the ear to hear and the eye to see, we are accountable for what we hear and see. Perception is a divine trust.
disparagement — the buyer decries the goods to lower the price
the disparaging 'bad, bad' the buyer says of the goods to beat down the price
ra (bad/evil) — ''BAD, bad,' says the buyer'; the haggler runs down the goods he means to buy, to lower the price. The read exposes the buyer's dishonesty.
disparagement — the repeated decrying of the goods
the repeated 'bad' by which the buyer runs down the goods before purchase
ra (bad) — 'bad, BAD'; the doubled disparagement of the haggler, hypocritical since he wants the goods.
boasting — the buyer brags afterward of his bargain
the boasting of the buyer once he has gone off with the goods he decried
(the disparagement he used to get them)
the brag that exposes the earlier disparagement as a ruse

halal (boast/praise, Hithpael) — 'when he goes away, then he BOASTS'; having beaten down the price by decrying the goods, the buyer brags of his bargain. Hypocrisy in trade — disparage to buy, boast to keep.
knowledge — the rarest, most precious treasure
the knowledge whose lips are more precious than gold or costly stones
the knowledge-bearing lips worth more than any wealth
daath (knowledge) — 'the lips of KNOWLEDGE are a precious jewel'; there is much gold and many jewels, but lips that speak knowledge are the rarest treasure of all. Wisdom's speech outvalues wealth.
surety-securing — take the rash guarantor's garment in pledge
the taking-in-pledge of the garment of one who has rashly stood surety for a stranger
the prudent securing against a foolish guarantor

chabal (bind/take a pledge) — 'hold it in PLEDGE when he puts up security for foreigners'; if a man is rash enough to guarantee a stranger, take his garment as security — his folly makes him a bad risk. Emergent: the pledge-taking that guards against rash surety (cf 6:1-5; 11:15). Prudence about others' imprudence.
deceit — bread by fraud, sweet then bitter as gravel
the deceit by which bread is gained — sweet at first, but afterward the mouth is full of gravel
the fraud whose sweetness turns to grit

sheqer (falsehood/deceit) — 'bread gained by DECEIT is sweet to a man, but afterward his mouth will be full of gravel'; ill-gotten gain is delicious at first but ends bitter — a mouthful of gravel. The deceptive arc of dishonest gain (cf 9:17). Sweet now, grit later.
the plans/purposes that are made firm and established by taking counsel
welded to the counsel that steadies them
machashabah (plan/purpose) — 'PLANS are established by counsel'; purposes stand firm when built on counsel. Consultation steadies the plan (cf 15:22).
the counsel/consultation by which plans are made firm
welded to the plans it establishes
etsah (counsel) — 'established by COUNSEL'; the consultation that makes purposes firm. Counsel is the foundation of good planning.
wise steering — needed to wage war
the wise guidance/steering by which war is rightly waged
(the plans established by counsel, in parallel)
the strategic direction that war requires
tachbuloth (guidance/wise direction) — 'by wise GUIDANCE wage war'; even war needs wise steering, not just force. The value of counsel and direction in great undertakings (cf 24:6).
talebearing — the gossip who reveals secrets
the going-about-slandering/talebearing that betrays confidences and reveals secrets
welded to the confidences it betrays
rakil (slander/talebearer) — 'whoever goes about SLANDERING reveals secrets'; the gossip betrays confidence — so avoid him. The talebearer cannot keep a secret; do not entrust one to a babbler.
the secrets/confidences that the going-about slanderer reveals
welded to the talebearing that exposes them
sod (secret/confidence) — 'reveals SECRETS'; the confidences the gossip betrays. Trust is broken by the loose-tongued babbler — avoid him.
dread — the terror a king inspires, like a lion's growl
the terror/dread that a king inspires, fearsome as the growling of a lion
welded to the roar it is likened to
emah (terror/dread) — 'the TERROR of a king is like the growling of a lion'; royal power inspires dread. To rouse it is deadly (cf 19:12).
menace — the lion's growl of royal terror
the growling/roar, like a lion's, to which the king's terror is likened
welded to the royal dread it pictures
naham (growl/roar) — 'like the GROWLING of a lion'; the deadly roar of royal power. Emergent: the growl as the image of imminent, dangerous wrath.
self-endangering — provoking a king forfeits one's life
the forfeiting/sinning-against-oneself of the one who provokes a king to anger
welded to the life he throws away
chata (sin/forfeit/miss) — 'whoever provokes him to anger FORFEITS his life'; to provoke a king is to sin against one's own soul, forfeiting life. Recklessness before power is self-destruction.
the life — forfeited by provoking a king
the life/soul that the one who provokes a king throws away
welded to the reckless provoking that costs it
nephesh (life/soul) — 'forfeits his LIFE'; the self is the price of provoking power. To anger a king is to gamble one's own life.
grasping haste — an inheritance seized too fast
the hasty, greedy grasping of an inheritance at the beginning, which forfeits blessing at the end
welded to the blessing that hasty grasping loses

bahal (hasten/be greedy) — 'an inheritance GAINED HASTILY in the beginning'; grasping wealth too quickly (greedily, perhaps wrongly) forfeits its blessing. Impatient, greedy acquisition curses its own gain.
unblessing — the hastily-gained inheritance is not blessed
the blessing that the hastily-gained inheritance will NOT have in the end
the grasping haste that forfeits it (264955)
welded to the greed that loses it
barak (bless) NEGATED — 'will NOT be blessed in the end'; wealth grasped in greedy haste has no blessing on it. What is seized impatiently does not prosper.
vengeance — the impulse to repay evil, forbidden
the impulse to repay evil for evil, which the wise are forbidden to indulge
waiting for the LORD, by contrast (264964)
set against the patient trust that leaves vengeance to God

shalam (repay/requite) — 'do not say, I will REPAY evil'; the impulse to take one's own vengeance, which the wise renounce. Retaliation is forbidden — the wronged must not repay evil for evil (cf 24:29; Rom 12:19).
patient trust — wait for the LORD instead of avenging
the waiting/hoping in the LORD, in place of vengeance, trusting him to deliver
set against the impulse to repay evil

qavah (wait/hope) — 'WAIT for the LORD, and he will deliver you'; instead of avenging, wait in patient trust for God, who will deliver. The great non-retaliation word — leave vengeance to God and wait on him. Faith replaces the fist.
divine abhorrence — dishonest weights detestable to God
the LORD's abhorrence of unequal weights — of fraud in dealing
the divine detestation of dishonest trade
toebah (abomination) — 'unequal weights are an ABOMINATION to the LORD' (cf 20:10; 11:1); God detests fraud in commerce. Locus external:god — honest dealing grounded in God's character.
deceit — the false scales that are 'not good'
the deceit of false scales/balances used to cheat
welded to the wrong they work
mirmah (deceit) — 'false SCALES are not good'; the fraudulent balance, the tool of cheating. Deceit in trade.
wrongness — false scales are not good
the not-good-ness of false scales — the moral wrong of cheating
welded to the deceit it condemns
tob (good) NEGATED — 'false scales are NOT good'; the moral wrong of the cheating balance, understated but real.
limited comprehension — man cannot fully understand his own way
the limit of human understanding of one's own way, since a man's steps are directed by the LORD
the bounded human comprehension of a divinely-ordered path

bin (understand) — 'a man's steps are from the LORD; how then can man UNDERSTAND his way?'; since God directs a man's steps, the man cannot fully comprehend his own path. The read holds the humbling limit of self-understanding under divine sovereignty (cf 16:9).
rash consecration — a snare to vow 'holy' hastily
the rash saying 'it is holy' (a hasty vow of dedication) that becomes a snare, reflected on only afterward
the hasty dedication that entangles the vower

qodesh (holy/consecrated) — 'it is a snare to say rashly, It is HOLY, and to reflect only after making vows'; hasty consecration/vowing is a trap. The read warns against rash dedication — count the cost before vowing, not after (cf Eccl 5:4-5).
wisdom — the king who winnows out the wicked
the wise king who sifts and winnows out the wicked, driving the threshing-wheel over them
welded to the wicked his wisdom separates out
chakam (wise) — 'a WISE king winnows the wicked'; the discerning king sifts the wicked from the good and executes judgement (cf 20:8). Wisdom in a ruler is the power to separate and punish evil.
wickedness — winnowed and crushed by the wise king
the wicked whom the wise king winnows out and threshes
the wise king who sifts them (264992)
welded to the discerning judgement that separates them
rasha — 'winnows the WICKED and drives the wheel over them'; the wicked are sifted out and crushed by the just king's judgement. Evil cannot hide from the discerning ruler.
conscience — the God-lit lamp searching the inner depths
the spirit/conscience of man, which is the LORD's lamp, searching out all the innermost parts of a person
the God-given inner light that illumines and probes the depths of the self

neshamah (breath/spirit) — 'the SPIRIT of man is the lamp of the LORD, searching all his innermost parts'; the human spirit/conscience is God's searchlight within, illuminating and probing the deepest self. A profound word on the conscience — God's lamp in the inner being, from which nothing is hidden (cf 20:12; 21:2).
loyal love — which preserves the king
the steadfast love/loyalty that, with faithfulness, preserves and guards the king
welded to faithfulness as the twin guardian of the throne
chesed (steadfast love) — 'STEADFAST LOVE and faithfulness preserve the king'; loyal love and truth are the guardians of a throne. A king stands by chesed, not by force (cf 16:12).
the faithfulness/reliability that, with steadfast love, preserves the king
welded to steadfast love as the twin guardian
emet (faithfulness/truth) — 'and FAITHFULNESS'; reliability paired with loyal love as the twin preservers of the king. Truth upholds a throne.
loyal love — which upholds the throne
the steadfast love by which the king's throne is upheld and made secure
the loyal love that is the throne's foundation
chesed (steadfast love) — 'by STEADFAST LOVE his throne is upheld'; loyal love is the foundation of stable rule. A throne rests on chesed.
vigour — the glory of the young
the strength/vigour that is the glory of young men
the splendour of the old, by contrast (265017)
set against the gray-haired dignity of age
koach (strength/power) — 'the glory of young men is their STRENGTH'; each age has its glory — the young their vigour. Emergent: strength as the ornament of youth, set against the dignity of age.
dignity — the splendour of the old, their gray hair
the splendour/dignity of old men, which is their gray hair
the strength of the young, by contrast (265016)
set against the vigour of youth

hadar (splendour/dignity) — 'the SPLENDOUR of old men is their gray hair'; age has its own glory — the honour of gray hair (cf 16:31). The read affirms both — youth's strength and age's dignity, each in its season.
honour — of keeping aloof from strife
the honour a man has in keeping aloof from and ceasing strife
welded to the conflict he honourably shuns
kabod (honour/glory) — 'it is an HONOUR for a man to keep aloof from strife'; to avoid conflict is not cowardice but honour (cf 20:3b). Restraint from quarreling adorns a man.
the strife/quarrel that the honourable man keeps aloof from
welded to the honour of restraint
rib (strife/quarrel) — 'to keep aloof from STRIFE'; the conflict the wise avoid to their honour, against the fool who plunges in.
folly — every fool will be quarreling
the fool who, unlike the honourable, will always be embroiled in quarrels
(the honour of avoiding strife, by contrast)
set against the honour of keeping aloof
evil (fool) — 'every FOOL will be quarreling'; folly cannot leave a quarrel alone. Where honour keeps aloof, folly plunges in and shows itself.
sloth — who will not plow in season
the sluggard who will not plow in autumn (the cold), and so begs empty-handed at harvest
welded to the seasonable labour he refuses
atsel (sluggard) — 'the SLUGGARD does not plow in the autumn'; laziness skips the necessary labour in its season. Emergent: the sluggard who forfeits harvest by shirking the plough.
labour — the seasonal plowing the sluggard skips
the plowing/labour, done in its season, that the sluggard refuses
welded to the sluggard who will not do it
charash (plough) — 'does not PLOW in the autumn'; the labour the sluggard shirks in its season, and so has nothing to reap. Work missed at its time cannot be recovered.
futile begging — the sluggard begs at harvest and gets nothing
the seeking/begging of the sluggard at harvest, who finds nothing because he did not sow
the empty begging that follows shirked labour
shaal (ask/seek/beg) — 'he will SEEK at harvest and have nothing'; the sluggard begs where he did not work. Emergent: the futile seeking of one who shirked the labour that would have provided.
hidden counsel — the deep purpose in a man's heart
the purpose/counsel in a man's heart, deep and hidden as deep water
welded to the deep heart where it lies
etsah (counsel/purpose) — 'the PURPOSE in a man's heart is like deep water'; the inner intentions of a person are deep, hidden, not easily reached. The privacy and depth of the heart's counsel.
the heart — a deep well of hidden purpose
the heart, a deep well in which a man's purpose lies hidden as deep water
welded to the counsel hidden in it
leb (heart) — 'in a man's HEART'; the deep, hidden inner well where purpose lies. The heart's depths are not open to view.
discernment — which draws out the deep heart's counsel
the understanding by which a discerning man draws out the deep, hidden purpose of another's heart
the discernment that reaches the hidden depths of the heart

tebunah (understanding) — 'a man of UNDERSTANDING will draw it out'; the discerning can reach and draw up what lies deep in another's heart. Insight into others is a mark of understanding — the wise read the hidden.
self-advertising — many proclaim their own loyalty
the proclaiming/advertising by many of their own steadfast love, more claimed than real
welded to the chesed they advertise
qara (call/proclaim) — 'many a man PROCLAIMS his own steadfast love'; many advertise their loyalty. The read notes the gap between the loud claim and the rare reality.
the steadfast love/loyalty that many proclaim of themselves but few truly have
welded to the boasting that advertises it
chesed (steadfast love/loyalty) — 'his own STEADFAST LOVE'; the loyalty men love to claim. Everyone advertises his own kindness; the question is who truly has it.
faithfulness — the rare, truly faithful man
the truly faithful/reliable man, who — unlike the many who merely proclaim loyalty — is hard to find
set against the many who only boast of loyalty
emun (faithful/trustworthy) — 'but a FAITHFUL man who can find?'; the genuinely reliable are rare. Many claim loyalty; few are actually faithful. The scarcity of the real thing.
righteousness — who walks in integrity, blessing his children
the righteous man who walks in his integrity, so that his children after him are blessed
welded to the blameless walk that blesses his line

tsaddiq — 'the RIGHTEOUS who walks in his integrity — blessed are his children after him'; a righteous man's integrity is an inheritance of blessing to his children. Character blesses the generations.
integrity — the blameless walk that blesses one's children
the integrity/blamelessness in which the righteous man walks, a blessing to his descendants
the righteous whose walk it is (265051)
welded to the righteous it characterises
tom (integrity) — 'walks in his INTEGRITY'; the blameless walk of the righteous, whose benefit reaches his children. Integrity is a generational legacy.
discernment — the king's judgment that sifts out evil
the judging/discernment by which a king on his throne winnows out all evil with his eyes
the discerning royal gaze that separates evil from good

din (judgment/justice) — 'a king who sits on the throne of JUDGMENT winnows all evil with his eyes'; the just king's discerning gaze sifts and scatters evil. Emergent: judgment as the discerning power that separates evil out — the ideal of the seeing, sifting ruler.
the heart — which no one can honestly call pure
the heart that no one can truly claim to have made pure and clean from sin
welded to the purity no heart honestly reaches

leb (heart) — 'who can say, I have made my HEART pure?'; no one can honestly claim a pure heart. The universal sinfulness of the human heart — none is clean before God (cf 1 Kgs 8:46). A humbling word on the depth of sin.
cleanness — the impossible claim to be free from sin
the cleanness from sin that no one can honestly claim
the sin none is free of (265075)
welded to the sin that clings to all
taher (be clean/pure) — 'I am CLEAN from my sin'; the claim no honest person can make. Cleanness from sin is beyond human self-achievement. All fall short.
sin — from which no one is truly clean
the sin from which no one can honestly claim to be clean
welded to the purity no one reaches
chattah (sin) — 'clean from my SIN'; the sin that clings to every heart. The universal human condition — none can say he is free of it. Sin is the common inheritance.
the king's heart — turned wherever God wills
the king's heart, which is like a stream of water in the LORD's hand, turned wherever God wills
the royal heart wholly under divine direction

leb (heart) — 'the king's HEART is a stream of water in the hand of the LORD; he turns it wherever he will'; even the most powerful heart is God's to direct, channelled like water wherever he pleases. The supreme statement of divine sovereignty over the human heart — if the king's heart, how much more every heart (cf 16:9; 19:21).
appetite — the wicked's soul craves evil
the very soul/appetite of the wicked, which craves and desires evil
welded to the desire for evil that fills it
nephesh (soul/appetite) — 'the SOUL of the wicked desires evil'; the wicked's inmost appetite is set on evil. Evil is not their occasional deed but their soul's craving.
wickedness — whose soul craves evil and shows no mercy
the wicked whose soul desires evil and who shows his neighbour no mercy
the wicked character craving evil and pitiless
rasha — 'the soul of the WICKED desires evil'; wickedness is a craving of the soul, issuing in mercilessness. The wicked want evil and pity none.
craving — the wicked soul's appetite for evil
the craving/desiring of evil by the wicked soul
welded to the soul whose appetite it is
avah (crave/desire) — 'DESIRES evil'; the wicked soul's active craving for evil. Their inner appetite is fixed on wrong.
mercilessness — the wicked shows no mercy to his neighbour
the mercy/pity that the wicked withholds — his neighbour finds none in his eyes
the pitilessness that flows from a soul craving evil
chanan (show mercy/favour) NEGATED — 'his neighbour finds no MERCY in his eyes'; the evil-craving soul is merciless. A heart set on evil has no pity for others.
scorn — the scoffer whose punishment teaches the simple
the scoffer who, when punished, becomes a lesson to the simple
the incorrigible scorner whose fate warns others
luts (scoff) — 'when a SCOFFER is punished'; the scoffer himself learns nothing, but his punishment warns the naive. The incorrigible serve as a lesson.
naivety — the simple made wise by the scoffer's punishment
the naive who become wise when a scoffer is punished
welded to the wisdom the example teaches
pethi (simple/naive) — 'when a scoffer is punished, the SIMPLE becomes wise' (cf 19:25); the naive learn from another's punishment. Correction of the scoffer teaches the simple.
growing-wise — the simple made wise by the example
the becoming-wise of the simple through the scoffer's punishment
welded to the simpleness it corrects
chakam (be/become wise) — 'the simple BECOMES wise'; the naive gain wisdom from seeing the scoffer punished. What warns the simple is another's fate.
wisdom — who gains knowledge from instruction
the wise man who, when instructed, gains yet more knowledge
welded to the instruction that enriches him
chakam (wise) — 'when a wise man is instructed, he gains knowledge'; the wise grow directly from teaching, needing no punishment (cf 9:9; 21:11a). Teachability graded by character.
being-taught — the wise man instructed to knowledge
the instructing/teaching by which the wise man gains knowledge
welded to the knowledge it imparts
sakal (instruct/make wise) — 'when a wise man is INSTRUCTED'; the teaching that directly enriches the wise. They learn from a word.
knowledge — the wise man's gain from instruction
the knowledge that the wise man gains when instructed
welded to the teaching that imparts it
daath (knowledge) — 'he gains KNOWLEDGE'; the wise man's direct harvest from teaching. Instruction enriches the wise.
divine justice — the Righteous One observes and judges the wicked
the Righteous One who observes the house of the wicked and casts them down to ruin
welded to the discerning judgment that casts them down

tsaddiq (Righteous One) — 'the RIGHTEOUS One observes the house of the wicked; he throws the wicked down to ruin'; God, the Righteous One, watches and judges the wicked, overthrowing them. Locus external:god — divine justice observing and casting down.
discerning judgment — the Righteous One considers the wicked's house
the observing/considering by which the Righteous One weighs the house of the wicked before casting it down
welded to the divine justice that watches

sakal (consider/observe wisely) — 'OBSERVES the house of the wicked'; God's discerning attention to the wicked, prelude to judgement. Locus external:god — the divine gaze that weighs before it strikes.
wickedness — observed and cast down by the Righteous One
the wicked whose house the Righteous One observes and overthrows
welded to the ruin the Righteous One works on it
rasha — 'the house of the WICKED'; the wicked under God's observing judgement, destined to be cast down.
overthrow — the Righteous One casts the wicked to ruin
the throwing-down/overthrowing by which the Righteous One casts the wicked to ruin
the divine overthrow of the wicked
salaph (overthrow/subvert) — 'he THROWS the wicked down to ruin'; God overthrows the wicked. Locus external:god — the divine act of casting the wicked to their ruin.
wickedness — cast down to ruin by the Righteous One
the wicked whom the Righteous One throws down to ruin
welded to the overthrow they suffer
rasha — 'throws the WICKED down to ruin'; the wicked overthrown by divine justice. Their house does not stand before the Righteous One.
unanswered cry — the pitiless man's own cry goes unheard
the crying-out of the one who closed his ear to the poor — his own cry will go unanswered
the measure-for-measure silence that meets the pitiless

qara (call/cry out) — 'whoever closes his ear to the cry of the poor will himself CALL OUT and not be answered'; the merciless man's own cry is met with the silence he gave the poor. Measure-for-measure justice — mercy withheld is mercy denied (cf 14:31; Matt 5:7).
anger — averted by a secret gift
the anger that a gift given in secret turns away and pacifies
the wrath a quiet gift subdues
aph (anger) — 'a gift in secret averts ANGER'; a discreet gift pacifies anger. The read observes the power of gifts over wrath (a fact of life, neither wholly endorsed nor condemned).
fierceness — the strong wrath a concealed bribe subdues
the strength/fierceness of the wrath that a concealed bribe subdues
welded to the fierce wrath it describes
az (strong/fierce) — 'STRONG wrath'; the fierceness of the anger that even a hidden bribe can quiet. The intensity of the wrath subdued.
wrath — subdued by a concealed bribe
the fierce wrath that a concealed bribe subdues
welded to the strength that marks it
chemah (wrath) — 'a concealed bribe, strong WRATH'; even strong wrath is quieted by a secret gift. The read notes the sway of gifts over the passions of the powerful.
justice — whose doing brings joy or terror by character
the doing of justice that brings joy to the righteous and terror to evildoers
the joy it brings the righteous (265128)
welded to the gladness justice gives the upright

mishpat (justice) — 'when JUSTICE is done, it is a joy to the righteous but terror to evildoers'; the same justice gladdens the righteous and terrifies the wicked. One's response to justice reveals one's character.
joy — the righteous rejoice when justice is done
the joy the righteous feel when justice is done
welded to the justice they delight in
simchah (joy) — 'a JOY to the righteous'; the righteous delight in justice done. Love of justice marks the righteous heart.
righteousness — who rejoice when justice is done
the righteous to whom the doing of justice is a joy
the righteous who delight in justice, against the terrified evildoers
tsaddiq — 'a joy to the RIGHTEOUS'; the righteous welcome justice, while it terrifies the wicked. Character determines the response.
dread — evildoers are terrified when justice is done
the terror/dread that seizes evildoers when justice is done
(the joy of the righteous, by contrast)
set against the joy justice gives the righteous
mechittah (terror/ruin) — 'but TERROR to evildoers'; justice done terrifies the wicked, who have everything to fear from it. The same event, opposite responses.
straying — wandering from the way of good sense
the wandering/straying from the way of good sense that ends in death
welded to the prudence he abandons
taah (go astray/wander) — 'one who WANDERS from the way of good sense'; to stray from prudence is to wander toward death. The drift from wisdom is fatal.
prudence — the way wandered from, toward death
the way of good sense/prudence from which the wanderer strays, ending among the dead
welded to the straying that abandons it
sakal (good sense/prudence) — 'the way of GOOD SENSE'; the road of prudence, abandoning which leads to the grave. To leave wisdom's way is to leave life.
grim repose — the strayer will 'rest' among the dead
the grim 'resting' in the assembly of the dead that awaits the one who strays from good sense
the dead among whom he rests (265139)
welded to the shades he joins
nuach (rest/settle) — 'will REST in the assembly of the dead'; the wanderer's final, grim repose — among the shades. The 'rest' of death for the one who left the way of life.
death — the assembly of shades the strayer joins
the assembly of the dead/shades in which the one who strays from good sense comes to rest
the grim rest he finds there (265137)
welded to the death that receives him

rephaim (the dead/shades) — 'the assembly of the DEAD'; the company of shades that receives the wanderer from wisdom. Emergent: the dead as the destination of those who stray from good sense (cf 2:18; 9:18).
the love of pleasure/indulgence that leads a man to poverty
welded to the indulgence it pursues
aheb (love) — 'whoever LOVES pleasure will be a poor man'; the love of pleasure impoverishes. Indulgence drains the purse (cf 23:20-21). Where the affections go, the wealth follows.
indulgence — the pleasure whose love brings poverty
the pleasure/indulgence that the pleasure-lover craves, to his impoverishment
welded to the love that craves it
simchah (pleasure/merriment) — 'whoever loves PLEASURE'; the merriment and indulgence that, loved, impoverish. Pleasure pursued for itself is costly.
love-of-luxury — wine and oil, which keep a man from riches
the love of wine and oil (luxury) that keeps a man from ever growing rich
welded to the wealth it never gains
aheb (love) — 'he who LOVES wine and oil will not be rich'; the love of luxury (wine and oil) drains a man. Indulgence and wealth do not go together.
impoverishment — the luxury-lover will not be rich
the wealth that the lover of wine and oil will never attain
the love of luxury that forfeits it (265144)
welded to the indulgence that drains it
ashar (be/grow rich) NEGATED — 'will NOT be rich'; the lover of luxury forfeits wealth. Emergent: the failure to grow rich as the fruit of loving indulgence.
wickedness — ransomed away in the righteous's place
the wicked who becomes a ransom, suffering in the righteous man's stead
set against the righteous he suffers for
rasha — 'the WICKED is a ransom for the righteous'; the wicked's calamity spares the righteous. Retributive substitution — trouble that seeks the righteous falls instead on the wicked (cf 11:8).
righteousness — spared, the wicked ransomed in its place
the righteous for whom the wicked becomes a ransom, delivered from the trouble
set against the wicked who suffers in his stead
tsaddiq — 'a ransom for the RIGHTEOUS'; the righteous delivered, the wicked bearing the calamity. Righteousness is spared where wickedness pays.
treachery — given for the upright's ransom
the traitor who is given as ransom for the upright
the upright he is given for (265153)
set against the upright he ransoms
bagad (deal treacherously) — 'the TRAITOR for the upright'; the treacherous pays where the upright is spared. Treachery bears the ruin it courts.
uprightness — spared, the traitor given in its place
the upright for whom the traitor is given as ransom
set against the treachery ransomed for him
yashar — 'the traitor for the UPRIGHT'; the upright delivered while the treacherous pays. Integrity is preserved where treachery falls.
evaluation — a desert beats a home with a contentious wife
the judgement that a desert land is better than a house shared with a quarrelsome, fretful woman
welded to the strife it would escape
tob (better) — 'it is BETTER to live in a desert land than with a quarrelsome and fretful wife' (cf 21:9; 25:24); a barren wilderness beats a home full of strife. Peace outweighs comfort.
contention — the wife whose strife drives one to the desert
the quarreling/contention of the wife that makes even a desert preferable to home
welded to the vexing anger that goes with it
