midyan (quarrel/contention) — 'a QUARRELSOME wife'; incessant strife makes home unbearable (cf 21:9; 19:13). Contention exiles a man to the wilderness.
vexation — the fretful anger paired with the quarreling
the vexation/fretful anger of the wife, joined to her quarreling
welded to the contention it goes with
kaas (vexation/anger) — 'and FRETFUL woman'; the vexing, irritable anger that, with quarreling, makes a home a torment. Strife and vexation together.
self-justification — every way seems right to the man himself
the self-approval by which every man reckons his own way right
the heart God weighs, by contrast (265169)
set against the LORD who weighs the heart
yashar (right/straight) — 'every way of a man is RIGHT in his own eyes'; the near-universal self-justification (cf 16:2). Everyone thinks his own way right — the blindness of self-approval.
the heart — weighed by the LORD
the heart/motives that the LORD weighs, behind a man's self-approval
set against the man's self-justifying view
leb (heart) — 'the LORD weighs the HEART'; God assays the inner motives that a man's self-approval overlooks. The true test is God's weighing of the heart, not one's own eyes (cf 16:2; 24:12).
the wise man in whose dwelling precious treasure and oil are laid up and kept
set against the fool who consumes his store
chakam (wise) — 'precious treasure and oil are in the WISE man's dwelling'; the wise store and preserve, keeping a reserve. Prudence lays up; folly squanders.
folly — who devours his store instead of keeping it
the foolish man who devours/swallows up whatever he has, keeping nothing
set against the wise man who lays up treasure
kesil (fool) — 'but a FOOLISH man devours it'; the fool consumes all he has, saving nothing. Where the wise store, the fool swallows. Improvidence is folly's mark.
the righteousness that a man pursues, and by pursuing finds — righteousness rewarding its own pursuit
welded to the very righteousness the pursuit yields

tsedaqah (righteousness) — 'whoever pursues RIGHTEOUSNESS and kindness will find... righteousness'; the pursuit of righteousness is rewarded with righteousness itself. What you chase in the moral life you become.
the steadfast love/kindness that a man pursues together with righteousness, finding life and honor
welded to the righteousness it is sought with
chesed (steadfast love/kindness) — 'pursues righteousness and KINDNESS'; the loyal love pursued alongside righteousness. The good life is a pursuit of both right and love.
righteousness — found as the fruit of pursuing it
the righteousness a man finds as reward for pursuing righteousness and kindness
welded to the pursuit that earns it
tsedaqah — 'will find life, RIGHTEOUSNESS, and honor'; righteousness is both the road and the reward. The pursuit is self-fulfilling.
honor — found by the one who pursues righteousness
the honor a man finds as reward for pursuing righteousness and kindness
welded to the righteousness whose reward it is
kabod (honor/glory) — 'will find life, righteousness, and HONOR'; honor crowns the pursuit of righteousness. The moral quest ends in dignity, not just virtue.
wisdom — that overpowers might and its strongholds
the wise man who scales the mighty's city and brings down the stronghold of their confidence
set against the false confidence wisdom overthrows

chakam (wise) — 'a WISE man scales the city of the mighty and brings down the stronghold in which they trust' (cf 24:5; Eccl 9:16); wisdom outdoes brute strength, toppling what force and confidence had thought secure. Wisdom is mightier than might.
misplaced confidence — the mighty's trust in their stronghold, overthrown
the confidence/trust the mighty place in their stronghold, which the wise man brings down
set against the wisdom that overthrows it
mibtach (trust/confidence) — 'the STRONGHOLD in which they trust'; the mighty's confidence in their defences, undone by wisdom. Trust in strength is no match for wisdom.
self-restraint — guarding the mouth and tongue
the guarding/keeping of one's mouth and tongue that keeps a man from trouble
welded to the self it keeps safe
shamar (guard/keep) — 'whoever KEEPS his mouth and his tongue'; the disciplined guarding of speech. To watch the tongue is to guard the soul (cf 13:3; 18:21).
the self preserved — kept from trouble by guarded speech
the soul/self that a man keeps out of trouble by guarding his speech
the guarding of speech that saves it (265193)
welded to the tongue-keeping that preserves it
nephesh (soul/self) — 'keeps HIMSELF out of trouble'; the soul preserved by a guarded tongue. Restraint of speech is self-preservation.
scorn — the name earned by insolent pride
the scoffer — the name that belongs to the arrogant, haughty man who acts in overweening pride
the pride that earns the name (265206)
welded to the arrogant pride that defines him
luts (scoff/mock) — 'SCOFFER is the name of the arrogant, haughty man'; scorn is the fruit and name of pride. The scoffer is pride made a person.
insolence — the proud insolence that names the scoffer
the insolent arrogance that, with haughtiness, marks the man called a scoffer
welded to the haughty pride beside it
zed (insolent/proud) — 'the name of the ARROGANT, haughty man'; overbearing insolence, the substance of scorn. Arrogance and scoffing are one.
haughtiness — the proud loftiness paired with insolence
the haughty loftiness that, with arrogance, defines the scoffer
welded to the arrogance beside it
yahir (haughty/proud) — 'the arrogant, HAUGHTY man'; proud loftiness, twin of insolence in the scoffer. Height of self makes the scorner.
arrogance — the overweening pride in which the scoffer acts
the arrogance/presumption in which the scoffer acts, overflowing in pride
welded to the overflowing pride it expresses
zadon (arrogance/presumption) — 'who acts with ARROGANT pride'; presumptuous arrogance driving the scoffer's deeds. Scorn acts out of arrogance.
overweening pride — the overflowing pride of the scoffer's action
the overflowing, overweening pride in which the scoffer acts
welded to the scoffing it names
ebrah (overflow/arrogant pride) — 'acts with arrogant PRIDE'; the surging, overflowing pride that issues in scorn. Pride at flood is the scoffer's engine.
craving — the sluggard's desire that kills him
the craving/desire of the sluggard that kills him, because his hands refuse to labor
welded to the refusal to work that dooms it
taavah (desire/craving) — 'the DESIRE of the sluggard kills him'; the sluggard craves but will not work, and the unfulfilled craving destroys him. Want without labor is fatal.
sloth — whose craving kills because he will not work
the sluggard/lazy man whose desire kills him because his hands refuse to labor
welded to the refusal to labor
atsel (sluggard) — 'the desire of the SLUGGARD kills him'; sloth is a craving that will not lift a hand. The lazy man dies of his own unworked desire (cf 13:4; 20:4).
refusal — the sluggard's hands refuse to labor
the refusing of the sluggard's hands to labor, which turns his craving deadly
welded to the deadly desire it will not feed
maen (refuse/decline) — 'his hands REFUSE to labor'; the sluggard's refusal to work is the ground of his ruin. Desire he has; only labor he refuses.
insatiable craving — all day long the sluggard craves
the all-day craving of the sluggard, never satisfied and never acting
welded to the craving that redoubles it
avah (crave) — 'all day long he CRAVES and craves'; the sluggard's craving is ceaseless and empty. Endless want, no work.
insatiable craving — the redoubled desire that never acts
the redoubled craving of the sluggard, set against the righteous who gives
set against the righteous who gives instead of grasping
taavah (craving/desire) — 'craves and CRAVES'; the doubled, insatiable want of the sluggard, contrasted with the open-handed righteous. Grasping that never gives.
righteousness — who gives freely and does not hold back
the righteous man who gives and does not hold back, against the sluggard's endless craving
welded to the open-handed generosity that defines him
tsaddiq — 'but the RIGHTEOUS gives and does not hold back'; the righteous is open-handed where the sluggard only grasps. Generosity against craving.
generosity — the righteous gives and holds nothing back
the giving of the righteous, freely and without holding back, against the sluggard's grasping
the righteous whose act it is (265218)
welded to the righteousness that gives

natan (give) — 'the righteous GIVES and does not hold back'; open-handed generosity, the opposite of the sluggard's grasping craving. Emergent: the free giving of the righteous as the antithesis of insatiable want.
wickedness — whose very sacrifice is loathed
the wicked whose sacrifice is an abomination, worse still when brought with evil intent
the evil intent that worsens it (265228)
welded to the wicked scheme behind the offering
rasha — 'the sacrifice of the WICKED is an abomination'; the wicked man's worship is loathsome, for the heart behind it is corrupt (cf 15:8). Ritual cannot cleanse a wicked heart.
divine abhorrence — God loathes the wicked's sacrifice
the abhorrence with which God regards the sacrifice of the wicked
God's loathing of hollow, wicked worship
toebah (abomination) — 'is an ABOMINATION'; the wicked's sacrifice is loathsome to God. Locus external:god — the divine abhorrence of worship offered from a corrupt heart (cf 15:8; Isa 1:11-15).
wicked scheme — the corrupt purpose behind the offering
the evil intent/scheme with which the wicked brings his sacrifice, deepening its offence
welded to the wickedness whose scheme it is
zimmah (evil scheme/intent) — 'how much more when he brings it with EVIL INTENT'; the wicked scheme behind the sacrifice makes it doubly loathsome. Worship weaponised is worst of all.
falsehood — the lying witness who will perish
the falsehood of the lying witness, whose testimony (and he) will perish
set against the man who truly hears and endures
kazab (lie/falsehood) — 'a FALSE witness will perish'; the liar's word, and the liar, come to nothing. Falsehood has no future.
attentive truthfulness — the man who listens speaks enduringly
the man who truly hears/listens, whose word endures where the liar's perishes
set against the false witness who comes to nothing
shama (hear/listen) — 'but the word of a man who HEARS will endure'; the one who listens carefully speaks truth that lasts. Attentive truth outlives glib falsehood.
wickedness — who brazens out a bold face
the wicked man who puts on a brazen, defiant face instead of considering his way
set against the upright who weighs his ways
rasha — 'a WICKED man puts on a bold face'; the wicked masks his way with brazen effrontery. Where the upright reflects, the wicked bluffs.
brazenness — the wicked's hardened, defiant face
the making-bold/brazening of the wicked's face, a mask of defiant hardness
welded to the wickedness it fronts for
azaz (be strong/brazen) — 'puts on a BOLD face'; the wicked hardens his face in effrontery, presuming instead of considering. Brazenness in place of reflection.
uprightness — who gives thought to his ways
the upright man who gives careful thought to his ways rather than brazening them out
welded to the considered reflection that defines him
yashar (upright) — 'but the UPRIGHT gives thought to his ways'; the upright examines his path, where the wicked merely fronts. Reflection is the upright's way.
discernment — the upright considers his ways
the giving-thought/considering by which the upright examines and orders his ways
the upright whose reflection it is (265240)
welded to the uprightness that reflects
bin (discern/consider) — 'gives THOUGHT to his ways'; the upright's discerning consideration of his path, opposite the wicked's brazen face. He weighs where the wicked bluffs.
righteousness — the doing of which God prefers to sacrifice
the doing of righteousness that is more acceptable to the LORD than sacrifice
welded to justice as the twin conduct God prefers

tsedaqah (righteousness) — 'to do RIGHTEOUSNESS and justice is more acceptable to the LORD than sacrifice'; God prefers righteous conduct to ritual offering. The ethical over the ceremonial (cf 15:8; 1 Sam 15:22; Micah 6:6-8).
justice — the doing of which God prefers to sacrifice
the doing of justice that, with righteousness, God prefers to sacrifice
welded to righteousness as the twin conduct God prefers
mishpat (justice) — 'righteousness and JUSTICE'; just dealing, paired with righteousness, is what God desires above ritual. Right living outweighs right ritual.
preference — righteousness chosen by God over sacrifice
the being-chosen/preferred — God's choosing of righteous conduct over sacrifice
the divine preference for right conduct above ritual
bachar (choose/prefer) — 'is MORE ACCEPTABLE to the LORD than sacrifice'; God chooses righteous action over offering. The read holds God's own preference — mercy and justice above ceremony.
human wisdom — impotent against the LORD
the human wisdom that, however great, cannot avail or stand against the LORD
welded to the understanding equally helpless before God
chokmah (wisdom) — 'no WISDOM... can avail against the LORD'; even the highest human wisdom is powerless before God's purpose. Man's best wisdom bows to divine sovereignty (cf 19:21; 16:9).
human understanding — helpless before the LORD
the human understanding that cannot prevail or stand against the LORD
welded to the counsel equally powerless before God
tebunah (understanding) — 'no UNDERSTANDING... against the LORD'; human insight is no counterweight to God. Discernment cannot overrule the Almighty.
human counsel — cannot stand against the LORD
the human counsel/plan that cannot avail or stand against the LORD
the wisdom and understanding beside it (265252)
welded to the wisdom and understanding equally vain before God
etsah (counsel/plan) — 'no COUNSEL can avail against the LORD'; human planning is vain before God's will. No scheme outwits the Almighty (cf 19:21).
the haughtiness of lofty, proud eyes that look down on others
welded to the proud heart as the twin pride
rum (high/lofty) — 'HAUGHTY eyes and a proud heart'; the lofty look of the proud, sin in itself. Emergent: haughtiness of eyes as an outward mark of the proud heart (cf 6:17).
the proud heart — sin in itself
the proud/broad heart that, with haughty eyes, is sin — the very 'lamp' of the wicked
welded to the haughty eyes as the twin pride
leb (heart) with rachab (broad/proud) — 'and a PROUD heart'; the swollen, self-exalting heart. Pride of heart is sin, the inner root of the haughty look.
the wicked whose very lamp — their life, prosperity, guiding light — is sin itself
welded to the sin their whole life amounts to
rasha — 'the lamp of the WICKED'; the wicked's guiding light — their whole prospering life — is nothing but sin. Not just their deeds but their very being is sinful.
sin — what haughty eyes, proud heart, and the wicked's lamp all are
the sin that haughty eyes, a proud heart, and the very lamp of the wicked all amount to
the wicked whose lamp it is (265264)
welded to the wickedness it defines
chattah (sin) — 'are SIN'; pride of eye and heart, and the wicked's whole way of life, are sin. The verse names pride itself — not just its acts — as sin.
planning — the diligent's careful plans lead to abundance
the plans/purposes of the diligent, carefully made, that lead surely to abundance
(the hasty who come to poverty, by contrast)
the careful planning of the diligent set against reckless haste
machashabah (plan/purpose) — 'the PLANS of the diligent lead surely to abundance'; careful, diligent planning yields plenty, where haste brings only want. Diligence plans; folly rushes.
falsehood — the lying tongue that amasses fleeting treasure
the lying tongue by which a man gets treasures — a fleeting vapour and a snare of death
welded to the deadly pursuit of wealth by lies

sheqer (falsehood) — 'the getting of treasures by a LYING tongue is a fleeting vapour and a snare of death'; wealth amassed by lies vanishes like vapour and ensnares to death. Deceitful gain is deadly and empty.
pursuit — the seeking of treasure by falsehood, deadly and empty
the getting/seeking of treasures by a lying tongue, which proves a vapour and a death-snare
the lying tongue that drives it (265276)
welded to the falsehood that pursues it
baqash (seek/get) — 'the GETTING of treasures'; the pursuit of wealth by deceit, which is fleeting vapour and a snare of death. Ill-gotten pursuit ends in ruin.
wickedness — swept away by their own violence
the wicked whose own violence sweeps them away, because they refuse justice
the wicked destroyed by the violence they choose
rasha — 'the VIOLENCE of the wicked will sweep them away'; the wicked are dragged off by their own violence. Their evil recoils on them.
refusal — the wicked refuse to do what is just
the refusing/declining of the wicked to do what is just, which brings their ruin
welded to the justice they will not do
maen (refuse/decline) — 'because they REFUSE to do what is just'; the wicked's deliberate refusal of justice is the ground of their destruction. Ruin follows the refusal of right.
justice — which the wicked refuse to do
the justice/right that the wicked refuse to do, and so are swept away
welded to the refusal that dooms them
mishpat (justice) — 'to do what is JUST'; the justice the wicked will not do. To refuse right is to invite ruin.
guilt — the guilty, whose way is crooked
the guilt-laden man whose way is twisted and crooked
welded to the twisted way it takes
vazar (guilty/laden with guilt) — 'the way of the GUILTY is crooked'; the guilt-burdened walk a twisted path. Guilt bends the way.
crookedness — the guilty man's twisted way
the crooked/twisted way of the guilty, bent away from the straight
welded to the guilt whose way it is
hafakpak (crooked/perverse) — 'is CROOKED'; the twisted, devious way of the guilty. Emergent: crookedness of way as the mark of the guilt-laden, against the upright conduct of the pure.
purity — the pure, whose conduct is upright
the pure man whose conduct is straight and upright
welded to the straight conduct it produces
zak (pure/clean) — 'the conduct of the PURE is upright'; purity of heart shows in straight conduct. The clean walk straight.
uprightness — the pure man's straight conduct
the upright, straight conduct of the pure man
welded to the purity it expresses
yashar (upright) — 'is UPRIGHT'; the straight conduct of the pure, the antithesis of the guilty's crooked way. Character shows in the way.
evaluation — a rooftop corner beats sharing with a quarrelsome wife
the judgement that solitude in a rooftop corner is better than a house shared with a contentious wife
welded to the contention it flees

tob (better) — 'it is BETTER to live in a corner of the housetop than in a house shared with a quarrelsome wife' (cf 21:19; 25:24); peaceful solitude beats a comfortable house full of strife. Peace is worth more than space.
contention — the quarrelsome wife who makes home unbearable
the quarreling/contention of a wife that makes a shared house worse than a rooftop corner
welded to the peace one flees to escape it
midyan (quarrel/contention) — 'a QUARRELSOME wife'; incessant strife makes a home unbearable (cf 19:13; 27:15). Contention drives a man to the roof.
reputation — a good name, more to be chosen than riches
the good name/reputation that is to be chosen rather than great riches
welded to the valuing that prefers it to wealth

shem (name/reputation) — 'a good NAME is to be chosen rather than great riches'; a sound reputation, earned by character, outweighs wealth. What men think of your integrity is worth more than what you own (cf Eccl 7:1).
valuing — preferring a good name to great riches
the choosing/preferring of a good name over great riches — the value-judgement that prizes character above wealth
welded to the reputation it prefers to wealth
bachar (choose) — 'is to be CHOSEN rather than great riches'; the deliberate valuing of reputation above wealth. Wisdom weighs a good name heavier than gold.
esteem — grace/favour better than silver or gold
the favour/esteem/grace that is better than silver or gold
welded to the judgement that ranks it above wealth
chen (favour/grace) — 'and FAVOUR is better than silver or gold'; the esteem and goodwill of others outweighs riches. To be well-regarded is worth more than to be wealthy.
evaluation — favour ranked above silver and gold
the judgement that favour is better than silver or gold — esteem preferred to riches
welded to the esteem it ranks above wealth
tob (better) — 'favour is BETTER than silver or gold'; the value-judgement that prizes esteem over wealth, parallel to preferring a good name to riches. The intangible goods outrank the material.
scorn — the source of strife, whose removal brings peace
the scoffer whose presence breeds strife, and whose removal ends contention and abuse
welded to the contention that leaves with him
luts (scoff/mock) — 'drive out a SCOFFER, and strife will go out'; the scorner is the engine of conflict; remove him and peace returns. Contention has a face — the mocker's (cf 26:20).
contention — that departs when the scoffer is driven out
the strife/contention that goes out the moment the scoffer is removed
welded to the scorner whose exit ends it
madon (strife/contention) — 'and STRIFE will go out'; the conflict the scoffer generates, leaving with him. Drive out the source and the strife follows.
dispute — that ceases with the scoffer's removal
the quarreling/dispute that ceases when the scoffer is driven out
welded to the contention it goes with
din (dispute/quarrel) — 'and QUARRELING... will cease'; the litigious wrangling that dies once the scorner is gone. Emergent: quarreling as part of the scoffer's train of conflict.
reviling — the shame and insult that cease with the scoffer
the abuse/reviling and dishonour that cease when the scoffer is removed
welded to the dispute it goes with
qalon (shame/dishonour/abuse) — 'and abuse will CEASE'; the shaming insults that end with the scorner's departure. Remove the mocker and reviling stops.
the loving of purity of heart, joined to gracious speech, that wins the king's friendship
welded to the pure heart it prizes
aheb (love) — 'he who LOVES purity of heart'; the affection set on inner cleanness. To love a pure heart is to be drawn toward it. Where love goes, character follows.
purity of heart — loved, and joined to gracious speech
the purity/cleanness of heart that a man loves, which with gracious speech wins favour
welded to the heart whose purity it is
tahor (pure/clean) — 'PURITY of heart'; inner cleanness of the heart, the object of the good man's love. A clean heart, not mere clean hands (cf Ps 24:4; Matt 5:8).
the heart — the seat whose purity is loved
the heart, the inner seat whose purity the good man loves and cultivates
welded to the cleanness that fills it
leb (heart) — 'purity of HEART'; the inner seat that must be pure. The heart is the ground; purity is what it must bear.
graciousness — gracious speech that wins the king's friendship
the graciousness/grace of speech that, with a pure heart, wins the king as friend
the purity it is paired with (265320)
welded to the pure heart it accompanies

chen (grace/favour) — 'and whose speech is GRACIOUS, will have the king as his friend'; gracious lips joined to a pure heart win the highest favour. Inner purity and gracious words together commend a man.
knowledge — kept and preserved under the LORD's watch
the knowledge that the eyes of the LORD watch over and preserve, against the traitor's words he overthrows
the traitor whose words are overthrown (265332)
set against the treachery the LORD undoes
daath (knowledge) — 'the eyes of the LORD keep watch over KNOWLEDGE'; true knowledge is guarded by God, while treachery is overthrown. God preserves the truth and undoes the liar.
divine overthrow — the LORD frustrates the traitor's words
the overthrowing by which the LORD frustrates and ruins the words of the treacherous
the divine act that undoes treachery
salaph (overthrow/subvert) — 'but he OVERTHROWS the words of the traitor'; God frustrates the treacherous. Locus external:god — the divine overthrow that answers the LORD's watch over knowledge.
treachery — whose words the LORD overthrows
the treacherous man whose words the LORD overthrows, against the knowledge he preserves
welded to the divine overthrow of his words
bagad (deal treacherously) — 'but he overthrows the words of the TRAITOR'; the treacherous, whose plans God frustrates. Treachery is undone by the God who watches.
evasive sloth — the lazy man inventing dangers to avoid work
the sluggard who says 'there is a lion outside!' — sloth so inventive in evasion that it conjures imaginary dangers to justify staying idle, laziness rationalising itself with absurd fears
the laziness that invents perils rather than go to work

atsel (sluggard) — 'the SLUGGARD says, 'there is a lion outside!'' (22:13; cf 26:13); sloth is fertile in excuses, conjuring imaginary lions to avoid the street and the work. The lazy mind invents dangers where there are none.
seduction — whose flattering mouth is a deep pit
the forbidden/strange woman whose seductive mouth is a deep pit into which a man falls
the divine anger that abandons a man to her (265344)
welded to the judgement that lets a man fall into her pit

zur (strange/forbidden) — 'the MOUTH of forbidden women is a deep pit'; the seductress's flattering speech is a deadly trap (cf 2:16; 5:3; 7:21). Emergent: seduction as a pit that swallows the unwary.
divine displeasure — the LORD's wrath dooms a man to fall
the indignation/displeasure of the LORD, under which a man is abandoned to fall into the seductress's pit
welded to the seduction he is given over to

zaam (be indignant/angry) — 'he with whom the LORD is ANGRY will fall into it'; divine displeasure gives a man over to the trap. Locus external:god — God's judicial anger that abandons the reprobate to the seductress (cf Rom 1:24-28).
innate folly — bound up in the heart of a child
the folly bound up in the heart of a child, native to it until driven out
the discipline that drives it out (265353)
set against the corrective rod that expels it
ivveleth (folly) — 'FOLLY is bound up in the heart of a child'; folly is native to the child's heart, not merely learned. The bent to foolishness is inborn and must be corrected (cf 13:24; 29:15).
corrective discipline — the rod that drives folly far
the rod of discipline/correction that drives the child's bound-up folly far from him
set against the innate folly it drives out
musar (discipline/instruction) — 'but the rod of DISCIPLINE drives it far from him'; loving correction expels the folly the heart was born with. Discipline is folly's cure.
exploitation — grinding the poor for one's own gain
the oppressing of the poor to increase one's own wealth — self-enrichment by exploitation, which ends in poverty
welded to the self-serving giving to the rich

ashaq (oppress/exploit) — 'whoever OPPRESSES the poor to increase his own wealth... will only come to poverty'; grinding the weak for gain, like flattering the rich, ends in loss. Greed that exploits defeats itself.
sycophancy — giving to the rich for advantage
the giving to the rich (already full), a self-serving flattery that, like oppressing the poor, ends in poverty
welded to the exploiting of the poor
natan (give) — 'or GIVES to the rich, will only come to poverty'; currying favour with the wealthy is as self-defeating as robbing the poor. Both are greed's miscalculation.
attentive listening — inclining the ear to the words of the wise
the attentive hearing/listening — inclining the ear to take in the words of the wise
welded to the applied heart that receives with it
shama (hear/listen) — 'incline your ear, and HEAR the words of the wise'; the receptive listening that wisdom requires. To learn, first bend the ear (opening the 'words of the wise', 22:17-24:22).
wisdom — whose words are to be heard and taken in
the wise, whose words the learner is to hear and lay to heart
the source whose words the learner receives
chakam (wise) — 'hear the words of the WISE'; the sages whose sayings are to be received. Wisdom speaks; the learner must listen.
application — setting the heart on knowledge
the applying/setting of the heart on knowledge — inward engagement, not mere hearing
welded to the attentive ear that hears with it
leb (heart) — 'and apply your HEART to my knowledge'; wisdom is received not by ear alone but by the engaged heart. Learning is inward attention, not passive hearing.
delight — the sweetness of wisdom kept within
the pleasantness/delight of the wise words when they are kept within and ready on the lips
welded to the inward retention that makes it sweet
naem (be pleasant/sweet) — 'for it will be PLEASANT if you keep them within you'; wisdom retained is a delight, not a burden. The words treasured inwardly become sweet (cf 2:10; 24:13-14).
retention — keeping the wise words within, ready on the lips
the keeping/treasuring of the wise words within, so they are ready on the lips
welded to the sweetness inward keeping yields
shamar (keep/guard) — 'if you KEEP them within you, if all of them are ready on your lips'; wisdom must be stored in the heart and kept ready for speech. Retained within, it rises to the lips.
trust in God — the very aim of the instruction
the trust/confidence in the LORD that is the whole aim of the wise instruction
welded to the teaching given to produce it

mibtach (trust/confidence) — 'that your TRUST may be in the LORD, I have made them known'; the goal of wisdom-teaching is trust in God, not mere cleverness. All the sayings aim at a heart resting on the LORD (cf 3:5).
instruction — imparting wisdom to ground trust in the LORD
the making-known/imparting of the wise words, given expressly so that the learner's trust may rest in the LORD
welded to the confidence in God it is meant to build
yada (make known) — 'I have made them KNOWN to you today, even to you'; the teacher imparts wisdom with a purpose — that the learner may trust God. Instruction is aimed at faith.
wealth — meeting the poor as fellow-creatures of one Maker
the rich man who meets the poor on common ground, both made by the same LORD
the poor he meets as equal (265390)
welded to the poor with whom he shares one Maker

ashir (rich) — 'the RICH and the poor meet together'; wealth confers no difference of origin — rich and poor share one Maker. Emergent: riches levelled by common creation. Wealth is no ground for pride before God.
poverty — meeting the rich as fellow-creature of one Maker
the poor man who meets the rich on common ground, both made by the same LORD
the rich he meets as equal (265389)
welded to the rich with whom he shares one Maker
rush (be poor) — 'the rich and the POOR meet together; the LORD is the Maker of them all'; poverty is no mark of lesser worth — the poor share the rich man's Maker. Common creation levels the ranks.
counsel — the wise guidance of the thirty sayings
the counsel/wise guidance written in the thirty sayings, joined with knowledge
welded to the knowledge it is paired with
moetsah (counsel) — 'thirty sayings of COUNSEL and knowledge'; the practical guidance of the sages, set down for the learner. Wisdom offers counsel for living.
knowledge — the sound understanding of the thirty sayings
the knowledge/sound understanding written in the thirty sayings, joined with counsel
welded to the counsel it is paired with
daath (knowledge) — 'thirty sayings of counsel and KNOWLEDGE'; the reliable understanding the sayings impart, paired with counsel. Wisdom is both guidance and grasp.
knowing truth — being made to know what is right and true
the coming-to-know what is right and true, the purpose of the wise instruction
the certainty of truth it grasps (265403)
welded to the sure rightness it takes hold of
yada (know) — 'to make you KNOW what is right and true'; wisdom's aim is sure knowledge of truth, that a man may stand on solid ground. To know the truth is to be able to answer.
certainty of truth — knowing what is sure and reliable
the rightness/certainty of the truth that the learner is made to know — sure and dependable words
welded to the knowledge that lays hold of it
qoshet (truth/certainty) — 'what is RIGHT and true'; the sureness and reliability of the truth taught. Wisdom gives not opinion but certainty.
truthful reply — answering truly those who sent you
the true/faithful answer a man can give to those who sent him, because he knows the certain truth
welded to the sure knowledge that grounds it
emet (truth/faithfulness) — 'that you may give a TRUE answer to those who sent you'; sure knowledge issues in a trustworthy reply. Emergent: the truthful answer as the fruit of knowing certain truth.
oppression — crushing the afflicted at the gate
the crushing/oppressing of the afflicted at the gate — exploiting the weak where they should find justice
welded to the humble poor it oppresses
daka (crush/oppress) — 'or CRUSH the afflicted at the gate'; oppressing the weak in the very place of justice is forbidden. To grind the helpless is to invite God's own vengeance (22:23).
the humble poor — not to be crushed at the gate
the afflicted/humble poor who must not be crushed, defenceless at the gate
the crushing they must be spared (265414)
welded to the oppression forbidden against them
ani (afflicted/humble) — 'nor crush the AFFLICTED at the gate'; the lowly and defenceless, whom the powerful are forbidden to exploit. Their weakness is God's concern.
divine advocacy — the LORD takes up the cause of the poor
the pleading/contending by which the LORD takes up the cause of the oppressed poor and requites their robbers
welded to the poor's plea he takes as his own

rib (plead/contend) — 'for the LORD will PLEAD their cause'; God himself is the advocate of the exploited poor, pressing their case and avenging them. Locus external:god — the divine defender of the defenceless (cf 23:11; Ps 68:5).
the poor's plea — championed by the LORD himself
the cause/plea of the oppressed poor, which the LORD takes up as his own and vindicates
welded to the divine advocacy that champions it
rib (cause/dispute) — 'the LORD will plead their CAUSE'; the case of the wronged poor, which becomes God's own. The plea of the helpless is heard in heaven.
hot temper — the man given to anger, no fit friend
the anger/hot temper of the man with whom one is warned not to make friendship
welded to the wrathful temper it goes with
aph (anger/nostril) — 'make no friendship with a man given to ANGER'; the hot-tempered man is a dangerous companion, his anger contagious. Choose friends by their temper (cf 15:18; 29:22).
wrath — the wrathful man whose company is to be shunned
the wrath/hot fury of the man one is warned not to accompany
welded to the hot temper it goes with
chemah (wrath/hot fury) — 'nor go with a WRATHFUL man'; the man of fury is to be avoided, lest his ways rub off. Bad temper is caught by keeping bad company.
imperilled self — the soul entangled by learning the angry man's ways
the soul/self that becomes ensnared through learning the angry man's ways — the peril of imitation
the self caught in the trap of a bad companion's temper

nephesh (soul/self) — 'lest you learn his ways and entangle YOURSELF in a snare'; keeping the angry man's company, one learns his temper and the soul is trapped. Companionship shapes the soul — and can ensnare it (cf 13:20; 1 Cor 15:33).
prudence — foreseeing danger and taking cover
the prudent man who sees danger coming and hides himself from it
set against the naive who walk heedlessly into harm
arum (prudent/shrewd) — 'the PRUDENT sees danger and hides himself' (cf 27:12); foresight perceives trouble and takes cover. Prudence is danger seen in time.
naivety — blundering on into harm unheeded
the naive who go blindly on and suffer for it, seeing no danger
set against the foresight that hides from harm
pethi (simple/naive) — 'but the SIMPLE go on and suffer for it'; the naive see no danger and walk into it. Heedlessness is folly's cost.
humility — rewarded, joined to the fear of the LORD
the humility that, with the fear of the LORD, brings riches, honour, and life
the fear of the LORD beside it (265452)
welded to the reverent fear it goes with

anavah (humility) — 'the reward for HUMILITY and the fear of the LORD is riches and honour and life'; lowliness before God, twinned with reverent fear, is the root of true reward. Humility and the fear of God together open life.
reverent fear — joined to humility, the root of blessing
the reverent fear of the LORD that, with humility, brings riches, honour, and life
welded to the lowliness it goes with
yirah (fear/reverence) — 'and the FEAR of the LORD'; reverent awe of God, paired with humility, as the source of blessing. The fear of the LORD is the beginning of every good.
perversity — whose way is set with thorns and snares
the crooked/perverse man in whose way thorns and snares lie, the fruit of his twisted path
set against the vigilant who keep far from such a way

iqqesh (crooked/perverse) — 'thorns and snares are in the way of the CROOKED'; perversity plants its own path with traps. Emergent: the crooked way self-ensnaring, against the guarded soul that keeps clear.
vigilance — guarding the soul to keep far from harm
the guarding/watching over one's soul that keeps a man far from the thorns and snares of the crooked way
welded to the soul it keeps safe
shamar (guard/keep) — 'whoever GUARDS his soul will keep far from them'; watchful care of the soul keeps one clear of the crooked's traps. Vigilance is self-preservation.
the self kept safe — guarded far from the snares
the soul/self that the vigilant man guards, keeping it far from thorns and snares
welded to the vigilance that preserves it
nephesh (soul/self) — 'whoever guards his SOUL will keep far'; the soul preserved by watchful care. To guard the soul is to escape the crooked's traps.
the durability of early training — the trained way not departed from in age

the not-departing, even in old age, from the way in which a child was trained — the enduring formation of early character, the ingrained path that holds fast through a lifetime because it was set in youth
(the way he was trained in, which he keeps)
the lasting hold of a way instilled early, kept even to old age

sur (turn aside/depart), negated — 'even when he is old he will not DEPART from it' (22:6); character formed early endures. What is trained into a child in the way he should go holds fast through life. Early formation shapes the whole course.
wealth-as-power — the rich rule over the poor
the rich who, by wealth, rule and hold power over the poor
set against the poor subjected by their wealth

ashir (rich) — 'the RICH rules over the poor'; wealth confers power, and the poor fall under it. Emergent: riches as dominion — an observation of how wealth bends the social order (cf 22:2's levelling before God).
subjection — the poor ruled by the rich, the debtor enslaved
the poor who are ruled by the rich, as the borrower is slave to the lender
set against the wealth that dominates them
rush (be poor) — 'the rich rules over the POOR, and the borrower is the slave of the lender'; poverty and debt bring servitude. The proverb marks, soberly, the bondage that want and borrowing impose.
injustice — sown, it reaps a harvest of calamity
the injustice/wrong a man sows, which reaps calamity in its harvest
welded to the ruin its sowing brings
avel (injustice/wrong) — 'whoever sows INJUSTICE will reap calamity'; wrongdoing is a seed whose harvest is ruin. What injustice plants, it must reap (cf Gal 6:7; Hos 8:7).
ruin — the harvest reaped from sown injustice
the calamity/trouble reaped as the harvest of sown injustice
welded to the wrong whose harvest it is
aven (trouble/iniquity) — 'will reap CALAMITY'; the ruinous harvest of injustice. The wrong a man sows returns to him as disaster.
spent wrath — the rod of the unjust man's fury will fail
the fury/wrath whose rod, wielded by the unjust, will fail and come to nothing
welded to the wrongdoing whose passion it is
ebrah (fury/overflowing wrath) — 'and the rod of his FURY will fail'; the unjust man's angry power spends itself and collapses. Wrath wielded in injustice has no lasting force.
generosity — the good eye that is blessed
the bountiful/good eye — the generous disposition that shares and so is blessed
welded to the giving of bread it produces

tob (good) + ayin (eye) — 'whoever has a BOUNTIFUL eye will be blessed'; the 'good eye' is Hebrew idiom for generosity (opp. the 'evil eye' of 23:6; 28:22). A generous disposition draws down blessing.
giving — sharing his bread with the poor
the sharing/giving of bread with the poor, in which the bountiful eye is expressed
the good eye whose act it is (265488)
welded to the generous disposition that gives
natan (give) — 'for he SHARES his bread with the poor'; generosity in act — the good eye opens the hand. Emergent: the sharing of bread as the outworking of a bountiful heart.
discernment — carefully weighing what is before you at a ruler's table
the careful observing/discerning of what is set before one when dining with a ruler — alert self-awareness in a place of danger
the emphatic care that sharpens it (265500)
welded to the diligence that makes the discernment keen

bin (discern/consider) — 'when you sit down to eat with a ruler, OBSERVE carefully what is before you'; dining with the powerful calls for wary discernment, not appetite. Watch yourself where a slip is costly (cf 23:2).
diligent discernment — the emphatic care of the wary guest
the diligent, emphatic care (the doubled 'discern-discern') with which the wise guest weighs his situation before a ruler
welded to the discernment it sharpens
bin (doubled, emphatic) — 'observe CAREFULLY'; the Hebrew doubles the verb for emphasis — discern well, be doubly alert. Watchful care, not casual ease, at the ruler's table.
divine Redeemer — the strong kinsman-defender of the fatherless
the Redeemer — the LORD as the strong kinsman-defender of the fatherless, who takes up their case against any who wrong them
welded to the orphans' plea he makes his own

goel (redeemer/kinsman-avenger) — 'for their REDEEMER is strong'; God himself is the mighty next-of-kin of the fatherless, obliged to avenge their wrong. Locus external:god — the divine defender of the defenceless (cf 22:23; Ex 22:22-24).
divine advocacy — the LORD contends for the fatherless against their wrongers
the pleading/contending by which the strong Redeemer takes up the fatherless's cause against those who would rob them
welded to the orphans' cause he presses

rib (plead/contend) — 'he will PLEAD their cause against you'; the mighty Redeemer presses the case of the fatherless against their oppressor. Locus external:god — God as advocate, contending for the weak (cf 22:23).
the fatherless's plea — championed by the strong Redeemer
the cause/plea of the fatherless, which their strong Redeemer takes up as his own and presses against their oppressor
welded to the divine advocacy that champions it
rib (cause/dispute) — 'he will plead their CAUSE against you'; the case of the wronged orphan becomes God's own suit. The plea of the defenceless is answered from heaven.
application — setting the heart on instruction
the applying/setting of the heart to instruction, with the ear to words of knowledge — inward engagement with teaching
welded to the knowledge the ear receives with it
leb (heart) — 'apply your HEART to instruction'; wisdom is received by the engaged heart, not the passing ear. Set the inner self on what is taught (cf 22:17).
knowledge — the words of knowledge the ear is bent to
the words of knowledge to which the learner bends his ear, joined to the heart applied to instruction
welded to the heart set on instruction
daath (knowledge) — 'and your ear to words of KNOWLEDGE'; the sound understanding the learner takes in. Heart and ear together receive it.
correction — not to be withheld from a child
the discipline/correction that must not be withheld from a child — loving firmness, not cruelty, that does him no lasting harm
the corrective firmness the child needs

musar (discipline/instruction) — 'do not withhold DISCIPLINE from a child; if you strike him with a rod, he will not die'; correction firmly given is love, not harm. To spare the rod is to fail the child (cf 13:24; 22:15).
deliverance — discipline rescues the child from death
the saving/delivering of the child's soul from Sheol by discipline — correction that snatches him from ruin
welded to the child's life it delivers
natsal (deliver/rescue) — 'you will SAVE his soul from Sheol'; discipline is deliverance, pulling the child back from the path of death. Firm love saves a life.
the child's life — rescued from Sheol by discipline
the soul/life of the child, which timely discipline delivers from Sheol — correction as rescue, not injury
welded to the saving from death that discipline works
nephesh (soul/life) — 'you will save his SOUL from Sheol'; loving discipline is life-saving, turning a child from the road to death. The rod that corrects rescues the soul (cf 23:13).
the son's heart — its wisdom the father's joy
the son's heart, whose wisdom is the very thing that gladdens the father — the inner life of the child as the parent's deepest concern
welded to the wisdom that makes it glad news
leb (heart) — 'if your HEART is wise'; the father's joy hangs not on the son's success but on his wise heart. The inner life of the child is what a parent most longs to see right.
wisdom — the son's, which gladdens his father's heart
the wisdom of the son's heart, which reaches across and gladdens the father's own heart
welded to the father's joy it produces
chakam (be wise) — 'if your heart is WISE, my heart too will be glad'; the son's wisdom is a joy that passes into the father. A child's wise heart is a parent's gladness.
the father's heart — gladdened by the son's wisdom
the father's own heart, gladdened through and through by the wisdom of his son's heart
welded to the joy that floods it
leb (heart) — 'my HEART too will be glad'; the father's heart answers the son's — the two joined in the son's wisdom. Parental joy is heart answering heart.
gladness — the father's joy at his son's wisdom
the gladness/joy that floods the father's heart when his son's heart proves wise
the son's wisdom that stirs it (265534)
welded to the wise heart that causes it
samach (be glad) — 'my heart too will be GLAD'; the deep gladness a wise child brings a parent. No gift a son gives gladdens like a wise heart.
the deepest self — that exults at the son's right words
the inmost being/kidneys — the father's very deepest self, which exults when his son's lips speak what is right
welded to the exultation that floods it
kilyah (kidneys/inmost being) — 'my INMOST BEING will exult'; the deepest seat of the father's feeling responds to his son's uprightness. Joy at a child's right speech reaches the very core.
exultation — the father's deep joy at his son's upright speech
the exulting/rejoicing of the father's inmost being when his son's lips speak what is right
the right words that stir it (265543)
welded to the son's upright speech that causes it
alaz (exult/rejoice) — 'my inmost being will EXULT when your lips speak what is right'; the father's core leaps for joy at his son's right words. Uprightness in a child is exultation to a parent.
uprightness — the son's lips speaking what is right
the upright, right speech of the son's lips, which makes the father's inmost being exult
welded to the deep joy it stirs in the father
meshar (uprightness/what is right) — 'when your lips speak what is RIGHT'; the son's upright words are the father's joy. Right speech reveals a right heart, and gladdens those who love it.
the heart — guarded against envy of sinners
the heart that must be guarded from envying sinners, kept instead in the fear of the LORD
the envy it must not feel (265546)
welded to the envying it is warned against
leb (heart) — 'let not your HEART envy sinners'; the battleground is the heart, tempted to envy the wicked's ease. Guard the heart from resentful longing.
envy — the heart's forbidden longing after sinners' lot
the envying/jealous longing of the heart toward sinners and their apparent prosperity — the very thing forbidden
set against the fear of the LORD that is its cure
qana (envy/be jealous) — 'let not your heart ENVY sinners'; to envy the wicked their ease is a snare, for their end is ruin (cf 24:1, 19; Ps 73). Envy of sinners forgets the fear of the LORD.
the wicked — envied for their ease, not to be
the sinners whose apparent prosperity tempts the heart to envy, though their end is ruin
welded to the forbidden longing they stir
chatta (sinner) — 'let not your heart envy SINNERS'; the wicked, whose seeming success baits envy. Their prosperity is a mirage the fear of God dispels.
reverence — the day-long alternative to envying sinners
the fear of the LORD in which one is to continue all the day, the cure for and antithesis of envying sinners
set against the envy of sinners it replaces
yirah (fear/reverence) — 'but continue in the FEAR of the LORD all the day'; reverent awe of God, held all day long, drives out envy of the wicked. Fill the heart with God and envy finds no room.
enduring hope — the assurance of a future that will not be cut off

the hope of the one who keeps the fear of the LORD — the assurance that there is a future and that his hope will not be cut off, an expectation grounded not in circumstance but in God's ordering of the end
the confident expectation that the God-fearer's end is secure

tiqvah (hope) — 'surely there is a future, and your HOPE will not be cut off' (23:18; cf 24:14); the fear of the LORD (23:17) grounds a hope that endures. The God-fearer's expectation of a good end is sure, where the wicked's hope perishes.
heeding — the son called to hear and be wise
the hearing/heeding by which the son is summoned to receive wisdom and set his course
welded to the wisdom hearing leads to
shama (hear/listen) — 'HEAR, my son, and be wise'; the first step to wisdom is a listening ear. Heed the father, and wisdom follows.
wisdom — that the son is to grow in by hearing
the wisdom the son is to gain by hearing, which then directs his heart in the right way
the hearing that leads to it (265559)
welded to the heeding that yields it
chakam (be wise) — 'and be WISE'; the wisdom that hearing opens to, which then steers the heart. Listen, and become wise.
steering — guiding the heart in the right way
the directing/guiding of one's heart into the right way — wisdom applied to set the inner course
welded to the heart it guides
ashar (go straight/direct) — 'and DIRECT your heart in the way'; wisdom is not passive but steers the heart onto the right road. Guide the inner life, do not let it drift.
the heart — to be directed in the way
the heart that the son must actively direct and keep in the right way
welded to the guiding that keeps it on the road
leb (heart) — 'direct your HEART in the way'; the heart is the thing to be steered — kept on the right road by wisdom. Where the heart is aimed, the life goes.
gluttonous craving — to be checked as with a knife to the throat
the appetite/greed of the throat that, unchecked, endangers a man at the ruler's table — to be curbed as drastically as a knife held to the throat
the craving that self-control must violently curb

nephesh (appetite/throat/desire) — 'put a knife to your throat if you are given to APPETITE'; gluttonous craving must be checked with violent resolve. Where appetite rules, self-mastery must intervene sharply (cf 23:1).
intemperance — the company of drunkards to be shunned
the drunkenness/heavy drinking of those the son is warned not to join — dissipation that wastes body and soul
welded to the gluttonous excess it keeps company with

soba + yayin (heavy drinkers of wine) — 'be not among DRUNKARDS'; the intemperate given to wine, whose company drags a man to poverty and ruin (23:21). Emergent: drunkenness as dissipation to be shunned.
gluttony — the greedy excess of the flesh-glutton
the gluttonous, greedy eating of the flesh-glutton, twin of drunkenness in the life of dissipation
welded to the drunkenness it keeps company with

zalal (be a glutton/worthless) — 'or among GLUTTONOUS eaters of meat'; unchecked appetite for food, paired with drink, marks the dissipated life. Emergent: gluttony as intemperance, ruinous like drunkenness.
filial heeding — to the father who gave one life
the listening/heeding of the son to the father who gave him life — the honour of attending to a parent's word
set against the contempt for a parent it excludes
shama (hear/listen) — 'LISTEN to your father who gave you life'; filial reverence heeds the parent whose gift is one's very life. To honour father and mother is to hear them (cf Ex 20:12).
contempt — not to be shown a mother grown old
the despising/contempt that must not be shown one's mother when she is old — the filial sin of scorning the aged parent
set against the listening reverence owed a parent
buz (despise/scorn) — 'and do not DESPISE your mother when she is old'; to hold an aged parent in contempt is a grievous filial sin. Age in a mother calls for honour, not scorn.
truth — to be bought at any cost, never sold
the truth that is to be bought at any price and never sold — held as beyond all barter
welded to the wisdom it is acquired alongside
emet (truth) — 'buy TRUTH, and do not sell it'; truth is to be acquired whatever it costs and parted with never. It is priceless, and once gained, kept.
wisdom — among the goods to be bought and kept
the wisdom that, with instruction and understanding, is to be bought and never sold
welded to the instruction it is gained with
chokmah (wisdom) — 'buy WISDOM'; wisdom is worth every cost to acquire. With truth, instruction, and understanding, it is a possession never to be surrendered.
instruction — among the goods to be bought and kept
the instruction/discipline that, with wisdom and understanding, is to be bought and held fast
welded to the understanding it is gained with
musar (instruction/discipline) — 'INSTRUCTION'; the corrective teaching to be acquired with wisdom. Part of the priceless store never to be sold.
understanding — among the goods to be bought and kept
the understanding/discernment that, with wisdom and instruction, is to be bought and never parted with
welded to the wisdom it is gained with
binah (understanding) — 'and UNDERSTANDING'; discernment, completing the store of wisdom to be bought and kept. These goods, once gained, are held for life.
righteousness — the son whose father greatly rejoices
the righteous son in whom the father greatly rejoices — a child's righteousness as the parent's joy
welded to the great joy it brings the father
tsaddiq — 'the father of the RIGHTEOUS will greatly rejoice'; a righteous child is the crown of a parent's joy. Righteousness in a son gladdens the father's whole heart.
rejoicing — the father's great joy in a righteous son
the great rejoicing/exulting of the father in a righteous son — joy heaped up (the emphatic 'greatly rejoice')
welded to the son's righteousness that causes it
gil (rejoice, emphatic 'greatly') — 'the father of the righteous will greatly REJOICE'; the doubled verb piles joy on joy. A righteous child is a father's exultation.
wisdom — the son in whom the father is glad
the wise son in whom the one who fathered him is glad — wisdom in a child as the parent's gladness
welded to the joy it gives the father
chakam (wise) — 'he who fathers a WISE son will be glad in him'; a wise child gladdens the father who begot him. Wisdom, like righteousness, crowns a parent's hope.
gladness — the father's joy in a wise son
the gladness/joy of the father in his wise son, parallel to the great rejoicing over the righteous
welded to the wise son who gives it
samach (be glad) — 'will be GLAD in him'; the father's gladness in a wise son. A child's wisdom is a parent's delight.
gladness — the joy the son is to bring both parents
the gladness the son is to give his father and mother — living so that those who bore him rejoice
welded to the joy of her who bore him
samach (be glad) — 'let your father and mother be GLAD'; the son is charged to live so as to gladden his parents. A child's life is meant to be his parents' joy.
rejoicing — the joy of the mother who bore him
the rejoicing of the mother who bore the son, when he lives wisely and rightly
welded to the gladness of father and mother
gil (rejoice) — 'let her who bore you REJOICE'; the mother's joy in a son who lives well. Live so that the one who bore you may rejoice.
harlotry — a deep pit that swallows the unwary
the harlot/prostitute who is a deep pit — illicit seduction as a trap from which escape is hard
welded to the adulteress who is the same deadly snare
zanah (be a harlot) — 'for a PROSTITUTE is a deep pit'; illicit sex is a pit that swallows a man (cf 22:14; 5:3-5; 7:27). Harlotry lures down into ruin.
the strange woman — a narrow well, a trap hard to escape
the adulteress/strange woman who is a narrow well — a trap that grips and does not readily release
welded to the harlot who is the same deep pit

nokri (foreign/strange woman) — 'an ADULTERESS is a narrow well'; the strange woman is a narrow well — easy to fall in, hard to climb out. Emergent: the adulteress as an inescapable trap, twin of the harlot's deep pit.
predatory seduction — the adulteress ambushing her prey like a robber
the lying-in-wait of the adulteress, ambushing men like a robber to draw them into unfaithfulness
welded to the faithlessness her ambush breeds
arab (lie in wait/ambush) — 'she LIES IN WAIT like a robber'; the seductress is a predator, ambushing the unwary. Emergent: seduction as calculated predation, not mere invitation.
multiplied treachery — the faithless men the adulteress breeds
the treachery/faithlessness the adulteress multiplies among men — each conquest a man made unfaithful
welded to the predatory seduction that produces it
bagad (deal treacherously) — 'and increases the TRAITORS among mankind'; the adulteress's work is to multiply faithlessness, turning men into betrayers. Seduction breeds treachery across society.
woe — the drunkard's cry of wretchedness
the woe/wretchedness that marks the drunkard — the first of the miseries drink heaps on its lover
welded to the grief that goes with it
oy (woe) — 'who has WOE?'; the drunkard's wretchedness, first in the litany of drink's fruits. Emergent: woe as the misery wine breeds in the one it enslaves.
sorrow — the grief that dogs the drunkard
the sorrow/grief that dogs the drunkard, second in the litany of drink's woes
welded to the contention that goes with it
aboy (sorrow) — 'who has SORROW?'; the grief drink brings its lover. Emergent: sorrow as one of the drunkard's inseparable miseries.
contention — the quarrels drink stirs up
the strife/contention the drunkard falls into, wine loosing his tongue to quarrel
welded to the anxious lament that goes with it
midyan (strife/contention) — 'who has STRIFE?'; drink breeds quarrels. The drunkard is contentious, wine turning fellowship to fighting.
anxious lament — the drunkard's muttering complaint
the complaining/anxious muttering of the drunkard, babbling his grievances in his cups
welded to the contention it goes with
siach (complaint/musing) — 'who has COMPLAINING?'; the drunkard's rambling, self-pitying lament. Drink loosens a tongue to grievance and woe.
craving — do not crave the ruler's deceptive delicacies
the craving/desire for the ruler's delicacies, to be resisted because the food is deceptive — its lavishness a snare, not a kindness
the craving that reaches for what only seems good

avah (crave/desire) — 'do not DESIRE his delicacies, for they are deceptive food'; the ruler's rich fare is a trap baited to obligate or expose; craving it is folly. Not all that is offered is given (cf 23:6-8).
captivated gaze — the fascinated look that kindles craving for drink
the looking/gazing at wine in its allure — the fascinated eye that must be refused before it kindles craving
(the wine's allure it is drawn to)
the gaze that must be checked before desire takes hold

raah (look/see) — 'do not LOOK at wine when it is red, when it sparkles'; the warning strikes at the eye, where the fall begins. Refuse the fascinated gaze, for desire follows the look (cf 23:33; the eye as the gateway of temptation). Emergent.
derangement — the drunk heart uttering perverse things
the heart of the drunkard, so deranged by wine that it utters perverse and twisted things
welded to the twisted speech it pours out
leb (heart) — 'and your HEART utter perverse things'; drink deranges the very heart, so that the inner self speaks perversity. Wine unhinges the seat of thought and will.
perversity — the twisted speech of the drunk heart
the perverse, twisted things the drunkard's deranged heart utters — distorted perception issuing in distorted speech
the deranged heart that utters it (265651)
welded to the wine-deranged heart it flows from
tahpukoth (perverse/twisted things) — 'and your heart utter PERVERSE things'; drink twists perception ('strange things') and speech alike. The drunk heart sees crooked and speaks crooked.
insensibility — the drunkard senseless even to blows
the not-feeling/insensibility of the drunkard, so numbed by wine that he does not even feel the blows that strike him
the craving for more that follows (265662)
welded to the addiction that seeks yet another drink
yada (know/feel), negated — 'they beat me, but I did not FEEL it'; drink numbs a man past pain and shame alike. Insensibility is the drunkard's stupor — struck, yet unaware.
addiction — the drunkard's craving to return to drink
the seeking/craving of the drunkard for yet another drink, even from his stupor — the bondage of the appetite that enslaves him
welded to the numbness that still craves more

baqash (seek) — 'when shall I awake? I must have ANOTHER drink'; even senseless and beaten, the drunkard's first thought is the next cup. Addiction is a bondage that craves the very thing destroying it.
wealth-striving — wearing oneself out to grow rich
the wearying toil/striving to acquire wealth, driven by anxious desire for riches — to be reined in
set against the wisdom that knows when to stop
yaga (toil/weary oneself) — 'do not TOIL to acquire wealth'; the anxious, exhausting pursuit of riches is folly, for wealth flies away (23:5). Striving after wealth wears the soul for nothing.
restraint — the wisdom to cease from chasing wealth
the discernment/understanding to desist from the anxious pursuit of riches — knowing when to stop
set against the striving it halts
binah (understanding/discernment) — 'be DISCERNING enough to desist'; wisdom knows when to stop chasing wealth. Self-restraint born of understanding checks greed's toil.
miserliness — the 'evil eye' that grudges its own bread
the stinginess/grudging of the man with the 'evil eye', whose bread and delicacies are given without heart
the craving one must not spend on him (265674)
set against the desire the guest must not feel for a grudging host's food

ra + ayin (evil eye) — 'do not eat the bread of a man who is STINGY'; the 'evil eye' is Hebrew idiom for miserliness (opp. the 'bountiful eye', 22:9). The grudging host's hospitality is a hollow show.
craving — do not crave the grudging host's delicacies
the craving/desire for the stingy man's delicacies, to be resisted since his welcome is false
set against the grudging host whose food it wants
avah (crave/desire) — 'do not DESIRE his delicacies'; craving a miser's food is folly, for his heart is not in the giving. What is grudged is not truly given (23:7).
hidden reckoning — the miser's soul computing the cost even as he says 'eat'
the inward reckoning/calculating of the miser's soul — silently counting the cost of every morsel while his mouth says 'eat and drink'
welded to the withheld heart behind the welcome

nephesh (soul/self) — 'for he is like one who is inwardly CALCULATING'; behind the host's generous words his soul is reckoning the cost. The self within belies the words without — hospitality as accountancy.
insincerity — the host's heart withheld from the guest he feeds
the heart of the host that is 'not with' his guest — words of welcome without inward good-will, feeding the body while grudging the gift
welded to the inward reckoning that withholds it
leb (heart) — ''Eat and drink!' he says to you, but his HEART is not with you'; the divided man whose mouth welcomes while his heart withholds. The gift without the heart is no gift (cf Matt 15:8).
wasted graciousness — the kind words spent in vain on a grudging host
the pleasant/gracious words the guest spends on the miser — wasted, once the false welcome is seen for what it is, along with the very morsels eaten
(the grudging host on whom they are wasted)
the graciousness squandered on one whose heart was never in it

naem (pleasant/sweet) — 'and waste your PLEASANT words'; the courtesy and gracious speech spent on a grudging host is thrown away, and the meal itself becomes nausea. Graciousness is wasted where the heart is closed.
folly — the fool who despises wise words spoken to him
the fool in whose hearing wise words are wasted, for he despises the good sense they carry
the contempt he shows for wisdom (265698)
welded to the scorn with which he meets good sense
kesil (fool) — 'do not speak in the hearing of a FOOL'; the fool cannot receive wisdom — words spent on him are wasted. Do not offer pearls to those who trample them (cf 9:8; Matt 7:6).
contempt — the fool's scorn for the good sense of wise words
the despising/contempt with which the fool meets the good sense of wise words — scorning what he cannot value
the fool whose scorn it is (265696)
welded to the folly that cannot prize wisdom
buz (despise/scorn) — 'for he will DESPISE the good sense of your words'; the fool holds wisdom in contempt, unable to prize it. Scorn of good sense is folly's reflex.
envy — the forbidden envying of evil men
the envying/jealous longing toward evil men and their apparent success — the very thing forbidden
welded to the wicked it is warned against envying
qana (envy) — 'be not ENVIOUS of evil men'; to envy the wicked is a recurring snare (cf 23:17; 24:19; Ps 37, 73). Their prosperity is a mirage, their hearts set on violence (24:2).
wickedness — the evil not to be envied or joined
the evil men whose apparent success tempts envy and whose company tempts desire, though their hearts devise violence
welded to the longing for their company that is forbidden
ra (evil) — 'be not envious of EVIL men'; the wicked, whose seeming good fortune baits envy and whose fellowship lures. Neither envy them nor wish to be with them.
longing — the forbidden wish to join the wicked
the desiring/longing to be with evil men — the wish for their company that must be refused
the evil men it longs for (265704)
welded to the wicked whose company it craves
avah (desire/crave) — 'nor DESIRE to be with them'; the longing for the wicked's company is forbidden, for their fellowship corrupts. Do not wish to be where evil plots (cf 1:10-15).
faintheartedness — collapsing in the day of trouble reveals a small strength

the fainting in the day of adversity that exposes how small one's strength is — the faintheartedness that gives way under pressure, adversity testing and revealing the true measure of a soul's fortitude
welded to the meagre strength the collapse exposes

raphah (grow faint/slack) — 'if you FAINT in the day of adversity, your strength is small' (24:10); trouble is the test of strength. To collapse under pressure reveals a fortitude that was never great. Adversity does not make character; it shows it.
exposed weakness — the meagre fortitude revealed by fainting in trouble
the smallness of strength that fainting in adversity lays bare — the fortitude proven meagre when tested, strength measured not in ease but in the day of trouble
welded to the collapse that exposes it

koach (strength) — 'your STRENGTH is small' (24:10); strength is measured in adversity. The one who faints when tested shows a fortitude that was small all along. Real strength holds in the day of trouble.
active mercy — the duty to deliver those going to death
the rescuing/delivering of those being taken to death and stumbling to slaughter — the active obligation to intervene for the perishing, not stand by
(the perishing it is bound to save)
the mercy that will not stand idle while others die

natsal (deliver/rescue) — 'RESCUE those who are being taken away to death'; the wise heart is bound to act for the perishing, not plead ignorance (24:12). To know and do nothing is guilt. Active mercy is a duty, not an option.
feigned ignorance — the excuse that pleads not-knowing
the claim of not-knowing by which a man excuses his failure to rescue — feigned ignorance offered as a defence
the God who sees through it (265732)
set against the God who weighs the heart and is not deceived
yada (know), the excuse — 'if you say, 'we did not KNOW this''; the plea of ignorance by which men excuse inaction. But the heart's real knowledge is not hidden from God.
the heart laid open — weighed by God
the heart of a man, which God weighs and assays — the inner self, with all its real motives, open before him
welded to the divine discernment that weighs it
lebab (heart) — 'does not he who weighs the HEART perceive it?'; the heart is God's to weigh — its true motives, however concealed by excuses, are known to him (cf 16:2; 21:2; 1 Sam 16:7).
divine discernment — God weighs the heart and sees the truth
the perceiving/discerning by which God, who weighs the heart, sees through every excuse to the real motive within
welded to the heart laid open before him
bin (discern/perceive) — 'does not he who weighs the heart PERCEIVE it?'; God discerns the heart behind the excuse. Locus external:god — the divine insight from which no pretence hides.
the soul under God's eye — watched and known
the soul/self over which God keeps watch — every life open to the God who guards and observes it
welded to the divine knowing that watches it
nephesh (soul) — 'does not he who keeps watch over your SOUL know it?'; the soul is under God's constant watch. Nothing in a man's life escapes the One who keeps his soul.
divine knowledge — God who watches the soul knows and repays
the knowing by which God, keeper of the soul, knows each man's true deeds and repays him according to his work
welded to the soul kept under his eye

yada (know) — 'does not he... KNOW it, and will he not repay man according to his work?'; God knows all and requites accordingly. Locus external:god — the divine knowledge that grounds a just recompense (cf Rom 2:6).
assurance — knowing wisdom is sweet and life-giving to the soul
the knowing/assurance that wisdom is to the soul what honey is to the taste — sweet, good, and securing a future
welded to the wisdom whose sweetness it affirms
yada (know) — 'KNOW that wisdom is such to your soul'; be assured that wisdom is as sweet and good to the soul as honey to the tongue (24:13). Wisdom is a delight, not a duty merely.
wisdom — sweet to the soul, securing a future and hope
the wisdom that is sweet to the soul and, once found, secures a future so that hope is not cut off
welded to the enduring hope it guarantees
chokmah (wisdom) — 'if you find it, there will be a future'; wisdom is sweet now and safe hereafter, giving the soul a future. To find wisdom is to secure hope.
hope — that wisdom secures and will not cut off
the hope of the one who finds wisdom — a hope that will not be cut off, because wisdom gives a future
welded to the wisdom that guarantees it

tiqvah (hope) — 'and your HOPE will not be cut off'; wisdom secures a future, so that the hope of the wise endures. Emergent: hope grounded in wisdom, unbroken where the wicked's hope perishes (cf 24:20; 23:18).
predatory wickedness — ambushing the righteous's home
the wicked man who lies in wait against the righteous's dwelling to do violence — predatory evil against the good
set against the righteous whose home he attacks
rasha — 'lie not in wait as a WICKED man against the dwelling of the righteous'; the wicked prey on the good. But such ambush is warned against, for the righteous rise again (24:16).
the targeted righteous — whose home must not be despoiled
the righteous man whose dwelling the wicked would ambush, but who is under a protection the wicked lacks
set against the predatory wickedness that targets him
tsaddiq — 'against the dwelling of the RIGHTEOUS'; the good, targeted by the wicked yet resilient. Violence against the righteous rebounds, for they rise (24:16).
destruction — the violence forbidden against the righteous's home
the violence/destruction the wicked would do to the righteous's home, expressly forbidden
the destructive assault the wicked is warned against
shadad (destroy/do violence) — 'do no VIOLENCE to his home'; the wicked's destructive assault on the good is forbidden and futile. The righteous home stands.
resilience — the righteous falls seven times and rises again
the resilience of the righteous, who fall seven times yet rise again — down but never destroyed
set against the wicked who stumble in calamity and do not recover
tsaddiq — 'for the RIGHTEOUS falls seven times and rises again'; the righteous are resilient — repeatedly knocked down, they get up. Their falls are not final (cf Mic 7:8; Ps 37:24).
collapse — the wicked stumble in calamity and do not rise
the wicked who stumble in the time of calamity and do not recover — one fall enough to finish them
set against the resilient righteous who always rise
rasha — 'but the WICKED stumble in times of calamity'; the wicked, unlike the righteous, fall to stay down. One disaster is enough to overthrow them, for they have no foundation.
gloating — the forbidden joy at an enemy's fall
the rejoicing/gloating at an enemy's fall — the malicious satisfaction that is expressly forbidden
the gladness that goes with it (265784)
welded to the heart's gloating gladness
samach (rejoice) — 'do not REJOICE when your enemy falls'; gloating over a fallen foe is forbidden. Even an enemy's ruin is no occasion for malicious joy (cf 17:5; Job 31:29).
the heart — guarded against gloating over an enemy
the heart that must not be glad when an enemy stumbles — the inner self to be kept from malicious satisfaction
the gladness it must not feel (265784)
welded to the gloating gladness it is warned against
leb (heart) — 'and let not your HEART be glad when he stumbles'; the battleground is the heart, tempted to secret gladness at a foe's fall. Guard the heart from gloating.
malicious gladness — the heart's gloating at an enemy's stumble
the gladness/exultation of the heart at an enemy's stumble — the gloating joy that is forbidden
welded to the heart warned against it
gil (be glad/exult) — 'let not your heart be GLAD when he stumbles'; secret exultation at a foe's fall is a sin of the heart. Magnanimity forbids even inward gloating.
divine displeasure — the LORD's disapproval of gloating
the displeasure of the LORD, who sees a man gloating over a fallen enemy and is displeased — divine disapproval that reproves the malicious heart
welded to the wrath he could redirect

ra'a be-enayim (be evil in the eyes / displeased) — 'lest the LORD see it and be DISPLEASED'; God disapproves of gloating over a foe. Locus external:god — the divine displeasure that reproves malice, even toward enemies.
redirected wrath — the LORD may turn his anger from the enemy
the anger of the LORD, which he may turn away from the fallen enemy (perhaps toward the gloater) — divine wrath as sovereign, not to be presumed upon
welded to the divine disapproval that governs it

aph (anger) — 'and turn away his ANGER from him'; God may lift his wrath from your enemy if you gloat — divine anger is his to direct. Locus external:god — a sobering reason to renounce malice (the wheel may turn).
the fretting/heated agitation of a man over evildoers — the restless resentment forbidden, kin to envy of the wicked
welded to the wicked whose success it resents
charah (be heated/fret) — 'FRET not yourself because of evildoers'; the anxious, resentful stewing over the wicked's success is forbidden (cf Ps 37:1, 7-8). Do not let the wicked's ease agitate you.
wickedness — not to be fretted over or envied
the evildoers whose apparent success tempts fretting and envy, though they have no future
welded to the envious longing they provoke
ra'a (evildoer) — 'because of EVILDOERS'; the wicked, whose seeming prosperity provokes fretting and envy. But their lamp will be put out (24:20).
envy — the forbidden envying of the wicked
the envying of the wicked — the jealous longing after their lot that is forbidden, for their end is darkness
welded to the evildoers whose lot it covets
qana (envy) — 'and be not ENVIOUS of the wicked'; envy of the wicked recurs as a snare (cf 23:17; 24:1). Their prosperity is brief — envy forgets their end.
the wicked heart — that devises violence
the hearts of evil men, the inner workshop where violence is devised — why they are not to be envied
welded to the plotting of violence it produces
leb (heart) — 'for their HEARTS devise violence'; the evil man's heart is a forge of violence. What looks like success masks an inner life set on harm.
plotting — the heart's devising of violence
the devising/plotting of violence by the wicked heart — the inner muttering that plans harm
welded to the mischief their speech reveals
hagah (mutter/devise) — 'their hearts DEVISE violence'; the wicked heart broods and plots harm. Violence is conceived within before it is spoken or done.
mischief — the trouble the wicked lips speak
the trouble/mischief of which the wicked's lips talk — the overflow of a violent heart into harmful speech
welded to the plotting heart it flows from
amal (trouble/mischief) — 'and their lips talk of TROUBLE'; the violent heart's plotting spills into speech. What the heart devises, the lips betray.
reverent fear — of the LORD and the king
the fearing/reverence owed to the LORD and the king — awe of God and due honour of ordained authority, keeping one from rebellion
the reverent submission that steadies a man against sedition
yare (fear) — 'my son, FEAR the LORD and the king'; reverent fear of God, joined to honour of lawful authority, guards a man from ruinous rebellion (cf 1 Pet 2:17). Awe of God grounds ordered life.
the showing of partiality/favouritism in judging — recognising faces rather than facts, which is not good
welded to the 'not good' that condemns it

nakar panim (regard faces / show partiality) — 'PARTIALITY in judging is not good'; to judge by persons rather than justice is wrong (cf 18:5; 28:21; Deut 1:17). Emergent: favouritism in judgment as a corruption of the judge's heart.
moral verdict — partiality in judging is 'not good'
the judgement that partiality in judging is 'not good' — an understated but firm condemnation of favouritism
welded to the favouritism it rejects
tob (good), negated — 'is NOT good'; the litotes understates but firmly condemns. Partiality is a real evil, however mildly named.
perverse verdict — declaring the guilty innocent
the calling of the wicked 'righteous' — the perverse verdict that acquits the guilty, which brings down universal curse
welded to the loathing of the nations it provokes

tsaddiq (righteous), misapplied — 'whoever says to the wicked, 'you are in the RIGHT''; to declare the guilty innocent perverts justice and outrages all people (cf 17:15). Acquitting the wicked is an abomination.
condemnation — the peoples curse the corrupt judge
