the cursing with which whole peoples condemn the one who acquits the wicked — universal repudiation of injustice
welded to the nations' loathing that goes with it
qabab (curse) — 'will be CURSED by peoples'; the corrupt judge draws the curse of the very people he was meant to serve. Perverted justice earns a nation's malediction.
loathing — the nations abhor the one who acquits the guilty
the abhorrence/indignation with which nations regard the one who calls the wicked righteous — the outrage perverted justice provokes
the perverse verdict that earns it (265829)
welded to the acquittal of the wicked it condemns
zaam (be indignant/abhor) — 'abhorred by NATIONS'; whole nations recoil in indignation from the judge who acquits the guilty. Injustice at the bench is universally loathed.
moral courage — reproving the wicked, against acquitting them
the rebuking/reproving of the wicked — the moral courage to confront wrong, opposite the cursed acquittal of 24:24, which brings delight and blessing
welded to the delight that rewards it

yakach (rebuke/reprove) — 'those who REBUKE the wicked will have delight'; the courage to confront the wicked (not flatter them) is blessed. Emergent: moral reproof as the honourable opposite of acquitting the guilty (cf 24:24; 28:23).
delight — the reward of those who rebuke the wicked
the delight/pleasantness that comes to those who rebuke the wicked, with a good blessing upon them
welded to the courageous reproof it rewards
naem (be pleasant/delight) — 'will have DELIGHT'; those who confront wrong, rather than wink at it, find delight and blessing. Integrity is rewarded where flattery is cursed.
blessing — the good that comes on those who rebuke the wicked
the good blessing that comes upon those who rebuke the wicked — favour resting on the courageous and honest
welded to the delight it accompanies
berakah (blessing) — 'and a good BLESSING will come upon them'; blessing rests on those who deal honestly with wrong. To rebuke the wicked is to draw down good.
forthright truthfulness — a straight, honest answer, welcome as a kiss

the giving of an honest, straightforward answer — the forthright truthfulness that speaks what is right and true, so welcome and pleasing that it is like a kiss on the lips, candour that honours the one it answers
the straight, truthful reply that is received as a mark of respect and love

nakoach (right/honest/straightforward) — 'whoever gives an HONEST answer kisses the lips' (24:26); a straight, truthful answer is a gift, as welcome and intimate as a kiss. Honest candour honours and pleases where evasion or flattery would wound (cf 27:5-6).
the wisdom by which a house (household, family, life) is built up — the constructive power of wisdom
welded to the understanding that establishes what wisdom builds
chokmah (wisdom) — 'by WISDOM a house is built'; wisdom is constructive, raising a stable household and life. What folly tears down, wisdom builds (cf 14:1; 9:1).
the understanding by which the house wisdom builds is made firm and established — discernment that steadies what wisdom raises
welded to the wisdom whose work it steadies
tebunah (understanding) — 'and by UNDERSTANDING it is established'; discernment steadies and secures what wisdom builds. Wisdom raises; understanding makes it stand.
sloth — whose field lies neglected and overgrown
the sluggard whose field, passed by and observed, lies neglected — sloth read off the ruin it leaves
welded to the lack of sense that goes with it

atsel (sluggard) — 'I passed by the field of a SLUGGARD'; sloth is legible in a neglected field, its ruin a sermon. Emergent: the sluggard observed, his laziness written on his overgrown ground (24:31).
senselessness — the man without heart whose vineyard is ruined
the man 'lacking heart/sense' whose vineyard, like the sluggard's field, lies in ruin — folly and sloth as one
welded to the sluggard's laziness it accompanies

chasar leb (lacking heart/sense) — 'by the vineyard of a man LACKING SENSE'; the senseless man's neglect mirrors the sluggard's. Folly and sloth ruin alike — a heart without sense lets everything go to weeds.
reflection — setting the heart to learn from what is seen
the setting of the heart to consider what was seen — the reflective attention that turns observation into a lesson
welded to the instruction reflection yields

shith leb (set the heart/consider) — 'then I saw and CONSIDERED it'; the wise do not merely see but set the heart on what they see, drawing out its lesson. Emergent: reflection as the bridge from observation to instruction (the sage's method).
lesson learned — the instruction drawn from reflection
the instruction/lesson the observer received by looking and laying the sight to heart — wisdom gleaned from the sluggard's ruin
welded to the considering that produces it
musar (instruction) — 'I looked and received INSTRUCTION'; the reflective observer harvests a lesson from what he sees. Wisdom learns from the folly of others (24:33-34).
knowledge — that fills the house with precious riches
the knowledge by which the rooms of the wisely-built house are filled with all precious and pleasant riches — wisdom's fruitful furnishing
the knowledge that stocks what wisdom builds

daath (knowledge) — 'by KNOWLEDGE the rooms are filled with all precious and pleasant riches'; knowledge not only builds but furnishes, filling the house with true wealth. Wisdom's house is a rich one.
wisdom-as-strength — the wise man full of strength
the wise man who is full of strength — wisdom itself a kind of power, mightier than mere force
welded to the knowledge that increases his might
chakam (wise) — 'a WISE man is full of strength'; wisdom is power. The wise outmatch the strong, for understanding does what force cannot (cf 21:22; 24:6).
knowledge — that enhances a man's might
the knowledge by which a man enhances/increases his might — understanding that multiplies strength
welded to the strengthening of might it produces
daath (knowledge) — 'and a man of KNOWLEDGE enhances his might'; knowledge multiplies a man's power. The informed mind is stronger than the strong arm.
strengthening — knowledge increasing a man's power
the enhancing/strengthening of might that knowledge works in a man — wisdom making him more capable than force alone
welded to the knowledge that produces it
amats (be strong/strengthen) — 'ENHANCES his might'; knowledge actively increases a man's power. Wisdom is force multiplied.
strategy — the wise direction by which war is waged
the wise guidance/strategy by which one safely wages war — wisdom's skilled direction in great undertakings
welded to the many counselors who furnish it
tachbuloth (guidance/wise direction) — 'by WISE GUIDANCE you can wage your war'; skilled strategy, not brute force, wins wars. Wisdom directs great ventures to safety (cf 11:14; 20:18).
counsel — the many advisers in whom victory lies
the abundance of counselors/advisers in whom victory is found — wisdom multiplied through many minds
welded to the wise strategy they furnish

yaats (counsel/advise) — 'in abundance of COUNSELORS there is victory'; safety and success come through many wise advisers, not a lone judgement. Emergent: the counsel of many as the seat of victory (cf 11:14; 15:22).
wisdom — too lofty for the fool to reach
the wisdom that is too high for a fool — beyond his grasp, so that he has nothing to say where counsel is given
the fool who cannot reach it (265921)
set against the fool for whom it is unattainable
chokmah (wisdom) — 'WISDOM is too high for a fool'; wisdom is beyond the fool's reach, and so he is silent in the gate where the wise deliberate. Folly has nothing to contribute.
folly — silent in the gate, wisdom beyond his reach
the fool for whom wisdom is unattainable, who therefore has nothing to say in the gate where matters are weighed
set against the wisdom he cannot attain
evil (fool) — 'in the gate he does not open his MOUTH'; the fool, unable to reach wisdom, is dumb where counsel is given. Folly is exposed by silence in the place of decision.
the planning/plotting of one who devises evil — the calculating mind bent on harm, that earns the name 'master of intrigue'
welded to the harm its plotting intends
chashab (plan/devise/reckon) — 'whoever PLANS to do evil'; the deliberate, calculating plotting of harm. To scheme evil is to be marked as a schemer (cf 6:14; 24:2).
malice — the evil the schemer plots to do
the evil/harm that the schemer plans to do — the malicious end of his calculating
welded to the scheming mind that plans it
ra'a (do evil/harm) — 'whoever plans to do EVIL will be called a schemer'; the malice that is the schemer's aim. His name is fixed by what his plotting is for.
scheming — the plotting of folly, which is sin
the devising/scheming of folly — the mind's plotting of foolish, wicked ends, which is itself counted sin
welded to the folly its plotting serves
zimmah (scheme/devising) — 'the DEVISING of folly is sin'; even the inward plotting of folly, before any act, is sin. The scheming heart is already guilty.
folly — whose very devising counts as sin
the folly whose scheming is sin — foolishness not as harmless error but as culpable wrong
welded to the guilt its devising incurs
ivveleth (folly) — 'the devising of FOLLY is sin'; folly is no innocent lack but a moral fault. To plot foolishness is to sin.
guilt — the verdict on folly's devising
the sin/guilt that folly's devising amounts to — the moral weight of a scheming, foolish heart
welded to the folly it declares guilty
chattah (sin) — 'the devising of folly is SIN'; folly's plotting is reckoned sin before God. Foolishness is a moral, not merely intellectual, failure.
scorn — the mocker whom all mankind abhors
the scoffer/mocker who is an abomination to mankind — scorn so odious that it earns universal loathing
welded to the loathing all men feel for him
luts (scoff/mock) — 'the SCOFFER is an abomination to mankind'; the mocker is detested by all — his scorn poisons every relation. Scoffing makes a man loathsome to his fellows.
loathsomeness — the scoffer detested by all mankind
the abomination/loathsomeness that the scoffer is to all people — the universal revulsion his scorn provokes
welded to the scorn that earns it
toebah (abomination) — 'the scoffer is an ABOMINATION to mankind'; here the loathing is human, not divine — men abhor the scoffer. Scorn isolates a man from all society.
disgrace — the reproach that falls on the betrayer of secrets
the shame/reproach that whoever hears brings on the one who betrayed a confidence — public disgrace as the fruit of loose talk
the lasting ill repute it brings (265950)
welded to the endless bad name it fixes
chasad (reproach/shame) — 'lest he who hears you bring SHAME upon you'; betraying a secret earns reproach from all who hear. Loose lips reap disgrace.
lasting disgrace — the bad name that never ends
the ill repute/evil report that clings to the betrayer of secrets and never ends — a ruined name that no correction erases
welded to the shame that fastens it
dibbah (evil report/ill repute) — 'and your ILL REPUTE have no end'; the betrayer of confidences earns a bad name that never lifts. A reputation for treachery is permanent (cf 25:9).
valued correction — the wise rebuke, precious as gold
the wise reprover whose correction, to one who will hear it, is as precious and fitting as a gold ornament — rebuke as a gift, not an insult
the listening ear that prizes it (265966)
welded to the receptive ear that treasures it
chakam (wise) — 'a WISE reprover to a listening ear'; wise correction, gladly received, is as beautiful and valuable as gold jewellery. A good rebuke well heard is a treasure (cf 27:5-6).
receptivity — the ear that welcomes wise correction
the listening/receptive ear that makes a wise rebuke precious — the teachableness without which correction is wasted
welded to the wise correction it treasures
shama (hear/listen) — 'to a LISTENING ear'; only the teachable ear turns rebuke to gold. Correction is precious only where there is a heart willing to hear it (cf 15:31).
faithfulness — the reliable envoy, refreshing as snow-cool in harvest
the faithfulness/reliability of a trustworthy messenger, refreshing to those who send him as the cool of snow in the heat of harvest
welded to the masters' soul his faithfulness revives

aman (be faithful/reliable) — 'a FAITHFUL messenger to those who send him'; a trustworthy envoy is as refreshing as cold in harvest-heat. Reliability in a servant revives the soul of his master (cf 13:17; 10:26).
refreshment — the masters' soul revived by a faithful servant
the soul of the masters that a faithful messenger refreshes — the relief and gladness a reliable servant brings to those who depend on him
welded to the reliable messenger who refreshes it
nephesh (soul) — 'he refreshes the SOUL of his masters'; the faithful servant revives his master's spirit. Trustworthiness in others is a refreshment to the soul.
empty boasting — vaunting a gift one does not give
the boasting/vaunting of a man who brags of a gift he never gives — all show and no substance, like clouds and wind that bring no rain
welded to the empty promise it makes

halal (boast/praise oneself) — 'a man who BOASTS of a gift he does not give'; the empty braggart promises much and gives nothing. His words raise hope like gathering clouds, then disappoint like a dry wind.
empty promise — the false gift, all boast and no substance
the gift of falsehood — the promised generosity that never comes, the deceptive emptiness of the man who boasts but does not give
welded to the empty vaunting that promises it
sheqer (falsehood/deception) — 'a gift he does NOT give'; the boaster's gift is a lie — clouds without rain. Empty promises are a deception, raising hope only to dash it (cf 25:14).
forbearance — the long patience that wins over a ruler
the patience/long-suffering by which even a ruler is at length persuaded — the quiet power of forbearance to overcome resistance
welded to the gentle speech that works with it

erek apayim (long of anger / patience) — 'with PATIENCE a ruler may be persuaded'; forbearance succeeds where force fails, wearing down even a ruler's resistance. Emergent: patience as a persuasive power (cf 15:1; 16:14).
gentleness — the soft speech that breaks hard resistance
the soft/gentle tongue that, like patience, breaks a bone — gentle speech overcoming the hardest opposition
welded to the forbearance that works with it
rak (soft/gentle) — 'a SOFT tongue will break a bone'; gentleness is stronger than force, breaking resistance that hardness only stiffens. The soft answer conquers (cf 15:1).
excess — eating past enough, till the sweet nauseates
the being-filled/sated with honey past what is enough, so that the sweet becomes sickening — the principle of moderation even in good things
the surfeit of company beside it (266009)
welded to the overstaying that likewise cloys
saba (be sated/full) — 'lest you have your FILL of it and vomit it'; even honey, eaten to excess, nauseates. Moderation is wisdom even with good things — too much of the sweet turns sour.
overstaying — wearing out a welcome till it turns to loathing
the being-had-one's-fill-of by a neighbour, when one's visits grow too frequent — the surfeit of presence that breeds distaste
welded to the loathing overstaying produces
saba (be sated/full) — 'lest he have his FILL of you and hate you'; as with honey, so with company — too much of a good guest cloys. Moderation preserves welcome (cf 25:16).
revulsion — the hatred that overstaying breeds in a neighbour
the hatred/revulsion a neighbour comes to feel for the guest who wears out his welcome by too-frequent visits
welded to the overstaying that produces it
sane (hate) — 'and HATE you'; welcome overdone turns to loathing. Even affection sours under surfeit — the wise guest keeps his visits rare.
perjury — testimony as deadly as a weapon
the false witness a man bears against his neighbour — perjury that strikes and destroys like a war club, a sword, a sharp arrow
the lie that kills as surely as a weapon

sheqer (falsehood) — 'a man who bears FALSE witness against his neighbor is like a war club, a sword, a sharp arrow'; perjury is a weapon that maims and kills a reputation, a life. False testimony is violence by words (cf 12:18; Ex 20:16).
misplaced reliance — leaning on a treacherous man in the crisis
the trust/reliance placed in a treacherous man in the time of trouble — confidence that fails just when it is needed, like a bad tooth or a foot that slips
the treacherous man it leans on (266022)
welded to the faithless man it wrongly relies on

mibtach (trust/confidence) — 'TRUSTING in a treacherous man in time of trouble'; to rely on the unreliable is agony in the crisis — the support gives way underfoot. Misplaced trust wounds like a rotten tooth.
unreliability — the faithless one who fails in the crisis
the treacherous, faithless man on whom one leans in trouble, only to be failed — reliability absent just when it matters
the trust that leans on him (266021)
welded to the misplaced reliance he betrays
bagad (deal treacherously) — 'a TREACHEROUS man in time of trouble'; the faithless man collapses under weight, failing precisely in the crisis. His unreliability is a snare to those who lean on him.
divine majesty — God's glory in concealing things
the glory/majesty of God shown in concealing things — the divine prerogative of hiddenness, wisdom too deep for men to fathom
set against the royal glory that seeks things out

kabod (glory) — 'it is the GLORY of God to conceal things'; God's majesty is partly in his hiddenness — his purposes are his own to veil. Locus external:god — the divine glory of mystery, which men are not to pry into (cf Deut 29:29).
royal honour — the king's glory in searching things out
the glory/honour of kings shown in searching things out — the royal duty and dignity of investigation, discerning what is hidden in a matter
set against the divine glory of concealment

kabod (glory) — 'but the glory of KINGS is to search things out'; where God's glory conceals, the king's glory investigates. It is a ruler's honour to probe a matter to its truth. Wise governance searches out.
insensitivity — tactless mirth that jars against sorrow
the singing of merry songs to a grieving heart — the tactlessness that jars against sorrow like vinegar on soda or a coat stripped off in the cold
the heavy heart it grates on (266039)
welded to the grief it offends

shir (sing) — 'is like one who takes off a garment on a cold day, and like vinegar on soda'; cheerfulness ill-timed is cruelty. To sing to a mourner is to grate, not to comfort. Empathy reads the heart before it speaks (cf Rom 12:15).
grief — the sad heart to which cheer is an offence
the heavy/sad heart, weighed down with grief, to which glib cheerfulness is not comfort but cruelty
welded to the insensitive mirth that grates on it
ra + leb (heavy/sad heart) — 'whoever sings songs to a HEAVY heart'; grief needs sympathy, not forced merriment. The sad heart is a real, respected state, not a mood to be jollied away.
enemy-love — feeding the very one who hates you
the returning of good for evil — giving bread and water to a hungry, thirsty enemy, overcoming his hatred with kindness rather than repaying it
the mercy that answers hatred with bread, and is rewarded by God

sane (enemy / one who hates) — 'if your ENEMY is hungry, give him bread to eat'; the astonishing ethic of returning good for evil, feeding the one who hates you (cf Ex 23:4-5; quoted Rom 12:20). Mercy overcomes enmity, and God rewards it (25:22).
divine recompense — God rewards kindness shown to an enemy
the reward the LORD gives to the one who feeds his enemy — divine recompense crowning the mercy that returns good for evil
the divine reward that answers mercy toward a foe

shalam (repay/reward) — 'and the LORD will REWARD you'; God himself recompenses the one who shows kindness to an enemy (the 'burning coals' melting him to shame or repentance). Locus external:god — the divine reward that makes enemy-love wisdom, not weakness (cf Rom 12:20-21).
slander — the secret tongue that provokes angry looks
the backbiting/secret-slandering tongue that, as surely as the north wind brings rain, brings forth angry looks and indignation
welded to the indignant looks it stirs up

sether (secret / backbiting) — 'a BACKBITING tongue, angry looks'; slander spoken in secret produces open indignation as reliably as the north wind brings rain. Emergent: the backbiting tongue as the cause of anger and strife (cf 26:20).
indignation — the angry faces a slandering tongue calls up
the angry/indignant looks that a backbiting tongue brings forth — the offended indignation that secret slander inevitably provokes
welded to the secret slander that produces it
zaam (indignation/anger) — 'and a backbiting tongue, ANGRY looks'; slander sows indignation, faces darkening with anger. What the backbiter whispers, the offended face repays.
evaluation — a rooftop corner beats a house of strife
the judgement that a corner of the housetop is better than a house shared with a quarrelsome wife — peace preferred to comfort
welded to the contention it would escape
tob (better) — 'it is BETTER to live in a corner of the housetop than in a house shared with a quarrelsome wife' (= 21:9); solitude with peace beats a full house with strife. Peace outweighs comfort.
contention — the wife whose strife drives one to the roof
the quarreling/contention of a wife that makes a shared house worse than a rooftop corner
welded to the peace one flees to escape it
midyan (quarrel/contention) — 'a QUARRELSOME wife'; incessant strife makes a home unbearable (cf 21:9, 19; 27:15). Contention exiles a man to the corner of the roof.
refreshment — the soul revived by good news, as by cold water
the soul that good news from a far country refreshes, as cold water revives a thirsty, fainting man
the good news that revives it (266087)
welded to the welcome tidings that refresh it
nephesh (soul) — 'like cold water to a thirsty SOUL, so is good news from a far country'; welcome tidings revive the weary soul as cold water a fainting body. Good news is refreshment to the spirit.
glad tidings — the news that refreshes a weary soul
the good news from a far country that revives the soul — long-awaited glad tidings, precious as cold water in thirst
welded to the fainting soul it revives
tob (good) — 'so is GOOD news from a far country'; glad tidings, long awaited, refresh the soul. In a world of slow news, good word from afar is a deep draught to the spirit.
compromise — the good man giving way before the wicked, and so defiled
the righteous man who gives way/caves before the wicked — the tragedy of the good man compromising, becoming a fouled spring that fails all who looked to him
set against the wickedness before which he wrongly gives way

tsaddiq — 'a RIGHTEOUS man who gives way before the wicked'; when the good man caves to the wicked he is like a muddied spring — his defilement poisons all who depended on his integrity. The righteous must stand, not yield (cf 24:16).
intimidation — the wicked before whom a righteous man wrongly gives way
the wicked before whom the righteous man gives way — the pressure of evil that, when yielded to, fouls the good man's witness
the righteous who yields to him (266095)
set against the compromise it wins from the righteous
rasha — 'who gives way before the WICKED'; the wicked's pressure, when the righteous cave to it, corrupts a clear spring. Evil triumphs where the good man surrenders his integrity.
immoderation — the 'not good' of eating too much honey
the judgement that eating much honey is 'not good' — self-indulgent excess, paired with the self-seeking of chasing one's own glory
welded to the self-exaltation it is set beside

tob (good), negated — 'it is NOT good to eat much honey'; excess even of the sweet is harmful, an image for the self-indulgence of seeking one's own honour. Too much of self, like too much honey, sickens.
vainglory — seeking one's own glory, which is not glorious
the seeking of one's own glory — self-exaltation that, far from being glorious, is as unseemly as gorging on honey
welded to the immoderation it is likened to
kabod (glory) — 'nor is it glorious to seek one's own GLORY'; to chase one's own honour is not honourable but shameful. Self-seeking glory, like surfeit of honey, cloys and demeans (cf 27:2; 25:6-7).
self-mastery — its absence leaves a man defenceless
the self-control/restraint of spirit whose absence leaves a man as defenceless as a city broken open and left without walls — the ruin of ungoverned passions
(the breached city he is likened to)
the self-mastery whose lack exposes a man to every assault

matsar ruach (restraint of spirit / self-control) — 'a man without SELF-CONTROL is like a city broken into and left without walls'; without command of his own spirit a man has no defence — every passion and impulse storms in at will. Self-mastery is the wall of the soul (cf 16:32).
inscrutability — the unsearchable depth of a king's heart
the heart of kings, unsearchable as the height of heaven and depth of earth — the inscrutable inner counsel of a ruler, beyond an ordinary man's fathoming
(the heavens and earth it is likened to)
the royal mind whose depths no subject can plumb

leb (heart) — 'so the HEART of kings is unsearchable'; a king's inner thought is as unfathomable as sky and earth. The counsels of power run deeper than a subject can see — a caution to those who would read or manipulate a ruler.
corruption — the wicked whose removal purifies the throne
the wicked at the king's court, whose removal is required if the throne is to stand — corruption near power that must be purged
the righteousness that then establishes the throne (266126)
set against the righteousness a purged court secures

rasha — 'take away the WICKED from the presence of the king'; wicked counsellors corrupt a reign; remove them and the throne stands. Righteousness, not the wicked, secures a kingdom (cf 16:12; 20:8, 28).
just rule — that establishes the throne once the wicked are gone
the righteousness in which the king's throne is established once the wicked are removed — justice as the foundation of enduring rule
the wicked whose removal frees it (266121)
set against the corruption a purged court removes
tsedeq (righteousness) — 'his throne will be established in RIGHTEOUSNESS'; a throne stands not on power but on justice. Purge the wicked, and righteousness secures the reign.
presumptuous self-advancement — pushing oneself forward before the king

the putting of oneself forward in the king's presence, claiming the place of the great — the presumptuous self-advancement that grasps at honour ungiven, the pride that seats itself high only to risk being told to come down
the self-thrusting ambition that grabs at status before the great

hadar (honour / exalt oneself) — 'do not put YOURSELF FORWARD in the king's presence' (25:6); self-promotion before the great is folly and pride. Better to be raised than to grab the high place and be lowered (25:7; cf Luke 14:8-10). Humility waits to be called up.
prudent humility — better to be raised than to be put lower
the judgement that it is better to be invited up than to be demoted before a noble — the wisdom of taking the low place and being raised, not the high and being shamed
set against the being-put-lower it would spare one

tob (better) — 'it is BETTER to be told, 'come up here,' than to be put lower'; humility that takes the lower seat and is raised beats presumption that grabs the high seat and is demoted (cf Luke 14:8-10). Better raised from low than lowered from high.
humiliation — the demotion of the presumptuous before a noble
the being put lower/demoted before a noble — the public humiliation that befalls the one who presumed to the high place
set against the being-raised it loses

shaphel (be low/be put down) — 'than to be PUT LOWER in the presence of a noble'; the shame of demotion before the great. Emergent: the humiliation of the presumptuous, the cost of grasping honour ungiven.
litigiousness — rushing to law before thinking it through
the hasty bringing of a matter to court, before the end is weighed — rash litigation that ends in one's own shame
welded to the disgrace hasty suit invites
rib (contend/go to law) — 'do not hastily bring into COURT'; rushing to litigation is folly, for it may end in your own humiliation. Weigh the end before you sue (cf 25:9).
disgrace — the shame a neighbour may put on the hasty litigant
the shame/disgrace a neighbour may bring on the one who rushed to court — the humiliating end of rash litigation
the hasty suit that risks it (266150)
welded to the rash litigation that courts it
kalam (be put to shame) — 'when your neighbor puts you to SHAME'; the hasty litigant may find himself shamed in the end. Rash suits recoil on those who bring them.
discreet resolution — settling with the neighbour himself
the arguing/pleading of one's case with the neighbour himself — direct, discreet resolution rather than public exposure
the secret it must not betray (266164)
welded to the confidence it must keep
rib (contend/plead) — 'ARGUE your case with your neighbor himself'; settle disputes privately and directly, not by dragging in others. Discreet resolution preserves both parties (cf Matt 18:15).
discretion — not betraying a confidence in the dispute
the secret/confidence of another that must not be revealed even in pressing one's case — the discretion that keeps a trust
welded to the discreet resolution it belongs with
sod (secret/confidence) — 'and do not reveal another's SECRET'; discretion forbids betraying a confidence, even to win an argument. To expose a secret is to earn lasting disgrace (25:10).
incongruity — honour given a fool, absurdly out of season
the honour that, given to a fool, is as out-of-place as snow in summer — dignity conferred where folly makes it ridiculous
set against the fool on whom it sits absurdly
kabod (honour) — 'HONOR is not fitting for a fool'; honour on a fool is incongruous, unnatural, doomed to look ridiculous. Some do not deserve, and cannot carry, the dignity given them.
folly — unworthy of honour, which sits on him absurdly
the fool for whom honour is as unfitting as snow in summer or rain in harvest — folly and honour are incongruous
set against the honour that does not suit him
kesil (fool) — 'so HONOR is not fitting for a FOOL'; to honour a fool is as absurd and out-of-season as snow in summer. Folly and dignity do not belong together (cf 26:8).
liability — the fool (or drunkard) hired, wounding all around like a random archer
the fool or drunkard whom one hires, a liability that wounds indiscriminately like an archer shooting at random — folly loosed into responsibility harms everyone
the folly that, given work, injures at random
kesil (fool) — 'like an archer who wounds everyone is one who hires a passing FOOL' (26:10); to employ a fool is to loose random harm on all around. Folly in service wounds indiscriminately.
incorrigibility — the fool who repeats his folly like a dog its vomit
the fool who returns to and repeats his folly as a dog returns to its vomit — folly's disgusting, incorrigible cycle, learning nothing
welded to the folly he cannot leave

kesil (fool) — 'like a dog that returns to his vomit is a FOOL who repeats his folly' (26:11); folly is incorrigible, cycling back to the same disgusting error. The fool learns nothing and returns to his sin (cf 2 Pet 2:22).
relapse — the folly the fool returns to again and again
the folly to which the fool returns again and again, as a dog to its vomit — the same error repeated, no lesson learned
the fool who returns to it (266185)
welded to the incorrigible fool it belongs to
ivveleth (folly) — 'repeats his FOLLY' (26:11); the folly relapsed into, again and again. Folly's mark is not one error but the endless return to it.
self-conceit — the worst folly, worse than a fool's
the man wise in his own eyes — self-conceit so blinding that there is more hope for a fool than for him, the crowning folly that cannot be taught
set against the hope even a fool has more of

chakam (wise, in his own eyes) — 'do you see a man who is WISE in his own eyes? there is more hope for a fool than for him' (26:12); self-conceit is the deepest folly — a fool may yet learn, but the self-wise never will. Pride in one's own wisdom is beyond cure (cf 3:7; 28:26).
hopelessness — the self-wise beyond even the fool's hope of learning
the hope that the self-conceited man forecloses — less than a fool's, because he cannot be taught what he thinks he already knows
set against the self-wisdom that leaves him beyond teaching

tiqvah (hope) — 'there is more HOPE for a fool than for him' (26:12); the self-wise are more hopeless than fools, for they will never seek what they think they possess. Emergent: hopelessness as the fruit of self-conceit — the one folly wisdom cannot reach.
teachable folly — with more hope than the self-conceited
the fool who, for all his folly, has more hope than the self-conceited man — because a fool may yet be brought to see his need, where the self-wise cannot
the self-wise who has less hope (266191)
set against the self-conceit that has even less hope
kesil (fool) — 'more hope for a FOOL than for him' (26:12); even the fool is better placed than the self-conceited, for folly may be owned and cured. To know one is a fool is the beginning of hope.
evasive sloth — inventing lions in the road to avoid going out
the sluggard who says 'there is a lion in the road!' — sloth conjuring imaginary perils to excuse staying in, laziness so inventive that it peoples the streets with lions rather than step out to work
(the imagined lion that keeps him in)
the idleness that invents dangers rather than face the day's work

atsel (sluggard) — 'the SLUGGARD says, 'there is a lion in the road!'' (26:13; cf 22:13); sloth excuses itself with fantastic fears. The lazy man sees lions where none are, sooner than admit he simply will not work.
fruitless sloth — the lazy man turning in bed, all motion and no progress
the sluggard who turns on his bed as a door turns on its hinges — sloth that has motion but no progress, endless turning that goes nowhere, activity that never rises to action
the busy idleness that turns and turns yet never gets up or gets on

atsel (sluggard) — 'as a door turns on its hinges, so does a SLUGGARD on his bed' (26:14); the lazy man is all motion and no advance, hinged to his bed. He stirs endlessly and arrives nowhere — the perfect image of fruitless sloth.
sloth — too lazy even to feed himself
the sluggard so sunk in laziness that, having put his hand in the dish, he is too weary to bring it back to his mouth — sloth at its absurd extreme
the weariness it feels at the least effort (266213)
welded to the exhaustion the smallest task costs him

atsel (sluggard) — 'the SLUGGARD buries his hand in the dish; it wears him out to bring it back to his mouth' (cf 19:24); sloth grown so total it will not lift food to feed itself. Emergent: laziness as a self-defeating paralysis, comic and tragic at once.
enervation — the sluggard exhausted by the least effort
the weariness that overcomes the sluggard at the least exertion — the enervation that makes even self-feeding too much trouble
welded to the laziness that produces it
laah (be weary/exhausted) — 'it WEARS him out to bring it back to his mouth'; the sluggard is exhausted by the smallest task. Sloth turns the least effort into an unbearable labour.
self-deception — the sluggard sure of his own wisdom
the sluggard who, for all his uselessness, thinks himself wiser than seven sensible men — sloth compounded by self-conceit, blind to its own folly
welded to the self-wisdom that blinds him

atsel (sluggard) — 'the SLUGGARD is wiser in his own eyes than seven men who can answer sensibly'; the lazy man is also self-deceived, rating his idle opinions above real wisdom. Emergent: the sluggard's self-conceit, sloth armoured against correction.
the sluggard's conceit of being 'wiser in his own eyes' than seven who answer with sense — the self-flattery that shields him from ever learning
welded to the laziness it armours

chakam (wise, in his own eyes) — 'is WISER in his own eyes than seven men who can answer sensibly'; the sluggard's self-conceit rates his idleness above real discernment. Self-flattery keeps the lazy from ever being taught (cf 26:12).
officiousness — seizing a quarrel not one's own, like grabbing a stray dog's ears
the meddling that seizes on a quarrel not one's own, as reckless as grabbing a passing dog by the ears — officiousness that invites a bite for nothing
(the quarrel not his own that he seizes)
the officious intrusion that courts needless harm

chazaq (seize/take hold) — 'whoever meddles in a quarrel not his own is like one who TAKES a passing dog by the ears' (26:17); to intrude on others' disputes is to court a bite for nothing. Officiousness invites the harm it had no need to risk.
malice masked as humour — deceiving a neighbour, then pleading 'only joking'

the deceiving of a neighbour followed by 'I am only joking!' — the malice that does real harm and then hides behind humour, treating deception as a game and refusing responsibility for the wounds it inflicts, as dangerous as a madman scattering firebrands
the harmful deceit that shelters behind the excuse of jest

ramah (deceive/betray) — 'is the man who DECEIVES his neighbor and says, 'I am only joking!'' (26:18-19); deceit dressed as humour is like a madman flinging firebrands. To do real harm and plead 'just joking' is malice evading its own guilt.
impotent malediction — the undeserved curse that finds no rest
the curse that is causeless — the undeserved malediction which, like a flitting bird, never lands or takes hold, powerless where there is no ground for it
the empty curse that finds no place to settle

qelalah (curse) — 'a CURSE that is causeless does not alight'; an undeserved curse has no power to land — it flutters off like a bird with nowhere to perch. Innocence is a shield against malediction (cf Num 23:8).
contentiousness — the man who kindles strife as fuel feeds fire
the quarrelsome/contentious man who is to strife what charcoal is to embers and wood to fire — a nature that kindles and feeds conflict wherever he goes
welded to the conflict his nature feeds

midyan (strife/contention) — 'so is a QUARRELSOME man for kindling strife' (26:21); some men are fuel for conflict — their very presence sets disputes ablaze. Contentiousness is a fire-starter (cf 15:18).
conflict — the strife a quarrelsome man sets ablaze
the strife/quarrel that the contentious man kindles — conflict flaring up wherever his combustible nature is added, as fire leaps up on fresh fuel
the quarrelsome man who kindles it (266259)
welded to the contentious nature that feeds it
rib (strife/dispute) — 'for kindling STRIFE' (26:21); the conflict a quarrelsome man ignites. Where he is added, disputes catch and blaze.
dissembling malice — the hater who masks himself with his lips
the hatred of one who disguises himself with his lips, masking his enmity behind smooth speech while the malice burns unseen within
welded to the deceit stored inside
sane (hate) — 'whoever HATES disguises himself with his lips' (26:24); the enemy hides his hatred behind a smooth-spoken mask. Malice learns to wear the face of friendship (cf 26:25-26).
inward treachery — the deceit stored in the hater's heart
the deceit/treachery the hater harbours within his heart, hidden beneath his disguising lips — the store of duplicity behind the friendly mask
the disguised hatred that hides it (266263)
welded to the masked malice it serves
mirmah (deceit/treachery) — 'and harbors DECEIT in his heart' (26:24); behind the smooth lips is a hoard of treachery. The disguise is the lips; the reality is the deceit within.
deceptive charm — the smooth words masking a heart of abominations
the gracious, charming speech of the hater — not to be believed, for it is a mask over a heart full of abominations
welded to the seven abominations it hides
chanan (be gracious) — 'when he speaks GRACIOUSLY, believe him not' (26:25); the smooth charm of a malicious man is a lure, not a kindness. Gracious words from a hateful heart are to be distrusted.
hidden depravity — the mass of evil in the deceiver's heart
the 'seven abominations' — the full measure of hidden depravity in the deceiver's heart, belying every gracious word his lips can shape
the gracious speech that masks them (266270)
welded to the charming words that hide them
toebah (abomination) — 'for there are seven ABOMINATIONS in his heart' (26:25); 'seven' signals a heart wholly full of evil. However fair the speech, the heart behind it is utterly corrupt.
the corrupt heart — full of abominations behind fair words
the heart of the deceiver, filled with abominations that no gracious speech can cover — the true self behind the charming mask
welded to the seven evils it harbours
leb (heart) — 'seven abominations in his HEART' (26:25); the heart is the reality, the gracious lips only the disguise. What a man is, is in his heart, not his charm.
concealed enmity — the hatred masked with deception for a time
the hatred that is covered over with deception — enmity hidden behind guile, but only for a time, until it is dragged into the light
the wickedness that will be exposed (266281)
welded to the wickedness time will reveal
sinah (hatred) — 'though his HATRED be covered with deception' (26:26); malice can be masked for a while, but not forever. Hidden hatred is on borrowed time.
revelation — the hidden evil dragged into the assembly's light
the wickedness that, however long masked by deception, will at last be exposed in the public assembly — evil that cannot stay hidden forever
the hidden hatred it flows from (266278)
welded to the masked enmity it finally reveals

ra (evil/wickedness) — 'his WICKEDNESS will be exposed in the assembly' (26:26); the truth outs. Hidden malice is finally dragged into public light, unmasked before all. Concealment is only ever temporary (cf Luke 12:2).
falsehood — the lie that masks hatred of its victims
the lying tongue that, far from being neutral, hates the very ones it crushes with its falsehoods — deceit springing from and serving malice
welded to the hatred that drives it
sheqer (falsehood) — 'a LYING tongue hates its victims'; the lie is not idle but hostile, wielded against those it wounds. Falsehood serves hatred (cf 26:24-26).
malice — the hatred behind the lying tongue
the hatred with which the lying tongue regards its victims — the malice that the falsehood both hides and serves
the lying tongue that masks it (266290)
welded to the falsehood that carries it
sane (hate) — 'a lying tongue HATES its victims'; behind the lie is real enmity. To slander a man is to hate him. The tongue's falsehood is malice in action.
smooth ruin — the flattering mouth that works destruction
the flattering, smooth-talking mouth that, for all its sweetness, works ruin — praise deployed to destroy, the twin of the lying tongue's hatred
the smooth speech that flatters in order to destroy

chelqah (smoothness/flattery) — 'and a FLATTERING mouth works ruin'; flattery is not kindness but a weapon, smooth words that undermine and destroy. Emergent: flattery as covert ruin, kin to the hateful lie (cf 29:5).
restraint — not answering a fool on his own foolish terms
the folly of a fool that one must NOT answer according to, lest one sink to his level — the wisdom of not stooping to a fool's terms
the conceit that must be punctured (266311)
set against the times a fool must be answered to check his conceit

ivveleth (folly) — 'answer not a fool according to his FOLLY, lest you be like him' (26:4); do not descend to a fool's level of argument. Yet the paired verse (26:5) balances it — wisdom knows WHEN to engage and when to refrain.
discernment — answering a fool to deflate his self-conceit
the fool's being 'wise in his own eyes', which must sometimes be answered and punctured — the discernment to know when a fool's conceit needs checking
the folly not to stoop to (266301)
set against the restraint of not answering on foolish terms

chakam (wise, in his own eyes) — 'answer a fool according to his folly, lest he be WISE in his own eyes' (26:5); sometimes a fool must be answered, to deflate his conceit. The paradox with 26:4 teaches discernment — knowing which response each moment needs.
unreliability — sending a message by a fool cuts off one's own feet
the fool entrusted with a message, who is so unreliable that to use him is to cripple oneself — folly as a liability that wounds the one who trusts it
welded to the violence one drinks by relying on him
kesil (fool) — 'whoever sends a message by the hand of a FOOL cuts off his own feet' (26:6); to rely on a fool is to maim oneself. Folly entrusted with responsibility injures the one who trusted it.
injury — the violence one 'drinks' by trusting a fool
the violence/harm a man brings on himself by entrusting a fool with his affairs — self-inflicted injury, drunk down like poison
welded to the folly relied on that wounds him
chamas (violence) — 'and DRINKS violence' (26:6); to depend on a fool is to swallow harm. The imprudence recoils on the one who commits it.
danger — giving honour to a fool, like binding a stone in a sling
the giving of honour to a fool, as futile and dangerous as binding a stone in a sling — dignity that will only fly back and harm
the honour that, given a fool, recoils like a slung stone

kabod (honour) — 'like one who binds the stone in the sling is one who gives HONOR to a fool' (26:8); honour on a fool is not only absurd (26:1) but dangerous — it flies back to wound. Emergent: honouring folly as a self-defeating, hazardous act.
incapacity — wisdom useless in a fool's mouth, like a thorn in a drunkard's hand
the fool in whose mouth a proverb hangs useless (26:7) or does harm (26:9) — wisdom he cannot wield, dangerous or limp in his handling
the folly that cannot carry or use true wisdom

kesil (fool) — 'a proverb in the mouth of FOOLS' (26:7, 9); wisdom on a fool's lips is like a lame man's useless legs, or a thorn in a drunkard's hand — either limp or harmful. Folly cannot handle wisdom rightly.
presumption — vaunting a future one does not command
the boasting about tomorrow — the presumption that vaunts a future one neither owns nor knows, forgetting how contingent every day is
welded to the not-knowing that should humble it
halal (boast) — 'do not BOAST about tomorrow'; to vaunt the future is presumption, for a man commands nothing of what a day may bring. Humility holds tomorrow lightly (cf Jas 4:13-16).
humbling ignorance — not knowing what a day may bring
the not-knowing of what a day may bring — the humbling ignorance of the future that should silence all boasting
welded to the presumption it rebukes
yada (know), negated — 'for you do not KNOW what a day may bring'; man's ignorance of the future is the ground of humility. Not knowing tomorrow, he must not boast of it.
proximate loyalty — a near neighbour worth more than a distant brother
the judgement that a neighbour who is near is better, in the day of calamity, than a brother far away — the value of steadfast, close friendship over distant kinship
the near, faithful friend prized above the far-off kinsman

tob (better) — 'BETTER is a neighbor who is near than a brother who is far away'; in trouble, a faithful friend at hand is worth more than a brother at a distance. Cultivated, proximate friendship is a treasure not to be forsaken (cf 18:24; 17:17).
the son's wisdom — that gladdens and vindicates the father
the wisdom the father urges on his son — a wisdom that both gladdens the father's heart and lets him answer any who reproach him
the gladness it brings the father (266365)
welded to the joy a wise son gives
chakam (be wise) — 'be WISE, my son, and make my heart glad'; the son's wisdom is the father's joy and vindication. A wise child gladdens the parent and silences his critics (cf 23:15, 24-25).
parental joy — gladdened by a wise son, answering reproach
the gladness a wise son brings the father's heart — joy that also arms him to answer those who reproach him, the wise child being the parent's living vindication
the son's wisdom that brings it (266362)
welded to the wisdom that gladdens and vindicates

samach (be glad) — 'and make my HEART glad, that I may answer him who reproaches me'; a wise son is a parent's gladness and his answer to critics. The child's wisdom vindicates the parent's labour (cf 23:15-16).
taunt answered — the critic a wise son lets the father silence
the one who reproaches the father, whose taunt a wise son enables him to answer — the critic silenced by the living evidence of a well-raised child
the wise son who answers him (266362)
set against the wise son whose life refutes the taunt
charaph (reproach/taunt) — 'that I may answer him who REPROACHES me'; the critic who taunts the parent is answered not by words but by a wise child. A son's wisdom is the father's reply to reproach.
prudence — foreseeing danger and taking cover
the prudent man who sees danger coming and hides himself from it — foresight that reads trouble in advance and acts to avoid it
set against the naive who walk heedlessly into harm
arum (prudent/shrewd) — 'the PRUDENT sees danger and hides himself' (= 22:3); foresight perceives trouble and takes cover. Prudence is danger seen and shunned in time.
naivety — blundering on into harm unheeded
the naive who go blindly on and suffer for it, seeing no danger where the prudent would have taken cover
set against the foresight that hides from harm
pethi (simple/naive) — 'but the SIMPLE go on and suffer for it' (= 22:3); the naive see no danger and walk into it. Heedlessness pays folly's price.
tactless flattery — praise so loud and ill-timed it grates like a curse
the blessing of a neighbour with a loud voice, rising early — effusiveness so excessive and ill-timed that it is taken not as kindness but as a curse
the over-loud praise that offends where it means to please

barak (bless) — 'whoever BLESSES his neighbor with a loud voice, rising early... will be counted as cursing'; praise overdone and ill-timed becomes an offence. Effusive flattery grates like the very curse it is not. Tact reads the moment.
contention — the wife whose strife is a ceaseless drip
the quarreling/contention of a wife, as maddening and relentless as a continual dripping on a rainy day — strife that wears by sheer persistence
(the ceaseless dripping it is likened to)
the endless contention that wears a man down drop by drop

midyan (quarrel/contention) — 'a continual dripping on a rainy day and a QUARRELSOME wife are alike' (cf 19:13; 21:9); nagging strife wears by relentless repetition, like water dripping without end. Contention's power is its ceaselessness.
faithful service — loyal care that earns honour
the guarding/faithful care of one's master, like tending a fig tree — diligent, loyal service that is rewarded with honour as the tree rewards its keeper with fruit
welded to the reward faithful service brings

shamar (guard/keep) — 'he who GUARDS his master will be honored'; faithful, attentive service is rewarded, as tending a fig tree is rewarded with its fruit. Loyalty and diligence earn honour (cf 22:29).
reward — the honour that crowns faithful service
the honour that comes to the one who faithfully guards his master — the due reward of loyal, diligent service
the faithful guarding that earns it (266416)
welded to the loyal service it rewards
kabad (honour) — 'will be HONORED'; the reward of faithful service is honour. As the fig-tender eats fruit, the loyal servant reaps honour.
vainglory — praising oneself instead of leaving it to others
the praising of oneself with one's own mouth, instead of leaving praise to another — the vanity of self-commendation, which cheapens what it claims
the self-flattery that should be left to another's lips
halal (praise) — 'let another praise you, and not your own MOUTH'; self-praise is worthless and unseemly — genuine honour comes from others' lips, not one's own (cf 25:27; 2 Cor 10:18).
the assay of praise — how a man handles praise reveals him
the testing of a man by his praise — as fire assays metal, so praise assays the person, revealing by his response to it whether he is humble or vain, solid or hollow
(the fire that assays silver and gold)
the praise that proves a man's true mettle
mahalal (praise) — 'a MAN is tested by his praise'; praise is a crucible — how one bears it (with humility or vanity) reveals the true metal of the soul. Applause assays character (cf 27:2; 12:8).
incorrigible folly — folly that clings through any crushing
the fool whose folly is so ingrained that even crushing him in a mortar with a pestle will not separate it from him — folly welded to the person, past all remedy of force
the folly that will not leave him (266439)
welded to the ineradicable folly that clings to him
evil (fool) — 'crush a FOOL in a mortar... yet his folly will not depart'; folly is not a surface stain but the man's very grain. No violence removes it — the fool cannot be pounded into wisdom.
obstinacy — the folly that no crushing can remove
the folly that will not depart from the fool even under the pestle — obstinate, ingrained foolishness that no force or punishment can drive out
welded to the fool from whom it will not part

ivveleth (folly) — 'yet his FOLLY will not depart from him'; ingrained folly is beyond the reach of mere force. What is bound into the heart is not pounded out — only wisdom willingly received can cure it.
diligent oversight — knowing thoroughly the state of one's affairs
the knowing-well of the condition of one's flocks — the diligent, thorough oversight of what one is responsible for, the opposite of careless neglect
welded to the heartful attention that goes with it

yada (know, emphatic) — 'KNOW well the condition of your flocks'; wise stewardship knows its charge thoroughly. Diligent attention to one's responsibilities, not careless assumption, is the mark of prudence (cf 27:24).
attentive care — setting the heart on one's responsibilities
the giving of attention (lit. 'setting the heart') to one's herds — the engaged, careful stewardship that watches over what is entrusted to it
welded to the diligent oversight it goes with

leb (heart / set the heart) — 'give ATTENTION to your herds'; wise stewardship sets the heart on its charge. Diligent care, not idle possession, preserves what one has — for riches do not last of themselves (27:24).
folly — whose provocation is a crushing weight
the fool whose provocation lies heavier on a man than stone or sand — folly as an intolerable, exhausting burden to those who must bear it
welded to the vexation it heaps on others
evil (fool) — 'but a FOOL's provocation is heavier than both'; the fool's needling is a crushing weight, harder to bear than stone or sand. Folly wearies all who must endure it.
vexation — the fool's needling, heavier than stone or sand
the provocation/vexation a fool inflicts — the exasperating irritation that weighs on others more heavily than any physical burden
welded to the fool whose weight it is
kaas (provocation/vexation) — 'a fool's PROVOCATION is heavier than both'; the fool's exasperating needling is an intolerable weight. To bear with folly is heavier labour than carrying stone.
cruel fury — overwhelming, yet less than jealousy
the wrath that is cruel and the anger that overwhelms — violent passions hard to withstand, yet named here only to be exceeded by jealousy
welded to the overwhelming anger it is paired with
chemah (wrath) — 'WRATH is cruel, anger is overwhelming'; wrath is savage and anger a flood, terrible passions — but the verse ranks them below jealousy. Even cruel fury is exceeded (cf 6:34).
overwhelming rage — a flood, yet less than jealousy
the anger that overwhelms like a flood — a passion hard to stand against, yet still surpassed by the irresistible force of jealousy
welded to the cruel wrath it is paired with
aph (anger) — 'ANGER is overwhelming'; anger floods and overwhelms, hard to resist. Yet fierce as it is, it yields to jealousy in destructive power.
irresistible jealousy — before which none can stand
the jealousy before which no one can stand — the most irresistible of the destructive passions, fiercer even than cruel wrath and overwhelming anger
the wrath and anger it exceeds (266476)
set above the fury and rage it surpasses
qinah (jealousy) — 'but who can stand before JEALOUSY?'; jealousy is the most implacable passion, outstripping even wrath and anger. Against a jealous fury there is no defence (cf 6:34-35; Song 8:6).
honest rebuke — open reproof preferred to concealed love
the judgement that open rebuke is better than love that stays hidden — honest correction that helps preferred to affection that, unspoken, does nothing
set against the concealed love that fails to help
tob (better) — 'BETTER is open rebuke than hidden love'; love that will not speak a needed rebuke is inferior to honest reproof. Real love risks confrontation for the beloved's good (cf 27:6; 28:23).
unhelpful affection — love that stays concealed and silent
the love that remains hidden — affection real enough but concealed, silent where an honest rebuke was needed, and so of less worth than open reproof
the open rebuke that outranks it (266482)
set against the honest reproof that surpasses it

ahabah (love) — 'than HIDDEN love'; love that hides itself, failing to speak the correction the beloved needs, is worth less than an open rebuke. Affection unspoken and unhelping is a lesser thing than honest reproof.
faithfulness — the friend's honest hurt, to be trusted
the faithfulness of a friend's wounds — the honest, painful correction that can be trusted because it is meant for good, unlike an enemy's flattering kisses
the loving friend who gives them (266489)
welded to the true friend whose wounds they are
aman (be faithful) — 'FAITHFUL are the wounds of a friend'; a true friend's rebuke, though it hurts, is trustworthy and for one's good. Better an honest wound than a false caress (cf 27:5; 28:23).
true friendship — the loving friend whose rebuke is faithful
the friend, moved by love, whose painful wounds are faithful — real friendship that risks hurting for the sake of good, against the enemy's deceitful sweetness
set against the enemy whose profuse kisses betray
aheb (love/friend) — 'the wounds of a FRIEND'; the friend who loves enough to wound honestly. His hurts are faithful where an enemy's kisses are treacherous.
treacherous flattery — the enemy whose caresses deceive
the enemy whose kisses are profuse but false — flattering affection that betrays, the deceitful opposite of a friend's faithful wounds
the faithful friend it is set against (266489)
set against the loving friend whose wounds are faithful

sane (enemy/one who hates) — 'profuse are the kisses of an ENEMY'; the enemy's caresses are lavish but treacherous. Sweet words from a foe are more dangerous than a friend's honest wounds (cf 26:24-25).
satiety — the full soul that loathes even honey
the soul so full that it loathes even honey — satiety breeding disdain for good things, unable to relish what want would make sweet
the hungry soul it is set against (266497)
set against the hungry soul that relishes even the bitter
nephesh (soul/appetite) — 'one who is FULL loathes honey'; satiety despises even the sweetest good. Abundance can dull appetite and gratitude, so that plenty loathes what want would prize.
hunger — the soul to which even the bitter is sweet
the hungry soul to which everything bitter tastes sweet — want that makes even the harsh welcome, the mirror of satiety's disdain
the sated soul it is set against (266493)
set against the full soul that loathes even honey

nephesh (soul/appetite) — 'but to one who is HUNGRY everything bitter is sweet'; want transforms the bitter into the sweet. Hunger prizes what plenty scorns — a parable of how need reshapes desire and gratitude.
restless wandering — a man who strays from home, exposed like a bird from its nest

the straying of a man from his home, like a bird fluttering from its nest — the restless wandering that abandons one's proper place, leaving a man exposed and vulnerable, out of the shelter where he belongs
the rootless restlessness that abandons one's place and its shelter

nadad (wander/flee/stray) — 'like a bird that strays from its nest is a man who STRAYS from his home' (27:8); to abandon one's proper place is to be exposed and vulnerable, as a bird driven from its nest. Restless wandering forfeits the shelter of belonging.
cheer — the heart made glad, as by oil and perfume
the heart that oil and perfume gladden — the inner self cheered, an image for the gladness a friend's earnest counsel brings
welded to the joy that cheers it
leb (heart) — 'oil and perfume make the HEART glad'; the heart is cheered by pleasant things — and, the verse turns, by the sweet counsel of a friend. Friendship's counsel is a perfume to the soul.
gladness — the cheer a friend's counsel brings the heart
the gladness that cheers the heart as oil and perfume do — and above them, the sweetness of a friend's heartfelt counsel
the friend's counsel that brings it (266518)
welded to the earnest counsel whose sweetness it is
samach (be glad) — 'make the heart GLAD'; the cheer of pleasant things, and more, of a friend's sweet counsel. Good advice from a true friend gladdens like the finest perfume.
heartfelt counsel — the sweetness of a friend's earnest advice
the earnest, soul-deep counsel of a friend, whose sweetness gladdens the heart more than oil or perfume — the true friend's advice given from the heart
welded to the heart-cheer its sweetness gives

etsah (counsel) — 'the sweetness of a friend comes from his earnest COUNSEL'; a friend's heartfelt advice is sweeter than perfume. Genuine counsel, given from the soul, is one of friendship's chief gifts.
guilty fear — the wicked fleeing where no one pursues
the wicked who flee when no one is pursuing — the guilty conscience that startles at shadows, fear born not of danger but of guilt within
the righteous boldness it is set against (266524)
set against the clear-conscienced boldness of the righteous
rasha — 'the WICKED flee when no one pursues'; guilt makes cowards, startling at nothing. The wicked are haunted by a fear their own conscience breeds (cf Lev 26:17, 36).
clear-conscienced courage — the righteous bold as a lion
the righteous who are bold as a lion — the courage a clear conscience gives, unafraid because there is nothing within to accuse
the guilty flight it is set against (266519)
set against the wicked's groundless fear
tsaddiq — 'but the RIGHTEOUS are bold as a lion'; a clear conscience makes a man fearless. Integrity has nothing to flee from and so stands its ground like a lion.
confidence — the lion-like boldness of a clear conscience
the boldness/confidence of the righteous, fearless as a lion — the settled courage that flows from innocence, needing no flight because it fears no accuser
the righteous whose boldness it is (266524)
welded to the integrity that grounds it
batach (trust/be confident) — 'the righteous are BOLD as a lion'; the confidence of a clear conscience. Where guilt makes the wicked flee, innocence makes the righteous stand fearless.
targeted integrity — the upright the wicked try to lead astray
the upright whom the wicked seek to mislead into an evil way — integrity targeted for corruption, yet preserved while the seducer falls into his own pit
welded to the blamelessness that inherits good

yashar (upright) — 'whoever misleads the UPRIGHT into an evil way will fall into his own pit'; the upright, though targeted by seducers, are safe — the trap recoils on the trapper. Integrity is protected (cf 26:27).
blamelessness — that inherits good while the seducer falls
the blamelessness that receives a goodly inheritance while the one who would corrupt the upright falls into his own pit — integrity rewarded, corruption self-destroyed
the upright it is joined with (266528)
welded to the upright who cannot be led astray

tamim (blameless/whole) — 'but the BLAMELESS will have a goodly inheritance'; blamelessness is rewarded with good, where the seducer of the upright is ruined. The whole-hearted inherit; the corrupt fall.
self-conceit — the rich man's flattering self-estimate
the rich man's conceit of his own wisdom — wealth breeding a flattering self-estimate that a discerning poor man easily sees through
the poor man's discernment that exposes it (266541)
set against the true understanding that finds him out
chakam (wise, in his own eyes) — 'a rich man is WISE in his own eyes'; wealth tempts a man to overrate his own wisdom. Riches flatter the self, but do not confer discernment (cf 26:12; 28:26).
true understanding — the poor man who sees through the rich man's conceit
the understanding of a poor man who searches out and exposes the self-conceited rich — true discernment, unbought by wealth, that sees a man for what he is
set against the rich man's flattering self-estimate

bin (understand/discern) — 'but a poor man who has UNDERSTANDING will find him out'; real discernment, which wealth cannot buy, sees through the rich man's self-conceit. Understanding is no respecter of purses.
public good — the glory when the righteous prevail
the righteous whose triumph brings great glory — the public flourishing and joy of a society when good men hold sway, the opposite of the fear the wicked's rise brings
the wicked's rise it is set against (266547)
set against the wicked whose ascendancy makes people hide

tsaddiq — 'when the RIGHTEOUS triumph, there is great glory'; the ascendancy of the good is a public blessing, a time of glory and confidence (cf 28:28; 29:2). Who holds power shapes a whole people's life.
public fear — people hiding when the wicked come to power
the wicked whose rise to power makes people hide themselves — tyranny driving the populace into concealment, the dark opposite of the glory the righteous bring
the righteous triumph it is set against (266543)
set against the righteous whose triumph brings glory
rasha — 'but when the WICKED rise, people hide themselves'; the ascendancy of the wicked spreads fear, driving good people into hiding. Bad rulers make a whole society cower (cf 28:28; 29:16).
cover-up — sins hidden, which cannot prosper
the transgressions a man conceals rather than confesses — sin covered up, which festers and forbids prosperity, the opposite of open confession
set against the confessing that forsakes and finds mercy
pesha (transgression) — 'whoever conceals his TRANSGRESSIONS will not prosper'; hidden sin cannot be healed and blocks all true prospering. Cover-up is the enemy of the soul (cf Ps 32:3-5).
penitence — owning and abandoning sin, which finds mercy
the confessing and forsaking of sin — the penitence that both owns the wrong and turns from it, and so obtains mercy where concealment brings only ruin
welded to the divine mercy it receives

yadah (confess/acknowledge) — 'but he who CONFESSES and forsakes them will obtain mercy'; true repentance owns sin and abandons it — and finds mercy. Confession, not cover-up, opens the way to grace (cf 1 John 1:9).
divine mercy — granted to the one who confesses and forsakes
the mercy obtained by the one who confesses and forsakes his sin — the divine compassion that answers penitence, freely given where concealment would have found only ruin
welded to the penitence God answers with mercy

racham (have mercy/compassion) — 'will obtain MERCY'; God's mercy is the reward of confession and forsaking. Locus external:god — the divine compassion that meets true repentance (cf Ps 32:5; 1 John 1:9).
reverent dread — the blessed, continual fear of the LORD
the fearing of the LORD always — the continual, reverent dread of God that keeps a man from evil and is pronounced blessed, the opposite of the hardened heart
the hardened heart it is set against (266563)
set against the heart that hardens and falls
pachad (fear/dread) — 'blessed is the one who FEARS the LORD always'; a heart kept in continual reverent awe of God is blessed and safe. The fear of the LORD is a perpetual guard (cf 23:17; 28:14b).
obduracy — the hard heart that falls into calamity
the hardening of the heart — the obduracy that refuses to fear God and reverence his word, and so falls headlong into calamity, the ruin of the unfearing
the reverent fear it is set against (266560)
set against the blessed fear of the LORD
qashah (harden) — 'but whoever HARDENS his heart will fall into calamity'; the heart hardened against God and correction runs to its own ruin. Obduracy is the road to disaster (cf 29:1).
menacing greed — the predatory roar of the wicked ruler
the roaring/growling rapacity of the wicked ruler — the menacing hunger of a lion or bear, an image of power that terrifies and consumes the poor
the wicked ruler whose menace it is (266570)
welded to the tyranny it expresses
naham (roar/growl) — 'like a ROARING lion'; the wicked ruler's rapacity roars like a hunting beast. His power is felt as a predator's menace by those beneath him.
tyranny — the wicked ruler preying on the helpless poor
the wicked ruler over a poor people who is like a roaring lion or a charging bear — tyranny that preys on the defenceless, power turned predator
welded to the roaring rapacity that marks it

rasha — 'like a roaring lion or a charging bear is a WICKED ruler over a poor people'; a corrupt ruler is a beast of prey to the helpless. Power without righteousness devours those it should protect (cf 28:3; 29:2).
senseless cruelty — the ruler without understanding, a great oppressor
the lack of understanding in a ruler that makes him a cruel oppressor — folly in power turning to tyranny, senselessness that crushes those it governs
the hatred of unjust gain it is set against (266580)
set against the ruler who hates ill-gotten gain and endures

tebunah (understanding) — 'a ruler who LACKS understanding is a cruel oppressor'; folly in a ruler becomes cruelty. Without understanding, power oppresses; the senseless ruler grinds his people (cf 28:15).
incorruptibility — the ruler who spurns ill-gotten gain and lives long
the hating of unjust gain by a ruler who therefore prolongs his days — the incorruptibility that refuses to profit by wrong, the opposite of the cruel oppressor's greed
the senseless cruelty it is set against (266577)
set against the understanding-less ruler who oppresses
sane (hate) — 'but he who HATES unjust gain will prolong his days'; the ruler who spurns corruption endures. To hate ill-gotten gain is the mark of a ruler who lasts (cf 28:16a; 29:4).
haunted guilt — the murderer driven a fugitive by the blood he shed
the being burdened/crushed with the blood of another — the guilt of murder that makes a man a restless fugitive until death, a conscience that will not let him rest
(the blood of the victim that haunts him)
the bloodguilt that drives a man in ceaseless flight

ashaq (burdened/oppressed with) — 'if one is BURDENED with the blood of another, he will be a fugitive until death'; the guilt of shed blood haunts the murderer, driving him restless to the grave. Bloodguilt is a burden no man carries in peace (cf Gen 4:12-14).
wholeness — the blameless walk that is delivered
the integrity in which a man walks and by which he is delivered — the whole, honest life that stands and is saved, against the crookedness that suddenly falls
the crookedness it is set against (266597)
set against the crooked ways that end in sudden fall
tamim (blameless/whole) — 'whoever walks in INTEGRITY will be delivered'; the whole-hearted, honest walk is safe and saved. Integrity is deliverance; crookedness is ruin (cf 28:6; 10:9).
duplicity — the crooked ways that end in sudden fall
the crookedness of a man's ways that brings him to a sudden fall — the duplicity and double-dealing that, unlike integrity, collapses without warning
the integrity it is set against (266595)
set against the blameless walk that is delivered

iqqesh (crooked/perverse) — 'but he who is CROOKED in his ways will suddenly fall'; duplicity brings sudden ruin. Emergent: the crooked way that seems to prosper, then collapses all at once (cf 28:18a).
diligent labour — the honest work that brings plenty of bread
the working of one's land that yields plenty of bread — steady, honest labour, the opposite of chasing worthless fantasies
the empty pursuits it is set against (266606)
set against the vain chasing that brings poverty
abad (work/serve) — 'whoever WORKS his land will have plenty of bread' (cf 12:11); honest, steady labour feeds a man. Diligence brings plenty; fantasy brings want.
fantasy-chasing — the empty schemes that bring plenty of poverty
the following of worthless pursuits — the chasing of empty schemes and vain fantasies that yields not bread but a full measure of poverty
the honest labour it is set against (266601)
set against the diligent work that brings plenty

req (empty/worthless) — 'but he who follows WORTHLESS pursuits will have plenty of poverty'; chasing vain fantasies instead of working brings only want. Emergent: the get-rich fantasy as the road to poverty (cf 12:11; 28:22).
rebellion — a land's sin that breeds instability and many rulers
the transgression of a land that throws it into instability — sin and rebellion multiplying rulers, no throne standing long where wrong prevails
set against the discernment that gives stability
pesha (transgression/rebellion) — 'when a LAND transgresses, it has many rulers'; national sin breeds chaos and a churn of rulers. Where wrong prevails, no government stands (cf 29:2, 16).
discernment — that gives a land long stability
the understanding of a man of discernment and knowledge, by which a land's stability is long preserved — wisdom in leadership as the ground of enduring order
set against the sin that breeds instability

bin (understand/discern) — 'but with a man of UNDERSTANDING and knowledge, its stability will long continue'; wise, knowing leadership steadies a nation where sin would topple it. Understanding in a ruler is a land's long peace.
knowing rule — that with understanding preserves a land
the knowledge that, joined to understanding in a ruler, long preserves a land's stability — informed, discerning governance against the chaos of transgression
welded to the discernment it is paired with

yada (know/knowledge) — 'a man of understanding and KNOWLEDGE, its stability will long continue'; knowledge in leadership, with understanding, gives a nation enduring order. Wise rulers are a land's stability.
the faithfulness of the reliable man who abounds with blessings — trustworthy steadiness, the opposite of the greedy haste that grasps and is punished
welded to the blessings faithfulness draws down

emunah (faithfulness) — 'a FAITHFUL man will abound with blessings'; steady faithfulness is richly blessed, where greedy haste is punished. Reliability, not shortcuts, draws down good (cf 28:20b; 20:21).
greedy haste — the rush to wealth that goes not unpunished
the hastening to be rich — the impatient greed that grasps at wealth by any means and does not go unpunished, the opposite of the faithful man's blessed steadiness
the faithfulness it is set against (266618)
set against the faithful man who abounds in blessing

uts (hasten/press) — 'but whoever HASTENS to be rich will not go unpunished'; the rush to wealth, impatient of honest gain, ends in punishment. Emergent: greedy haste as a punished folly (cf 28:22; 13:11; 20:21).
injustice — the favouritism that is 'not good'
the showing of partiality that is 'not good' — favouritism in judgement, an injustice made worse by how cheaply a man will sell his integrity for it
welded to the wrong a trifle can buy
tob (good), negated — 'to show PARTIALITY is not good' (cf 24:23); favouritism perverts justice. And the corruptible will pervert it for the smallest bribe.
corruptibility — a man transgressing for a mere piece of bread
the doing of wrong for a mere piece of bread — the shocking cheapness of the corruptible man, who will transgress justice for the smallest gain
welded to the favouritism that sells justice cheap
pasha (transgress/do wrong) — 'but for a piece of BREAD a man will do wrong'; the corruptible will pervert justice for a trifle. Integrity has no price the greedy will not undercut.
miserly greed — the 'evil eye' hastening after wealth
the stinginess/greed of the man with the 'evil eye' who hastens after wealth — grasping miserliness so fixed on getting that it is blind to the ruin ahead
welded to the greedy rush after wealth

ra + ayin (evil eye) — 'a STINGY man hastens after wealth' (opp. the 'bountiful eye', 22:9); miserly greed drives a frantic pursuit of riches. The grasping eye is fixed on gain and blind to the poverty it courts.
anxious grasping — the frantic pursuit of riches
the hastening/anxious rushing of the stingy man after wealth — the frantic grasping that cannot wait, driven by greed and blind to its own end
the blindness to ruin it breeds (266639)
welded to the not-knowing of the poverty coming
bahal (hasten/be anxious) — 'HASTENS after wealth'; greed makes a man frantic, grasping impatiently at riches. The rush itself blinds him to the poverty rushing toward him.
blind greed — not seeing the poverty his haste invites
the not-knowing of the stingy man that poverty will come upon him — the blindness that greed breeds, so fixed on getting that he cannot see the ruin his haste is bringing
the anxious haste that blinds him (266636)
welded to the frantic grasping that hides his end from him
yada (know), negated — 'and does not KNOW that poverty will come upon him'; greed blinds a man to his own ruin. The miser, fixed on gain, never sees the want his grasping invites (cf 28:20).
honest reproof — the rebuke that in the end wins more favour than flattery
the rebuking of a man that afterward wins more favour than flattery — the honest reproof that, though it stings at first, earns lasting gratitude, unlike the flatterer's momentary charm
the flattery it is set against (266650)
set against the flattering tongue that pleases then fails

yakach (rebuke/reprove) — 'whoever REBUKES a man will afterward find more favor than he who flatters'; honest correction, resented at first, is valued in the end above flattery. Emergent: the reprover ultimately more loved than the flatterer (cf 27:5-6; 29:5).
flattery — the smooth tongue that pleases now but fails in the end
the flattering with the tongue that pleases for the moment but wins less lasting favour than honest rebuke — smooth speech that gratifies now and is valued less in the end
the honest rebuke it is set against (266644)
set against the reprover who wins lasting favour

chalaq (be smooth/flatter) — 'than he who FLATTERS with his tongue'; flattery charms momentarily but earns less true favour than an honest rebuke. Emergent: the flatterer preferred at first, forgotten at last (cf 26:28; 29:5).
self-justifying sin — robbing a parent and denying it is wrong
the transgression of robbing father or mother while saying 'that is no transgression' — sin excused and rationalised, the self-justification that makes a plunderer of his own parents feel innocent
the destroyer he is kin to (266660)
welded to the destructiveness his excuse makes him share

pesha (transgression) — 'whoever robs his father or mother and says, 'that is no TRANSGRESSION''; to sin and rationalise it away is doubly evil. Self-justification hardens a plunderer into a destroyer (cf 30:11-14).
destructiveness — the ruin-worker whose companion the self-excusing robber is
