the destroyer/ruiner to whom the one who robs his parents and excuses it is a companion — the destructive nature that self-justified plundering makes a man share
the self-excused sin that joins him to it (266657)
welded to the rationalised robbery that makes him kin to ruin
shachath (destroy/ruin) — 'is a companion to a man who DESTROYS'; the self-excusing robber of his parents is kin to the wanton destroyer. To rationalise plunder is to join the ranks of the ruinous.
covetousness — the greedy man who stirs up strife
the greedy/wide-appetite soul that stirs up strife — covetousness that, grasping for more, breeds conflict wherever it reaches, the opposite of trust that is enriched
welded to the conflict greed provokes
nephesh (soul/appetite) + rachab (wide/greedy) — 'a GREEDY man stirs up strife'; covetousness breeds conflict, grasping hands colliding. Greed sets men against one another (cf 15:18; 13:10).
conflict — the strife a greedy soul stirs up
the strife/contention that a greedy man stirs up — the conflict covetousness breeds as grasping appetites clash, set against the peace and enrichment of trusting God
welded to the covetousness that breeds it
madon (strife) — 'stirs up STRIFE'; greed's grasping breeds conflict. Where covetousness reaches, contention follows.
God-reliance — the trust that is enriched
the trusting in the LORD that is enriched — reliance on God rather than grasping greed, the confidence that receives plenty where covetousness only breeds strife
the greed it is set against (266662)
set against the greedy soul that stirs strife

batach (trust) — 'but the one who TRUSTS in the LORD will be enriched'; reliance on God, not greedy grasping, is the way to true plenty. Trust is enriched where greed is only embroiled (cf 28:26; 16:20).
self-reliance — trusting one's own heart, which is folly
the trusting in one's own mind/heart that makes a man a fool — self-reliant confidence in one's own judgement, the folly opposite to walking in wisdom and being delivered
the wisdom it is set against (266672)
set against the walk in wisdom that delivers
batach (trust) — 'whoever TRUSTS in his own mind is a fool' (cf 3:5-7); to lean on one's own understanding is folly. Self-trust, not humble wisdom, is the fool's undoing.
humble wisdom — the walk that is delivered
the walking in wisdom that delivers a man — the humble reliance on wisdom rather than one's own mind, the safe opposite of self-trusting folly
the self-trust it is set against (266668)
set against the fool who trusts his own mind
chokmah (wisdom) — 'but he who walks in WISDOM will be delivered'; humble wisdom, not self-confidence, is the way of safety. To walk in wisdom is to be delivered where self-trust falls (cf 3:5-6).
generosity — the open hand that never wants
the giving to the poor of the generous man who therefore will not want — the open hand that God supplies, the opposite of the one who hides his eyes from need
the callous hiding it is set against (266678)
set against the shut eyes that earn many curses
natan (give) — 'whoever GIVES to the poor will not want' (cf 11:24-25; 19:17); the generous never lack, for God supplies the open hand. Emergent: generosity to the poor as the way to never wanting.
callous blindness — willfully not seeing the poor's need, and cursed for it
the hiding of the eyes from the poor's need — the willful blindness that refuses to see suffering, and so earns many a curse, the opposite of the open hand that is supplied
the generosity it is set against (266674)
set against the giving hand that never wants

alam (hide/conceal) — 'but he who HIDES his eyes will get many a curse'; to look away from the poor's need is a cursed callousness. Emergent: willful blindness to suffering as a cursed refusal of mercy (cf 21:13).

the wicked's tyranny it is set against (266682)
set against the wicked whose rise made people hide
tsaddiq — 'but when they perish, the RIGHTEOUS increase'; the fall of the wicked lets the righteous flourish. Good multiplies where tyranny is removed.

the exploitation that, coming from a fellow-sufferer, ruins utterly

the seeking of God that opens it (266710)
set against the God-seeking that grasps it fully

God-ward pursuit — the seeking that opens understanding of justice

welded to the complete grasp of justice it yields

moral clarity — the complete understanding of the God-seeker
the complete understanding of justice that comes to those who seek the LORD — moral clarity as the fruit of a God-ward heart, against the evil's blindness
set against the evil's failure to understand
bin (understand) — 'understand it COMPLETELY'; those who seek God grasp justice fully. The moral sight the wicked lack is given to the seeking heart. To know God is to understand what is right.

the integrity in which the poor man walks — the wholeness and honesty of life that makes him better than a crooked rich man, wealth notwithstanding
welded to the evaluation that ranks it above riches
tom (integrity/wholeness) — 'a poor man who walks in his INTEGRITY'; honest, whole-hearted living is worth more than a crooked fortune. Integrity is the true wealth (cf 10:9; 28:18).
discernment — the law-keeping son who honours his father

the shame it is set against (266727)
set against the son who shames his father
bin (understand/discern) — 'the one who keeps the law is a son with UNDERSTANDING'; law-keeping is the mark of a discerning son, and an honour to his father. Obedience and understanding go together.

the understanding it is set against (266724)
set against the discerning son who honours his father

set against the kindness to the poor that finally gains it

set against the exploitative amassing that ends in its hands

the willful deafness that provokes it (266739)
welded to the refusal of the law that poisons the prayer

welded to the innocence its hatred targets

welded to the bloodthirsty enmity that seeks its life

the fool's unrestraint it is set against (266761)
set against the fool who vents everything

the wickedness it breeds in officials (266775)
welded to the corrupt servants his credulity produces

the ruler's credulity that breeds it (266770)
welded to the lie-heeding rule that produces it

the just care for the poor that founds a lasting reign

set against the wisdom the rod and reproof impart

welded to the wicked whose increase multiplies it

the fool he is set below (266836)
set against the fool who has more hope than he

welded to the sin his anger multiplies

the pride it is set against (266848)
set against the pride that brings a man low

welded to the self-hatred complicity amounts to

the wise pacifiers they are set against (266927)
set against the wise who turn away wrath

anshe latson (men of scorn / scoffers) — 'SCOFFERS set a city aflame'; scorn is incendiary, inflaming a whole community to strife. Emergent: the scoffer as an arsonist of conflict, against the wise peacemaker (cf 22:10).
peacemaking — the wise who calm the wrath scoffers inflame
the wise who turn away wrath — the peacemaking discernment that calms the anger scoffers inflame, quenching the fire scorn had lit
the scoffers' incendiary scorn it is set against (266924)
set against the scoffers who set a city aflame
chakam (wise) — 'but the WISE turn away wrath'; wisdom is a peacemaker, calming the anger that scorn inflames. Where scoffers kindle, the wise quench (cf 15:1).
unreachable folly — the fool who rages and mocks, giving no quiet
the fool who, when a wise man argues with him, only rages and laughs so that there is no resolution — folly beyond the reach of reasoning, turning debate into noise
welded to the raging and mocking that leaves no quiet

evil (fool) — 'if a wise man has an argument with a FOOL, the fool only rages and laughs'; there is no reasoning with folly — the fool answers argument with rage and mockery, never with quiet. Debating a fool is futile.
turbulence — the fool's raging that admits no resolution
the raging and agitation of the fool in argument — the turbulent anger and mockery that make any quiet resolution impossible, folly's refusal of reasoned peace
the fool whose turbulence it is (266935)
welded to the unreachable folly it expresses
ragaz (rage/be agitated) — 'the fool only RAGES and laughs, and there is no quiet'; the fool meets argument with turbulent rage, so no calm settling is possible. Folly cannot be reasoned to rest.
wisdom coming INTO the heart, taking up residence within
welded to the heart it indwells
chokmah pictured as ENTERING (bo) the heart — wisdom is not external instruction but an inward guest that settles in the seat.
the heart — the seat wisdom enters
the inner seat that wisdom comes to indwell
leb as the SEAT that receives wisdom — the destination of the whole search; wisdom lodges in the heart.
knowledge become sweet/pleasant to the inner self
welded to the soul's pleasure in it
daat here not merely possessed but ENJOYED — knowledge becomes pleasant, an affective good, not a burden.
pleasantness — knowledge's sweetness to the soul
knowledge being pleasant/sweet to the soul
the soul that finds it sweet
the affective bond between knowledge and the self
naem (be pleasant/sweet) — the read surfaces that wisdom's goal is not grim duty but DELIGHT: knowledge pleasing the nephesh.
the soul — the self to which knowledge is sweet
the inner self that finds knowledge pleasant
the seat of the pleasure in knowledge
nephesh as the seat of ENJOYMENT here (cf 1:18-19 where it was forfeited) — the self savouring knowledge; the whole inner person delighting.
discretion — shrewd forethought that guards the person
discretion keeping watch over the person, warding off danger
mezimmah (cf 1:4, positive) now PERSONIFIED as a guardian — the same shrewdness that could scheme here stands sentinel over the one who has it.
understanding standing guard over the person
paired with discretion as twin protectors
tebunah paired with mezimmah as inner GUARDIANS — the moral goods actively defend the one who has taken them in (2:10).
deliverance — wisdom's rescue from the way of evil
being delivered from the way of evil and perverse men
welded to the evil it rescues from
natsal (snatch away/deliver) — the protective goods (2:11) issue in RESCUE: wisdom actively pulls the person out of evil's way.
evil — the way from which one is delivered
the way of evil, the danger wisdom rescues from
paired with perverted speech as the danger
ra (cf 1:16) as the WAY delivered-from — a whole path/manner of life, embodied in 'men of perverted speech'.
perversity — the twisted speech of evil men
the perverse, twisted things such men speak
welded to the way of evil
tahpukot (perversities/things-turned-upside-down) — the crookedness of the wicked's speech; the inner distortion that marks the way of evil.
uprightness — the straight paths the wicked forsake
the upright way abandoned for the ways of darkness
the darkness it is traded for
the good forsaken in the turn to darkness
yosher (straightness) as the good ABANDONED — the wicked's descent is an active forsaking of the straight for the dark; uprightness surfaced only as what is left behind.
rejoicing — gladness perversely taken in doing evil
rejoicing in the doing of evil — joy fixed on wrong
the perverse coupling: gladness welded to evil-doing
sameach (rejoice) at its darkest: the affect of joy turned on EVIL itself — not weakness but delight in wrong. Read at full weight.
evil — the doing in which they rejoice
the evil deeds that are the object of their joy
ra as the object of rejoicing — evil not merely done but ENJOYED.
delight — exultation in the perverseness of evil
the second perverse affect, paired with rejoicing
gil (exult/spin-with-joy) intensifies sameach: not just gladness but exultant delight in perversity — the affect doubled.
perversity — the twistedness of evil in which they delight
the perverse crookedness of evil that they exult in
welded to the evil it twists
tahpukot (cf 2:12) here the OBJECT of delight — the wicked exult not just in evil but in its very perversity/upside-downness.
the evil whose perversity they exult in
the delight fixed on its perversity
the substance of the perversity delighted in
distinct third ra of the passage (2:14): the evil whose PERVERSENESS (not just deed) is the object of exultation — the deepest point of the descent.
perversity — the twisted, crooked way of the evil man
the crookedness of the paths of evil men — the moral perversity that bends its way from the straight, twisted in its very course
welded to the devious wandering that goes with it
iqqesh (crooked/perverse) — 'men whose paths are CROOKED' (2:15); the wicked walk a twisted road, their way bent from the straight. Crookedness of path images crookedness of heart (cf 4:24; 28:18).
deviousness — the underhanded, winding ways of the evil
the deviousness of evil men who are twisted and underhanded in their ways — the furtive, winding course of those who cannot go straight
welded to the crookedness it accompanies

luz (be devious/turn aside) — 'and who are DEVIOUS in their ways' (2:15); the wicked are underhanded, their ways winding and furtive. Deviousness pairs with crookedness in the man who has left the straight path.
forgetting — the adulteress's forgetting of the covenant of her God
forgetting the covenant of her God — a culpable letting-slip of sacred bond
welded to the covenant it lets fall
shakach (forget) here is not mere lapse but MORAL forgetting — the sacred covenant deliberately let slip; the inner root of her betrayal.
attentiveness — making the ear strain toward wisdom
bending the ear attentively toward wisdom
the deliberate turning of attention that seeking requires
qashab (make attentive) is the first CONDITION-operation: wisdom is not received passively but by an ear made to strain — the effortful attention the whole ch.2 protasis builds on.
wisdom — what the attentive ear is bent toward
wisdom as the object the ear strains after
the goal of the bent ear
chokmah as the target of active listening (qashab); the seeking of wisdom requires the ear's deliberate turn.
the heart — the inner faculty inclined toward understanding
the heart as the organ that must be bent, not just the ear
leb here is the SEAT actively 'inclined' (natah) — wisdom is sought not only by the ear (attention) but by turning the whole inner faculty. A rare explicit seat-as-actor.
understanding — toward which the heart inclines
the object of the inclined heart
tebunah (discernment) as the heart's target; first of two occurrences in 2:2-3.
the good — the way the wise walk
walking in the way of good people
tob (the good ones/good way) — the positive outcome: deliverance from evil issues in walking WITH the good.
keeping — holding to the paths of the righteous
keeping/guarding one's steps to the righteous paths
welded to the righteous way it holds to
shamar (keep/guard) read as a characteristic — the vigilant holding-to the right way; the active adherence that completes the deliverance (contrast the wicked's forsaking, 2:13).
the righteous — whose paths one keeps to
the righteous whose paths the wise hold to
tsaddiq (the righteous) as the goal-company — the delivered walk in and hold to the way of the righteous; the chapter closes on belonging to the good.
uprightness — the straight who will inhabit the land
the upright who abide/inherit the land
paired with integrity as the enduring character
yashar (cf 2:7) as the character that ENDURES — uprightness rewarded with permanence.
blamelessness — the whole who remain in the land
the blameless who remain, not cut off
welded to uprightness as the abiding pair
tamim (blameless/whole) — distinct from tom(2:7): here the completeness that remains; the upright and the whole together outlast the wicked.
wickedness — the guilty who are cut off from the land
the wicked cut off, not enduring
paired with the treacherous as the doomed
rasha (the guilty/wicked) — the antithesis of the upright (2:21); character determines whether one abides or is cut off.
treachery — the faithless torn out of the land
welded to wickedness as the uprooted
bagad (act treacherously/deal faithlessly) — betrayal of trust; the treacherous share the wicked's uprooting. Read at full weight.
calling out — crying aloud for insight
raising the voice, calling out for insight as for a treasure
the vocal, urgent seeking that matches the bent ear and heart
qara here is the seeker's cry (contrast Wisdom's qara, 1:20-24): the search for understanding becomes a loud, urgent calling-out — desire made vocal.
insight sought by raising the voice, called for like a treasure
the object of the vocal seeking
binah as the thing 'called out for' — the search for understanding is vocal, urgent, like crying for help (2:3).
understanding — for which the voice is raised
understanding sought by lifting the voice
the aim of the raised voice
distinct second tebunah (2:3): understanding now the object of the raised voice — the seeking intensifies from bent ear to lifted cry.
seeking — searching for wisdom as for silver/hidden treasure
seeking wisdom with the intensity of a treasure-hunt
welded to the treasure-image: the search is costly, deliberate, prized
baqash raises the seeking of 2:2-3 to its peak: wisdom pursued like buried silver — the effort that the whole ch.2 promise turns on.
understanding — grasping the fear of the LORD as the fruit of seeking
coming to understand the fear of the LORD
the payoff of the search: understanding opens onto reverence
bin here yields not data but the fear of God — understanding terminates in reverence (inverting 1:7: fear begins knowledge, knowledge deepens fear).
reverent fear of God — what the seeker comes to understand
the reverence gained by the one who seeks wisdom
paired with the knowledge of God
yirah as the SUMMIT of the search (cf 1:7 as its beginning) — God the target, the fear the human interior.
knowledge — the knowing of God found by the seeker
coupled to the fear of the LORD as its twin
daat-elohim: knowing God, paired with fearing him — the two faces of the seeker's reward.
wisdom given by God, the source of the seeker's competence
the gift whose source is God's own mouth
chokmah's SOURCE named as God — the human good is given, not self-generated (cf the register: God = source D3).
knowledge coming from the mouth of God
distinct daat from 267043: here the knowledge that ISSUES from God, a gift, alongside understanding.
paired with knowledge as the twin gift
tebunah given by God — the discernment the seeker sought (2:3) is finally God's to give.
sound wisdom — the effectual competence God stores for the upright
the practical, sound wisdom God lays up for the upright
the reserve God keeps for the upright
tushiyyah = success/sound-competence, distinct from chokmah — the effective wisdom that actually works, stored as a treasure for the upright.
uprightness — the straight of heart for whom wisdom is stored
the upright for whom sound wisdom is reserved
paired with integrity in the next line
yashar (straight/upright) — the moral condition that qualifies one for the stored wisdom; the character God rewards.
integrity — the wholeness of those God shields
walking in integrity, under God's shield
welded to the walk it describes
tom (completeness/integrity) — the undivided moral wholeness; those who walk in it have God as shield. Distinct from yashar (straightness): tom is wholeness, yashar is straightness.
the just order that God protects
mishpat here = the paths of justice God keeps; the moral order upheld from above.
the faithful/pious — those God watches over
the devoted faithful whose way God watches over
chasidim = the covenant-faithful/devout; a char of settled loyalty. God's watching-over (267062) is its qualifier — God-content guarding the pious.
coming to understand righteousness, justice, equity, every good path
the discernment that opens the whole moral field
bin here yields the ETHICAL triad (cf 1:3) — understanding terminates in moral perception, not just theory.
righteousness — first of the moral triad understood
rightness of the person, now understood
tsedeq (cf 1:3) recurs as the object of understanding — the moral goods are not just given but grasped.
just judgement grasped by the seeker
distinct mishpat from 267061 (God's paths): here the justice the seeker comes to understand — the same good, now internalised.
even, straight dealing grasped by the seeker
mesharim (cf 1:3) as the third moral good understood — the level, fair dealing of the discerning.
the good — every good course the seeker discerns
the summation of the moral goods
tob ('every good path') gathers up the triad — the whole field of good conduct now open to the one who understands.
malicious tale-bearing — accusing a servant to his master, and incurring guilt
the slandering of a servant to his master — malicious tale-bearing against one who cannot easily defend himself, which recoils in a curse and guilt on the slanderer
(the guilt it brings on the slanderer)
the malicious accusation that rebounds on the one who makes it

lashan (slander/accuse) — 'do not SLANDER a servant to his master, lest he curse you, and you be held guilty' (30:10); malicious accusation, especially of the lowly, brings guilt on the accuser. To injure a servant with the tongue is to court a curse (cf 6:16-19).
filial impiety — the generation that curses its father and will not bless its mother
the impiety of a generation that curses its father and does not bless its mother — the contempt for parents that heads Agur's portrait of a corrupt generation, honour owed and withheld
the contempt for father and mother that marks a corrupt generation

barak (bless), negated + curse — 'there are those who curse their fathers and do not BLESS their mothers' (30:11); the first mark of a wicked generation is contempt for parents. To curse a father and withhold blessing from a mother is a foundational impiety (cf 20:20; 30:17; Ex 21:17).
self-righteous self-deception — thinking oneself pure while unwashed of filth
the being 'clean in one's own eyes' while unwashed of one's filth — the self-righteous self-deception that congratulates itself on a purity it does not have, blind to its own defilement
(the unwashed filth it will not see)
the self-flattering blindness that mistakes its own filth for cleanness

tahor (clean/pure), self-assessed — 'there are those who are CLEAN in their own eyes but are not washed of their filth' (30:12); the second mark of a corrupt generation is self-righteous self-deception — a purity claimed, not real. The heart most defiled may be surest of its own cleanness (cf 16:2; 20:9; Luke 18:11).
insatiable craving — the greed that, like the leech, never says 'Enough'
the never-being-satisfied of the leech's daughters ('Give, Give') and the four insatiable things — an image of greed and craving that, like Sheol and fire, can never be filled and never says 'Enough'
(the four insatiables it is likened to)
the bottomless appetite that no amount of getting ever contents

saba (be satisfied), negated — 'the leech has two daughters: Give and Give... never SATISFIED... never say, 'Enough'' (30:15-16); greed is bottomless, insatiable as the grave, the barren womb, the parched land, and fire. Craving is a hunger nothing fills (cf 27:20; Eccl 5:10).
filial derision — the eye that mocks its father
the mocking of a father with the eye — the derision of a parent that, with scorn for a mother's authority, draws a terrible judgement, contempt for the parents who gave one life
the scorn of the mother it is joined with (267134)
welded to the scorning of a mother's authority

laag (mock/deride) — 'the eye that MOCKS a father' (30:17); to deride one's father is a grievous impiety, judged with horror (the corpse left for ravens). Contempt for parents is contempt for the source of one's life (cf 30:11; 20:20).
filial contempt — scorning obedience to a mother
the scorning to obey a mother — the contempt for maternal authority that, with mockery of a father, marks the rebellious child on whom a fearful judgement falls
the mockery of the father it is joined with (267132)
welded to the eye that mocks a father
buz (despise/scorn) — 'and SCORNS to obey a mother' (30:17); contempt for a mother's authority, twin to mockery of a father, brings terrible judgement. To scorn the parents is to invite ruin.
reverent wonder — things too wonderful to grasp

the wonder Agur feels at things too wonderful for him — the reverent amazement before mysteries that exceed his grasp (the eagle's flight, the ship's course, the way of a man with a maid), humility that marvels rather than presumes
the acknowledged ignorance it goes with (267146)
welded to the not-understanding Agur openly confesses

pala (be wonderful/beyond) — 'three things are too WONDERFUL for me' (30:18); the wise heart marvels at what it cannot fully grasp. Wonder before mystery is a mark of humility, not ignorance ashamed (cf 30:2-4).
owned mystery — Agur confessing four things he cannot understand
the not-understanding that Agur confesses of the four wonderful things — the honest owning of mystery, refusing to pretend a comprehension he lacks, wonder joined to humble ignorance
welded to the reverent amazement Agur feels
yada (know/understand), negated — 'four I do not UNDERSTAND' (30:18); Agur openly owns what he cannot comprehend. To confess the limits of one's understanding is wisdom, not failure (cf 30:2-3).
humble self-abasement — Agur owning himself too stupid to be a man
the confession of Agur that he is too stupid/brutish to be a man — the profound humility that, before God's wisdom, owns its own ignorance, the ground on which true wisdom begins
welded to the human understanding he confesses to lack

baar (be brutish/stupid) — 'surely I am too STUPID to be a man'; Agur opens by confessing his own ignorance. Such humility is not despair but the beginning of wisdom — the wise know how little they know (cf 30:3; 26:12; Job 42:3).
owned ignorance — Agur disclaiming a man's understanding before God
the understanding that Agur confesses he does not have — the honest disclaiming of his own wisdom before the knowledge of the Holy One, humility that makes room for God to teach
the confessed brutishness it belongs with (267164)
welded to the self-abasement that owns it

binah (understanding) — 'I have not the UNDERSTANDING of a man'; Agur owns that he lacks true understanding, disclaiming wisdom before God (30:3-4). To confess ignorance before the Holy One is the humility on which real knowledge is built.
habitual adultery — sin grown as casual as a meal

the way of the adulteress who eats, wipes her mouth, and says 'I have done no wrong' — habitual sin grown so casual that it is committed and dismissed as easily as a meal, no more troubling to the conscience
the brazen denial that accompanies it (267179)
welded to the seared conscience that denies all wrong

naaph (commit adultery) — 'this is the way of an ADULTERESS'; habitual sin becomes as routine and untroubling as eating. The chilling ease with which she sins and dismisses it shows a conscience wholly seared (cf 5:6; 1 Tim 4:2).
seared conscience — brazen denial of guilt after sin
the saying 'I have done no wrong' after the deed — the brazen, self-acquitting denial of a conscience so seared that it feels no guilt, wiping the mouth as if nothing had happened
welded to the casual adultery it dismisses

aven (wrong/iniquity), denied — 'and says, 'I have done no WRONG''; the deepest horror of habitual sin is not the deed but the untroubled conscience that denies it. Sin becomes invisible to the one hardened in it (cf 30:12; Jer 6:15).
instinctive prudence — the great wisdom of small, weak creatures

the exceeding wisdom of four small creatures — the instinctive prudence and foresight of the weak and lowly (ant, badger, locust, lizard) that shames the great, wisdom being a matter not of size or strength but of provident sense
the prudent wisdom that dwells in the humble and weak

chakam (wise) — 'four things on earth are small, but they are exceedingly WISE' (30:24-28); wisdom is not a function of size or power. The ant's foresight, the badger's shelter, the locust's order, the lizard's boldness put the great to shame. The weak, provident, and orderly are wise (cf 6:6-8).
foresight — the ants storing food in summer against winter

the ants' providing of their food in the summer — the provident foresight that, though the ants are weak, lays up in the time of plenty against the time of need, diligence and forethought outweighing strength
(the weakness it more than makes up for)
the forethought that provisions the future in the season of plenty

kun (prepare/provide) — 'the ants are a people not strong, yet they PROVIDE their food in the summer' (cf 6:6-8); foresight and diligence, not strength, secure the future. The weak ant's provident planning is wisdom to be imitated. Emergent: provident forethought as the wisdom of the small.
provident wisdom — the feeble badger securing its home in the rock

the rock badgers who, though not mighty, make their homes in the cliffs — the provident wisdom of the weak that compensates for want of strength by shrewd security, finding in the rock a refuge no strength could win
the shrewd wisdom that, lacking strength, secures itself in the safety of the rock

atsum (mighty), negated — 'the rock badgers are a people not MIGHTY, yet they make their homes in the cliffs' (30:26); one of the four small-but-wise creatures (30:24). The feeble badger's wisdom is to build where no strength can reach it. Prudence compensates for weakness by choosing a sure refuge (cf 30:25).
dignified confidence — the majestic, unhurried bearing of the assured

the stately tread of four creatures (lion, strutting cock, he-goat, and the king with his army) — the dignified, confident, unhurried bearing that comes of assurance and mastery, majesty expressed in how one carries oneself
the confident dignity that shows itself in an unhurried, majestic gait

yatab (be good / stately) — 'three things are STATELY in their tread' (30:29-31); dignity of bearing — the lion unafraid, the king secure among his people — expresses inner assurance and mastery. A stately walk is confidence made visible.
confessed ignorance — Agur owning he has not learned wisdom or known the Holy One
the confession that Agur has not learned wisdom nor gained knowledge of the Holy One — the deep humility that disclaims mastery of the highest things, refusing to presume on knowledge of God
welded to the challenge that exposes man's ignorance of God

yada (know) — 'I have not learned wisdom, nor have I KNOWLEDGE of the Holy One' (30:3); Agur disclaims comprehension of God. Such humility, far from irreverence, is reverence — the wise do not claim to have plumbed the Holy One (cf 30:2; Job 42:3).
proud folly — vaunting oneself, to be stopped with silence
the folly of exalting oneself — the proud, foolish self-vaunting that, once recognised, calls for a hand clapped over the mouth, silence to halt the boasting before it does more harm
the evil-devising it is paired with (267251)
welded to the scheming of evil it is set beside

nabal (be foolish) — 'if you have been FOOLISH, exalting yourself... put your hand on your mouth' (30:32); proud self-exaltation is folly to be stopped by silence. When caught vaunting oneself, the wise course is to shut the mouth (cf 17:28).
malicious scheming — plotting evil, to be halted by silence
the devising of evil — the malicious plotting that, like proud folly, should be halted by clapping a hand over the mouth, stopping the scheme before it becomes speech and deed
the self-exalting folly it is paired with (267248)
welded to the proud folly it is set beside

zamam (devise/plot) — 'or if you have been DEVISING evil, put your hand on your mouth' (30:32); malicious scheming, like proud folly, is to be checked by silence — stop the plot before it hatches. Restraint of mouth restrains the evil (cf 30:33).
provoked wrath — forcing anger, which inevitably yields strife
the pressing/forcing of anger — the stirring and provoking of wrath that yields strife as surely as churning milk yields curds and a struck nose yields blood, anger pressed always producing conflict
welded to the conflict pressing anger produces

aph (anger/nose, wordplay) — 'pressing ANGER produces strife' (30:33); as pressure on milk makes curds and on the nose makes blood, so pressing anger inevitably makes strife. Provoke wrath and conflict must follow — a reason to check the mouth (30:32).
conflict — the inevitable yield of pressed anger
the strife that pressing anger produces — the conflict that follows as inevitably from provoked wrath as curds from churned milk, the guaranteed harvest of stirring up anger
the pressed anger that yields it (267264)
welded to the provoked wrath that produces it
rib (strife) — 'pressing anger produces STRIFE'; strife is the certain product of provoked anger. Stir the wrath and the quarrel is assured (cf 15:18; 29:22).
humbled knowing — the rhetorical challenge exposing man's ignorance of the transcendent God

the ironic challenge 'surely you know!' — the string of unanswerable questions (who ascended to heaven, gathered the wind, established the earth, what is his name?) that exposes how little any human truly knows of the transcendent God
welded to Agur's disclaiming of wisdom before God

yada (know) — 'what is his name... surely you KNOW!' (30:4); the irony humbles — no man has ascended to heaven or can name the Almighty and his Son. Human knowledge is dwarfed before God's transcendence, and wisdom begins in owning it.
God-reliance — the trust that shelters in God as a shield
the taking of refuge in God, who is a shield to all who do so — the reliance that shelters in God and his ever-true word, finding him a proven protection
(God the shield in whom refuge is taken)
the trust that flees to God for shelter and is not disappointed

chasah (take refuge/shelter) — 'he is a shield to those who TAKE REFUGE in him' (30:5); God's word is flawless and he himself a shield to those who trust him. To take refuge in God is to be sheltered by a proven, faithful protection (cf 18:10; Ps 18:30).
humble request — asking two things of God before death
the asking of two things of God before death — Agur's humble, earnest petition, a prayer that knows its own need and lays two specific requests before God with reverent urgency
the humble, self-knowing prayer that asks God for what the soul truly needs

shaal (ask/request) — 'two things I ASK of you; deny them not to me before I die' (30:7); Agur prays with humble, urgent specificity. His is a prayer that knows its own weakness and asks God to guard it — the model of self-knowing petition (30:8-9).
contentment — the prayer for sufficiency, wanting neither want nor wealth

the desire for neither poverty nor riches but only one's needful food — the contentment that prays to be spared both extremes, wanting neither the want that tempts to theft nor the wealth that tempts to deny God, asking only for enough
(the falsehood he also prays to be spared)
the contented spirit that asks only for sufficiency, fearing the perils of both want and wealth

osher (riches) — 'give me neither poverty nor RICHES; feed me with the food that is needful for me' (30:8); the prayer of contentment. Agur asks to be spared both extremes, knowing wealth tempts to deny God and want to steal (30:9). To desire only enough is a rare and wise contentment (cf 1 Tim 6:8).
self-sufficient forgetting — the satiety that denies God, 'who is the LORD?'
the denying of God in plenty — the danger that satiety breeds self-sufficient forgetting, so that the full man says 'who is the LORD?', needing God no longer in his own eyes
the theft of want it is set against (267322)
set against the poverty that drives to steal and profane God's name

kachash (deny/deceive) — 'lest I be FULL and DENY you and say, 'who is the LORD?'' (30:9); prosperity tempts a man to self-sufficient forgetting of God. Agur prays against riches lest plenty make him deny his Maker (cf Deut 8:12-14).
desperation-sin — the poverty that drives to steal and profane God's name
the stealing that poverty may drive a man to, profaning the name of his God — the danger that want breeds desperation-sin, dishonouring God by the theft it provokes
the denial of plenty it is set against (267316)
set against the satiety that denies God

ganab (steal) — 'or lest I be poor and STEAL and profane the name of my God' (30:9); poverty too has its spiritual peril, driving a man to theft that shames God. Agur prays against want no less than wealth. Emergent: desperation-sin as the danger of poverty (cf 6:30-31).
excellence — the capable wife, worth far more than jewels
the excellence/valour of the capable wife whom the acrostic celebrates — the woman of strength and worth ('eshet chayil') who is far more precious than jewels, the sum of the virtues the poem unfolds
the strong, capable excellence that surpasses all price

chayil (strength/valour/excellence) — 'an EXCELLENT wife who can find? She is far more precious than jewels' (31:10); 'eshet chayil' — a woman of valour, whose worth the whole acrostic (31:10-31) unfolds. Her excellence is a strength and capability beyond price (cf 12:4; Ruth 3:11).
reliability — the wife her husband's heart safely trusts
the trustworthiness of the wife in whom her husband's heart can safely trust, so that he lacks no gain — the reliability and faithfulness that makes her a partner he can rest his confidence in wholly
(the husband's trusting heart that rests on her)
the dependable faithfulness that earns a husband's full confidence

batach (trust) — 'the heart of her husband TRUSTS in her, and he will have no lack of gain' (31:11); her trustworthiness is such that her husband confides in her without reserve. Reliability of character is the foundation of the marriage's prosperity and peace.
steadfast good — doing her husband good, never harm, all her days

the doing of good and not harm to her husband all the days of her life — the steadfast, lifelong benevolence that seeks his welfare constantly, a goodness sustained not for a season but for a whole life
the constant, lifelong good-will that never turns to harm

tob (good) — 'she does him GOOD, and not harm, all the days of her life' (31:12); her benevolence is lifelong and unwavering — not fitful kindness but a settled disposition to seek her husband's good always. Constancy of good-will marks her character.
enterprise — she seeks out wool and flax to work
the seeking-out of wool and flax to work — the diligent industry and enterprise that goes looking for materials and labour, an active, resourceful diligence rather than idle waiting
the willing eagerness it works with (267352)
welded to the glad willingness of her labour

darash (seek/seek out) — 'she SEEKS wool and flax, and works with willing hands' (31:13); her diligence is enterprising, actively seeking out work. Industry that goes and finds, not idleness that waits, marks the capable woman (cf 31:27).
glad labour — working with eager delight, not grudging toil
the working with willing/delighting hands — the glad, eager spirit in which she labours, delight rather than drudgery, industry animated by good-will and pleasure in the work
welded to the enterprising industry it gladdens

chephets (delight/willingness) — 'and works with WILLING hands' (31:13); her labour is glad, not grudging — she works with delight. The willing spirit turns toil into a pleasure and marks the difference between drudgery and industry.
diligent provision — rising in the night to feed her household

the rising while it is yet night to provide food for her household and portions for her maidens — the diligent, self-denying provision that puts the household's needs before her own rest, industry that begins before dawn for others' sake
(the household and maidens she provides for)
the early-rising diligence that provisions the whole household before the day begins

natan (give/provide) — 'she rises while it is yet night and PROVIDES food for her household' (31:15); her diligence is self-denying and others-directed, rising before dawn to feed household and servants alike. Industry in the service of those in her care.
shrewd enterprise — deliberating, buying, and investing to plant a vineyard

the considering of a field before buying it, and planting a vineyard with the fruit of her hands — the shrewd deliberation and enterprise that weighs an investment, acts on it, and turns earnings into new productivity
the prudent business judgement that considers before it buys and invests its gains

zamam (consider/plan/purpose) — 'she CONSIDERS a field and buys it; with the fruit of her hands she plants a vineyard' (31:16); her enterprise is deliberate, not rash — she weighs, then acts, then reinvests. Prudent business judgement joined to bold enterprise marks the capable woman.
vigour — the energetic strength she brings to her work
the dressing of herself with strength and making her arms strong — the energetic vigour she brings to her labour, girding herself for work as for a task worth her full power, strength put to purpose
the purposeful vigour that girds itself for its labour

amats (be strong/strengthen) — 'she dresses herself with STRENGTH and makes her arms strong' (31:17); she brings energetic vigour to her work, girding herself for labour. Strength willingly spent in purposeful industry is part of her excellence.
discerning diligence — sensing her venture prospers, she works on into the night

the perceiving that her merchandise is profitable, so that her lamp does not go out at night — the discerning judgement that senses a venture is prospering, joined to the tireless diligence that presses on late to make the most of it
the discernment that reads her venture's worth and the diligence that works late upon it

taam (taste/perceive) — 'she PERCEIVES that her merchandise is profitable. Her lamp does not go out at night' (31:18); she has a discerning sense for what prospers and the diligence to labour late upon it. Discernment and tireless industry together make her enterprise thrive.
generosity — the open hand and reaching arm toward the poor and needy

the opening of her hand to the poor and reaching out of her hands to the needy — the active generosity that, amid all her industry and enterprise, turns outward to give to the weak, prosperity flowing into compassion
(the poor and needy she gives to)
the open-handed compassion that shares her plenty with the weak

paras (spread/open) — 'she OPENS her hand to the poor and reaches out her hands to the needy' (31:20); her capability is not self-serving — she gives generously to the poor. Enterprise and compassion meet in her: what she gains, she shares. Emergent: open-handed generosity crowning her industry (cf 31:19; 11:24-25).
provident security — no fear of snow, for her household is well provided

the being unafraid of snow for her household, because all are warmly clothed — the settled security that comes of provident foresight, a fearlessness born not of denial but of preparation, having provided against the hard season before it comes
(the well-provided household that grounds her calm)
the calm confidence that provident preparation gives against hard times

yare (fear), negated — 'she is not AFRAID of snow for her household, for all her household are clothed in scarlet' (31:21); her fearlessness is the fruit of foresight — she has provided against winter in advance. Provident preparation turns anxiety into calm security (cf 31:25; 6:6-8).
inner strength — the settled strength she wears like a garment

the strength that clothes the excellent wife — an inner fortitude and capability worn like a garment, settled and habitual, so that she is arrayed in strength and can laugh, unafraid, at the days to come
the dignity it is paired with (267415)
welded to the dignity that clothes her with it

oz (strength) — 'STRENGTH and dignity are her clothing, and she laughs at the time to come' (31:25); her strength is not occasional but habitual, worn like a robe. Clothed in strength, she meets the future with serene, fearless confidence (cf 31:21).
dignity — the honour and poise that adorn her

the dignity that, with strength, clothes the excellent wife — the honour, poise, and self-possessed gravity that adorn her character, a bearing that commands respect and rests secure about what is to come
the strength it is paired with (267414)
welded to the strength that clothes her with it

hadar (dignity/splendour) — 'strength and DIGNITY are her clothing'; dignity adorns her like a robe — the honourable poise of a settled, capable character. She wears her worth, and laughs, secure, at the future.
wisdom — the wisdom with which she opens her mouth
the wisdom with which the excellent wife opens her mouth — speech governed by wisdom, so that what she says is sound and worth hearing, wisdom shaping her words as it shapes her deeds
welded to the loving instruction her tongue carries
chokmah (wisdom) — 'she opens her mouth with WISDOM' (31:26); her speech, like her work, is governed by wisdom. She speaks not idly but with sense, her words carrying weight and worth.
gracious instruction — the 'law of kindness' on her tongue
the teaching of kindness ('torat chesed') on her tongue — the gracious, loving instruction that colours her speech, so that her wisdom is spoken with kindness and her counsel is loyal love made word
welded to the wise speech it graces

chesed (kindness/steadfast love) — 'and the teaching of KINDNESS is on her tongue' (31:26); the 'law of kindness' governs her speech — her wisdom is spoken graciously, her instruction warm with steadfast love. Wisdom and kindness meet on her lips (cf 15:1; 16:24).
vigilant diligence — watching over her household, never idle

the looking well to the ways of her household and refusing the bread of idleness — the vigilant diligence that oversees all her household's affairs and will not be idle, industry that watches as well as works, the opposite of the sluggard's paralysis
the watchful diligence that oversees the household and never sits idle

atsluth (idleness/sloth), negated — 'she looks well to the ways of her household and does not eat the bread of IDLENESS' (31:27); her diligence is vigilant oversight — she watches over all and is never idle. The very antithesis of the sluggard closes her portrait: industry that both works and watches.
earned blessedness — the honour her children rise to give her

the blessedness her children rise up to ascribe to her — the honour a life of strength, wisdom, and kindness earns from those closest to it, children moved to bless the mother whose character has shaped them
welded to the praise her husband adds

ashar (call blessed) — 'her children rise up and CALL her BLESSED' (31:28); the truest testimony to her worth is her family's honour. A life of tried excellence earns the blessing of those who know it best (cf 31:31).
cherished worth — the praise her husband adds to the children's blessing
the praise her husband gives her, joining the children's blessing — the cherishing esteem of the one who knows her best, whose heart trusted her (31:11) and who now openly commends her worth
welded to the blessedness her children ascribe

halal (praise) — 'her husband also, and he PRAISES her' (31:28); the husband whose heart trusted in her now praises her openly. Her worth, tried over a lifetime, draws praise from the one closest to her.
pre-eminent worth — she excels even the excellent

the surpassing excellence of the woman of valour, who does excellently beyond even the many women who have done well — pre-eminent worth that stands above all comparison, the 'chayil' of 31:10 now crowned at the summit
the pre-eminent excellence that outdoes even the excellent

chayil (excellence/valour) — 'many women have done EXCELLENTLY, but you surpass them all' (31:29); the acrostic's climax of praise. Hers is not merely excellence but pre-eminence — she stands above even the many who have done well. The 'eshet chayil' crowned.
self-squandering lust — spending one's vigour on women, the ruin of kings

the giving of one's strength to women — the squandering of vigour and rule on sexual indulgence, the dissipation that has destroyed kings, a man's powers poured out on lust rather than kept for his calling
the vigour wasted on lust that has toppled kings

chayil (strength/vigour) — 'do not give your STRENGTH to women, your ways to those who destroy kings' (31:3); Lemuel's mother warns against squandering one's powers on lust. Sexual indulgence has been the ruin of kings — strength spent there is strength lost from the throne (cf 5:9-11; 7:26).
fleeting allure — charm and beauty, deceptive and vain, not the ground of praise
the charm that is deceitful and the beauty that is vain — the fleeting, deceptive allure that passes and cannot bear the weight of praise, set against the enduring worth of the fear of the LORD
the fear of the LORD it is set against (267462)
set against the God-fearing worth that alone deserves praise

chen (charm/grace) — 'CHARM is deceitful, and beauty is vain' (31:30); outward attractiveness deceives and fades. It is not the measure of a woman's worth — the acrostic's whole portrait has been of character, not looks. What passes cannot ground true praise.
reverent awe — the God-fearing woman who alone is to be praised

the fear of the LORD in the woman who is to be praised — the reverent awe of God that is the root of all the strength, wisdom, kindness, and excellence the acrostic has celebrated, the enduring worth that outlasts charm and beauty and alone deserves praise
the deceptive charm it is set against (267457)
set against the fleeting allure it surpasses

yare (fear) — 'but a woman who FEARS the LORD is to be praised' (31:30); the summit and root of it all. The whole portrait rests here — the fear of the LORD is the source of her every virtue, closing the book where it began (1:7). This, not charm, is the ground of true praise.
deeds as testimony — let her own works commend her in the gates

the praising of the excellent wife by her own works in the gates — the public testimony of a life's deeds, which speak for themselves and commend her before all, so that her actions are her honour and her reward is the fruit of her own hands
the life-testimony of deeds that commend her before all

halal (praise) — 'let her WORKS praise her in the gates' (31:31); the book closes by letting her deeds speak. A tried character needs no other advocate — her works are her testimony and her honour, earning public praise where the elders sit. So Proverbs ends: character, rooted in the fear of the LORD, vindicated by its fruit.
intoxicated dereliction — drink making a ruler forget the law and pervert the poor's rights

the forgetting of what has been decreed through drink — the intoxicated dereliction by which a ruler loses hold of the law and perverts justice for the afflicted, wine drowning the judgement the weak depend on
the drink-drowned memory that fails the poor who look to the judge

shakach (forget) — 'lest they drink and FORGET what has been decreed and pervert the rights of all the afflicted' (31:5); drink is perilous for rulers, drowning the memory of the law and corrupting justice for the weak. A judge in his cups fails the afflicted (cf 31:4).
anguish — the bitter distress that wine may ease
the bitterness of soul of those in distress, to whom wine may bring relief — the deep anguish of the suffering and perishing, for whom drink is a mercy where for a ruler it is a peril
welded to the anguished soul it describes

mar (bitter) — 'and wine to those in BITTER distress' (31:6); the anguish of the suffering, for whom wine is a comfort. What corrupts the judge (31:4-5) may mercifully ease the dying and the broken-hearted — drink judged by its use.
suffering — the anguished soul given wine for relief
the distress of soul of the perishing and heavy-hearted — the suffering spirit for whom strong drink is offered as a mercy, to help them forget their misery for a while
welded to the bitter anguish it feels

nephesh (soul) — 'to those in bitter DISTRESS' (31:6, 'bitter of soul'); the anguished spirit of the suffering, for whom wine is a comfort. The same drink that endangers the ruler mercifully eases the perishing (cf Job 3:20).
compassionate relief — wine given the wretched to forget poverty and misery

the forgetting of poverty and misery that wine may bring the wretched — the compassionate relief offered the perishing and heavy-hearted, a mercy that lets the suffering lay down their grief for a while
the merciful oblivion granted the crushed and suffering

shakach (forget) — 'let them drink and FORGET their poverty and remember their misery no more' (31:7); the same wine that endangers the ruler (31:4-5) is a mercy to the perishing, easing a grief too heavy to bear. Compassion, not indulgence, is the note here (cf 31:6).
just advocacy — speaking up and judging rightly for the voiceless

the righteous judging and defending of the rights of the poor and needy — the just advocacy that opens its mouth for the voiceless, using power to secure justice for those who cannot secure it themselves
the righteous use of authority to protect the defenceless

tsedeq (righteousness) — 'open your mouth, judge RIGHTEOUSLY, defend the rights of the poor and needy' (31:9); the crown of Lemuel's mother's counsel — power exists to protect the weak. Righteous rule speaks up for those who have no voice (cf 29:7, 14; 31:8).
forgetting — here forbidden: do not forget the teaching
the failure-to-retain that the son is commanded to avoid
shakach (cf 2:17, where the adulteress forgets the covenant) here NEGATED — forgetting is the danger the heart's keeping guards against; memory as moral fidelity.
the heart — commanded to keep the commandments
the heart made the keeper/guardian of the commandments
the seat charged with retention and obedience
leb here is an ACTIVE keeper (natsar) — not merely where teaching lands but the faculty that guards it; the inner organ of fidelity.
delight — a father's pleasure in his son, the simile for God's love-discipline
a father delighting in his son, the human mirror of God's reproving love
coupled to the LORD's love (267517) as its human analogy

ratsah (be pleased with/delight in): the HUMAN paternal affect that the verse uses to illumine God's discipline. Screen 0 — the LORD's own 'love' (267517) is the divine arena (qualifier); the char here is the father's delight, a genuine human interior.
blessedness — the happy state of the one who finds wisdom
the blessed/happy condition of the wisdom-finder
esher (O the blessedness of...) — the beatitude opening the encomium; the inner well-being that attends the finding of wisdom.
wisdom — the prize found and made blessed
chokmah as the thing found, source of the blessed state
welded to understanding as the twin prize
chokmah here the OBJECT of finding — the possessing of which makes one blessed; the book's central good.
tebunah gained/drawn out, paired with wisdom
welded to wisdom as the twin prize
tebunah (discernment) paired with chokmah — to 'get' understanding is to draw out discernment; both together constitute the blessed possession.
surpassing worth — wisdom's gain exceeds silver and gold
the surpassing worth of wisdom over precious metal, as the seeker esteems it
the valuation of wisdom above wealth
tob here comparative WORTH: wisdom's yield is 'better' than silver/gold — an evaluation of the inner good above material gain; what the wise heart prizes most.
desire — all your desirable things, none comparing to her
the objects of one's desire, all outweighed by wisdom
the desires measured against and surpassed by wisdom
chephets (delight/desirable-things) — the sum of what one wants; the verse sets the whole field of human desire below wisdom. The desiring faculty made the measure that wisdom exceeds.
honor — the esteem wisdom bestows on her holder
the honour/glory that wisdom confers, held out in her hand
paired with riches as wisdom's bestowal
kabod (honour/glory) here a GIFT of wisdom — the social-and-inner esteem that attends the wise; cf the favour/repute of 3:4. Wisdom's left hand holds it out.
pleasantness — the agreeable delight of wisdom's way
the pleasant, agreeable quality of the path of wisdom
welded to peace as the twin quality of her paths
noam (pleasantness/delight) — wisdom's way is not grim but PLEASANT; the inner agreeableness of the wise life. Paired with shalom.
peace — the wholeness of all wisdom's paths
the shalom/wholeness that marks every path of wisdom
welded to pleasantness as the twin quality of her ways
shalom (wholeness/welfare) — 'all her paths are peace'; the settled wellbeing of the wise walk. Cf 3:2.
holding fast — grasping wisdom firmly as one's life
those who lay hold of her
the tenacious grasp of wisdom, clinging to the tree of life
the holding that issues in the blessed state
chazaq (Hiphil: seize/hold fast) — the disposition of gripping wisdom as life itself; not passive possession but active clinging. The tree of life is held, not merely admired.
blessedness — pronounced happy for holding wisdom fast
the blessed/happy state declared of the one who clings to wisdom
the blessed state that crowns the tenacious grip
ashar (Pual: be pronounced happy) — echoing esher (3:13); the one who holds wisdom fast is declared blessed. The encomium's inclusio of blessedness.
wisdom — the LORD's, by which he founded the earth
the divine wisdom as the instrument of creation, founding the earth
welded to understanding as the creative pair

chokmah here God's own creative wisdom — the SAME wisdom the son is to pursue, here shown supreme: God made the world by it. Locus external:god (divine attribute), read to dignify the human pursuit, not to import God's inner life as a human char.
understanding — the LORD's, by which he established the heavens
the divine understanding establishing the heavens
welded to wisdom as the creative pair
tebunah as God's creative discernment, paired with chokmah; the cosmic dignity of the discernment the wise are to seek.
peace — wholeness/welfare added to the obedient
the shalom (wholeness, welfare) that the kept commandments confer
paired with length of days and years of life
shalom = not mere absence of strife but full welfare/wholeness of life — the crowning gift of the retained teaching; an inner-and-outer flourishing.
knowledge — the LORD's, by which the deeps broke open
the divine knowledge as the agency by which the deeps burst and clouds drop dew
completing the creative triad with wisdom and understanding
daath as God's creative knowledge — the third of the wisdom-triad (chokmah/tebunah/daath) by which the world was made; the supreme worth of the knowledge the son pursues.
letting-slip — here forbidden: do not let them depart from your eyes
the turning-aside/losing-from-view that the son is to avoid
sound wisdom and discretion (not to be lost)
set against the keeping of wisdom
luz (turn aside/depart) NEGATED — 'let them not slip from your eyes'; the danger of inattention that loses wisdom. Emergent (no prior candidate): the movement of losing-sight is itself the finding.
sound wisdom — effective competence to be kept
the sound, effective wisdom the son is to guard
welded to discretion as the guarded pair
tushiyah (sound/effective wisdom, competence) — practical, resourceful wisdom; paired with mezimmah as the two things kept before the eyes.
discretion — prudent purpose to be kept
the discreet, purposeful prudence the son is to guard
welded to sound wisdom as the guarded pair
mezimmah (discretion/purpose — neutral-to-good here, cf its dark sense elsewhere) — deliberate prudence; kept together with tushiyah as inner safeguards.
the soul — to which wisdom is life
the nephesh/inner life that wisdom vivifies
paired with the neck-adornment as the twofold gift
nephesh here the recipient of life — wisdom is 'life for your soul'; the whole inner self quickened by kept wisdom.
grace — the gracefulness wisdom lends, an adornment
the grace/adornment that wisdom hangs on the neck of its keeper
paired with soul-life as the outward-and-inward gift
chen (grace/favour, cf 3:4) here as ADORNMENT — 'grace for your neck'; the attractive gracefulness wisdom confers, worn like an ornament.
security — the assured, confident walk of the wise
the secure, confident manner in which the wise walk their way
the settled assurance that keeps the foot from stumbling
betach (security/confidence) — the inner assurance that comes of kept wisdom; one walks the road unafraid, the foot steady. The tranquil confidence of the guided life.
fearlessness — the dread that will not come when you lie down
the dread that is absent — no fear at rest
paired with sweet sleep as the twin rest
pachad (dread) NEGATED — the wise lie down without the start of terror; inner security expressed as fearless rest.
sweetness — the pleasantness of the wise one's sleep
the sweet, pleasant quality of untroubled sleep
welded to the freedom-from-fear as the twin rest
arev (be sweet/pleasant) — sleep made sweet by a clear, secure heart; the somatic-emotional peace of the guided life.
fear — here forbidden: do not dread the sudden terror
the fear the wise is commanded not to feel toward calamity
the dread-object the wise refuses to fear
yare (fear) NEGATED — the settled heart does not panic at sudden alarm or the wicked's downfall; trust displaces dread.
wickedness — the wicked whose ruin need not be feared
the wicked whose sudden ruin the wise does not dread
the doom of the wicked, held without fear
rasha — their 'ruin, when it comes' is the calamity in view; the wise, secure in the LORD, do not fear even that.
confidence — the LORD himself as one's assurance
the settled confidence the wise places in the LORD, the ground of fearlessness
coupled to the LORD's guarding of the foot

kesel (confidence/hope) — 'the LORD will be your kesel'; the inner assurance rests on God himself. Emergent (no prior candidate): confidence as an interior state grounded outside the self. The LORD's KEEPING (shamar) is the divine action (qualifier).
good — the benefit owed to others, not to be withheld
the one with power to do it
the good owed to one's neighbour, which the able must not hold back
the good set against the impulse to withhold
tob here the GOOD one owes and can give — generosity as duty; the inner readiness to render good when it is in one's power, against the mean impulse to withhold.
scheming — devising evil against a trusting neighbour
the plotting of harm against one who dwells trustingly beside
the scheme whose content is evil
charash (plough/devise) — to 'plough' evil, work it out inwardly against a neighbour; the covert malice the verse forbids, aggravated by the neighbour's trust.
trust — the neighbour who dwells securely beside you
the neighbour's trusting security, which the schemer would betray
the innocent trust set against the covert scheme
betach (security/trust) — the victim 'dwells trustingly'; his open, unsuspecting security is the very thing the schemer exploits. The read holds the contrast.
steadfast love — loyal covenant-love to be kept close
chesed bound to the person, not let go
welded to faithfulness as the covenant pair
chesed (loyal love/kindness) — the covenant-virtue to be worn and inscribed on the heart; a disposition of committed love that must not 'forsake'.
faithfulness/truth — reliability to be kept close
emet held fast, bound around the neck, written on the heart
welded to steadfast love as the covenant pair
emet (truth/faithfulness/reliability) — paired with chesed as the twin covenant virtues; together the trustworthy, loyal character to be internalised.
the heart — the tablet on which they are written
the heart as the tablet where chesed and emet are inscribed
the seat that internalises the virtues
leb as writing-tablet: the virtues are not worn only outwardly (neck) but ENGRAVED within — the deepest internalisation, a heart re-inscribed.
quarreling — contending with a man without cause
the groundless quarrel picked with one who has done no harm
the strife set against the fact that no wrong was done
rib (contend/bring a suit) NEGATED — do not manufacture conflict where there is no injury; the restless, litigious impulse the verse curbs.
envy — here forbidden: do not envy the violent man
the envy of the violent that the son must not feel
the envy set against the violent man it would covet
qana (be jealous/envy) NEGATED — the seductive envy of the successful-violent; the heart's covetous admiration the verse forbids.
violence — the violent disposition not to be envied
the violence that marks the man whose ways must not be chosen
the violence set against the envy it wrongly attracts
chamas (violence/wrong) — the character of 'a man of violence'; his way is what the son must neither envy nor choose.
choosing — the will's selection, here forbidden toward his ways
the deliberate choosing of the violent man's ways, forbidden
the will's selection turned from violence
bachar (choose/elect) NEGATED — 'do not choose any of his ways'; the volitional movement of the will, warned away from the path of violence. The choosing itself is the inner act.
the twisted, crooked character that God detests
the deviousness set against the divine abhorrence it draws
luz (Niphal: be devious/crooked) — the perverse bent of heart; kin to the 'losing-sight' of 3:21 but here settled character. Emergent. God's ABOMINATION (toebah) is the divine valuation (qualifier).
uprightness — the straight, who enjoy God's confidence
the upright character that God admits to his intimate counsel
the uprightness set against the divine intimacy it gains
yashar — the antithesis of the devious; the upright are not merely tolerated but taken into God's sod (intimate circle).
intimacy — the upright's privileged confidence with God
the intimate fellowship/counsel the upright enjoy with the LORD
the intimacy set against the uprightness that earns it
sod (intimate circle/counsel) — 'the upright are in his sod'; the inner privilege of divine friendship granted to straight-hearted, the counterpart to the devious one's exclusion as abomination.
wickedness — the wicked, whose house draws the curse
the wicked character on whose house the LORD's curse rests
the wickedness set against the divine curse it incurs
rasha — the wicked household under the LORD's meerah (curse); character determines the house's fate. The CURSE is the divine act (qualifier).
righteousness — the righteous, whose dwelling is blessed
the righteous character whose home the LORD blesses
the righteousness set against the divine blessing it receives
tsaddiq — the righteous dwelling under God's barak (blessing); the bright side of the ledger. The BLESSING is the divine act (qualifier).
scorn — the scoffers who meet God's derision
the scoffing disposition that draws the LORD's own scorn
the human scorn set against the divine scorn it earns
luts (scoff/mock) — the scoffer's contempt boomerangs: 'toward the scorners he is scornful'. The proud derider is met in kind. God's SCORNING (Hiphil) is the divine response (qualifier).
humility — the humble/afflicted, to whom favor is given
the lowly, unassuming character to whom the LORD gives grace
the humility set against the divine favour it receives
anav (humble/afflicted) — the opposite of the scoffer; the lowly heart receives chen (favour). The FAVOUR given is the divine gift (qualifier).
wisdom — the wise, who inherit honor
the wise character that comes into honour as its inheritance
the wisdom set against the honour it inherits
chakam — the wise 'inherit' kabod (honour); wisdom's outcome is lasting esteem.
folly — fools, who take up disgrace
the dull, self-satisfied fools whose portion is shame
the folly set against the disgrace it lifts up
kesil (dull fool) — fools 'get/lift up' qalon (disgrace); folly's outcome is shame, the dark mirror of the wise one's honour.
favor/grace — found before God and man
gaining favour in the sight of God and man
chen (cf 1:9) as the RESULT of the internalised virtues — favour/acceptance with both God and people; the social-and-divine fruit of a loyal, true heart.
being well-regarded, held in good esteem
paired with favour as the twofold standing
tob here (with sekel) = good standing/repute; the esteem in which the faithful person is held.
the sound sense/good understanding that wins esteem
welded to favour as the recognised good
sekel (good sense/prudence, also 'success/repute') — the inner soundness that is recognised as favour by God and man; discernment that shows.
trust — whole-hearted reliance on the LORD
trusting the LORD with the whole heart, resting one's confidence on him
welded to the whole heart; set against self-reliance
batach (trust/rely) is the CENTRAL command of ch.3 — the inner posture of total reliance on God, the counter to leaning on one's own mind. God the target; the trust the human interior.
the heart — the whole of it given to trust
the whole heart engaged in trusting — undivided reliance
the seat that must trust ENTIRELY ('with all')
leb here demanded WHOLLY ('with all your heart') — trust is not partial; the entire inner faculty is bent on God, leaving nothing for self-reliance.

lebab (heart) — the words are to be kept 'within the heart'; the inner treasury where teaching is stored, not merely before the eyes but deep inside.
