the heart — where the commands are bound always
the heart to which the father's commands are bound continually
the seat that wears the teaching bound upon it
leb (heart) — 'bind them on your heart ALWAYS'; the commandments fastened permanently to the inner centre, worn as a constant inner ornament (cf 3:3; 7:3).
inner communion — the internalised teaching converses with you
the teaching become an inner companion that talks/communes with the son on waking
the communion coupled to the teaching's guarding

siach (commune/meditate/talk) — 'when you awake, they will talk with you'; the word so internalised it becomes an inner interlocutor, a companion in meditation. The teaching's WATCHING (shamar) is its personified guarding (qualifier).
discipline — its reproofs are the way of life
the discipline whose correcting reproofs form the very road of life
(the lamp and light of the commandment)
the reproofs of discipline as the illumined way

musar (discipline) — 'the reproofs of musar are the way of life'; correction not as burden but as the lit path itself. Discipline valorised as life-giving illumination (cf 6:15 the alternative: broken beyond healing).
evil — the evil woman from whom the teaching preserves
the evil of the adulteress with her smooth, flattering tongue
the evil set against the teaching that guards from it

ra (evil) — 'the woman of evil', the adulteress whose smooth tongue is the danger the whole teaching (6:20-23) is aimed to guard against. The PRESERVING (shamar) is the teaching's protective action (qualifier).
coveting — here forbidden: do not desire her beauty
the illicit coveting of the adulteress's beauty that the son must not entertain
the coveting welded to the heart where it must be refused
chamad (covet/desire) NEGATED — 'do not COVET her beauty in your heart'; the lust warned against at its inner root, before it becomes act. The heart is where adultery begins or is refused.
the heart — where beauty must not be coveted
the heart in which the desire for the adulteress must not be allowed to form
the seat that must not harbour the illicit desire
lebab (heart) — 'in your heart'; the inner theatre where lust is entertained or expelled. The read locates the moral battle at the level of desire, not deed.
the soul — the precious life the adulteress hunts
the precious life/soul that the adulteress stalks and hunts down
(the cheap price of a prostitute, by contrast)
the priceless soul set against the loaf-cheap wage of vice
nephesh (life/soul) — 'she hunts a precious nephesh'; adultery is not a cheap transaction but a hunt for the very life. The whole self is the stake, not a loaf of bread. The predatory image is stark.
self-rescue — extricate yourself from the surety-trap
the urgent self-deliverance from having pledged for another, humbling oneself to plead
(the hand of the neighbor one is caught in)
the desperate extrication from the snare of surety
natsal (Niphal: deliver oneself) — 'save yourself'; the urgent inner resolve to escape a rash pledge, swallowing pride to plead with the neighbor. Prudent self-preservation, not passivity.
contempt — here withheld: people do not despise the desperate thief
the contempt that is NOT poured on a thief driven by hunger — a mitigated scorn
the withheld contempt set against the coming inexcusable adultery

buz (despise/hold in contempt) — 'people do not buz a thief' if hunger drove him; contempt withheld where need compels. Set up as a foil: the adulterer (6:32) will find no such mitigation. Degrees of scorn.
appetite — the hunger the thief steals to satisfy
the bodily appetite/craving the thief steals to fill
the appetite welded to the hunger that drives it
nephesh (appetite/self/craving) — 'to satisfy his nephesh when hungry'; the legitimate bodily need that partly excuses the theft. The HUNGER (raeb) is the driving condition (qualifier).
restitution — the thief can at least repay sevenfold
the restitution the thief makes, repaying sevenfold from all his house
(the theft that can be made good)
the reparability of theft set against the adulterer's irreparable ruin

shalam (repay/make whole/restore) — the thief, though caught, CAN make restitution; theft is reparable. The read sets this against 6:32-33: adultery admits no such making-good. Restitution as a moral capacity theft leaves intact.
adultery — the act that betrays covenant
the committing of adultery, the covenant-breaking act of the senseless man
the adultery welded to the heart-lessness that drives it
naaph (commit adultery) — the deed named plainly; but the read presses inward: it springs from and reveals a lack of sense (leb). The act is the symptom of an empty heart.
the absence of sense/heart that adultery both reveals and requires
the missing heart welded to the reckless deed

leb (heart/sense) — 'he who commits adultery LACKS leb'; sense located in the heart, and adultery diagnosed as its absence. Not passion overriding reason but reason (heart) simply gone. A chilling equation.
self-destruction — he ruins his own soul
the self-ruin the adulterer works on his own life
the destroying aimed at the man's own soul
shachath (destroy/ruin/corrupt) — 'he who does it DESTROYS HIMSELF'; adultery as suicide of the soul. The HIMSELF (nephesh) destroyed is the qualifier — the self is both agent and victim.
dishonor — the shame the adulterer earns
the dishonour/shame that adultery brings upon the man
welded to disgrace as the twin shame that clings
qalon (dishonour/shame) — 'wounds and qalon he will find'; the lasting shame of adultery, a wound that marks the person. Set against the thief's reparable case (6:31).
disgrace — the reproach that is never wiped away
the reproach that clings to the adulterer, indelible, never erased
welded to dishonour as the twin indelible shame

cherpah (reproach/disgrace) — 'his cherpah will NOT be wiped away'; the permanence of the shame. Where theft can be repaid, adultery leaves an ineradicable reproach. The read stresses the indelibility.
jealousy — the wronged husband's consuming zeal
the jealousy that seizes the husband whose wife is taken, kindling fury
welded to fury as the escalating rage

qinah (jealousy/zeal) — the husband's jealousy over his violated marriage; not petty envy but the fierce protective zeal of covenant love betrayed, which becomes rage. The adulterer's fatal miscalculation.
fury — the hot wrath jealousy kindles
the burning fury into which the husband's jealousy erupts
welded to jealousy as the rage it becomes
chemah (heat/wrath/fury) — 'jealousy makes a man FURIOUS'; the white heat of betrayed marriage. Paired with qinah as its inevitable eruption.
vengeance — the unsparing revenge of the jealous man
the merciless revenge the furious husband exacts, sparing nothing
the vengeance as the terminus of jealous rage
naqam (vengeance/revenge) — 'he will not spare in the day of naqam'; the implacable retribution of the wronged husband. The read traces the arc jealousy -> fury -> unsparing vengeance.
implacability — no ransom can appease the jealous husband
the appeasement/ransom the furious husband refuses, unbuyable by any gift
the refused ransom as the measure of implacable wrath

kopher (ransom/appeasement) — 'he will accept no kopher'; the jealous husband is beyond bribing. The read locates the inner reality: an implacability that no compensation touches, however multiplied. Adultery admits no buying-off (cf 6:31, the thief who CAN repay).
self-rescue — flee the trap like a gazelle, a bird
the swift, instinctive self-deliverance from the snare, like a hunted animal breaking free
the urgent flight from the trap of a rash pledge
natsal (deliver oneself) — 'save yourself LIKE A GAZELLE'; the image intensifies the urgency — escape as a wild thing bolts from the net. The whole self bent on breaking free.
sluggishness — the lazy man sent to school with the ant
the sluggishness that must be schooled by the industrious ant
the sluggard set against the wisdom he is urged toward
atsel (sluggard/lazy) — the settled disposition of laziness, addressed and rebuked; sent to the ant to learn diligence. Emergent: sloth as a character to be reformed, not merely a behaviour.
becoming wise — the sluggard's summons to gain wisdom
the imperative that the sluggard consider and grow wise
the wisdom set against the sloth it must cure
chakam (be/become wise, verb) — 'consider her ways and BE WISE'; wisdom as the reforming goal for the sluggard, learned by observing the ant's self-directed diligence.
sloth — the lazy man who will not rouse himself from sleep
the sluggard who lies abed and will not arise — sloth that clings to sleep and must be summoned to wake, the inertia that cannot rouse itself to the day's work
the laziness that lingers in bed past all reason

atsel (sluggard) — 'how long will you lie there, O SLUGGARD? When will you arise from your sleep?' (6:9); sloth is an inertia that clings to sleep. The sluggard must be roused; he will not rouse himself (cf 6:10-11; 26:14).
keeping — guarding and treasuring the father's words
the son's keeping and treasuring-up of the father's words within himself
the guarding set on the words as a stored treasure
shamar (keep/guard) — 'keep my words'; the retentive guarding that opens ch.7, paired with 'treasure up' (tsaphan). Obedience as safekeeping of the teaching.
accosting — the adulteress intercepts and meets the youth
the woman's predatory intercepting of the naive youth at dusk
the accosting welded to the harlot's guise and craft
qara (meet/encounter/befall) — 'the woman MEETS him'; the calculated interception, the huntress closing on her prey. Emergent: the meeting as an active, predatory movement, not chance.
harlotry — dressed in the garb and disposition of a prostitute
the harlot's dress and whorish intent with which she meets the youth
welded to the guarded, cunning heart beneath the garb
zanah (play the harlot) — 'dressed as a prostitute'; the outward garb of harlotry over an inward craft. Appearance and intent aligned in seduction.
craftiness — the guarded, cunning heart beneath the garb
the hidden, wily heart (netsurat leb) that schemes behind the harlot's dress
welded to the outward guise it directs

leb (heart) with natsar (guarded/hidden) — 'guarded/wily of heart'; her heart is cunning, concealed, calculating. The read notes the SAME heart-word that should treasure wisdom (7:3) here twisted to craft. Inner faculty inverted.
waywardness — her restless, defiant, ungovernable nature
the wayward, rebellious restlessness that will not keep her at home
the waywardness as the ungoverned restlessness of the seductress

sarar (be stubborn/rebellious/wayward) — 'loud and WAYWARD'; the defiant, unsettled character that spurns domestic order and roams the streets. Restlessness as a moral condition, the opposite of the settled, guarded heart.
aggression — she grabs and holds the youth
the aggressive seizing/gripping of the youth by the emboldened woman
the seizing welded to the brazenness that drives it
chazaq (seize/grasp/hold fast) — 'she SEIZES him'; the SAME verb as gripping wisdom as life (3:18; 4:13) here inverted to the predator's grab. The youth who should hold wisdom fast is himself seized.
brazenness — the shameless, hardened face with which she speaks
the brazen effrontery of face with which she accosts and addresses the youth
welded to the aggression it emboldens
azaz (be strong/bold/impudent) — 'with a BRAZEN face she says'; shamelessness hardened into effrontery, the loss of the blush that would restrain. Boldness curdled into impudence.
pursuit — she came out expressly to meet him
the deliberate coming-out to meet the youth, the hunt framed as devotion
the meeting welded to the eager search that flatters him

qara (meet/encounter) — 'I came out to MEET you'; the interception (7:10) now recast to the youth as flattering intent — as if he were the one sought. Emergent: predatory pursuit disguised as longing.
eager seeking — she sought him diligently and found him
the eager, diligent seeking with which she claims to have hunted the youth out
welded to the meeting it flatters into destiny

shachar (seek early/diligently) — 'to SEEK your face eagerly, and I have found you'; the language of ardent search (elsewhere used of seeking wisdom or God) here counterfeited by the seductress. Desire's vocabulary hijacked for the hunt.
illicit love — the lovemaking the adulteress offers
the illicit caresses/lovemaking she invites the youth to take his fill of
welded to the reveling delight she offers

dodim (love/lovemaking/caresses) — 'take our FILL of love till morning'; the counterfeit of the marital dodim the son should enjoy (cf 5:19). Illicit love dressed as satisfaction, but a hunt (7:23) beneath.
revelry — 'let us delight ourselves' in illicit love
the reveling, delighting-together the seductress proposes
welded to the lovemaking it savours
alas (rejoice/revel/delight) — 'let us DELIGHT ourselves with love'; the deliberate reveling, the counterfeit of the sanctioned joy in a wife. Pleasure hijacked, joy misdirected.
love-play — the illicit affection savoured together
the love/affection the seductress proposes to indulge in together till morning
welded to the delighting it fuels
ohabim (love/love-tokens) — 'delight ourselves with LOVE'; a third love-word crowning the seduction's rhetoric, all warmth on the surface, all trap beneath. The vocabulary of love emptied to bait.
keeping — guarding the commandments, that you may live
the son's keeping of the commandments, the condition of life itself
the keeping welded to the life it secures
shamar (keep/guard) — 'keep my commandments AND LIVE'; obedience directly tied to life, as at 4:4. The guarding is not burden but the very means of living.
life — the living that keeping the commandments secures
the life the son gains by keeping the commandments and teaching
welded to the keeping that produces it
chayah (live) — 'keep... and live'; life as the fruit of obedience, the teaching kept 'as the apple of the eye', most precious. The read binds guarding and living.
folly — the youth follows like a fool to punishment
the senseless, unresisting following of the youth, like a fool led to the stocks
(the ox to the slaughter beside it)
the folly that walks unknowing into death
evil (fool) — 'as a FOOL to the correction of the stocks'; the youth's folly imaged as an animal's unresisting march to death. No struggle, no perception — folly is a kind of sleepwalking into ruin.
oblivion — he does not know it will cost his life
the fatal ignorance of the youth, who does not perceive that this costs his life
the not-knowing set against the death it walks toward

yada (know) NEGATED — 'he does NOT KNOW it will cost his nephesh'; the crowning tragedy: total obliviousness to the stake. The senseless youth (7:7) cannot see his own death approaching. The LIVER (kabed) pierced is the mortal wound (qualifier).
the soul — the life the snare will cost him
the very life/soul the youth forfeits, all unknowing, in the snare
the priceless life set against his blind ignorance of the cost
nephesh (life/soul) — 'it will cost him his nephesh'; the whole self is the price of the moment's pleasure. The read holds the horror: a life spent for a night, and spent blindly.
heeding — the sons' obedient hearing after the warning
the sons' hearing/heeding of the father in the wake of the deadly tale
welded to close attention as the doubled summons
shama (hear/heed) — the renewed 'listen to me' that closes the seduction narrative; the tale is told precisely to compel obedient hearing.
attending — inclining the ear closely to the words
the sons' close, ear-inclining attention to the father's words
welded to hearing as the intensified attention
qashab (attend/incline the ear) — paired with shama; the intensified attention the mortal warning demands. Hear AND attend.
the heart — must not turn aside to her ways
the heart guarded from turning aside toward the adulteress's ways
the seat set against the drift toward her paths
leb (heart) — 'let not your HEART turn aside to her ways'; the battle is again at the heart (cf 6:25) — the turning begins within, in the inclination of the heart, before the feet ever move.
straying — do not wander into her paths
the wandering-off into the adulteress's paths that the son must not do
welded to the heart's inclination it enacts
taah (go astray/wander) NEGATED — 'do not STRAY into her paths'; the outward wandering that follows the heart's turning. Heart and feet together warned. The drift into ruin refused at both levels.
the heart — the tablet on which the commands are written
the heart as the tablet where the father's commands are engraved
the seat inscribed with the teaching, deeper than the hand
leb (heart) — 'write them on the tablet of your heart'; the deepest internalisation (cf 3:3), the commands engraved within, not merely worn without. The heart re-inscribed by the teaching.
wisdom claimed and loved as a sister, close kin
welded to insight as the twin beloved kin
chokmah — 'say to wisdom, you are my SISTER'; wisdom as intimate family, the sanctioned intimacy set against the adulteress's false closeness. The relational language is deliberate.
claiming-as-kin — naming wisdom and insight one's family
the son's intimate claiming of wisdom as sister and insight as kinswoman
wisdom and insight (whom he so names)
the naming that binds wisdom to oneself as family

qara (call/name) — 'CALL insight your kinswoman'; the warm, relational claiming of wisdom as one's own household. Wisdom loved as family is the guard against the seductress (7:5) whose intimacy is counterfeit.
insight named an intimate friend/kinswoman, held close as family
welded to wisdom as the twin beloved kin
binah — 'call insight your kinswoman/intimate'; discernment embraced as beloved family, paired with wisdom-as-sister. Intimacy rightly placed.
being-guarded — wisdom-as-kin preserves from the adulteress
the preservation from the forbidden woman that loving wisdom secures
the guarding set against the seductress's flattery

shamar (keep/guard) — the purpose of embracing wisdom as sister (7:4): 'to KEEP you from the strange woman'. The inner intimacy with wisdom is itself the shield against the counterfeit intimacy of the adulteress with her smooth words.
simpleness — the naive, unformed among whom the youth is found
the naive simpleness of the youths among whom the sage spots the senseless one
welded to the senselessness that marks the naive youth
pethi (simple/naive) — the open, unguarded naivety of the young; not yet wicked but dangerously unformed, easy prey for the seductress. Paired with the lack of leb.
discernment — the sage's own perceiving of the scene
the sage's discerning perception, watching from the window and reading the youth
the observer's discernment set against the youth's lack of it
bin (discern/perceive) — 'I PERCEIVED among the youths'; the sage's own discernment, the very faculty the young man lacks. The teacher sees clearly what the naive cannot.
heartlessness — the young man who 'lacks heart'
the absence of sense/heart in the youth that makes him vulnerable
welded to the naivety that leaves him defenceless
leb (heart/sense) — 'a young man LACKING heart'; the same diagnosis as the adulterer (6:32), here of the victim. Senselessness as the fatal exposure, the empty inner chamber the seductress will fill.
Wisdom — who calls aloud in the open
personified Wisdom lifting her voice publicly, the bright counter to the seductress's whisper
welded to understanding as the twin voice of Wisdom
chokmah — 'does not WISDOM call?'; personified Wisdom now takes the stage (ch.8), her open, public cry the deliberate antithesis of the adulteress's furtive seduction (ch.7). Wisdom woos in daylight.
Wisdom's crying out, her open invitation to all who pass
the calling welded to the voice she lifts
qara (call/cry) — Wisdom CALLS; the same verb the seductress used to claim she sought the youth (7:15), here redeemed as Wisdom's honest, open summons. Two voices court the simple.
understanding — raising her voice with Wisdom
personified understanding lifting her voice alongside Wisdom
welded to wisdom as the twin public voice
tebunah — 'does not UNDERSTANDING raise her voice?'; discernment personified beside Wisdom, both crying aloud. The doubling underscores the openness of the appeal.
instruction — to be taken over silver
Wisdom's instruction/discipline, to be received in preference to silver
welded to knowledge as the twin prize above wealth

musar (instruction/discipline) — 'take my INSTRUCTION rather than silver'; discipline valued above precious metal (cf 3:14). The deliberate preference of the wise, wealth reckoned second to correction.
knowledge — to be chosen over choice gold
the knowledge to be preferred above even the choicest gold
welded to instruction as the twin prize above wealth
daath (knowledge) — 'knowledge rather than CHOICE GOLD'; knowledge outweighs the best wealth. The valuation that governs the wise heart, paired with instruction over silver.
preferring — knowledge chosen above the choicest gold
the deliberate preferring of knowledge over even the most select gold
the choosing that sets knowledge above the best wealth

bachar (choose/select) — 'CHOICE gold' surpassed; the read hears the volitional preference beneath the comparison — the wise deliberately CHOOSE knowledge over the choicest wealth. Valuing as an act of the will.
wisdom — better than jewels, beyond all desire
wisdom's worth surpassing jewels and every desirable thing
the wisdom whose value tops all treasure
chokmah — 'wisdom is better than jewels'; her supreme worth restated (cf 3:15) as the frame for her self-praise.
the surpassing value of wisdom over all precious things
welded to the desire it outweighs
tob — comparative worth: wisdom is 'better', outweighing all one could desire.
desire — all one could want cannot equal her
the whole field of human desire, none of it comparable to wisdom
welded to the worth that surpasses all desire
chephets — 'all you may desire cannot compare with her'; the sum of wants set below wisdom (cf 3:15).
personified Wisdom declaring she dwells/lodges with prudence
welded to prudence as her companion
chokmah — 'I, wisdom, DWELL with prudence'; Wisdom and shrewdness cohabit — sound wisdom keeps company with practical prudence.
prudence — the shrewdness Wisdom dwells with
the practical shrewdness that lodges with Wisdom
welded to wisdom as her housemate
ormah (prudence/shrewdness) — Wisdom's companion; the good craft (cf 8:5) that makes wisdom effective. Emergent.
the knowledge Wisdom discovers and possesses
welded to discretion as her twin finding
daath — 'I find knowledge'; Wisdom is the source and finder of true knowledge.
welded to knowledge as her twin finding
mezimmah (discretion/purpose) — 'I find knowledge and discretion'; Wisdom yields deliberate, purposeful prudence (good sense here, cf 1:4).
fear of the LORD — defined as the hatred of evil
the fear of the LORD, here equated with a settled hatred of evil
the reverence welded to the moral aversion that expresses it
yirah (fear) — 'the fear of the LORD IS hatred of evil'; a striking definition: reverence for God is not mere awe but an active moral revulsion. Fear and hatred-of-evil are one movement.
hatred — of evil, the substance of the fear of God
the hating of evil that constitutes the fear of the LORD
the hatred aimed at the evil it recoils from
sane (hate) — 'hatred OF EVIL'; the fear of God expressed as aversion. To revere God is to loathe what he loathes. The EVIL (ra) hated is the qualifier.
welded to arrogance as the twin hated vice
geah (pride) — 'PRIDE and arrogance... I hate'; self-exaltation heads the list of what Wisdom loathes, the root vice against the fear of God.
welded to pride as the twin hated vice
gaon (arrogance/loftiness) — paired with geah; the swollen self-regard that Wisdom, like the LORD, hates.
the twisted, perverse speech that Wisdom detests
welded to the hatred that recoils from it
tahpukoth (perversity/twisted things) — 'perverted speech I hate'; the crooked mouth (cf 6:12) among the things Wisdom loathes.
Wisdom's hatred — of pride, arrogance, evil, perversity
Wisdom's own hating of the swollen and the crooked
the way of evil (268488, an object)
the hatred aimed at the evils it names
sane (hate) — 'I HATE' — Wisdom's active moral aversion, mirroring the fear of the LORD (8:13a). Her purity is not passive but a settled loathing of evil. The way of EVIL (ra) is the qualifier.
the counsel/wise advice that belongs to Wisdom
welded to sound wisdom as her twin possession
etsah (counsel/advice) — 'counsel is mine'; Wisdom is the source of sound guidance, on which kings depend (8:15).
the effective, resourceful wisdom that is Wisdom's own
welded to counsel as her twin possession
tushiyah (sound/effective wisdom) — practical competence; Wisdom possesses the resourcefulness that makes counsel work.
the discernment/understanding that Wisdom claims as herself
welded to strength as her twin claim
binah (understanding) — 'I AM understanding'; Wisdom identifies herself with discernment itself.
the strength/might that belongs to Wisdom
welded to insight as her twin claim
geburah (might/strength) — 'strength is mine'; Wisdom is not weak counsel but has power to establish rulers and cities. Understanding wedded to might.
righteousness — what rulers decree by Wisdom
the righteous decrees that rulers issue by means of Wisdom
welded to just rule as Wisdom's political fruit
tsedeq (righteousness) — 'rulers decree what is JUST' by Wisdom; right government flows from her. Wisdom is the source of just authority.
nobility — the willing/noble who govern by Wisdom
the noble, willing-hearted rulers who govern by Wisdom
welded to just governance as their character
nadib (noble/willing) — 'nobles, all who govern'; the generous, noble-minded rulers whose authority rests on Wisdom. Nobility of spirit behind just rule.
the just governing/judging that rulers exercise through Wisdom
welded to righteousness as the manner of rule
shaphat (judge/govern) — 'all who govern justly'; the exercise of just judgement, dependent on Wisdom. Emergent: governing/judging as an act grounded in Wisdom.
righteousness — the just manner of governing
the righteousness that marks governance done by Wisdom
welded to the righteous decrees of 8:15
tsedeq (righteousness) — 'govern JUSTLY/in righteousness'; the rightness of rule that Wisdom supplies, framing kings' and nobles' authority.
Wisdom's love — for those who love her
Wisdom's returning love toward those who love her
welded to the human love it answers
aheb (love) — 'I LOVE those who love me'; Wisdom's reciprocal affection. Devotion to wisdom is met with wisdom's love — a real relationship, not transaction.
love — the human devotion to Wisdom she answers
the love for Wisdom that draws her love in return
welded to the love it evokes
aheb (love) — 'those who LOVE me'; human devotion to wisdom (cf 4:6), here answered by her own love. The mutual bond.
eager seeking — those who seek Wisdom early find her
the diligent, early seeking of Wisdom that is rewarded with finding
the eager pursuit that Wisdom answers by being found
shachar (seek early/diligently) — 'those who seek me diligently FIND me'; the SAME verb the seductress counterfeited (7:15) here in its true object: earnest pursuit of Wisdom is never disappointed.
the riches that attend Wisdom, hers to bestow
welded to honor as Wisdom's paired gift
osher (riches) — 'RICHES and honor are with me'; material good in Wisdom's train, but (8:18b) subordinate to the enduring righteousness she truly gives. Emergent.
welded to riches as Wisdom's paired gift
kabod (honor) — the esteem that comes with Wisdom (cf 3:16); paired with riches as her lesser, outward gifts.
the durable wealth that Wisdom carries
welded to righteousness as the enduring pair
hon (wealth) — 'ENDURING wealth'; not fleeting gain but lasting substance, yet still paired with and crowned by righteousness. Emergent.
the righteousness that is Wisdom's deepest gift, above riches
welded to wealth but surpassing it as the real treasure
tsedaqah (righteousness) — the climax: riches/honor/wealth are with Wisdom, but RIGHTEOUSNESS is the true endowment. The read notes the ascent from material to moral.
surpassing worth — Wisdom's fruit exceeds fine gold
the surpassing worth of Wisdom's fruit over gold and fine gold
welded to the preference of Wisdom over choice silver
tob — 'my fruit is BETTER than gold'; Wisdom's yield outvalues the finest metal (cf 3:14; 8:10).
preferring — Wisdom's yield chosen above choice silver
the deliberate preferring of Wisdom's yield over even choicest silver
welded to the worth that merits the choice
bachar (choose/select) — 'choice silver' surpassed; the wise deliberately prefer Wisdom's yield to the choicest wealth (cf 8:10). Valuing as an act of will.
the righteous way in which Wisdom herself walks
welded to justice as the twin path
tsedaqah (righteousness) — 'I WALK in the way of righteousness'; Wisdom does not merely commend righteousness but embodies it, walking it herself.
the just paths along which Wisdom walks
welded to righteousness as the twin way
mishpat (justice/judgement) — 'in the paths of justice'; Wisdom's road is right judgement. She leads by walking, her own conduct the pattern.
love — the devotion Wisdom rewards with inheritance
the love for Wisdom that is granted a lasting inheritance
the love answered by an enduring endowment
aheb (love) — 'those who LOVE me' given an inheritance (yesh, substance) and full treasuries; devotion to Wisdom yields lasting, real endowment. The bond of 8:17 bears fruit.
being brought forth — Wisdom born before the deeps
Wisdom's being brought forth/birthed before the depths and springs existed
the primordial generation of Wisdom before the waters
chul (writhe/bring forth, birth imagery) — 'I was BROUGHT FORTH' before the depths; Wisdom generated (as if born) prior to creation. The maternal birth-language dignifies her as first of God's ways.
abundance — the water-heavy springs, absent at Wisdom's birth
the abounding, water-heavy springs that did NOT yet exist when Wisdom was brought forth
the absent abundance set against Wisdom's priority

kabad (be heavy/abounding) — 'no springs ABOUNDING with water'; the read notes the pre-creation void — even the heavy-flowing springs were not yet, but Wisdom already was. Her antecedence stressed by the not-yet scene.

the LORD's firming/strengthening of the skies at creation, with Wisdom present
welded to the establishing of the fountains

the LORD's strengthening/establishing of the deep's fountains at creation
welded to the firming of the skies above
azaz (be strong/establish) — 'he ESTABLISHED the fountains of the deep'; God's fixing of the primordial waters, paired with the firming of the skies. Wisdom present at the whole work.

Wisdom as God's daily delight, rejoicing before him always at creation
welded to her delight in the children of man

delight — Wisdom's joy in the children of man
Wisdom's delighting in God's inhabited world and in humankind
welded to her joy before God
shaashuim — 'DELIGHTING in the children of man'; Wisdom's joy turns toward humanity. The same delight that plays before God is directed to mankind — she loves to be with people.

the guarding/keeping of Wisdom's ways that brings blessing
welded to the listening that precedes it
shamar (keep/guard) — 'keep my WAYS'; obedience to Wisdom as active guardianship, the ground of the beatitude.

the hearing of instruction that issues in wisdom

shama (hear/heed) — 'HEAR instruction and be wise'; hearing that is not neglected (8:33b) but obeyed, producing wisdom. Instruction (musar) is the object heard (qualifier).

welded to the heeding that produces it

the blessed condition of the one who waits and watches at Wisdom's doors

the daily listening and watching at Wisdom's gates
welded to the waiting beside her doors
shama (hear/heed) — 'the one who LISTENS to me, watching daily at my gates'; not occasional but daily attendance, the posture of the devoted disciple.
the eager, watchful waiting beside Wisdom's doorposts, day by day
welded to the daily listening at her gates
shamar (watch/keep/wait) — 'WAITING beside my doors'; the lover's vigil at Wisdom's threshold, the same word for guarding turned to eager expectancy. Devotion as constant watching.

the missing/failing-to-find Wisdom that is a sin injuring oneself
the missing welded to the self-harm it causes
chata (miss/sin) — 'he who MISSES me wrongs his own soul'; the same word for sin and for missing a mark: to fail to find Wisdom is to sin against oneself. Self-harm as the fruit of missing her.

the very soul/self that is wronged and injured by missing Wisdom
the self injured by its own failure to find Wisdom
nephesh (soul/self) — 'wrongs his own NEPHESH'; the whole self is the casualty of missing Wisdom. Not an external penalty but self-inflicted injury to one's own life.
hatred — of Wisdom, which is love of death
the hating of Wisdom that is, in truth, a love of death
welded to the death-love it amounts to
sane (hate) — 'all who HATE me'; to hate Wisdom is the ultimate self-destruction. The read holds the terrible equation with 8:36b.
the perverse love of death that hatred of Wisdom amounts to
welded to the hatred it reveals
aheb (love) — 'all who hate me LOVE DEATH'; the chilling climax of ch.8: rejecting Wisdom is not neutral but a positive love of death. Desire itself inverted toward destruction.
calling — Wisdom's cry to all mankind
Wisdom's universal call, addressed to all men, all the children of man
(her cry to the children of man)
the calling extended to everyone without exception
qara (call/cry) — 'to you, O MEN, I call'; Wisdom's summons is universal, to all humanity — none excluded. The breadth of the appeal (contrast the seductress who picks one naive youth).
simpleness — the naive summoned to gain prudence
the naive, unformed ones Wisdom calls to acquire shrewdness
the simpleness set against the prudence Wisdom offers it
pethi (simple/naive) — Wisdom addresses the very ones the seductress preys on (7:7); but where she exploits their naivety, Wisdom would cure it, calling them to prudence.

the coming-to-understand that Wisdom presses on the simple
bin (discern/understand, Hiphil) — 'LEARN prudence'; the active gaining of discernment, the faculty the naive lack. Wisdom's remedy for simpleness.

the shrewd, sensible prudence Wisdom offers to cure naivety
the prudence set against the naivety it remedies

the folly set against the sense Wisdom offers it
kesil (dull fool) — even the kesil is addressed; Wisdom's call reaches the fool, offering the leb (sense) he lacks. No one beyond the summons.
discerning — the fools made to understand sense
the coming-to-understand that Wisdom presses on the fools
the learning aimed at an understanding heart
bin (discern/understand, Hiphil) — 'LEARN sense/heart'; the fool too is called to gain the discerning heart. The verb of remedy repeated.
sense — the understanding heart the fools must gain
the discerning heart/sense Wisdom offers the fool to fill his emptiness
the sense set against the folly it remedies
leb (heart/sense) — 'learn LEB'; the understanding heart the fool lacks (cf 6:32; 7:7), which Wisdom would give. Sense as an acquirable gift, not a fixed fate.
heeding — Wisdom's summons to hear her noble words
the hearing Wisdom asks, for she speaks noble and right things
the heeding set toward Wisdom's upright speech
shama (hear/heed) — Wisdom's own 'HEAR'; she commands the attention the father commanded (7:24), for her words are noble (negidim) and worth hearing.
uprightness — the right things that come from Wisdom's lips
the upright, equitable things that issue from Wisdom's lips
the rightness set as the reason to heed
meshar (uprightness/equity) — 'from my lips comes what is RIGHT'; Wisdom's speech is straight, equitable, without deceit. Her rightness is the ground of her claim on the hearer.
uttering — Wisdom's mouth speaks forth truth
the truth Wisdom's mouth mutters/utters, the outflow of her inner truthfulness
the uttering welded to the truth it speaks
hagah (mutter/utter/meditate) — 'my mouth will UTTER truth'; the same word for meditating on the law (cf Ps 1) here of Wisdom's truthful speech, an overflow from within.
the truth/faithfulness that is the content of Wisdom's speech
welded to the mouth that speaks it
emet (truth/faithfulness) — Wisdom speaks emet; her words are reliable, faithful, true. Truth as her very substance, set against the seductress's smooth lies (7:21).
wickedness — that which Wisdom's lips abhor
the wickedness that is detestable to Wisdom's lips
the wickedness set against the revulsion it provokes
resha (wickedness) — 'wickedness is an ABOMINATION to my lips'; Wisdom not only speaks truth but recoils from evil. Her purity is active aversion, not mere absence.
Wisdom's revulsion at wickedness, which her lips find detestable
welded to the evil it recoils from

the righteousness of all Wisdom's words, without a single twisted or crooked thing
the rightness set against the crookedness it excludes

the plain straightness of Wisdom's words to the one who understands
welded to rightness as the quality plain to the discerning

understanding — the discerning to whom the words are plain
the discernment that finds Wisdom's words plain and straight
welded to knowledge as the receiving faculty
bin (understand/discern) — 'to him who UNDERSTANDS'; the discerning receiver for whom wisdom is clear. The words are plain, but only to the one with the faculty to receive them.
rightness — the words right to those who find knowledge
the upright rightness of Wisdom's words to those who have found knowledge
welded to straightness as the twin plain quality
yashar (right/straight) — 'RIGHT to those who find knowledge'; the words are upright and plain to the knowing. Rightness paired with straightness (nakoach).
knowledge — the finding that makes the words plain
the knowledge whose finders perceive Wisdom's words as right
welded to understanding as the receiving faculty
daath (knowledge) — 'those who FIND knowledge'; knowledge as the key that unlocks Wisdom's plainness. To the knowing, the words are right; to the empty, riddles.
fear of the LORD — the beginning of wisdom
the fear of the LORD as the very starting-point and principle of wisdom
welded to the wisdom it begins
yirah (fear) — 'the fear of the LORD is the BEGINNING of wisdom'; the book's motto restated (cf 1:7). Reverence is not one virtue among others but the root and first principle of all wisdom.
wisdom — begun in the fear of the LORD
the wisdom whose beginning and foundation is the fear of the LORD
welded to the reverence that is its start
chokmah — 'the beginning of WISDOM'; wisdom is not self-generated but rooted in reverence for God. Without the fear of the LORD there is no true wisdom.
knowledge — of the Holy One, which is insight
the knowledge of the Holy One that constitutes understanding
the knowing of God that is insight

daath (knowledge) — 'the KNOWLEDGE of the Holy One is insight'; to know God is understanding itself. Knowledge of God, not information, is the substance of insight. The HOLY ONE (qadosh = God) is the object known (qualifier).
understanding — the knowledge of the Holy One
the understanding that IS the knowledge of the Holy One
welded to the knowing of God that constitutes it
binah (understanding) — 'the knowledge of the Holy One is INSIGHT'; understanding defined as knowing God. The intellect's summit is not data but communion with the Holy.
the utter ignorance of Folly, who for all her loud seduction knows nothing
the not-knowing beneath her noisy allure

yada (know) NEGATED — 'she KNOWS NOTHING'; Folly personified as the anti-Wisdom: loud, seductive, but utterly empty of knowledge. Her allure has no substance. The exact inverse of Wisdom who finds knowledge (8:12).
calling — Folly's counterfeit summons to passersby
Folly's call to those passing by, mimicking Wisdom's invitation to divert them
the counterfeit call that apes Wisdom's summons

the naive ones Folly invites, the very audience Wisdom also calls
welded to the senselessness Folly exploits
pethi (simple/naive) — Folly's invitation copies Wisdom's word for word (cf 9:4); the SAME simple are courted by both. The read holds the counterfeit: identical call, opposite end.
turning-in — to Folly's house, the fatal counterfeit
the turning-aside-in to Folly's house that her copied invitation calls for
the turning-in that, unlike Wisdom's (9:4), leads to death
sur (turn aside/in) — 'let him TURN IN here'; the same movement Wisdom invites (9:4), but into Folly's house of the dead (9:18). Emergent: the response-movement, here misdirected to ruin.
heartlessness — the one who lacks sense, Folly's target
the empty inner chamber Folly would fill with her deadly fare
welded to the naivety it accompanies
leb (heart/sense) — 'him who LACKS sense'; Folly, like Wisdom, targets the deficient — but to exploit, not to furnish. Same emptiness, opposite intent.
illicit sweetness — the deceptive pleasantness of stolen things
the pleasantness attributed to stolen water and secret bread — the allure of the forbidden
the sweetness that masks the way to Sheol

naem (be pleasant/sweet) — 'bread eaten in secret is PLEASANT'; Folly's philosophy: the forbidden is sweet precisely because stolen and secret. The read exposes the lie — the pleasantness is real but fatal (9:18). Illicit desire's self-justification.
oblivion — he does not know the dead are there
the fatal ignorance of Folly's guest, blind to the death her house holds
the not-knowing set against the death it cannot see
yada (know) NEGATED — 'he does NOT KNOW the dead are there'; the same blindness as the youth of 7:23. Folly's sweetness works precisely because her victim cannot see where it leads.
death — the shades that fill Folly's house
the dead/shades already gathered in Folly's house, her guests' destiny
welded to the guests who join them in the depths

rephaim (the dead/shades) — 'the DEAD are there'; Folly's house is a mortuary. Her guests do not merely risk death — the dead already fill her rooms. Emergent: death as the resident reality behind the feast.
the summoned — Folly's called ones, bound for Sheol
those Folly has called/invited, now in the depths of Sheol
the dead among whom they lie (268719)
welded to the shades they have joined

qara (call) as passive 'her called/invited ones' — Folly's GUESTS are 'in the depths of Sheol'; those who answered her call have descended. The counterfeit call (9:15) ends in the grave. The dark inverse of Wisdom's guests who 'live' (9:6).
calling — Wisdom's summons from the town's heights
Wisdom's public call, sent out by her young women from the high places
welded to the elevation of her open call
qara (call/cry) — Wisdom 'CALLS from the highest places'; her summons is public, elevated, open (contrast Folly's furtive doorway, 9:14). The same open call of 8:1-4.
openness — Wisdom calls from the town's high points
the elevated, public heights from which Wisdom's invitation goes out
welded to the calling it elevates

marom (heights/high place) — 'from the HIGHEST PLACES in the town'; the openness and elevation of Wisdom's appeal, broadcast where all can hear. Emergent: the public height of true wisdom's call, against Folly's low doorway.
simpleness — the naive Wisdom invites in
the naive/simple ones whom Wisdom invites to her feast
welded to the senselessness Wisdom would remedy
pethi (simple/naive) — 'whoever is SIMPLE, turn in here'; Wisdom invites the very naive that Folly also targets (9:16). Same audience, opposite feast.
the turning-aside-in to Wisdom's house that her invitation calls for
the turning-in that accepts the summons
sur (turn aside/in) — 'let him TURN IN here'; the decisive movement of accepting Wisdom's welcome, entering her house. Emergent: turning-in as the act of response to the call.
heartlessness — the one who lacks sense, invited
the lack of sense/heart in the one Wisdom addresses and would fill
welded to the naivety it accompanies
leb (heart/sense) — 'him who LACKS sense'; the empty inner chamber (cf 6:32; 7:7) Wisdom would furnish. She calls precisely the deficient, offering what they lack.
naivety — the simple ways to be forsaken
the naive ways/company the guest must leave behind at Wisdom's feast
the naivety abandoned for the way of understanding
pethaim (simple ones/naivety) — 'LEAVE your simple ways'; the forsaking of naivety as the condition of life. One cannot keep simpleness and live.
the life gained by forsaking naivety and walking in insight
welded to the way of understanding that gives life
chayah (live) — 'and LIVE'; life as the fruit of leaving simpleness (contrast 9:18, Folly's guests in the depths of Sheol). Wisdom's feast is life.
understanding — the way to walk in
the way of insight/understanding the guest is to walk after leaving naivety
welded to the life it secures
binah (understanding) — 'walk in the way of INSIGHT'; the road that replaces the simple ways. Understanding as the path of the living.

the scoffer whose correction earns the corrector only abuse
the scorn that turns correction into insult

luts (scoff/mock) — 'whoever corrects a SCOFFER gets abuse'; the scoffer is incorrigible, repaying reproof with insult. Correction wasted on contempt. Abuse (qalon) is the corrector's reward (qualifier).
wickedness — the wicked whose reproof brings injury
the wicked man whose reproof only injures the reprover
the wickedness that punishes its own correction
rasha (wicked) — 'he who reproves a wicked man incurs injury'; like the scoffer, the wicked resents correction. The reprover, not the reproved, suffers.
scorn — the scoffer who will hate the reprover
the scoffer who, reproved, will hate the one who reproves him
welded to the hatred reproof provokes in him
luts (scoff) — 'do not reprove a SCOFFER, or he will hate you'; the scoffer's fixed response to correction is hatred. Reproof is not merely wasted but resented.
hatred — the scoffer's response to reproof
the scoffer's hating of the one who dares reprove him
welded to the scorn that produces it
sane (hate) — 'he will HATE you'; the scoffer meets correction with hatred, the mark of the incorrigible heart.
wisdom — the wise who loves reproof
the wise man who, reproved, loves the one who corrects him
welded to the love reproof produces in him
chakam (wise) — 'reprove a WISE man, and he will love you'; the decisive contrast — the wise welcome correction and love the reprover. Teachability is wisdom's signature.
love — the wise man's response to reproof
the wise man's love for the one who corrects him
welded to the wisdom that produces it
aheb (love) — 'he will LOVE you'; the wise love correction, the exact opposite of the scoffer's hatred (9:8a). Response to reproof divides the wise from the scoffer.
imparting — give instruction to the wise, he grows wiser
the giving/imparting of instruction to a wise man, who then grows still wiser
welded to the wise man who receives and increases
nathan (give) — 'GIVE instruction to a wise man'; the imparting of teaching to the teachable, which compounds. Emergent: giving-instruction as an act that the wise multiply.
wisdom — the wise who grows still wiser
the wise man who, given instruction, becomes yet wiser
welded to the increase of wisdom he shows
chakam (wise) — 'a wise man, and he will be STILL WISER'; wisdom compounds in the teachable. The wise are not full but ever-growing.
growing wiser — the wise man's increase
the further growth in wisdom that instruction brings the wise
welded to the wise man who increases
chakam (be wise) — 'he will be still WISER'; wisdom's self-multiplying nature in the humble. Every teaching adds to the wise.
teaching — instruct a righteous man, he increases in learning
the teaching/making-known given to a righteous man, who increases in learning
welded to the righteous who grows in learning
yada (make known, Hiphil) — 'TEACH a righteous man, and he will increase in learning'; imparting to the righteous, who like the wise multiply what they receive.
righteousness — the righteous who increases in learning
the righteous man who, taught, grows in learning
welded to the instruction that grows him
tsaddiq (righteous) — 'teach a righteous man, and he will INCREASE in learning'; righteousness and teachability go together, the opposite of the scoffer's closed heart.
doom — the evil man who has no future
the evil man who has no future — the wicked whose apparent success ends in nothing, his lamp extinguished
the wicked whose lamp goes out (302400)
welded to the wicked whose light is snuffed
ra (evil) — 'for the EVIL man has no future'; the wicked's prosperity has no tomorrow. What looks enviable is a light about to go out (cf 13:9; 24:14's contrast — the wise HAVE a future).
extinction — the lamp of the wicked put out
the wicked whose lamp is put out — the light of life and prosperity snuffed, leaving no future
welded to the evil man who has no tomorrow
rasha — 'the lamp of the WICKED will be put out'; the wicked's light is extinguished, his line and hope ended. No future for those who envy nothing worth having.
self-surrender — giving the whole heart to wisdom's way
the giving/surrender of the whole heart that the father asks — willing devotion, not grudging obedience
welded to the heart it gives away
natan (give) — 'GIVE me your heart'; the whole-hearted surrender wisdom asks of the son. Emergent: the giving of the heart as the son's free devotion, the ground of all right learning.
whole-hearted devotion — the heart the father asks the son to give
the son's heart, which the father asks him to give wholly — the surrender of the inner self to wisdom's way
welded to the whole-hearted giving it asks
leb (heart) — 'my son, give me your HEART'; the father asks not outward compliance but the whole heart — the seat of will and love. Wisdom claims the inner self, not just the conduct (cf Matt 22:37).
corruption — the wickedness within, masked by warm words
the evil/corruption of the heart that fervent lips are used to disguise — the wrong within, papered over by a glaze of eager speech
welded to the heart it corrupts
ra (evil) — 'an EVIL heart' (26:23); the corruption glazed over by warm words. What the fervent lips coat is a heart full of wrong.
concealed corruption — the evil heart glazed over with fervent lips
the evil heart that fervent, smooth lips glaze over as cheap earthenware is glazed to look precious — corruption within, a shining coat of words without
welded to the wickedness it harbours
leb (heart) — 'fervent lips with an EVIL heart' (26:23); warm words can be a thin glaze over a corrupt heart, making cheap clay shine like silver. The mouth's warmth hides the heart's rot.
self-disclosure — the heart as the true mirror of a man
the heart of a man that reflects and reveals what he truly is, as water gives back a face — the inner self as the real index of the person, deeper than appearance
the heart that shows a man for what he really is

leb (heart) — 'so the HEART of man reflects the man'; what a man is, is in his heart — the inner self is the true mirror of the person. To know a man, read his heart, not his face (cf 27:21; Luke 6:45).

the making of linen garments to sell and the delivering of sashes to the merchant — the productive enterprise that turns skill and industry into trade, the capable woman's work reaching beyond the home into the market
the industry that makes, sells, and supplies, turning skill into gain

the naive whose backsliding is fatal to them
the simple-state welded to the apostasy that kills it
peti (cf 1:22) now under judgement: the naivety that is loved (1:22) here kills, via its turning.

the turning-away from wisdom that brings death
the fatal movement of the naive heart away from wisdom

complacency/false ease — the security that destroys fools
the careless ease of fools that destroys them
the fool's false security welded to his destruction
EMERGENT (seed-missed): shalvah = careless ease/complacency — the fool's fatal calm, set opposite the true security of 1:33 (betach). A key contrast the read surfaces.
the fool whose complacency is his ruin
welded to the complacency that destroys him
kesil (cf 1:22): here defined by a fatal ease — the fool is undone not by storm but by his own untroubled carelessness.

being delivered from the adulteress and her smooth words
the rescue wisdom works against seduction
natsal (cf 2:12) now aimed at the second great danger — the forbidden woman; wisdom's deliverance extends from the way of evil (men) to seduction (the adulteress).
despising — here forbidden: do not despise the LORD's discipline
rejecting/despising the LORD's discipline, which is forbidden
set against submissive reception of correction
maas (reject/despise) NEGATED — the son must not scorn God's discipline; the same contempt the fool shows (1:7) here warned against toward divine correction.

paired with despising as the twin forbidden reactions
quts (loathe/be-disgusted, kin to weariness) — the second forbidden reaction: not just despising discipline but LOATHING reproof. The read keeps the two aversions distinct (scorn vs disgust).
wickedness — their very sustenance, the bread they eat
wickedness consumed as daily bread, the staple of their life
welded to violence as their food and drink
resha (wickedness) — 'the bread of wickedness'; evil so ingrained it is their nourishment. They live ON it, not merely do it.
violence drunk like wine, intoxicating the wicked
welded to wickedness as their food and drink
chamas (violence) — 'the wine of violence'; violence as their drink, exhilarating and consuming. The metaphor fuses appetite and character.
ruin — the near-total disaster reached in public
the brink of utter ruin the man finds himself at, exposed in the congregation
the ruin as the terminus of despised discipline

ra (evil/ruin/disaster) — 'kol-ra', all-but-utter ruin, and that publicly, 'in the midst of the congregation'. The endpoint of the confession: contempt for correction lands one at the edge of total collapse, shamed before all.
the sudden, total breaking of the schemer, past any remedy
the absence of healing as the terminus of his mischief
marpe (healing/remedy) — 'broken WITHOUT marpe'; the schemer's ruin is beyond cure, sudden and final. Healing named by its impossibility — the opposite of the words that heal the flesh (4:22).
the imperilled self — the garment fire inevitably burns
the man who dallies with lust
the man's own person, imaged as clothing that fire in the bosom must consume
the garment/self set against the inescapable fire of lust

feigned piety — the vow-paying that furnishes the seduction's pretext
the discharged vows the woman parades as a pretext (fellowship-meat to share) for seduction
the show of piety cloaking the invitation to sin

shalam (pay/fulfil vows) — 'today I have PAID my vows'; religious duty invoked as a lure — she has peace-offering meat to feast on, a pretext to draw the youth in. The read exposes the cynical use of piety, devotion as camouflage for sin.
primordiality — Wisdom set up from everlasting
Wisdom's establishment from eternity, before the earth began
(the beginning of the earth she precedes)
the from-everlasting origin that grounds Wisdom's authority

olam (eternity/ancient time) — 'from OLAM I was set up (nasak)'; Wisdom's primordial, pre-cosmic establishment. Her from-everlasting origin is the ground of her supreme worth — she antedates all creation. Read as the eternality of Wisdom.
being brought forth — Wisdom born before the mountains
Wisdom's being brought forth before the mountains and hills were shaped
the birth of Wisdom before the mountains, restated
chul (bring forth/birth) — 'before the mountains... I was BROUGHT FORTH'; the birth-image repeated, hammering Wisdom's priority over every created thing. She precedes the most ancient solidities.
Wisdom — who builds her house and hews her pillars
personified Wisdom establishing her house, hewing seven pillars, preparing her feast
the industrious Wisdom who builds to welcome

chokmoth (Wisdom, plural of majesty) — 'Wisdom has BUILT her house'; she is the gracious, industrious hostess who prepares a place of welcome (contrast Folly who merely sits, 9:14). Her building frames the invitation of ch.9.
wisdom — one's own, its benefit to oneself
the wisdom that, if one has it, is chiefly for one's own good
welded to the personal profit of wisdom
chakam (be wise) — 'if you are WISE'; wisdom's reward is first personal — one is wise 'for oneself'. The moral weight of wisdom falls on its owner.
the personal profit of wisdom, which benefits its owner above all
welded to the wisdom that yields it
chakam — 'you are wise FOR YOURSELF'; wisdom is not merely for others' benefit but supremely one's own good. Personal responsibility for one's wisdom.
the scoffing whose penalty the scoffer alone must bear
(the personal weight of wisdom, by contrast)
the scorn whose cost is wholly personal
luts (scoff) — 'if you SCOFF, you alone will bear it'; as wisdom's profit is personal, so scoffing's penalty is borne alone. Each answers for his own inner posture.
self-justification — a man's ways seem pure to himself
the self-approval by which a man reckons all his own ways pure
the spirit God weighs, by contrast (308493)
set against the LORD who weighs the spirit
zak (pure/clean) — 'all the ways of a man are PURE in his own eyes'; self-justification — everyone thinks himself clean. The read notes the near-universal blindness of self-approval (cf 21:2).
the spirit — weighed by the LORD
the inner spirit/motives that the LORD weighs, behind the man's self-approval
set against the man's self-justifying view
ruach (spirit) — 'the LORD weighs the SPIRIT'; God assays the inner motives that a man's self-approval overlooks. The true test of the ways is the weighing of the spirit.
wisdom — a fountain, a bubbling brook of life-giving words
the wisdom that is a flowing fountain/bubbling brook, source of deep, life-giving words
the ever-flowing spring of wise speech
chokmah — 'the fountain of WISDOM is a bubbling brook'; wisdom is a living, flowing spring, its words deep waters. The wise heart pours out fresh, life-giving speech.
the spirit — which sustains a man through sickness
the spirit/inner life that will sustain and carry a man through bodily sickness
set against the crushed spirit that nothing sustains
ruach (spirit) — 'a man's SPIRIT will endure sickness'; the inner life can carry a man through bodily illness. The spirit sustains the body — the primacy of the inner over the outer.
the crushed spirit — which nothing can sustain
the crushed/broken spirit that no one can bear or sustain — when the inner support itself fails
the whole spirit that endures, by contrast (308518)
set against the spirit that sustains through sickness

ruach (spirit) — 'a CRUSHED spirit who can bear?'; when the spirit itself is broken, there is nothing left to sustain the man. Bodily sickness the spirit endures; but a broken spirit is unbearable. The deepest wound is inward (cf 15:13; 17:22).
satisfaction — filled by the fruit of one's own mouth
the satisfaction/filling that a man reaps from the fruit of his own mouth
welded to the yield of his own speech
saba (be satisfied/full) — 'from the fruit of a man's mouth his stomach is SATISFIED'; one's own words feed oneself. Speech has a harvest that returns to the speaker (cf 12:14; 13:2).
satisfaction — the harvest of one's own lips
the satisfaction a man gains from the yield/produce of his own lips
welded to the mouth's harvest that fills him
saba (be satisfied/full) — 'he is SATISFIED by the yield of his lips'; the produce of one's speech returns as one's own nourishment or ruin. Words are seeds with a harvest (18:21).
mockery — wine as a mocker that makes fools of men
wine personified as a mocker/scoffer, making a mockery of the one it masters
set against the wisdom the drinker forfeits
luts (mocker/scoffer) — 'WINE is a MOCKER'; drink is a scoffer that makes a fool of its lover. The read personifies wine's power to mock and unman the drinker.
unwisdom — whoever is led astray by drink is not wise
the lack of wisdom in the one who is led astray by wine and strong drink
the mocking wine that unmans him (308543)
set against the wine that mocks the drinker
chakam (be wise) NEGATED — 'whoever is led astray by it is NOT wise'; to be mastered by drink is folly. Wine mocks; its slave is unwise.
love-of-ease — loving sleep, which leads to poverty
the love of sleep/ease that, indulged, brings a man to poverty
(the wakeful diligence that brings plenty, by contrast)
the ease the sluggard loves, set against wakeful labour

aheb (love) NEGATED — 'LOVE not sleep, lest you come to poverty'; the love of ease and sleep impoverishes. Diligence ('open your eyes') brings bread. The heart's affections decide the outcome — love of sleep or love of work.
purged evil — driven out by painful discipline
the evil that painful blows/wounds cleanse away, purging the innermost parts
the evil driven from the heart by the pain of correction

ra (evil) — 'blows that wound cleanse away EVIL; strokes make clean the innermost parts'; painful discipline purges evil from the heart. The read holds the hard truth — correction that wounds can cleanse the inner being. Pain as purgation (cf 3:11-12).
forethought — the diligent readying for the day of battle
the making-ready/preparation of the horse for the day of battle — right human diligence and foresight
the victory that rests with God (308569)
set against the divine outcome no preparation can secure

kun (make ready/establish) — 'the horse is made READY for the day of battle'; human preparation is right and dutiful, yet it cannot itself command the outcome. Emergent: diligent forethought as the human part, whose result God alone gives (cf 16:1, 9).
divine sovereignty — the outcome belongs to the LORD
the victory/deliverance that belongs to the LORD, whatever man prepares
set against the diligence that cannot compel it
teshuah (victory/deliverance) — 'but the VICTORY belongs to the LORD'; the outcome rests with God, not the preparation. Locus external:god — man readies the means, God grants the end.
brutish folly — the fool corrected only as a beast is
the fool whose back needs the rod as the horse needs a whip and the donkey a bridle — folly so brutish it answers only to force, not reason
the folly that yields, like a beast, only to the rod
kesil (fool) — 'a rod for the back of FOOLS' (26:3); folly is so unreasoning it must be driven like a beast. The fool learns, if at all, only under discipline (cf 10:13; 19:29).
talebearing — the gossip whose whispers fuel strife
the whisperer/talebearer whose secret gossip is the fuel of strife — without whom, as without wood, the fire of quarreling dies down
welded to the strife his whispers feed

ragan (whisper/murmur) — 'where there is no WHISPERER, quarreling ceases' (cf 26:22; 16:28); the gossip is the fuel of conflict. Remove the talebearer and strife starves for lack of tinder. Emergent: the whisperer as the fire-wood of quarrels.
strife — that dies once the whisperer is gone
the quarreling/strife that ceases once the whisperer is removed — conflict starved of its fuel, dying like a fire without wood
welded to the gossip whose whispers feed it
madon (strife/contention) — 'quarreling CEASES' (26:20); strife dies when its fuel — the gossip's whispers — is withdrawn. Cut off the talebearer and the fire of conflict goes out.
unsatisfied craving — the eyes of man that never have enough
the never-satisfied eyes of man, insatiable as Sheol and Abaddon that are never full — the restless craving of desire that no amount of getting ever contents
(the grave's insatiability it is likened to)
the human craving that, like death, is never filled

saba (be satisfied), negated — 'never satisfied are the EYES of man'; human desire is bottomless as the grave, never content with what it has (cf 30:15-16; Eccl 1:8). The eye that craves is never filled — a warning against covetousness.
shared humanity — the poor who meet the oppressor before one God

the poor man who meets the oppressor on common ground, both alike receiving the light of life from the LORD — a levelling truth that neither poverty nor oppression escapes the one God who gives them both their sight and breath
welded to the oppressor with whom he shares one God's light

rush (be poor) — 'the POOR man and the oppressor meet together; the LORD gives light to the eyes of both'; poor and oppressor share one Maker who gives both life (cf 22:2). The common gift of life levels them before God — and reminds the oppressor he is no less accountable.
shared accountability — the oppressor who owes his life to the same God as the poor

the oppressor who meets the poor on common ground, receiving the light of life from the same LORD — the one who grinds the poor yet depends on the God who also gives the poor their sight, and to whom he too must answer
welded to the poor with whom he shares one God's light

tok (oppression/oppressor) — 'the poor man and the OPPRESSOR meet together'; the oppressor shares the poor man's Maker and owes him his very sight. Emergent: the oppressor levelled with his victim before the God who gives both life — and judges both.
presumption — tampering with revelation, exposed as falsehood
the being found a liar for adding to God's words — the presumption that tampers with or supplements divine revelation, exposed as falsehood when God rebukes it
(the true word it dares to add to)
the arrogance of amending God's flawless word, unmasked as a lie

kazab (lie/falsehood) — 'do not add to his words, lest he rebuke you and you be found a LIAR' (30:6); to supplement or tamper with God's flawless word is presumption that God exposes as falsehood. Revelation is not ours to amend (cf Deut 4:2; Rev 22:18-19).
rapacious cruelty — teeth like swords, consuming the poor and needy
the devouring of the poor and needy by those whose teeth are swords and fangs knives — the rapacious cruelty that consumes the weak off the earth, greed turned predator upon the helpless
the predatory cruelty that eats up the defenceless

akal (eat/devour) — 'to DEVOUR the poor from off the earth, the needy from among mankind' (30:14); the last mark of a corrupt generation is rapacious cruelty — greed with a predator's teeth, consuming the weak. Emergent: oppression as devouring, the wicked feeding on the poor (cf 28:15; Ps 14:4; Amos 8:4).
insufferable folly — the fool grown full and unbearable

the fool when he is filled with food — folly given plenty and ease, so that it swells into something the earth can hardly bear, a fool with abundance being intolerable where a fool in want was merely pitiable
the folly that plenty makes insufferable

nabal (fool) — 'a FOOL when he is filled with food'; one of the four things the earth cannot bear. A fool made comfortable and full grows insufferable — plenty gives folly power and removes its restraint (cf 1:32; 30:9).
